## REQ-699 — A quote can bill on a recurring schedule: a weekly / every-2-weeks / monthly payment term that signing turns into a Field subscription (demo-loop cycle 5, issue M20)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `M20` — "No monthly/recurring billing in the quote flow; Subscriptions not linked to quotes". Pair 2 typed "Cotización para María López, 305-555-0144, corte de césped y poda de setos, 4 visitas al mes, $180 al mes"; the payment step offered only one-off terms ("¿y cobro MENSUAL? No hay opción de mensual", fleet-1 stdout:406), the signature billed a one-time $180 (INV-001), and Campo → Suscripciones still said "0 ACTIVAS" (fleet-1 stdout:433). RCA analyst FEATURE_GAP (high), skeptic UPHELD, judge MISSING_IN_FLOW at demo-fixes `2444608a`. REQ-522 (cycle 3, m30) had already logged the quote→subscription half as a gap.
**Cause (RCA):** the payment step in `shared/quote-flow/wizard-terms.ts` offered only one-off schedules (due_now, net_15, 50_50, 30_30_40, deposit_bal, custom), and `SendSignedConfirmation` turned the pick into a fixed set of milestone invoices. A Subscription model existed only in the Field module (`backend/src/field/domain/data/field-stores/mod.ts` SubscriptionStore → the day's tasks → batch invoices), and nothing outside `backend/src/field` used it, so signing a quote could never start recurring billing. `shared/quote-flow/money-amounts.ts` already treated "$120 a month" as a recurring price, but nothing acted on it.
**Requirement:**
- The quote wizards' payment step (the generic one and the service-trade one; not the invoice wizard) offers **Recurring** / **Recurrente**. It opens a short form: how often (weekly, every 2 weeks, monthly), the amount per period (prefilled from the quote's total) and an optional end date. The term is stored in the English base as `Monthly · $180/mo`, `Weekly · $45/wk` or `Every 2 weeks · $90/2 wks`, with an optional ` · until YYYY-MM-DD`. Every reader localizes it: es `Mensual · $180/mes`, `Semanal · $45/semana`, `Cada 2 semanas · $90/2 semanas`, `… · hasta el 30 jun 2027`. The billing starts on the start-date term.
- `moneyAmounts` flags a price stated per period (`per`: weekly / biweekly / monthly / visit), e.g. "$180 al mes", "$180 a month", "$180/mo", "$45 a week", "$90 every 2 weeks", "$45 por visita". When the contractor's own words price the job that way, the payment step asks "You said $180 a month. Bill it once, or every month?" / "Dijiste $180 al mes. ¿Lo cobras una sola vez o cada mes?". One tap bills it on that schedule. The one-off options stay right there, and a per-visit price with no stated frequency opens the form instead.
- On the agreement (/q, the in-app preview and the PDF), the payment row reads the recurring term, and the payment schedule shows one row per period ("Monthly $180.00 · Billed every month"), never "Final payment on completion". `computePaymentSplit` never reads a recurring term as a percentage split.
- Signing a recurring quote creates no one-off milestone invoice. It creates ONE Field subscription linked to the quote (`quoteId`, `quoteNumber`) with the quote's customer, its job address (else the customer's address), one task type named after the job at the period amount, the cadence, the start day (never before the signing day), the optional end date (`isDue` is false after it) and the account's days to pay. The subscription is regrouped into a zone, so each period's visit lands on the day's round and, once done, the Field batch bills it (Field's own billing; no new cron). Creating it twice is a no-op. Paperwork reaches Field through a port (`QuoteSubscriptionPort`), because Field imports paperwork. If no subscription can be made (Field not booted, no customer), signing bills the period once, as before.
- `/field/subscriptions` and the customer card show the quote-linked subscription as "Monthly · $180/mo" / "Mensual · $180/mes", with the quote number. When the signature made that subscription (the public accept hands its id to the chat), the signed-quote chat line names the recurring charge and says it is billed from Field → Subscriptions; otherwise the line reads as before. The customer's confirmation email names the recurring charge.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/recurring-billing.test.ts` ("REQ-699 M20 …": the term's base / parse / en+es text; money-amounts `per`; quote-facts' recurring prefill from pair 2's sentence; the wizard option and termFromPick's canonical value; computePaymentSplit never splits a recurring term; localizeTermValue; the en/es keys; the island, form, doc-parts, Field page and customer-card wiring), `front-end/lib/recurring-billing.test.tsx` ("REQ-699 …": doc-parts computeMilestones gives one recurring row in en/es), `backend/src/field/domain/business/quote-subscription/test.ts` ("REQ-699 …": the subscription plan from a quote and its billing text) and `backend/src/field/domain/business/schedule/test.ts` ("REQ-699 isDue stops after endDate") · integration `backend/src/field/domain/coordinators/field-quote-subscriptions/int.test.ts` ("REQ-699 …": the port creates one linked, zoned subscription and is idempotent; a one-off quote makes none) `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-signed-confirmation/recurring.int.test.ts` ("REQ-699 …": a recurring quote bills no milestone invoice and asks the port; a non-recurring one never asks; no subscription → the period is billed once) and `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/accept-quote/signed-recurring.int.test.ts` ("REQ-699 …": the agents + Field app over HTTP, the owner's thread ends on "María López firmó Q-001 · Mensual · $180/mes — se cobra desde Campo → Suscripciones" with no invoice on the row; recordSigned names Field's billing only when a subscription was made) · e2e `backend/src/field/entrypoints/quote-subscription.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-699 M20 e2e …", the app booted over HTTP: pair 2's monthly quote is signed on the public accept; no invoice is billed; GET /field/subscriptions holds the linked monthly subscription reading "Monthly · $180/mo" / "Mensual · $180/mes"; the first period's visit, completed and pulled by the Field batch, becomes a $180 invoice) and the browser stories `e2e/recurring-billing/recurring-billing.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-699 M20: …": pair 2's sentence in Spanish, the payment step asks "Dijiste $180 al mes. ¿Lo cobras una sola vez o cada mes?" next to the one-off options, "Cobrarlo cada mes" stores "Monthly · $180/mo", /q reads "Mensual · $180/mes" and "Se cobra cada mes", the public signature bills no invoice, Campo → Suscripciones reads "De Q-001 · Mensual · $180/mes" and the thread's divider says it is billed from there; and, with no price per period typed, Recurring from the options opens its form, and every 2 weeks, $90 and a last day store "Every 2 weeks · $90/2 wks · until 2027-06-30").

## REQ-710 — The English version of a Spanish-typed quote or invoice reads in English: the base language comes from the typed text, not the app language (demo-loop cycle 5, issue M4)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, `demo-loop/runs/r37f88707/demo-report.md`), issue `M4` — "The English version of a quote or invoice written in Spanish keeps the Spanish title and line items" (STILL PRESENT from cycle 4 M32): pair 6 (app in English, quote typed in Spanish, fleet-5 stdout:40/126/132/240/243) saw "Reparación de puerta de cocina $175.00" under English headings, the title "Carmen Núñez's Reparación de puerta Agreement" and the English subject "Quote Q-001 from Ortega Handyman Services — Reparación de puerta"; pair 9's English INV-002 (fleet-8 stdout:88/274) had a translated title over the line "Retiro de refrigerador y lavadora" and "PAYMENT INSTRUCTIONS Zelle: +1 (512) 555-0108 · Efectivo" beside a "Cash" button; pair 7's English job details (fleet-6 stdout:90/217) read "Install kitchen backsplash 30 pies cuadrados subway tile". RCA analyst CONFIRMED (high), skeptic UPHELD, at 2444608a.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked in the worktree):** the quote's base language was the contractor's APP language, never the language of the text. "Lock it in" (`lock-quote/mod.ts:77,105`, `baseLang: me.language`) and the chat's lock branch (`handle-chat-message/mod.ts:3169`, `baseLang: replyLang` — `messageLang("lock it in")` is English) passed it to TranslateQuote, where the caller's word won (`translate-quote/mod.ts:195`); REQ-333 writes the base slots verbatim with no model call, so the typed Spanish became every English copy (`descriptionByLang.en`, each line's, `jobNameByLang.en`, `summaryByLang.en`), the model was asked for Spanish, `lang: "en"` was stored, and every English reader (the quote document, /q, the e-mail subject, the preview, the quote-linked invoice) showed the Spanish as English while the preview saw "nothing missing". TranslateInvoice (REQ-497) translated a standalone invoice's title and description, never its line items; the invoice stored its payment instructions as text frozen in the owner's language (`paymentInstructionsFromMethods`); the invoice e-mail and PDF drew a standalone invoice's title and concepts, and a quote-linked invoice's lines, as typed; and nothing checked a generated job-details line against its slot's language (pair 7). Introduced by 7cda0ef0 (REQ-333) and 9033db6e (REQ-497).
**Requirement:**
- A quote's base language is the language its own text reads in: `quoteTextLang` (`shared/quote-flow/quote-translations.ts`) — `messageLang` over the job name, summary, job details and every line item, each line's first capital lowered, a Spanish name's particles ("José de la Cruz", "Casa de la Rosa") not counted (`withoutNameParticles`, `shared/quote-flow/message-language.ts`). QuoteStore.create stamps it as `quote.lang`; TranslateQuote takes it first, then the caller's word, the stored `lang`, the app language, English. Lock and the chat's lock pass no base language.
- Repair: a quote whose stored `lang` disagrees with its text (`quoteLangStale`) is re-based by TranslateQuote — every per-language copy dropped, the base written verbatim, the other language translated; a failed model call still clears the wrong copies and the next run fills them. The send preview (PreviewQuoteSend) and the assistant preview (`previewTranslationMissing`) send a stale quote to the translator; the island takes the re-based `lang` from the reply.
- A standalone invoice's line items get `descriptionByLang` in the title's batch (TranslateInvoice; a batch invoice's visits, rendered by address, are left alone); its base language is read off its text the same way, the app language only a fallback; a PUT of the line items re-translates. `/invoices/:id/public` projects each line's copies while they still describe it (`invoiceLineItemsByLang`, `shared/documents/invoice-lang.ts`) and /i renders them through `localizeLineItems`.
- The invoice e-mail and PDF read the same copies: a standalone invoice's title and concepts (`invoiceTextByLang`), a quote-linked invoice's lines (`lineItemDescription` with the quote's base), in the document's language.
- Payment instructions read in the document's language at render time (`localizePaymentInstructions`, `shared/documents/invoice-form.ts`, on /i, the e-mail and the PDF): every " · " part or line that is a method's own label takes that label in the document's language; the details and the contractor's own words stay as typed.
- A generated job-details line (job name, summary, bullet) written in the other language for its slot — it reads as that language, or holds a unit or trade word only that language uses (`lineLangMismatch`) — is translated into the slot's language before the picker shows it (GenerateJobOptions: the picker and the chat-step rewrite); a failed fix keeps the line rather than dropping scope.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/c5-quote-base-lang.test.ts` ("REQ-710 …", 19: `quoteTextLang` — pair 6's quote reads Spanish, a line-initial capital is no name, an English quote with a Spanish customer name reads English, "José de la Cruz" / "María de los Santos" never make an English quote Spanish, too short → undefined; `quoteLangStale`; `previewTranslationMissing` true for the quote the old lock left; `lineLangMismatch` — "30 pies cuadrados" in English, "sq ft" in Spanish, a line in the other language, a name's particles, ordinary lines; `localizePaymentInstructions` — "· Efectivo" → "· Cash", every method's line round-trips, one method per line, free text untouched; `invoiceLineItemsByLang` — current copies projected, stale ones and no-`lang` ones dropped; the assistant island takes the re-based `lang` from the translate reply — a source check of `AsstChat.tsx`) · `backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/quote-store/base-lang.test.ts` (5: Spanish typed in an English account stamped `es`, English in a Spanish account `en`, the text over a caller's `lang`, too short → nothing, José de la Cruz never `es`) · `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/base-lang.test.ts` (3: pair 9's INV-002 e-mail in English — English title, concepts and "· Cash"; ## REQ-333 AMENDMENT (REQ-710, demo-loop cycle 5, M4) — the base language is the language the quote's text reads in
REQ-333's order for TranslateQuote's base language — "the caller's word (lock passes the contractor's app language …), else the quote's stored `lang`, else the contractor's `user.language`, else `en`" — is replaced: the language the quote's own text reads in (`quoteTextLang`) first, then the caller's word, the stored `lang`, the app language, English; QuoteStore.create stamps that language on the quote, and lock and the chat's lock pass no base language. A quote stored with a base its text disagrees with is re-based (REQ-710). REQ-333's rule itself — the base language is never sent to the model and its slots are the typed text — is unchanged. **Tests:** REQ-710's (above); REQ-333's own tests in `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-quote/int.test.ts` and `lock-quote/int.test.ts` stay green unchanged — their text ("Bathroom remodel", "Demo and haul-off") is too short to tell, so the caller's word and the stored language still decide there.

## REQ-497 AMENDMENT (REQ-710, demo-loop cycle 5, M4) — a standalone invoice's lines are translated too, from the language it was typed in
TranslateInvoice's base language is read off the invoice's own text first; the caller's word (the app language) and the stored `lang` decide only when the text can't tell. Its line items ride the title's batch (`lineItems[i].descriptionByLang`, the base slot the cache key; a batch invoice's visits excluded), a PUT of the line items re-translates them, and the public projection, the e-mail and the PDF read the per-language title, concepts and lines while they still describe the typed text. **Tests:** REQ-710's (above); REQ-497's in `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-invoice/int.test.ts` and `http.int.test.ts` stay green unchanged.

## REQ-715 — A customer carries the language they read; every send to them, and their /q /i /co pages, start in it (demo-loop cycle 5, issues m31 + c2-M29 + c3-m43 + c4-M34)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `m31` — "No per-client language" (pair 6: "¿cómo le digo que Carmen habla español? No veo campo de idioma del cliente."), merged with the backlog items `c2-M29` "Customer has no language setting; Message is only an sms: link", `c3-m43` "A client has no language preference" and `c4-M34` "No per-client language preference; assistant doesn't remember it". RCA analyst FEATURE_GAP (high), skeptic UPHELD at `2444608a`; judge MISSING_IN_FLOW for all four.
**Cause (RCA):** `backend/src/crm/dto/customer.ts` had no language field, so nothing could record that Carmen reads Spanish. Every send resolved its language as the per-send pick → the account's `commsLanguage` → en (`shared/quote-flow/comms-language.ts`), and the reminder, receipt, change-order and signed-confirmation dispatchers read `identity.commsLanguage` directly (`send-payment-reminder/mod.ts:152` `biz?.commsLanguage === "es" ? "es" : "en"`). Both send dialogs started "Sends in" on the app language; `/q` opened in English unless the visitor chose a language; `/i` and `/co` fell back to the contractor's default; and the assistant had nowhere to put "Ella habla español".
**Requirement:** A customer has an optional `language` (`"en" | "es"`). It is set in the /customers New customer form ("Customer's language" / "Idioma del cliente": Not set / English / Español, with a hint), changed in place on the card (a select row that saves on pick through `PUT /customers/:id`; "Not set" clears it), and set for the New invoice modal's inline new client. `POST` / `PUT /customers` accept en | es ("" clears it on edit and stores nothing on create) and refuse anything else with a 400. `resolveCommsLanguage` takes the customer's language between the per-send pick and `identity.commsLanguage`. Every customer-facing dispatcher resolves through it once the document's customer is known: quote and invoice email and text (paid included), the send preview, SendQuote's recorded `lastDelivery.lang` (for the published quote's customer), overdue reminders (their link carries `?lang=`), payment receipts (email, PDF, and a text link with `?lang=`), change-order requests (`/co/<id>?lang=`), the signed confirmation (email + countersigned PDF) and the field texts to a customer (service canceled, moved, on today's schedule). A per-send pick still wins. UX-28's adopt-the-first-pick rule never makes a pick that is only the customer's own language the account default (`commsLanguageToAdopt`). Both send dialogs (the /quotes panel and the assistant's review card) start "Sends in" on the customer's language (`defaultSendLang`; the review card's "Preview in" follows it until the contractor taps a pill) and offer it even when it is not one of the account's send languages (`sendLangChoices`). ## REQ-727 — /invoices never sends an invoice at once: Issue / Finish + send / Send now open a send sheet with the channel, the invoice's language and what they'll get (demo-loop cycle 5, issue c4-M16 / m56)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `c4-M16` "Invoices go out at once: no preview, confirmation or channel choice" (the merged report's m56, "'Finish + send' sends at once with no review"; fleet-r37f88707-7/stdout:311: "/invoices > 'Finish + send →' sent at once (no review/confirm step)"). Judge: MISSING_IN_FLOW, still present at demo-fixes `2444608a`.
**Cause (RCA):** `front-end/islands/InvoicesPage.tsx` sent the moment a button was pressed. The card CTA `ctaAction` → `doFinishDraft` / `doSendNow` → `dispatchInvoice` POSTed /invoices/:id/email AND /text with no body; New invoice `submit(true)` and "Send INV-001 now" (`sendPrior`) did the same. There was no dialog, no preview and no channel choice, while a quote goes through `QuoteSendDialog` (QuotesPage.tsx:64) with the channel, "Sends in" and "What they'll get". The invoice email/text routes took no language either, so a send could only go out in the Settings default.
**Requirement:**
- On /invoices, "Finish + send" (Drafting), "Send now" (Upcoming), "Issue invoice" (New invoice, client reachable) and "Send INV-001 now" (New invoice's earlier bill) send nothing by themselves. Each opens the invoice send sheet: the quote's send dialog (`SendDialog`, components/QuoteSendDialog.tsx, on lib/send-dialog.ts's rules) for the invoice. It reads "How do you want to send INV-001 to Juan Perez?" and offers Text + Email / Text / Email. Recommended and "needs an email" follow what is on file: the customer's live record, else the invoice's bill-to, which is what the send endpoints use. A missing contact is asked for in the sheet. "Sends in" starts on the invoice's own language: its typed language, else the language its quote went out in, else the Settings default. "What they'll get" shows the real email subject and body and the text, from `GET /invoices/:id/send-preview`, rendered by the send's own renderers with the dates the send will stamp. The preview sends nothing.
- Only the sheet's Send dispatches, on the picked channel(s) only, in the picked language (`POST /invoices/:id/email|text` now take `{ language }`). A one-channel send that fails names that channel only. Cancel sends nothing: a card stays where it was, and an invoice that "Issue invoice" just created stays a draft while the page says "INV-001 saved as a draft — not sent".

## REQ-730 — the /field/* list pages paint their rows in the first HTML, not a "Loading…" line waiting for hydration (demo-loop cycle 5, issue c2-p13-p)

Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none" — and, for this run, "we want to fix what we have identified as bug, polish or breaking."

Demo issue **c2-p13-p** (cycle 2 backlog, judged BUG_POLISH in cycle 5, RCA at 2444608a): "Brief 'Loading…' lines flash". Every `/field/*` route server-rendered its island with no data (`routes/field/workers.tsx` → `<FieldWorkersPage />`), and the island fetched its lists in a mount `useEffect` (`islands/FieldWorkersPage.tsx:98`), so the first HTML and the hydrated page showed a `field.common.loading` text line (`:457`) before the rows replaced it. The same held for assignments, subscriptions, batches and tasks.

Requirement: the field routes (`workers`, `assignments`, `subscriptions`, `batches`, `tasks`) read their first lists on the SSR side with the caller's session (`front-end/lib/field-ssr.ts`, the REQ-471 pattern) and pass them to the island as `seed`. A seeded island renders its rows on its first render and makes no mount fetch. A list that can't be read gives `null`, and the island fetches on hydration as before. `/field/tasks` seeds the server's day and the island uses it only when the browser's day is the same one.

**Tests:**
- unit `front-end/lib/field-ssr.test.tsx` ("REQ-730 (c2-p13-p) …"): each loader reads its paths with the session and returns null for no session or an unreadable/thrown main list; failed side reads fall back. Each seeded island (Workers, Assignments, Subscriptions, Batches, Tasks) renders its row (`wk-row`, `asg-region`, `subs-card`, `lt-past`, `tk-task`) with no "Loading…"/"Cargando…" line on its first render, and the unseeded Workers page still shows it. Every route calls its loader and passes `seed={seed}`. `jest/unit/c4-batch-checks-note-flash.test.ts` (REQ-608) now anchors on the mount effect's `load()` call, because the effect returns early when seeded.
- integration: n/a. No backend or wire change; the endpoints are the ones the islands already read, and the e2e below proves the SSR join against the real backend.
- e2e `e2e/field-ssr-first-paint/field-ssr-first-paint.e2e.test.ts`: (1) a signed-in owner with a worker gets a raw server answer for `/field/workers` that carries `data-cy="wk-row"` and the worker's name, with no browser and no JS, and none of the five `/field/*` pages contains "Loading…" or "Cargando…". (2) After a pull, the raw `/field/batches` HTML lists the batch and carries its draft's `lt-check` already ticked.

**Evidence (2026-11-12, Mac host, branch fix/c5-field-ssr-lists off demo-fixes 2444608a):**
- RED first. `deno test -A --no-check lib/field-ssr.test.tsx` with the loaders stubbed gave "FAILED | 0 passed | 10 failed" ("not implemented"; "AssertionError: a worker row is in the first HTML" / "a zone…" / "a card…" / "a past batch…" / "a task…"; "workers: the route calls loadFieldWorkersSeed("). With the loaders done and the islands at HEAD, the five render tests still failed on those same row assertions. `shots run e2e/field-ssr-first-paint` gave "✗ REQ-730 … expectation failed: the first HTML of /field/workers carries the worker row".
- GREEN. `deno test -A lib/field-ssr.test.tsx lib/field-map.test.ts lib/field.test.ts lib/quotes-ssr.test.tsx` gave "ok | 29 passed | 0 failed". `shots run e2e/field-ssr-first-paint` gave ✓ for both REQ-730 stories.
- Neighbours. jest unit project: "Test Suites: 392 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 3849 passed". `deno lint`, `deno check` and `deno fmt --check` are clean on every touched file. Browser stories, run in small batches because the host load average was 100–180: ✓ REQ-421 (field-worker-errors), ✓ REQ-365 (field-oneoff-zone), ✓ REQ-608 "pulled batch's drafts still ticked after a reload" (run alone), and ✓ REQ-143/144/145/152/157/159/163 (field-tasks).

## REQ-726 — the topbar activity pill is a short-lived notice out of the search row, and its link lands on Activity (demo-loop cycle 5, issues m6 + m57)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issues m6 "Toasts/top-bar notice stay for minutes and squeeze the search box" and m57 "Activity toast link doesn't scroll to Activity". RCA at 2444608a: m6 CONFIRMED (skeptic UPHELD), m57 CONFIRMED (skeptic CORRECTED).
**Cause (RCA):** m6: `DashTopbar` rendered `newestNotification(items)` whenever any notification existed. Nothing expired it, so "Pago registrado … hace 4m" sat on every page. `TOPBAR_CSS` hid the pill only at ≤1249px, so at 1280 and 1440 it shared the row with the greeting, the search and EN/ES. The search placeholder was cut, the sentence was clamped and the monospace time wrapped. m57: the pill links to `/dashboard#activity`, but the `DashboardPage` island's SSR render is the skeleton, so the parsed HTML has no `#activity` and the browser's fragment scroll finds nothing. The panel mounts later (at hydration on a warm start, after the fetch on a cold one), and nothing scrolled to it. The first-visit coach mark covered the page.
**Requirement:**
- The pill shows the newest event only while it is younger than 90 s (`TICKER_LIFETIME_MS`, `freshTickerItem` in `front-end/lib/ticker-pick.ts`). The 3.8 s age tick re-evaluates it, so it then goes away. An older event never stands in for it, and the Activity panel keeps the history.
- It is hidden below 1500px (`TOPBAR_CSS`), so it never shares the search row at 1280 or 1440.
- `.topbar__ticker-time` stays on one line in the body font. This supersedes REQ-542's wrap. The pill's floor is now 240px, so a one-line "ahora mismo" fits.
- On `/dashboard#activity` the island scrolls the Activity panel into view (`scrollToHashTarget`, `front-end/lib/dash-anchor.ts`), once it mounts and again when the lists land. The coach mark skips that arrival without persisting, so a later plain visit still teaches the assistant.
- Amended pins: REQ-406's 1249px test now accepts a higher breakpoint, REQ-319's source test accepts `freshTickerItem`, and REQ-542's "time may wrap" assertion is dropped. The pill-visible e2e stories (REQ-273/319/406/476/488/496/542) and cypress UX-21 now run at ≥1500px, and UX-21 uses a fresh stubbed event.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/topbar-ticker-expiry.test.ts` ("REQ-726 m6 …" ×8, "REQ-726 m57 …" ×4) · integration n/a: front-end only, with no backend or wire change. The notifications feed is unchanged. · e2e `e2e/topbar-ticker-expiry/topbar-ticker-expiry.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-726 m6 …": pill hidden at 1280/1440 with the search placeholder whole, time on one line at 1600, a 4-minute-old event not shown; "REQ-726 m57 …": cold and warm `/dashboard#activity` scroll `.content` to the panel, with no coach mark).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5-topbar-ticker off demo-fixes 2444608a):**

## REQ-714 — a signed-in worker's /worker page renders in the worker's language on the server — no English first paint (demo-loop cycle 5, m58) (2026-11-12)

The user: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707), issue **m58** — "worker view flashes English first" (BUG_POLISH, RCA CONFIRMED + skeptic UPHELD at 2444608a): `routes/worker/index.tsx` picked the SSR language from `?lang=`, the pm_worker_lang pick or the browser's pm_lang only, never the worker's session, so a Spanish worker on an English browser saw English until the island's `workerClient.me()` returned and REQ-285 flipped it to Spanish.

- With a `pm_worker` cookie, the route reads the worker on the server (GET /field/worker/me, as the island does; in-process on Deno Deploy, BACKEND_URL in dev) via `front-end/lib/worker-ssr.ts` `loadWorkerLang`, and renders in the worker's language unless `?lang=` (REQ-285) or the /worker pick (REQ-494) chose one. No cookie → no backend call; signed out or a failing backend → the old order.
- `workerRouteLang` also returns `pageLang` (the page's own, without the worker); the island gets it so Salir still returns to it and the worker's language is never written into the browser's pm_lang (REQ-416).
- The Spanish default for new workers (REQ-155, REQ-520) is unchanged; whether an English-only account should default new workers to English is left to the owner.

**Tests:**
- unit: `front-end/lib/worker-ssr-lang.test.ts` (REQ-714 workerRouteLang with a worker, readWorkerCookie, loadWorkerLang, the route + island wiring); updated `front-end/lib/worker-lang-pick.test.ts`, `jest/unit/worker-lang-session.test.ts` (REQ-416 source check follows `pageLang ?? initialLang`).
- integration: `backend/src/field/entrypoints/worker-ssr-lang.int.test.ts` — `loadWorkerLang` against the real FieldWorkerController (Spanish worker on an English browser → es; English worker → en; no cookie / signed out → null).
- e2e: `e2e/worker-language/worker-language.e2e.test.ts` "REQ-714 m58: a signed-in Spanish worker on an English browser gets a Spanish page from the server" — server HTML has `<html lang="es">` and the Spanish title; pm_lang stays en. Written, not run here (the browser lane is out of scope for this fix pass).

**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5-worker-lang-ssr off demo-fixes 2444608a):** RED on the original field.ts / WorkerScreen.tsx / route — `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/worker-ssr-lang.test.ts` → "FAILED | 3 passed | 2 failed": workerRouteLang gave `lang: "en"` (expected `"es"`, `pageLang: "en"`) for a Spanish worker on an English browser; "the route asks the backend" failed. GREEN — `deno test -A lib/worker-ssr-lang.test.ts lib/worker-lang-pick.test.ts lib/ssr-lang.test.ts` → "ok | 16 passed | 0 failed"; `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/entrypoints/` → "ok | 36 passed | 0 failed" (incl. the REQ-714 int test); `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 392 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 3849 passed"; deno lint, deno check and deno fmt --check clean on every touched file.

## REQ-732 — Escape closes every dialog on the shared Backdrop (demo-loop cycle 5, issue m26)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `m26` "Escape and backdrop click don't close dialogs" (BUG_POLISH): fleet-1 stdout:328 "Escape does not close it; the backdrop kept blocking clicks until I pressed Cancelar" on New invoice and Nueva suscripción.
**Cause (RCA, analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic CORRECTED, at demo-fixes 2444608a):** `front-end/components/Backdrop.tsx` (REQ-354) wired only `onPointerDown`/`onClick` through `createBackdropGuard`; Escape was per-dialog and opt-in. ClientsPage's New customer (REQ-289, its own document keydown listener), ClientsBoard's card and EndDemo had one; New invoice (`InvoicesPage.tsx` NewInvoiceModal) and Nueva suscripción (`FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx`) did not — and the subscription form's line search (`onComboKey`) stopped every Escape, open or not. The backdrop-click half was "plausible but unproven"; the e2e below shows a deliberate backdrop click does close both dialogs.
**Requirement:** every dialog on `<Backdrop>` closes on Escape. Open Backdrops form a stack (`createEscapeLayers` / `documentEscapeLayers` in `front-end/lib/backdrop-dismiss.ts`) with one document `keydown` listener: only the topmost dialog closes; an Escape a nested list already handled (`defaultPrevented`, or stopped before the document), one ending an IME composition, and other keys close nothing; a handled Escape is `preventDefault()`ed. Escape runs the Backdrop's `onEscape` when given, else `onClose` — so busy guards hold (New invoice `!busy`, Settings reset `!resetBusy`, work orders `!busy`). ClientsPage's own listener is removed: its Backdrop's `onEscape={() => !adding && setAddOpen(false)}` closes even a dirty draft (REQ-300: "Cancel / Escape still close it, and the draft is kept"). SearchSelect stops an Escape only while its list is open; the subscription line search only while its search is open.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/backdrop-escape.test.tsx` ("REQ-732 m26 …" ×8: Escape closes the one dialog and marks it handled; only the topmost closes; handled / composing / other keys close nothing; one listener while open, none after; out-of-order unmounts; a mounted `<Backdrop>` (preact render on deno-dom) closes on Escape, prefers `onEscape`, stops after unmount; ClientsPage has no own keydown listener and its Backdrop's `onEscape` closes unless saving; SearchSelect and the line search stop Escape only while open), `front-end/lib/form-a11y.test.tsx` (REQ-289's pin now reads the Backdrop's `onEscape`) · integration n/a — front-end keyboard behaviour only, no server path changes · e2e `e2e/backdrop-escape/backdrop-escape.e2e.test.ts` (en and es: New invoice closes on Escape, also with the focus in a field, and on a backdrop click; Nueva suscripción closes on Escape and on a backdrop click, and an Escape that shuts the open customer list leaves it up until the next Escape).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5-backdrop-escape off demo-fixes 2444608a):** RED — `deno test -A --no-check lib/backdrop-escape.test.tsx` → "SyntaxError: … does not provide an export named 'createEscapeLayers'"; with a no-op stub export: "FAILED | 1 passed | 7 failed" ("Escape calls onClose", "ClientsPage still registers its own keydown listener", "SearchSelect: an Escape that closes the open list must not also close the dialog"). `shots run e2e/backdrop-escape/backdrop-escape.e2e.test.ts` against `PORT=20508 deno task serve` → all four ✗ "timed out: New invoice closes on Escape" / "timed out: Nueva suscripción closes on Escape". GREEN — `deno test -A lib/backdrop-escape.test.tsx lib/backdrop-dismiss.test.ts lib/backdrop-overlays.test.ts lib/form-a11y.test.tsx lib/sb-drawer.test.tsx` → "ok | 28 passed | 0 failed"; `shots run e2e/backdrop-escape e2e/backdrop-dblclick e2e/form-a11y` → "9 pass · 0 fail" (REQ-732 ×4, REQ-354 ×2, REQ-289 ×3); `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint` on the 7 touched files and `deno check` on them plus every other Backdrop island clean; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 392 passed, 392 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 3849 passed, 3850 total".

## REQ-712 — No word stays in the other language: the invoice chip, the signed divider and the thread previews follow EN/ES, the nudge note follows a switch, the sidebar names the account in the page's language (demo-loop cycle 5, issue m7)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `m7` — "English left in Spanish screens and Spanish in English ones" (fleet-1 stdout:136,301; fleet-4:52; fleet-5:167; fleet-8:91,186,271; fleet-3:75; fleet-7:164). RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at demo-fixes `2444608a`; reported as cycle 4 m15/M15 and still present.
**Cause (RCA, re-checked at `2444608a`):** (2) `shared/quote-flow/chat-invoice-card.ts:107-110` `invoiceCardChipKey` mapped an invoice's `pending`/`sent`/`viewed` to the QUOTE keys `status.sent`/`status.viewed` — "Enviado"/"Visto" (masculine, a cotización's word) on a factura, although `invoices.state.sent` = "Enviada" exists (88f5458c, REQ-583). (3) `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/accept-quote/mod.ts:85-95` worded the "X signed Q-001 · deposit INV-001 … sent" divider with `t(lang, …)` when the signature arrived and stored only the string (content, `payload.label`, the thread preview), so it stayed in that moment's language. (4) `lock-quote/mod.ts:169-177` stored the thread preview "Quote locked: …" as a finished string. (5) `front-end/islands/InvoicesPage.tsx:2710-2711` kept the nudge's translated STRING in state (`setSendNote(tFor(lang, note.key))`, 7359499f, REQ-556), so "Recordatorio enviado" stayed after a switch to EN. (7) `front-end/islands/DashSidebar.tsx:65-69` worded the sidebar's identity ("Account") with `profile.user.language`, not the page's language — "Cuenta" in the English sidebar on /admin?lang=en (a gap left by REQ-592).
**Requirement:**
- An invoice card's chip in the chat reads the INVOICE's words: sent and pending → `invoices.state.sent` ("Sent" / "Enviada"), viewed and opened → `invoices.state.viewed` (new: "Viewed" / "Vista"). REQ-583's other states unchanged.
- The signed divider stores its key and vars (`payload.i18n`, REQ-589's `ChatI18nRef`; the "someone" / "the quote" fallbacks as nested keys) and the thread row stores `previewI18n` ("✓ {label}", `acceptQuote.signed.preview`); the lock's preview stores `previewI18n` (`lockQuote.preview.locked` / `.sent` + summary). The island re-renders them in the live language (`localizeChatMessage`, `localizedPreview`); the stored text stays as the fallback.
- An invoice card's send failure and note (nudge, send, delete, change date) are kept as something that words itself in a language, and are worded at render in the live language — never a string translated when the action ran.
- The sidebar's identity is worded in the page's language (`langSignal`), not the profile's saved language.
- Out of scope, per the RCA: (1) the browser's native "Please fill out this field." bubble (issue invoice-form-validate); (6) the forecast's "Invoice" label (issue customerless-invoices); the English demo pill on /worker stays (REQ-544).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/stale-lang-strings.test.ts` ("REQ-712 …": the chip keys and their Spanish words; InvoicesPage never puts a pre-worded string into the card's send state) and `front-end/lib/sidebar-identity-lang.test.tsx` (`cd front-end && deno test -A lib/sidebar-identity-lang.test.tsx` — "REQ-712 …": a Spanish profile with no name on an English page renders "Account", and "Cuenta" on a Spanish one); `jest/unit/chat-invoice-send-now.test.ts` updated (REQ-583's sent/viewed expectation now the invoice keys) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/accept-quote/signed-chat.int.test.ts` ("REQ-712 …": a Spanish owner's signed divider and thread preview re-render in English from their keys) and `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/lock-quote/int.test.ts` ("REQ-712 …": a Spanish lock's preview re-renders in English from `previewI18n`) · e2e n/a — the browser lane is not run in this cycle; the island already renders every message through `localizeChatMessage` and every thread row through `localizedPreview` (REQ-589's e2e), so the change is the data the server stores, which the integration tests drive on the real composed app / a real KV.

## REQ-742 — the landing tab title says what the hero says, and the labour line has one name (demo-loop cycle 5, issue p18-6e)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707), issue `p18-6e` "Landing title and hero differ" (BUG_POLISH).
**RCA (analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD, at 2444608a):** two copy sources for one thing. The es tab title (`front-end/lib/landing-dict.ts` `head.title`, and the SSR `<title>`, which `routes/index.tsx` read from a second copy at `lang/es.json` `landing.head.title`) said "Tú haces el trabajo. Nosotros el papeleo.", while the hero `hero.h1Sr` said "… Nosotros manejamos el papeleo.". The hero document card names the labour line from the dict (`doc.q.l3` "Mano de obra (3 días)" / "Labor (3 days)"), while the Quote showcase card in `front-end/static/landing-scripts.js` hard-coded "Plomería e instalación" / "Plumbing & install labor" for the same line.

## REQ-731 — a super admin cannot revoke their own admin (demo-loop cycle 5, issue m30)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue m30 "Owner can revoke their own admin" (BUG_HARM); RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at demo-fixes `2444608a`.
**Cause (RCA):** `front-end/islands/AdminPage.tsx` rendered the Grant/Revoke button on every /admin row, the signed-in admin's own included (REQ-227 hid only Impersonate and Demo behind `u.id !== selfId`). `POST /admin/users/:id/revoke` (`backend/src/users/entrypoints/admin-controller/mod.ts`) only checked that the caller was a super admin, then `setSuperAdmin(id, false)` — one click locked the operator out of /admin; recovery was the gated /admin/bootstrap.
**Requirement:** the revoke endpoint refuses the caller's own id with 409 `cannot_revoke_self` and the caller stays a super admin. Because the caller is always a super admin and never the target, a revoke can never leave zero super admins (the integration test pins the last-admin case). On /admin the own row's Revoke is disabled and its tooltip says why ("You can't revoke your own admin — ask another admin." / es "No puedes quitarte tu propio acceso de administrador — pídeselo a otro administrador."); every other row still grants and revokes.
**Tests:** integration `backend/src/users/entrypoints/admin-controller/revoke-self.int.test.ts` ("REQ-731 m30 …": self → 409 cannot_revoke_self and still admin; another admin → 200 revoked; the last admin still can't revoke themselves) · unit `jest/unit/admin-self-revoke.test.ts` ("REQ-731 …" ×3: `canToggleSuper` false only on the own admin row; AdminPage wires it and the en/es tooltip key exists) · e2e `e2e/admin-self-revoke/admin-self-revoke.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-731 m30: /admin disables Revoke on your own row; the API refuses a self revoke and you stay admin").

## REQ-737 — the sidebar follows a business rename in Settings without a reload (demo-loop cycle 5, issue p12)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707), issue `p12` "Sidebar keeps old business name after rename until navigation" (BUG_CONTRADICTION). RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD at demo-fixes `2444608a`.

DashSidebar applies any announced name or business name to its cached identity through `withSavedProfile` (front-end/lib/greeting-identity.ts), which re-derives the initials, and then refetches the dash cache. The sidebar does not render the business logo, so the logo is not part of the event.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/sidebar-biz-rename-c5.test.ts` ("REQ-737 …" ×5) · integration n/a — no backend or wire change; PUT /profile/identity is unchanged · e2e `e2e/sidebar-biz-rename/sidebar-biz-rename.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-737 p12: renaming the business in Settings updates the sidebar footer without a reload").

All 5 failures were the new REQ-737 cases, and every other suite passed. GREEN: `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'sidebar-biz-rename-c5|staff-placeholder-c2|topbar-page-title-c4|c3-shared-initials|admin-self-rename|welcome-toast-placeholder-c3|staff-name-placeholder'` gave "Test Suites: 7 passed · Tests: 63 passed". shots gave "✓ REQ-737 p12 … 65.5s", and the neighbouring "✓ REQ-355 …" staff-name story also passed. `deno lint` and `deno check` (front-end/) are clean on the four touched files, and `deno fmt --check` is clean on every touched file.

## REQ-734 — The field modals keep Cancel / Add in view on a laptop screen, clear of the demo pill, and the New subscription address example is neutral (demo-loop cycle 5, issue m69)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." **Cause (RCA):** `front-end/static/field.css` `.modal` is one scrolling column (`max-height: calc(100vh - 40px); overflow: auto`) and `.modal__foot` (Cancelar / Agregar) is its last child (`FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx`, the `modal__foot` at the end of the form). At 800 px tall the subscription form is taller than the box, so the footer sat below the fold of the modal's own scroller. It was not sticky, and `.modal-bg` had no demo-pill padding (REQ-618 fixed that only for the New invoice sheet). `field.subs.addressPh` was DocuMonster's own office ("4505 Socastee Blvd, Myrtle Beach, SC"), carried over from the A2Z field port (fd52cfa2, REQ-137..143).
**Requirement:** In every field-family modal (`field.css`: subscriptions, work orders, work-order delete), `.modal__foot` is sticky at the bottom of the box. It reaches over the box's own padding (`bottom: -24px`, edge to edge, white, with a soft top shadow), so the buttons are always visible and nothing scrolled under them shows through the box's bottom strip. `.modal-bg` still dims the whole window (`inset: 0`). Its bottom padding is `calc(20px + var(--demo-pill-h, 0px))` and the box's max-height subtracts the same band (as REQ-618 did), so the box ends above the demo pill. With no demo the band is 0. The address placeholder is a neutral example: "E.g. 123 Main St, Springfield" / "Ej: 123 Main St, Springfield" (en and es in sync). The legal pages' business address is untouched.

It checks that `.modal__foot` is sticky at `bottom: -24px` against `.modal`'s 24px padding, white with a shadow, and that the `.modal-bg` band padding, the `.modal` max-height minus the band, and the en/es placeholder are free of Socastee / Myrtle Beach.
- int: n/a. This is a CSS layout plus a lang string. There is no server or module seam.
- e2e: `e2e/field-subs-modal-foot/field-subs-modal-foot.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-734 (demo-loop cycle 5, m69): es|en — …"). At 1280x800 it signs in and opens /field/subscriptions → Nueva suscripción. It checks that the form scrolls, that Cancel and Add are inside the box's visible rect and within the viewport, and that a click at each button's centre hits the footer. With the form scrolled halfway, the box's bottom strip must be the footer. The address placeholder must not be DocuMonster's office.

- A first fix with `bottom: 0` passed the button checks. The added strip assertion then failed: `✗ … the footer covers the box's bottom strip — [false,false,false]`, because sticky stops at the content edge and left the 24px padding strip see-through. `bottom: -24px` fixes it.

## REQ-728 — no panel claims "0" or "none" before its data has loaded (demo-loop cycle 5, issue m15)

## REQ-717 — Change-order decision amounts are grouped like every other amount (demo-loop cycle 5, p11)

> "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none"

Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707), issue **p11** (BUG_POLISH, RCA CONFIRMED + skeptic UPHELD): when a customer approved or declined a change order on the public /co link, the owner's toast and activity feed read "(+$1600.00)". There was no thousands comma, unlike every other amount in the app. Root cause: `fmtDelta` in `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/mod.ts` built the string by hand with `toFixed(2)` and put it pre-formatted on the bus event. NotifyOnEvent then passed it through untouched in both EN and ES.

Fix: the public controller now emits only the raw signed `deltaAmountCents` (`fmtDelta` is deleted). NotifyOnEvent stores `deltaCents` in `titleParams`, and the shared renderer (`shared/quote-flow/notification-title.ts`) formats it when the title is rendered, with the same grouped money formatter used for every other amount: "+$1,600", "−$1,250.50". A legacy row that already holds a pre-formatted `delta` string still renders as before.

Tests:
- unit: `backend/src/communication/domain/coordinators/notify-on-event/test.ts` — "REQ-717 p11 (cycle 5): a change-order decision's deltaAmountCents renders grouped, signed, in en + es", "… the stored change-order row carries raw cents, never a pre-formatted string", "… a change-order row stored with the old pre-formatted delta still renders".
- int: `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/change-order-delta-format.int.test.ts` — "REQ-717 p11: the owner's feed shows a change-order decision's amount with a thousands comma (+$1,600 approved, −$1,250.50 declined)". This drives the real HTTP flow: public approve/decline → bus → NotifyOnEvent → GET /notifications.
- e2e: n/a — the int test already exercises the full server path over HTTP. The text is rendered by the shared renderer that the int test covers, and the next demo cycle re-checks it in the browser.

**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707), backlog issue `c4-m50` "Assignments map centred on Myrtle Beach SC for a Florida business" (BUG_POLISH).

## REQ-720 — a Spanish quote email's hero title is sentence case, not English Title Case (demo-loop cycle 5, issue p18-2a)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `p18-2a` "Spanish email title in English Title Case" (fleet-1 saw "Corte de Césped y Poda de Setos — María López"); RCA analyst CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_POLISH at demo-fixes `2444608a`.
**Cause (RCA):** the quote email hero runs `titleCaseJobName(summaryClean, lang)` (`backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/mod.ts:788`). For `es`, `titleCaseJobName` (`shared/quote-flow/email-format.ts`) upper-cased every word except six stopwords. ## REQ-754 — The owner's own writes reach his other open tabs: an invoice issued in one tab updates the open /customers page with no reload (demo-loop cycle 5v1, issue M5, re-opened after REQ-696)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." The owner issuing an invoice from Nueva factura (`dashboardClient.createInvoice` → `lib/api` POST /invoices) or marking one paid/deleting it (InvoicesPage's raw `fetch`es) announced nothing, so the open /customers tab never re-read.

The writing tab is marked (`announceChange(…, { fromThisTab: true })`) and does not re-read its own write; the public pages' announcements reach the owner's tabs as before. A failed write, a read, a chat post or any other path announces nothing.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/owner-write-announce.test.ts` ("REQ-754 …" ×9: path → change mapping; the verifier's two-tab situation with each tab its own module realm on a shared fake BroadcastChannel — POST /invoices through lib/api in tab A makes tab B's `followChanges(isDocChange, …)` re-read; an InvoicesPage raw write reaches tab B; a failed write announces nothing; the writing tab does not echo; REQ-493's public announcement still arrives; wiring) · integration n/a — no backend change; the cross-module path (lib/api → owner-writes → change-announce → change-feed → follower) is exercised whole, with two module realms, in the unit file, and end to end in the browser below · e2e `e2e/customers-live-owner-write/customers-live-owner-write.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-754 M5 (cycle 5v1) …": Ana owes $100; /customers open in one tab; another tab issues INV-002 from Nueva factura with no customer and BILL TO "Jorge Ramirez"; the open tab shows Jorge within 10 s without a reload and its hero equals a fresh load's).

## REQ-755 — a line correction is that line's new price, never a second line (demo-loop cycle 5v1, M15 re-test; REVISION of REQ-661)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5v1 (fix round after verify run rb88f5e5d), issue M15 "Correction sentence becomes the line-item name; requested change order filed as a revision". VERIFIER: NOT_FIXED — on Q-002 (Gomezes, "Door trim" $200), "door trim for the gomezes is not 200, it's 275" → "Updated the quote: Door trim $200 → $275. Total $2,000 → $2,075. Added Door trim ($75.00) to Q-002 … Total $2,000.00 → $2,150.00." (2 of 3 tries right).
**Why REQ-661 did not cover it:** REQ-661 (c178cd02) only read "<item> is $X not <old>" (new price first, with a `$`), and only inside a message that says "change order" (`parseChangeOrderRequest`). The verifier's sentence puts the old price first, has no `$` and no "change order", so it went to the model, which called revise_quote ($275) AND change_order "Door trim" +$75. `applyEditCalls` ran both: `changeOrderAsReprice` saw no reprice in "Door trim" or in the user's words, so the +$75 was appended as a second door trim line. RCA (analyst + skeptic, at 772ad910) for the original sentence: change-order-intent/mod.ts `parseChangeOrderRequest` / `isCleanChangeClause`; the revision (not CO) on an unsigned quote is by design (REQ-238/201).
**Requirement:**
- `parseLineCorrection` also reads the wrong price first: "<item> (for <customer>) is not / isn't / wasn't <old>, it's / should be <new>", es "<item> no es <old>, es <new>", and bare numbers ("is 275 not 200"). A unit after either number ("2 not 3 coats", "200 sqft") is not a price correction.
- `correctionForChange(change, userText)`: a change order the model sends about the line the user's words correct is that correction. The coordinator (single change_order and multi-tool `applyEditCalls`) reprices that line to the RIGHT price, never appends the difference; when a revise_quote in the same turn already set that line to that price, the change order is dropped. On a signed quote (reprice refused) it is a change order for the difference (`setsLinePrice`), once.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/change-order-intent/correction-flipped.test.ts` ("REQ-755 M15 …" ×4) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/co-correction-flipped.int.test.ts` ("REQ-755 M15 …" ×4: the verifier's revise+CO pair on draft Q-002; the CO alone; sent Q-002 → Version 2; signed Q-002 → $75 CO once) · e2e n/a — the failure is the live model sending two tool calls in one turn, which can't be produced on demand over HTTP; the integration tests drive the real chat coordinator, stores, ReviseQuote and ApplyChatChangeOrder with the model's exact calls, and the next demo cycle re-runs the scenario.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5v1-m15 off demo-fixes 772ad910):** RED — unit: "Module … has no exported member 'correctionForChange'"; integration ×3 FAILED: draft and sent kept the door trim at 27500 plus an appended 7500 line (the verifier's $2,150), and the CO-alone case left "Door trim" at 20000 with a +$75 line. GREEN — `deno test -A --unstable-kv` on both new files → "ok | 8 passed | 0 failed"; neighbours `deno test -A --unstable-kv --parallel src/agents/domain/coordinators/ src/agents/domain/business/ src/agents/entrypoints/chat-controller/` → "ok | 1092 passed | 0 failed"; `deno lint` + `deno fmt --check` clean on the 4 touched files.

## REQ-749 — /dashboard#activity stays on the Activity panel while the page settles, including the first load after login (demo-loop cycle 5v1, m57 re-opened)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5v1, issue m57 "Activity toast link doesn't scroll to Activity and catches clicks". The verifier re-tested REQ-726 on the merged demo-fixes and marked it NOT_FIXED: the first `/dashboard#activity` load right after login at 1280x720 left `.content` at scrollTop 410 of max 664, with `#activity` at top 762, which is off-screen. Three later loads reached 664 with the panel at top 508. RCA at 772ad910.
**Why REQ-726 missed it:** REQ-726 scrolled once when the panel mounted and once when the lists landed. On a cold first load the notifications feed fills the Activity panel after the lists, so at scroll time the page was shorter and `scrollIntoView` clamped at the bottom it had then (410). The feed then grew the page to 664 and nothing scrolled again. In the bad run and the good runs the panel sits at the same document position (762 + 410 = 508 + 664 = 1172), so nothing above it moved; the page below it grew late. REQ-726's e2e did not delay the feed, so it never hit this order.
**Requirement:** on `/dashboard#activity` the island holds the Activity panel in view while the layout settles. `holdHashTarget` in `front-end/lib/dash-anchor.ts` scrolls now and again on every size change of `.content`'s children or the panel (ResizeObserver). It stops when the user takes over (wheel, touchstart, keydown or pointerdown inside `.content`), after about 6 s, or on unmount. The "catches clicks" half is REQ-726 m6, unchanged: the pill expires after 90 s and is hidden below 1500px. Amends REQ-726's source pin (`scrollToHashTarget(` → `holdHashTarget(`).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/dash-anchor-hold.test.ts` ("REQ-749 m57 …" ×5: a re-scroll on every growth after the first scroll, release on user input, release after the settle window, null when there is no hash or panel, DashboardPage wiring) · integration n/a: front-end scroll behaviour only, no backend or wire change · e2e `e2e/topbar-ticker-expiry/topbar-ticker-expiry.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-749 m57 …": a fresh sign-in at 1280x720, a cold `/dashboard#activity`, the feed answering 8 events 2.5 s after the lists; `.content` must end on the panel).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5v1-m57 off demo-fixes 772ad910, `PORT=47507 deno task serve`, `shots run e2e/topbar-ticker-expiry -- --no-check`):**
- **RED** before the fix. Unit: "Tests: 5 failed" (`holdHashTarget is not a function`; DashboardPage has no `holdHashTarget(`). e2e: "✗ REQ-749 m57 … expectation failed: the page is on #activity after the feed landed (scrollTop 223 of max 355, want 355, panel top 508.375, viewport 720)". That is the verifier's clamp-then-grow.
- **GREEN:** e2e ✓ REQ-749 m57, ✓ REQ-726 m57 and ✓ REQ-726 m6. `npx jest --selectProjects=unit` gave "Test Suites: 469 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 4787 passed". `deno lint` and `deno check` are clean on `lib/dash-anchor.ts` and `islands/DashboardPage.tsx`.

## REQ-751 — "Polish this line?" never offers a line split into several unless it joins items with "+"/"plus" (demo-loop cycle 5v1, issue p18-7b re-test)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5v1, issue `p18-7b` "'Polish this line?' makes the text worse", re-tested NOT_FIXED by the verifier on merged demo-fixes (`runs/verify1/fleet-rb88f5e5d-16/stdout` l.19, l.23): "Install kitchen backsplash, 30 sq ft white subway tile with dark grout" was still offered "¿Pulir esta línea?" → "Install kitchen backsplash 30 sq ft white subway tile dark grout", and "Patch two holes in the drywall with joint compound and repaint the area" → "Patch two holes in drywall Apply joint compound Repaint the area".
**RCA (at 772ad910):** `ProfessionalizeBullet` (`backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/professionalize-bullet/mod.ts`) runs `prompts.professionalizeBullet`, whose "roughly 3–8 words" budget and "a permit … is its own line" rule push the model to compress and to SPLIT. REQ-675's deletion check (coordinator and `shared/quote-flow/polish-offer.ts` `polishOffer`) ran only when the reply was ONE line. The verifier's replies were several lines: "Apply"/"Repaint" are capitalised line starts, and the offer prints `after.join("\n")` under `white-space: pre-line`, which an accessibility snapshot reads as one run-on. The coordinator accepted any number of lines for a bullet with no "+", and `polishOffer` offered any balanced split.
**Requirement:** a bullet with no top-level "+"/"plus" joiner (`splitJoinedItems`, now in `shared/quote-flow/polish-offer.ts` and re-exported by the coordinator) names one item. An "A + B" / "A plus B" split is still offered. The prompt (en and es) says one bullet is one line however long, never split except at "+"/"plus", and no longer sets a 3–8 word budget: never cut, compress or split a clear longer line.

## REQ-753 — A change naming another customer finds that customer's quote by the name on it, from any thread (demo-loop cycle 5v1, issue M10 — REQ-654 follow-up)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5v1, issue `M10` "Assistant can't find the quote in front of it, or says it already did what was asked". The verifier re-tested REQ-654 on merged demo-fixes and found it NOT_FIXED: "In John Miller's Q-001 thread, 'Change Dana Whitfield's quote: add post caps for $300' -> 'I couldn't find a quote for Dana Whitfield, so I didn't make a new one.' though Q-002 (Dana Whitfield) exists (her own thread worked)". RCA (analyst + skeptic) at `772ad910`: `pickChangeOrderTarget` (`backend/src/agents/domain/business/change-order-intent/mod.ts`) chose the quote by name.
**Cause:** REQ-654 (`069c78b1`) read the name a quote carries (its customer's name or snapshot, or the "— Dana Whitfield" tail of its card title) only for the conversation's BOUND quote. Every other quote counted as the named customer's only when its `customerId` was one of the matched customer records. Dana's Q-002 was a chat draft with no customer linked. From her own thread it was the bound quote, so it worked. From John's thread it matched nothing, `theirs` was empty, and the result was `none`.
**Requirement:** when a customer is named, a live quote is theirs if it is linked to a customer of that name, OR if the quote itself names them (its snapshot name, or, with no customer linked, its card title). This applies to any quote, not only the bound one. An unlinked quote that names a customer on file counts as that customer's, so one linked quote and one unlinked quote of Dana's are not "ambiguous". A quote whose card names someone else is never matched. ReviseQuote, ApplyChatChangeOrder and the chat's pre-checks share this rule.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/change-order-intent/test.ts` ("REQ-753 M10 pickChangeOrderTarget: …" ×4: from John's thread, Dana's unlinked Q-002 by its card; Dana on file but Q-002 not linked, and a snapshot name; one linked + one unlinked quote of hers counts as one owner; a card naming someone else is never hers) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/apply-chat-change-order/named-other.int.test.ts` ("REQ-753 M10: from John's Q-001 thread, 'add post caps for $300' naming Dana Whitfield lands on her Q-002" ×2: no Dana record / Dana on file, Q-002 not linked; real QuoteStore + CustomerStore on in-memory KV) · e2e n/a — the failing turn depends on the live model choosing `customerName`; the real ApplyChatChangeOrder coordinator and stores are pinned by the integration test, and the chat UI only renders the reply text.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5v1-m10 off demo-fixes 772ad910):**
- RED: `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/agents/domain/business/change-order-intent/test.ts src/agents/domain/coordinators/apply-chat-change-order/named-other.int.test.ts` gave "FAILED | 35 passed | 4 failed". The int test failed with "AssertionError: Values are not equal: I couldn't find a quote for Dana Whitfield, so I didn't make a new one. Which job is this change order for?", the verifier's reply word for word.
- GREEN: the same command gave "ok | 39 passed | 0 failed".

## REQ-750 — a signature records the agreement's spelling of the signer: "Carmen Nunez" on Carmen Núñez's agreement signs and reads as "Carmen Núñez" (demo-loop cycle 5v1, issue p18-6a, re-verified after REQ-692)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5v1 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `p18-6a` "Signature labels: 'CARMEN NÚÑEZ SIGNATURE', 'SIGN HERE' kept after signing, 'Carmen Nunez' accepted vs 'Carmen Núñez'". The verifier re-tested the merged REQ-692 fix and found it NOT FIXED: the section title and the pre-sign suggestion were right, but the signed copy still read "FIRMA DE CARMEN NUNEZ" and "Gracias, Carmen Nunez — firmado…", because the unaccented name was accepted and stored although the agreement says "Carmen Núñez".
**Cause (RCA at 772ad910, plus `git show d1d1c98c`):** REQ-692 added `onFileSpellingSuggestion` only as a pad hint. The accept endpoint (`backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/mod.ts` `acceptQuote`, `acceptedName: dto.name`) still stored whatever was typed, and `quote-doc.tsx` showed `acceptedName` as is. A customer who ignored the hint left two spellings on the record, and REQ-692's own test pinned "Carmen Nunez's signature" as the expected label.
**Requirement:** when the typed name differs from the customer's name on the agreement (the issued snapshot, else the live customer) only by accents, case or spacing, the signature records the on-file spelling (`signerNameOnFile` in `shared/quote-flow/signer-name.ts`, one rule shared by the accept endpoint, the sign pad and the signed document). The accept response returns the recorded `acceptedName`. The signed copy shows that spelling on the label, heading, cursive, "By:" and thank-you, and this also covers quotes stored before the fix. ## REQ-752 — "Trabajo terminado con Juan Pérez, hazle la factura de $800": the invoice flow is prefilled with who to bill, also when the name follows "con / with / at / del" or is a possessive (demo-loop cycle 5v1, M9 re-test; amends REQ-656)

**Requirement (user's words):** "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5v1 (run r37f88707), issue M9 "Assistant will not invoice a finished job". The verifier re-tested REQ-656 on demo-fixes: the amount was prefilled 3/3, the customer only 2/3 — "Trabajo terminado con Juan Pérez, hazle la factura de $800" answered "Empecé la factura por $800: elige el cliente…" with the Nombre field empty.
**Root cause (RCA + git show a3a423f8):** REQ-656's `parseJobDoneInvoiceAsk` (backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-billing-intent/mod.ts) read the name only after invoice / bill / factura / cobrar / for / para / de / a / to. "con Juan Pérez" (and "with Mike Ross", "at Juan Pérez's", "Tom Baker's deck", "de la Sra. Ana Gómez") matched none, so the reply's `invoiceFlow` offer carried no `customerName` and the client flow had nothing to prefill. Fix: the name is also read after con / with / at / del / de la / from / of, past an honorific (Sr., Sra., Mr., don…), and from a possessive; a capitalised verb in front ("Finished Tom Baker's") is not part of the name.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-billing-intent/test.ts` ("REQ-752 M9 …" ×2) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/billing-actions.int.test.ts` ("REQ-752 M9: 'Trabajo terminado con Juan Pérez…'" → invoiceFlow {amountCents 80000, customerName "Juan Pérez"}, no model) · e2e `e2e/chat-invoice-intent/chat-invoice-intent.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-752 M9: …" on /assistant: pad at 800, the stored reply's invoiceFlow names Juan Pérez, the reply does not say "elige el cliente").

## REQ-748 — "Make the payment terms 50/50" says nothing about the start date: a payment split is not a day (REQ-663 AMENDMENT, demo-loop cycle 5v1, p18-7c)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5v1 (run r37f88707), issue `p18-7c` "Grammar 'The payment terms is already 50/50.'". The payment terms are already 50/50.".
**Cause:** RCA: the model re-sends the job's current terms through `update_terms` (the m40 mechanism). REQ-663's gate `askedTerms` (`backend/src/agents/domain/business/terms-edit/mod.ts`) counted any `\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}` as a start-date word, so "50/50" made the message "ask" about the start date, and the echoed start date got its "already" line. REQ-663's integration test re-sent only `paymentTerms`, so it never saw this.
**Requirement:** in `askedTerms` a slash pair counts as a day only when it is a real m/d or d/m (one side 1–12, the other 1–31) and is not the fraction in "2 1/2 weeks". "50/50", "30/70" and "40/60" ask about the payment terms only. "start 11/23", "12/1" and "23/11" still ask about the start date.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/terms-edit/test.ts` ("REQ-748 askedTerms: a payment split like '50/50' is not a day …") · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/terms-echo.int.test.ts` ("REQ-748 p18-7c (cycle 5v1 verifier): 'Make the payment terms 50/50' with all three terms re-sent …") · e2e n/a — the real model can't be made to echo terms deterministically in a browser run. The integration test drives the real HandleChatMessage → HandleWizardAnswer → stores path with the verifier's exact message and the demo's three-term echo.

## REQ-767 — a signed quote's line reprice offers the change order however it is asked, and whatever the line is called (demo-loop cycle 5v2, m43 re-test of REQ-664)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue m43 "Assistant refuses a signed-quote edit without offering to make the change order". The verifier re-tested REQ-664 on merged demo-fixes and found it NOT_FIXED, 1 of 3 (runs/verify1b/fleet-r2deb0973-4/stdout:31-33). Carmen Núñez's signed Q-001 has one Spanish line, "Reparar fuga debajo del fregadero (incluye cambiar llave del fregadero)" $350. Try 1 ("…to $425") offered +$75 and made draft CO-001. Try 2, in the same thread: "On Q-001, lower the line to $300 — I'm giving Carmen a discount." got a text-only "Would you like me to create a change order for a $100 discount", with no button and the wrong amount (should be −$50). Try 3, in a new thread: "Update Carmen Núñez's plumbing quote Q-001: the sink repair line should be $400 instead of $350." got the bare locked refusal with only [Open Q-001].
**RCA (analyst + skeptic, at 772ad910; re-checked here):** `ReviseQuote` returns `chatCoordinator.reviseQuote.locked` for a signed quote (revise-quote/mod.ts). REQ-664 added the offer, but only for the model's own `revise_quote` with a line name that `findLine` matches literally. In try 3 the model sent `match: "sink repair"`, which names no word of the Spanish line, so `lockedChangeOrderOffer` saw `unmatched` and offered nothing. In try 2 the model called no tool at all and did the subtraction itself, wrongly. None of `parseChangeOrderRequest` / `parseLineCorrection` / `parseTargetTotalChange` / `parseChangeOrderEdit` reads any of the three sentences (checked in a scratch run), so the offer depended entirely on the model.
**Requirement:** a line's new price on a SIGNED quote ("<line> should be $X", "lower/raise/change/set … <line> to $X", es "… debe ser $X", "baja … a $X"), on the quote it names (Q-00N) or the thread's bound quote, is read in code before the model and run as the revise. Its locked reply carries the REQ-664 one-tap offer for exactly the difference against the signed line (try 2 → −$50, try 3 → +$50). One tap or a "yes" makes that change order through `ApplyChatChangeOrder` as a draft that is not sent (REQ-652). The line is found by `findLine`, else by `pickRepriceLine`: the line sharing the most words with the name in any of its wordings (the description and each `descriptionByLang`), else the quote's only line; a tie or an unknown name on a multi-line quote is no pick. The same picker serves the model's own `revise_quote` on a signed quote. Asks about invoices, deposits, payments, CO-00N or a "change order" are not read this way. An unsigned quote's reprice is still the model's. Amendment to a REQ-315 test: "Change plumbing fixtures to $1,300 on Q-001" on a signed quote now gets the +$150 offer, and the yes makes the same +$150 change order (before, the model's own `change_order` made it directly).

Before the amendment the same run gave "1092 passed | 1 failed" on that test. `deno lint` is clean on the touched files, and `deno fmt --check` is clean on every created file and on mod.ts/revise-quote (int.test.ts was already unformatted on demo-fixes and was left so). ## REQ-766 — Monster Free's "Up to five quotes and contracts a month" is enforced: the sixth quote of the month is refused, on the API and in the assistant (demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue m17; amends REQ-733)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5v2 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue m17 "Plan lists disagree with what Free allows". The cycle-5 fix (REQ-733) moved the workers / e-signature / sending / payment-tracking / change-order lines to Free and removed Monster's "Free included" line, but explicitly left the five-quote cap neither dropped nor enforced. The VERIFIER re-tested demo-fixes and marked it NOT_FIXED: "Free still says 'Up to five quotes and contracts a month' (pricing-plans.ts:110, limits.quotesPerMonth:5) and backend/src has no cap enforcement".
**RCA (analyst + skeptic, at 772ad910):** there is no plan entitlement check in backend/src. `planOf` is used only in billing/admin code, and `PricingPlan.limits.quotesPerMonth` was "display-only" (its own comment). Neither `POST /quotes` (`backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/quote-controller/mod.ts`) nor the assistant's `create_quote` (`backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/mod.ts`) read the account's plan, so a Free account made unlimited quotes while its card promised five.
**Requirement:** the cap the plan names is the cap the app holds (Raphael's REQ-109 copy stays word for word, and it is now true). `quoteQuota` (`backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/quote-quota/mod.ts`) reads the account's plan record and its quotes. It counts the quotes created in the current calendar month (UTC), leaving out the onboarding sample (REQ-241). The cap is the plan's `limits.quotesPerMonth` (Free: 5). Paid plans have no cap, whatever their status. A downgrade to Free stays uncapped through its paid month (`paidThrough`, REQ-129). No plan on record yet is not capped (the wizard's plan step picks it before the dashboard). `QuoteAllowance` (`backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/quote-allowance/mod.ts`, a PaperworkModule injectable) is asked by every path that makes a new quote. `POST /quotes` answers the sixth with **402** `{ ok:false, reason:"quote_limit", limit:5, used:5 }` and stores nothing. The reply is `chatCoordinator.quoteLimit`: en "You've made your 5 quotes for this month on Monster Free, so I didn't start a new one. Monster has unlimited quotes: upgrade in Settings → Plan, or your 5 new quotes start again on the 1st." (es in sync). Revising the bound draft is not a new quote and goes on as usual. Amends REQ-733's "Not changed" note: the cap is enforced, not left open.
