## REQ-765 — a dialog's dim covers the demo pill and its band on the presenter's stage too, and softens the customer's pill (demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue p18-3d, re-opened after REQ-643)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5v2 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `p18-3d` "Send modal dim layer doesn't cover the demo pill". The verifier re-tested REQ-643's fix on demo-fixes and found it NOT FIXED: "live demo, customer 390x844 Send dialog open: .send-dialog__backdrop is position:fixed top 0 bottom 780 (h 780 of 844 vh), parent .quote-review__send-split (not portaled to body); stage shows the bottom 64px demo-pill band (beige strip + 'DocuMonster · Connected · End demo') at full brightness, not dimmed".
**RCA (analyst + skeptic at 772ad910):** the customer pill is z-index Z+3 (`DemoModeOverlay.tsx` `Z = 2147483000`), above every app dialog by design (REQ-379: End stays reachable), and a full-screen backdrop is not "page" for `dockPill` (`countsAsPage`, `PAGE_BACKDROP_AREA` 0.6), so it stays home and bright. On the phone the mobile `.app` is `position:fixed` + `transform` (`assistant-page.css` mobile `.app`), so the send backdrop's `inset:0` stops at the app's foot (780) and the band (z-index 1, root context) is not under it. **Why REQ-643 did not cover it:** REQ-643 (d5f31c4b) painted only the customer's OWN band in the backdrop's dim (`bandDim`). The mirror skips the overlay (REQ-242), so the stage draws the band and the pill itself (`demo-band-ghost`, `demo-pill-ghost`) from the `pill` peer message, which carried `band` + `bandBg` but no dim. Those ghosts sit over the replayed frame, so the presenter saw a bright beige strip and a bright pill under a dimmed page. REQ-643's e2e only checked the customer's window, and this story's red run shows that window was already dimmed: `"band":"linear-gradient(rgba(20, 44, 48, 0.45), …)"`.
**Requirement:** while a dialog's see-through dim is up on the customer's page, (a) the `pill` message carries that dim (`dim`, the backdrop's colour, validated like `bandBg`); (b) the stage paints its band ghost in it (`bandPaint(bandBg, dim)`) and softens its pill ghost (`opacity` `PILL_UNDER_DIALOG_OPACITY` = 0.6, `data-dim`); (c) the customer's own pill (and its folded tab) is softened to the same opacity. It stays above the dialog and clickable (REQ-379). An opaque full-screen sheet, or no dialog, means no dim, and everything is back at full brightness when the dialog closes. Portalling `Backdrop` to `<body>` is still not done, for REQ-643's reason (event bubbling and ancestor-scoped CSS for every app dialog). The stage would draw its ghosts over the frame anyway, so a portal would not fix the verifier's view.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-dialog-dim-stage.test.ts` ("REQ-765 …" ×6: `dialogDim` for the send backdrop / opaque / transparent; the softening opacity; `parsePeerMessage` keeps `dim` and drops junk; the verifier's beige band painted under the dim; the overlay sends `dim` and softens its pill; the stage paints the band ghost with `bandPaint(…, pillFace.dim)` and softens the ghost) · integration n/a — front-end overlay/stage and the peer message's parser only; the relay forwards any parsed message unchanged, and the parser is unit-tested · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-dialog-dim-stage.e2e.test.ts` (the verifier's situation: a live demo with the customer at 390×844 on /assistant and the send dialog's `.send-dialog__backdrop` inside `.quote-review__send-split` inside the transformed `.app`. The stage's band ghost is in the dim and its pill ghost is softened; on the customer's screen the band is in the dim and the pill is softened; when the dialog closes, everything is bright again).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, Mac host, branch fix/c5v2-p18-3d off demo-fixes 772ad910):** RED first. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --runTestsByPath unit/demo-dialog-dim-stage.test.ts` → "Tests: 6 failed, 6 total" (`dialogDim is not a function`, `Expected pattern: /dialogDim\(/`, `/dim: m\.dim/`). `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-dialog-dim-stage.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` → "✗ REQ-765 … timed out: stage: the band ghost is dimmed and the pill ghost softened — {"band":"none","bandBg":"rgb(242, 235, 224)","pill":true,"pillOpacity":1}" (the verifier's bright beige strip). An earlier ordering of the same story showed the customer's band already dimmed and her pill at `"pillOpacity":1` with the backdrop at `{"top":0,"bottom":780}` of 844. GREEN: `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'unit/demo-'` → "Test Suites: 58 passed · Tests: 735 passed". `shots run` of this story plus the demo-pill band-room / yield / folded-label / band stories → "✓ REQ-765 39.8s", "✓ REQ-643", "✓ REQ-545", "✓ REQ-637". REQ-440 (`demo-pill-band`) fails with "on /q the pill is a small tab" both here and on a pristine detached worktree at 772ad910 (REQ-637 keeps the /q pill whole), so it was already failing. `deno lint` and `deno check` are clean on the overlay, the stage, pill.ts and protocol.ts. `deno fmt --check` is clean on pill.ts, protocol.ts and the two new tests; the two islands were not fmt-clean at the base and were left unformatted.

## REQ-763 — a self-correction typed in the CHAT drafts only the correction; a deadline typed with a draft is said back (demo-loop cycle 5v2, M7 — REQ-653 not fixed)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue M7 "Assistant drops or garbles details (LVP/porcelain, niche, address, Thanksgiving, bad email ignored)". The verifier re-ran it on the merged demo-fixes (772ad910) after REQ-653 and found it NOT FIXED: "'install LVP no wait porcelain tile 12x24…' gave Q-001 'LVP and porcelain tile install' with lines 'LVP installation (200 sqft) $1,800' + 'Porcelain tile installation (200 sqft, 12x24) $1,800' = $3,600 (correction ignored; Thanksgiving deadline not shown). Address and bad email were handled correctly." RCA (analyst + skeptic at 772ad910): no correction or deadline rule reached the model; the REQ-439 typed-items check counts "LVP" as a typed item.
**Why REQ-653 missed it:** its `dropSelfCorrections` pre-pass ran only inside `GenerateJobOptions` (the job-options picker). The verifier typed the job in the chat, which drafts through `HandleChatMessage` → the chat model's `create_quote`. That model got the raw words, and the REQ-439 yardstick (`typedWorkItems` over the raw user turns) could re-ask for the "missing" LVP line. The pre-pass also took back as many words as the correction had, so "install LVP no wait porcelain tile 12x24" lost "install", and "Quote for Mark Henderson: install LVP no wait …" lost the name. REQ-653's deadline check only runs once terms exist, so a first draft typed with "done before thanksgiving" said nothing about it.
**Requirement:**
- The chat model reads every user turn through `dropSelfCorrections`. The REQ-439 typed-items yardstick, the REQ-445 stated-total read and `settleCreateQuote`'s typed amounts read the corrected text too. The transcript keeps the words as typed.
- `dropSelfCorrections` never takes back the clause's action word ("install", "replace", "instalar" …) or anything before it. It never takes back a typed quantity and its unit ("200 sqft"), unless the correction starts with a number ("3 windows make that 4 windows"). A size riding with the correction ("12x24") is not counted as a replacing word. ": " is a clause boundary.
- A `create_quote` turn whose message names a deadline adds `chatCoordinator.terms.deadline.noted` (en + es) to the reply: "Deadline noted: the job has to be done before Nov 26, 2026 …". The start and time to complete are checked against it when they are set (REQ-653).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/self-correction-chat.test.ts` ("REQ-763 …" ×4: the verifier's message, a kept action word, a lead-in and a typed quantity, a quantity corrected by a quantity) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/self-correction-chat.int.test.ts` ("REQ-763 M7 (cycle 5v2) …" ×2: the verifier's chat message drafts porcelain only, with no LVP sent to the model or the re-ask and the transcript as typed; the deadline is shown in the reply) · e2e n/a: there is no new UI. The change is what the model is sent and the reply text, and both are pinned through the real coordinator against the in-memory KV. The browser lane is not run per the cycle rules.

## REQ-760 — /quotes says "ready to send" only for drafts that are (demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue m14; re-fix of REQ-698)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5v2 (run r37f88707, demo-report.md), issue `m14` "Dashboard and Quotes counts disagree with the real state". A verifier re-tested REQ-698 on merged demo-fixes (`772ad910`) and found it NOT FIXED: the sidebar badge now follows a delete on /quotes, but the /quotes headline read "Nothing sent yet — 1 draft ready to send." for Q-002 Bob Smith, a draft the assistant had only drafted ("Quote drafted · review", card "Finish + send →"), never locked.
**Cause:** REQ-698 taught the DASHBOARD the thread status (`quotes.readyToSend`, ComputeDashboardStats) but GET /quotes (`BuildQuoteCards`) carried no readiness at all, and `QuotesHero` worded every non-undelivered draft as `quotesHero.draftsOnlyTitle` ("… ready to send"). QuotesPage never used the server's readyToSend rule.
**Requirement:**
- One backend rule, `readyToSendQuoteIds` (`backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/list-conversations/mod.ts`): of a user's drafts, the ids whose thread status (`threadFlowOf` + `threadStatus`, as the chat header and the thread list) is "readyToSend". The dashboard's `quotes.readyToSend` is its size; `BuildQuoteCards` marks every draft card `readyToSend: true|false` with it. The two pages can never disagree.
- The /quotes hero (`QuotesHero`, fed `readyCount` from `quotesHeroNumbers`) says "Nothing sent yet — {n} draft(s) ready to send." only for the drafts marked ready; with none ready it says en "Nothing sent yet — {n} draft(s) in progress." / es "Nada enviado todavía — {n} borrador(es) en curso." (`quotesHero.draftsInProgressTitle.one|other`). A card without the flag (older server) counts as ready.
**Tests:**
- unit: `front-end/lib/quotes-hero-ready.test.tsx` (deno, ×4 — the verifier's Q-002 reads "in progress" en/es, never "ready to send"; a ready draft still reads ready; `readyCount`), `jest/unit/c5v2-quotes-ready-to-send.test.ts` (×4 — mapCard carries `readyToSend`, QuotesPage passes `readyCount={heroNums.readyCount}`, client/Quote types, en/es keys).
- integration: `backend/src/analytics/domain/coordinators/build-quote-cards/ready-to-send.int.test.ts` (drafted-only assistant quote → `readyToSend: false`, finished-wizard draft → `true`, and the dashboard counts the same ones).
- e2e: `backend/src/analytics/entrypoints/quotes-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-760 …" — over HTTP, GET /quotes flags agree with GET /analytics/dashboard `quotes.readyToSend`). Browser lane n/a: the hero is a server-renderable component pinned by the deno render test, and its data path by the HTTP e2e.

## REQ-759 — the picker's internal version label ("· Versión breve") never becomes a job's title (demo-loop cycle 5v2, m49 re-open)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue m49 "Internal option name 'Concise' reaches the client", re-opened by the verifier on the merged demo-fixes after REQ-667: "Construir una terraza de madera de 12x16 para Marta Silva…" gave the cards "Terraza de madera [Breve]" and "Terraza de madera · Versión breve [Detallada]"; picking the second, the customer page /q/… read "Terraza de madera · versión breve".
**Why REQ-667 missed it:** REQ-667 (commit 6d1d039d) only replaced ROLE words (concise/standard/detailed, "scope of work") that the MODEL wrote into summary/jobName. This qualifier was added by our own code: `normalizeOptions` (`generate-job-options/mod.ts`) "disambiguated" two equal model jobNames with `disambiguateTitle`, which appends "· Versión breve" / "· Alcance ampliado" by position (so the DETAILED card was titled "breve"); `padToThree` and `fallbackOptions` titled their extra card with `versionTitle(…, "short")`, and the island's offline `localFallbackOptions` (`AsstChat.tsx`) did the same. The picked option's jobName is the quote's title.
**Requirement:** every version of a job keeps the job's own title, in every language — no "· Versión breve" / "· Short version" / "· Alcance ampliado" / "· Wider scope" qualifier in any jobName or summary, from the model path, the padding, the server fallback or the island's offline fallback. The cards are told apart by their `style` label (`labelVersionStyles`, REQ-446), now applied to both fallbacks too.
**Tests:** integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/generate-job-options/version-qualifier.int.test.ts` ("REQ-759 …": the verifier's terraza — two model options both "Terraza de madera" → both titled "Terraza de madera", styles concise/detailed; three equal jobNames in es+en → no qualifier, styles concise/standard/detailed; a padded version keeps the title; the degraded fallback keeps the title and is labelled detailed/concise) · unit `jest/unit/version-title-not-client.test.ts` ("REQ-759 …": the island's `localFallbackOptions` never calls `versionTitle` and labels its cards with `labelVersionStyles`) · `jest/integration/ux-job-name.int.test.ts` UX-41 amended (REQ-759 AMENDMENT: the second card is "Cambiar 12 tablas", no qualifier) · e2e n/a — the title is computed by the server's option set (pinned at integration level) and the picker renders it verbatim; the existing picker stories already show the `jobopt-style` label.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5v2-m49 off demo-fixes 772ad910):** RED: `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/agents/domain/coordinators/generate-job-options/version-qualifier.int.test.ts` → "FAILED | 1 passed | 3 failed": `internal version label reaches the client: "Terraza de madera · Versión breve"` (twice) and `"Construir terraza de madera · Versión breve"` (fallback); `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'unit/version-title-not-client\.test\.ts$'` → "Tests: 2 failed, 2 total" (`Expected pattern: not /versionTitle\(/`, `Expected pattern: /labelVersionStyles\(/`). GREEN: `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/generate-job-options/` → "ok | 54 passed | 0 failed"; jest unit (version-title-not-client, job-picker-keep-selection, ux-job-name-es, option-near-twins, job-options-seed) → "Tests: 43 passed, 43 total"; `deno check islands/AsstChat.tsx` and `deno lint` clean; backend `deno lint` on the folder clean; neighbours `deno test -A --unstable-kv` over generate-job-options, job-details-controller, es-trade-glossary, polish-job-details, handle-chat-message → "ok | 311 passed | 0 failed (8m15s)"; mod.ts (fmt-clean at base) and the new files formatted.

## REQ-761 — A resting demo pointer lets the label under it be read: the arrow turns see-through (demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue c4-S12b re-opened; REVISION of REQ-374 / REQ-633's always-opaque arrow)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12, on the 20-agent demo's findings: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5v2 (run r37f88707), issue c4-S12b: "Pair 5 employee misread 'TBD' as 'Today' because the customer's pointer covered it." The verifier re-tested the merged demo-fixes after REQ-633 and found it NOT FIXED: the tag is offset (a small 'A' bubble) but the arrow is "solid/opaque dark green (opacity 1) and covers part of the letters 'fo'"; `pointerLook()` returned `arrow: 1` always.
**Why the previous fix missed it (git log -S pointerLook: 352ea567 REQ-374, a390ff57 REQ-633):** REQ-374 (cycle 2, p8) made the arrow always opaque because a dimmed arrow (.45/.55, a thin 1.6 px stroke) read as faint; REQ-633 kept that on purpose ("c4-S12b is met by moving and shrinking the tag, not by fading the pointer") and only moved the TAG. The arrow itself — the part resting on the letters — was never changed, so `shared/demo-mode/motion.ts` `pointerLook(resting)` still returned `arrow: 1` and `DemoPointer.tsx` drew the CUSTOMER_COLOR body solid over 'TBD' on the employee's stage (DemoStage → DemoPointer) and the presenter's on the customer's screen.
**Requirement:** a MOVING arrow stays fully opaque (REQ-374 p8: easy to follow). Once the pointer rests (TAG_IDLE_MS, the same rest the tag uses) the arrow's svg drops to `ARROW_REST_OPACITY = 0.8` — the white halo and dark outline stay clearly visible, never the faint .45/.55 of old — and its coloured body to `fill-opacity` `ARROW_REST_FILL = 0.5`, so at most 40 % of the colour lies over the letters under it; a see-through arrow drops its drop-shadow (it would haze the text). The tag is unchanged (REQ-633: opaque, compact). Any re-placement makes the arrow solid again. Applies to every DemoPointer: the customer's pointer on the employee's stage, a presenter's on the customer's screen, a peer's.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-pointer-see-through.test.ts` ("REQ-761 …": moving look solid; resting `arrow` < 1 and ≥ .7; `arrow × fill` ≤ .5 and > .2; tag still opaque + compact) and `front-end/lib/demo-pointer-see-through.test.tsx` ("REQ-761 …": the exported `PointerArrow` rendered for real (SSR) in the customer's green with the resting look — svg opacity < 1 and ≥ .7, body ≤ .5, dark outline kept; with the moving look opacity 1, fill 1); REQ-374 / REQ-242 / REQ-633 "arrow always 1" assertions amended in `jest/unit/demo-mode-pointer-look.test.ts`, `jest/unit/demo-mode-mirror.test.ts`, `jest/unit/demo-pointer-tag-text.test.ts` · integration n/a — no backend or wire change; the look is client-only rendering, pinned by the SSR test · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-pointer-coachmark.e2e.test.ts` amended (REQ-633 m35 story: the resting arrow's body pixel is his colour blended at svg opacity × fill-opacity over the scrim sampled with the arrow hidden; m2 + c4-S12b story: at rest the arrow on the button is not solid — opacity < 1, ≥ .7, body ≤ .5) — written, not run: the browser lane is not run in the demo-loop fix step.

## REQ-758 — a signature that SCHEDULES the bill binds it to the thread: header and list say "Signed · Invoice scheduled" (demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue m20 re-opened; amends REQ-700)
"Fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo issue m20 ("Status names disagree between the chat header, the list and the client card"), cycle 5v2: the verifier, live on demo-fixes after REQ-700, signed a "Payment upon completion" quote (INV-001 scheduled) and saw chat header "Q-001 · QUOTE ACCEPTED" and list chip "Quote accepted" while /invoices said "SCHEDULED". RCA: REQ-700 made ListConversations / LoadConversation read the row bound by `conversation.invoiceId`, but `AcceptQuote.recordSigned` (backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/accept-quote/mod.ts) bound the conversation — and stamped the divider's `invoiceStatus` — only when the signature SENT an invoice; REQ-697's scheduled completion invoice was never bound, so both readers had no row and fell back to "Quote accepted". REQ-700's integration test hand-built a conversation already bound to the scheduled invoice, so it never exercised the real coordinator. Fix: recordSigned binds the bill the signature made, sent or scheduled (`invoiceId` + `invoiceStatus` on the conversation, `invoiceStatus` on the divider); "send the invoice" in the chat then sends that bill instead of drafting a second one. The client card's "Active job" is the client's lifecycle stage, not the bill's status, and is left as is.
**Tests:** integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/accept-quote/signed-scheduled-status.int.test.ts` ("REQ-758 m20 (5v2) …": the real composed app, the customer signs on /q with "Payment upon completion" → the list row and the thread snapshot carry "scheduled" and the header and list chip both read `asstChat.header.signedScheduled`; the bill sent on the paperwork side → both read `asstChat.header.signedInvoiced`) · unit n/a — the chip/header words for "scheduled" are already pinned by REQ-700's `jest/unit/live-invoice-status.test.ts`; the defect was the missing server binding · e2e n/a — the integration test drives the real HTTP app (public sign → list → thread GET); the browser lane is not run by fix agents.

## REQ-764 — "Text + Email" on a quote never tries to text a number that can't receive texts; the divider says "not texted: <reason>" (demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue m12)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5v2 (run r37f88707), issue m12 "'This number can't receive texts' gives no reason while assistant still tries to text" — re-test of REQ-681. The verifier, on merged demo-fixes, saw the dialog note's reason (REQ-681 fixed that), but after "Text + Email" to Maria's (512) 555-0144 the quote divider said "Quote + Agreement emailed to maria@example.com — text failed (that's a reserved test number …)".
**Why REQ-681 missed it (git log -S phoneCantReceiveTexts → 62b1be78):** REQ-681 added the `phoneCantReceiveTexts` skip only to `SendChangeOrderAlert`. The quote dispatcher `SendQuote` (`backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote/mod.ts`) still called `SendPaperworkSms.run` for every "both" send. The guarded dispatch refused the 555 number with `failureCode: "fictional"`, and `buildDivider` turned that into `sendQuote.divider.emailedTextFailed`.
**Requirement:** On a "both" quote send, `SendQuote` first asks `SendPaperworkSms.recipientCantText`, which resolves the recipient the way `run` does and applies the shared REQ-569 predicate. When the number can't take texts, `SendPaperworkSms.run` is never called. The email still goes out, and the divider reads `sendQuote.divider.emailedNotTexted`: "Quote + Agreement emailed to {emailedTo} — not texted: {reason}" / "Cotización + Acuerdo enviada por correo a {emailedTo} — no se envió por texto: {reason}", with the `sms.fictionalNumber` reason. It never reads "text failed". The payload carries `smsSkipped: true` and keeps `smsFailureCode: "fictional"`, so REQ-226's "check the number" form still offers the fix. A text-only send still reports its refusal (REQ-226/525), and the dialog never offers one for such a number (REQ-569).
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote/divider.test.ts` ("REQ-764 m12 divider: email + skipped text says 'not texted: <reason>' in en and es") · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote/int.test.ts` ("REQ-764 m12 (cycle 5v2) send-quote: 'Text + Email' to a 555-01XX cell emails, never dispatches the text …", "REQ-764 m12 (cycle 5v2) send-quote: the Spanish divider …") · e2e n/a: the divider is a server-composed string that the existing markup renders as is, and the integration test drives the real SendQuote → SendPaperworkEmail/SendPaperworkSms path with the verifier's exact customer. The browser lane is not run per fix.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5v2-m12 off demo-fixes 772ad910):** RED: `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote/int.test.ts src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote/divider.test.ts --filter REQ-764` gave "0 passed | 3 failed". The integration failure was "never 'text failed': Quote + Agreement emailed to maria@example.com — text failed (that's a reserved test number (555-01XX or area code 555) — it can't receive texts. Check the number or send by email)", which is the verifier's line. GREEN: `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote/ src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-sms/ src/agents/domain/coordinators/list-conversations/` gave "ok | 53 passed | 0 failed". `deno lint` and `deno check` are clean on the touched modules. ## REQ-762 — one typed price put on every job is one line too; REQ-666 re-verified NOT FIXED (demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue m48)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5v2, issue `m48` "Assistant split $350 into $175 + $175 without asking". A verifier re-tested REQ-666's fix on the merged demo-fixes and found it NOT FIXED: try 1 "Carmen… fregadero, $350" gave one $350 line (ok), but try 2 "Cotización para Rosa Delgado: cambiar el calentador de agua y reparar la llave de la regadera, $900" gave "Cambio de calentador de agua $900.00" + "Reparación de llave de regadera $900.00", total $1,800.00.
**RCA (analyst + skeptic, at 772ad910):** the message is not read as a stated total (`statedTotalCents` → undefined), so the model priced several jobs from one typed amount on its own. Why REQ-666 missed it: `keepOnePrice` (`backend/src/agents/domain/business/stated-price/mod.ts`) only acts when the lines add up to EXACTLY the typed amount (the $175 + $175 split). The model's other move, putting the one typed price on every job ($900 + $900 = $1,800), sums to twice the price, so it was saved as drafted. The prompt rule only said "never split it evenly".
**Requirement:** on a new quote (not a revision of the draft on file), when the contractor typed exactly one amount (no rate) and two or more of the model's priced lines each carry that same amount (any $0 lines beside them included), the quote is saved as ONE line at that amount, and the largest line names the rest ("Cambio de calentador de agua (incluye reparación de llave de regadera)" $900). The REQ-666 exact-sum split still folds. A typed price on one job beside a job the model priced itself, and a draft revision, are unchanged. `prompts.systemQuote` and `prompts.tools.createQuote.lineItems` (en and es) add "never put that same price on each job".
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/stated-price/test.ts` ("REQ-762 m48 …" ×3: the verifier's $900 + $900 is saved as one $900 line in es; the typed price on three jobs plus a $0 line is one line in en; a per-job typed price beside a model estimate, and a draft revision, are kept) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/price-target.int.test.ts` ("REQ-762 m48: the verifier's Rosa Delgado job at one typed $900 is saved as ONE $900 line …" runs the real coordinator and quote store with the verifier's model answer stubbed; "REQ-762 m48: the quote-phase prompt and the create_quote lineItems description (en and es) …" checks prompt text an agent executes) · e2e n/a — the model is stubbed in every browser lane, so a browser test cannot produce the repeated price; the integration test drives the real chat coordinator end to end on the backend.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5v2-m48 off demo-fixes 772ad910):** RED first. Unit `--filter REQ-762` gave "FAILED | 1 passed | 2 failed" (`settleCreateQuote` returned `keep`, not `save`). Integration `--filter REQ-762` on the unfixed code gave "FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed": the stored estimatedTotal was 180000, not 90000, which is the verifier's $1,800, and the prompt had no rule. GREEN: `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/ src/agents/domain/business/stated-price/ src/agents/domain/business/tool-calls/ src/agents/domain/business/llm-prompts/ src/agents/domain/business/openai-tools/` gave "ok | 363 passed | 0 failed" and "ok | 30 passed | 0 failed". `deno lint`, `deno fmt --check` and `deno check` are clean on the touched backend files.

## REQ-768 — "Job done, invoice X" for a customer whose quote was never signed (unsent or sent) opens the invoice flow prefilled from that quote, never "send it first" / "hasn't signed yet" (demo-loop cycle 5v3, M9 re-test; amends REQ-656 / REQ-752 / REQ-583)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5v3 (run r37f88707), issue M9 "Assistant will not invoice a finished job (makes a quote / refuses / schedules)". The verifier re-tested REQ-656 + REQ-752 on merged demo-fixes and found it NOT_FIXED: "Ya terminé el trabajo de Mike Johnson, mándale la factura" (Mike's quote never sent) still answered "Esta cotización aún no se ha enviado. Envíala primero — la primera factura sale automáticamente cuando el cliente firme."; a lead's "Finished the job for Maria Lopez, need to invoice her" (sent, unsigned quote) answered "The customer hasn't signed yet — the first invoice goes out automatically…", with no invoice flow. New customers (no quote) did get the prefilled flow.
**Cause (RCA at 7c9671b3 + git show of REQ-656/752):** REQ-656 opened the invoice flow only when no job could be found (`handle-chat-message` "no job bound" branch). When the message names a customer who HAS a quote (`namedCustomersJob`), the thread was bound to it and `AnswerBilling` → `billingReply` (`backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-answers/mod.ts`) answered; REQ-656 taught `billingReply` the job-done cue only for a SIGNED job with a scheduled invoice. For an unsigned quote it returned REQ-368's `notSent` / `notSigned` before ever reading `jobDone`. REQ-583's pair-6 integration test even pinned "hasn't signed" for a job-done ask on a sent quote.
**Requirement:** a job-done invoice ask (`parseJobDoneInvoiceAsk`) about a quote that is not signed — draft/unsent or sent/viewed — is answered with the invoice flow: `billingReply` returns `invoiceFlow: { details (the quote's description, else summary, else job name), amountCents (an amount typed with the ask, else the quote's total), customerName, customerEmail }` and the text "Job's done — let's bill it. The quote was never signed, so I've started an invoice for {name}, {amount}: check the details and send it." (es: "Trabajo terminado — vamos a cobrarlo. La cotización no se firmó, así que empecé la factura para {name}, {amount}: …"; a no-amount variant asks for the amount). `AnswerBilling` puts the offer on its reply's payload, so the chat opens the invoice flow on arrival. In a new chat the found job is bound only when the answer is NOT the invoice flow — the flow makes its own invoice and the thread keeps its "Start the invoice" button. Nothing is created or sent by the reply. Without the job-done cue an unsigned quote still answers REQ-368's notSent / notSigned; a signed job keeps REQ-656's Send-now answer. en + es in sync.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-answers/test.ts` ("REQ-768 M9 billingReply: …" ×4: unsent quote → offer with Mike Johnson, $1,250, his email, no "Envíala primero"; sent unsigned → offer, no "hasn't signed"; a typed amount wins; no cue → unchanged) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/billing-actions.int.test.ts` ("REQ-768 M9: …" ×3: the verifier's two exact sentences in a new chat → invoiceFlow offer, no model, no invoice, thread unbound; a thread bound to the unsigned quote → the same offer), plus "REQ-583 M2: pair 6 …" amended (REQ-768 AMENDMENT: the job-done ask on a sent unsigned quote now gets the $450 invoice flow, thread unbound) · e2e `e2e/chat-invoice-intent/chat-invoice-intent.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-768 M9: 'Ya terminé el trabajo de Mike Johnson, mándale la factura' …": a customer with an unsent $1,250 quote; typed on /assistant, the invoice flow's pad opens at 1250, the offer names Mike Johnson, no "Envíala primero").

## REQ-769 — "Change Dana Whitfield's quote: add post caps for $300", typed in another customer's thread, lands on her quote without asking for a quote number (demo-loop cycle 5v4, issue M10 re-test; follows REQ-654 / REQ-753)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5v4 (run r37f88707), issue `M10` "Assistant can't find the quote in front of it, or says it already did what was asked". The verifier re-tested on merged demo-fixes (`a2492852`) and found it NOT_FIXED: from Tom Henderson's Q-002 thread, "Change Dana Whitfield's quote: add post caps for $300" and "Change Dana Whitfield's quote: add a shower niche for $250" both got "Please provide the quote number for Dana Whitfield's quote so I can add the post caps for $300.", though Dana's only quote, Q-001, existed. The variant "Add post caps for $300 to Dana Whitfield's quote" worked and made CO-001.
**Cause:** REQ-654 and REQ-753 fixed `pickChangeOrderTarget`, but this reply never reached it. "Please provide the quote number…" is not one of the app's own strings. It is model text, which means the model made no tool call. The coordinator reads a change in code only when the words "change order" are present (REQ-238 `parseChangeOrderRequest`) or when a new total is given (REQ-377). "Change <name>'s quote: add <item> for $N" matched neither, so whether anything happened depended on the model, which asked for a number instead.
**Requirement:** "<name>'s quote/estimate/job" plus an added or credited item with exactly one amount is read in code. That covers "Change Dana Whitfield's quote: add post caps for $300", "Add post caps for $300 to Dana Whitfield's quote" and "On Tom Henderson's job, credit $100 for the missed visit". It becomes the same `change_order` action that ApplyChatChangeOrder runs, so `pickChangeOrderTarget` finds her quote by name, linked or not. The change is applied by the quote's state: added to a draft, a pending revision on a sent quote, or a change order on a signed one. The model is never asked. These cases are left to the model: no add/credit verb (a reprice such as "cabinets $7,000"), no amount, two amounts, nobody named ("the customer's quote"), a narrative clause, or a NEW quote asked for (`parseNamedQuoteChange` in `backend/src/agents/domain/business/change-order-intent/mod.ts`).
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/change-order-intent/test.ts` ("REQ-769 M10 parseNamedQuoteChange: …" ×2: the verifier's sentences and variants; and the cases left to the model) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/named-quote-change.int.test.ts` ("REQ-769 M10: …" ×2: from Tom's Q-002 thread, with the stub model scripted to give the verifier's exact "Please provide the quote number…" reply, both of the verifier's messages land on Dana's sent Q-001 as Version 2 lines "Post caps" $300 + "Shower niche" $250, and Tom's quote is untouched. The same message also adds the line to her unlinked chat draft. Uses real HandleChatMessage → ApplyChatChangeOrder → QuoteStore/CustomerStore on in-memory KV) · e2e n/a — the failing turn was the live model choosing not to call a tool. The fix takes the model out of the path, and the integration test pins the whole coordinator path with the model's bad answer scripted. The chat UI only renders the reply text.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5v4-m10 off demo-fixes a2492852):**
- RED: `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/named-quote-change.int.test.ts src/agents/domain/business/change-order-intent/test.ts` gave "FAILED | 0 passed | 3 failed". Both int tests failed with "AssertionError: Please provide the quote number for Dana Whitfield's quote so I can add the post caps for $300.", the verifier's reply word for word. The unit file failed with "does not provide an export named 'parseNamedQuoteChange'".
- GREEN: the unit file gave "ok | 39 passed | 0 failed", and the int file gave "ok | 2 passed | 0 failed".
- Neighbours: `deno test -A --unstable-kv --parallel` over handle-chat-message/, revise-quote/, apply-chat-change-order/, update-chat-change-order/ and business/ gave "ok | 771 passed | 0 failed".
- `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint` and `deno check` are clean on the touched files.

## REQ-772 — "Job done, invoice her" in the thread of a never-signed draft (no saved customer) names the customer and Continue reaches the invoice's customer step in its own thread (demo-loop cycle 5v5, M9 re-test; amends REQ-768)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle 5v5 (run r37f88707), issue M9 "Assistant will not invoice a finished job (makes a quote / refuses / schedules)". The verifier re-tested REQ-768 on merged demo-fixes and found it NOT_FIXED: "Draft Q-001 (Maria Lopez $800) never signed; typed 'Job done for Maria, need to invoice her' and 'Trabajo terminado, necesito facturar.' both reply 'started an invoice for The customer / para El cliente, $800' (customer name lost) and open the price step ($800, 'Fence painting — Maria Lopez'), but clicking Continue closes the panel and leaves the plain composer: no customer/review step, no invoice created (2 of 2 never-signed tries). A fresh chat without a quote did reach 'Who is this for? Maria Lopez'."
**Cause (git show 8fc01299 = REQ-768, at 64a5acb7):** two gaps REQ-768's tests never reached. (1) Q-001 was drafted by the chat for a customer not yet saved, so it has no `customerId` / `customerSnapshot`; the model names her only in the summary's "— Maria Lopez" tail (REQ-576). `billingReply`'s `jobDoneInvoiceOffer` read the snapshot / acceptedName only, so the offer had no `customerName` and the text fell back to `chatCoordinator.billing.customerFallback` ("The customer" / "El cliente"). REQ-768's fixtures all had a saved customer. (2) The verifier typed in Q-001's OWN thread (bound: `quoteId` + `convoId` set). `AsstChat.startQuoteFromRaw` read `quoteId && convoId` as "Back to the price step of a quote that already exists" and took the edit branch: it rewrote Q-001, never called `transition-to-terms?docKind=invoice`, and closed the panel. REQ-768's e2e test ran in a new, unbound chat and stopped at the price pad, so it never pressed Continue.
**Requirement:** (a) a job-done offer on an unsigned quote names the customer from the snapshot, else the signer, else the summary's "— <Name>" tail (`customerNameFromSummary`); when nobody is named, the reply uses a nameless line ("…I've started an invoice for $800: pick who it's for…" / "…empecé la factura por $800: elige a quién va…"), never "The customer" / "El cliente". (b) The price step's Continue edits a bound quote only when it is the flow's OWN quote. When the invoice flow started in a thread bound to another quote (`flowStartedOnQuoteRef`), Continue makes the invoice's own quote and thread and runs the invoice wizard ("Who is this for?", prefilled with the offer's name). The bound quote is not touched (`invoiceFlowContinueTarget` in `shared/quote-flow/chat-invoice-flow-offer.ts`: edit / newThread / bindDraft / newConversation). en + es in sync.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-answers/test.ts` ("REQ-772 M9 billingReply: …" ×2: the "— Maria Lopez" draft names her in en + es with offer.customerName; a nameless draft never says "The customer" / "El cliente") · unit `jest/unit/chat-invoice-flow-offer.test.ts` ("REQ-772 M9 invoiceFlowContinueTarget" ×4: bound-at-start → newThread; the flow's own quote → edit; draft thread → bindDraft; none → newConversation; AsstChat wires it) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/billing-actions.int.test.ts` ("REQ-772 M9: …" ×2: the verifier's two exact sentences in the thread of a customer-less draft "Fence painting — Maria Lopez" $800 → the offer for Maria Lopez, $800, no model, no invoice) · e2e `e2e/chat-invoice-intent/chat-invoice-intent.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-772 M9: in draft Q-001's thread …": typed on /assistant/<Q-001 thread>, the reply names Maria Lopez, the pad opens at 800, Continue lands on "Who is this for?" in a new thread whose docKind is invoice, Q-001's summary and total untouched).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, branch fix/c5v5-m9 off demo-fixes 64a5acb7):**

## REQ-770 — A customer whose phone can't take texts is never offered or attempted a text on a change order or a chat invoice send; the reply says "not texted: <reason>" (demo-loop cycle 5v5, issue m12 re-test; follows REQ-569 / REQ-681 / REQ-764)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle 5v5 (run r37f88707), issue m12 "'This number can't receive texts' gives no reason while assistant still tries to text". The verifier, on merged demo-fixes, found the quote send fixed (REQ-764) but the change-order path wrong on 2 of 3 tries with Maria's (512) 555-0188: the CO-001 offer said "tap Send CO-001 to email and text it", and one send reply read "The text didn't go: that's a reserved test number…" instead of "not texted: <reason>".

Two places were left: (1) `ApplyChatChangeOrder`'s not-sent offer (`chatCoordinator.changeOrder.createdNotSent`, REQ-652) always says "email and text it"; (2) `ChatBilling.send` (the chat's "send it to her" / `send_invoice` path) still dispatched the text, and the guarded refusal became `chatCoordinator.sendInvoice.partial` → "The text didn't go: …". ## REQ-212 — Settings: connect the business's own Stripe; card payments land in THEIR account, never ours
(built 2026-11-06, recovered from an uncommitted checkout 2026-11-12)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-06 ("in settings we want stripe integration; meaning that the customer can put in their stripe details like api key and shit and it takes credit cards for the customer without the money ever touching our bank. use our credit card widget but set up their merchant and logo.").
**Requirement:** Settings gets a "Card payments (Stripe)" card. The business pastes its Stripe publishable key and secret key; the backend checks the pair against Stripe (`GET /v1/account` with the secret; the two keys must be the same mode, test or live), stores the secret encrypted at rest (AES-GCM under `SECRETS_KEY`; off the real deploy a fixed dev key, on it the key is required), and shows the connection back: the Stripe account's name, the mode, the publishable key and the last 4 of the secret — never the secret itself. The card previews the merchant the customer will see on the card page: the business name and its logo (the identity card's logo), and says in one line that payments go straight to the business's Stripe account and DocuMonster never holds the money. Disconnect removes the keys. Every charge this app makes for the business runs against the business's own secret key, so the funds settle in the business's Stripe balance; no Stripe Connect, no platform account, no fee. Off the real deploy a key of the form `sk_test_fake…` / `pk_test_fake…` talks to an in-process fake Stripe (the gate's lanes, like the fake link builder); on the real deploy such a key is refused.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/stripe-settings.test.ts` (the pure key rules of `shared/payments/stripe-keys.ts`: kinds, modes, mismatches, masking; the settings card's wiring), `backend/src/core/business/secret-box/test.ts` (seal/open round trip, a wrong key fails, the dev key only off the real deploy), `backend/src/core/data/stripe-gateway/test.ts` (the fake: account, a bad key is 401, fake keys refused on the real deploy) · integration `backend/src/users/entrypoints/stripe-settings-controller/e2e.test.ts` (PUT connects and answers the status with no secret in it; a mode mismatch is 422; a key Stripe rejects is 422; GET reads it back; DELETE forgets it) · e2e `e2e/stripe-card/stripe-card.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-212: …" — the settings card connects with the fake test keys, shows the account, the mode, the masked secret, the merchant name and logo line; disconnects).

## REQ-213 — The public invoice takes the card on the flip-card widget, branded with the business, charged on the business's Stripe
(built 2026-11-06, recovered from an uncommitted checkout 2026-11-12)
**Source:** same message as REQ-212 ("it takes credit cards for the customer … use our credit card widget but set up their merchant and logo").
**Requirement:** When the invoice's business has Stripe connected (REQ-212) and the invoice has a balance, the public invoice page (/i/:id) offers "Pay by card" above the manual "I sent it" methods: the CRM's flip pay card (ppwk-crm REQ-010/013, ported: the card draws the number, holder and expiry as they are typed, detects the brand, flips to its back while the CVV has focus) under a merchant header that carries the business's logo and name, and one button naming the amount. The card details go from the browser straight to Stripe with the business's publishable key (a PaymentMethod; the number never reaches this app's server); the server then creates and confirms a PaymentIntent on the business's secret key for the invoice's current balance (a stale balance or version is refused with the current one, like the claim). A succeeded charge records the payment the same way the contractor's "I got it" does (a Payment row, method card, the Stripe PaymentIntent id as its reference; the balance, the PAID stamp, the receipt email and text), and the page says so without a reload; a declined card says so and keeps the form; a card that needs 3-D Secure is handed to Stripe.js for the challenge and then completed server-side (the intent is re-read on the business's key, never trusted from the browser). With fake keys (REQ-212) the whole flow runs on the in-process fake: 4242… succeeds, 4000 0000 0000 0002 declines. The manual "card" instructions chip is dropped from the methods list while Stripe is connected.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/card-entry.test.ts` (the pure `shared/payments/card-entry.ts`: brand detection, Luhn, number/expiry formatting, the draft's validity, the server's decision mapping), `jest/unit/stripe-card-pay.test.ts` (the island and the route are wired: the widget, the merchant header, the apiBase, the SSR config) · integration `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/card-pay.e2e.test.ts` — the app booted on the fakes (GET config off/on and the manual card chip dropped; POST charges on the fake and pays the invoice through RecordCardPayment: one Payment row, method card, the intent as reference, the same intent again records nothing, a paid invoice refuses a second charge before Stripe is asked; declined is 402 with Stripe's words; a stale balance is 409 with the current one; no Stripe is 404; 3-D Secure: requires_action, an early /complete is not a payment, the settled intent pays, another invoice's intent is refused) · e2e `e2e/stripe-card/stripe-card.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-213: …" — the customer types 4242… on the flip card, the card flips on CVV, pays, the page reads PAID and the office's invoice is paid; the declined card keeps the form with the message).

**Evidence (2026-11-06, local, REQ-212 + REQ-213):** RED first — `jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'stripe-settings|card-entry|stripe-card-pay'` → "Test Suites: 3 failed" (the shared modules did not exist); `deno test` on the four backend files → "Type checking failed" (the modules did not exist). GREEN — `cd jest && jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 103 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 925 passed, 926 total" (the REQ-055 stylesheet-key check caught the second `<link>` on /i, fixed with `key="css-paycard"`); `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/users/entrypoints src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller src/core/data/stripe-gateway src/core/business/secret-box` → "ok | 128 passed | 0 failed"; `shots run e2e/stripe-card e2e/invoice-polish e2e/linked-documents` → "9 pass · 0 fail" (the REQ-212/213 story 3.7 s: connect with the fake pair, the status survives a reload, 4242 pays on the flip card — the card flips while the CVC has focus, the badge reads paid without a reload, the office's invoice is paid with a card payment whose reference is `pi_fake_…`; 4000 0000 0000 0002 keeps the form with "Your card was declined."; disconnect brings the manual card chip back). `deno check` + `deno lint` + `deno fmt --check` clean on every touched file. Screenshots (scratchpad `shot-stripe-settings-on.png`, `shot-card-phone-front.png`, `shot-card-desktop-back.png`, `shot-card-phone-paid.png`): the settings card connected ("✓ Connected · Acme (fake Stripe account) · TEST MODE · pk_test_fake_acme · sk_test_••••acme", the merchant preview with the uploaded logo); the pay card on a phone with the business's logo printed into the card as a foil mark and "Pay $1,485.00"; the back with the CVV band; the paid state. Known design limits, stated: no Stripe Connect (each business's own keys; nothing is reconciled on our side), no webhook (a charge is recorded at the charge reply or the 3-D Secure completion; a browser that closes between the two leaves a succeeded intent in the business's Stripe and an open invoice — the office confirms it by hand), the card form is ours (the business's PCI scope is SAQ A-EP, not SAQ A; Stripe Elements would be the SAQ A path), USD only. The CRM's card art was NOT shipped (it carries that brand's watermark): the card is a brand gradient with the business's own logo.

## REQ-216 — The public invoice's card is the CRM's pay-card widget, whole — every animation it has — with the gateway behind it a *provider*, "stripe" first

(built 2026-11-06, recovered from an uncommitted checkout 2026-11-12)

**Source (2026-11-06):** "this component does not have all the nice animations ours has. why dont you just reuse the one we have and just add a provider 'stripe'." (on the REQ-213 card: it flipped, and nothing else)

**Requirement:** The card on `/i/:id` is a faithful port of the CRM's pay-card (ppwk-crm `ui/src/pages/charge/components/pay-card` + the charge island's card motion), not a lookalike: the number, holder and expiry print on the card **one character per cell**, and each cell that changes slides in (`pc-anim-slide-fade-up` on number/expiry cells, `pc-anim-holder-fade-up` on holder cells, dropped on `animationend` so the next change re-fires); a **focus ring** on the card glides (transform only, from the card-sized host box; the very first placement does not travel) onto the number, the name or the expiry zone as the matching field takes focus, and goes out on blur; the number is **masked** (`4242 **** **** 4242`) whenever the number field does not have focus; the **brand mark** (Visa/Mastercard/Amex/Discover) fades up when the brand is known and sits on the back too; the CVV band shows one `*` per digit typed; the card **flips** while the CVC has focus; the business's logo is **printed into the art** as the issuer mark, placed by data (anchor / size / opacity, the CRM's REQ-033 rules and fallbacks); the art is the CRM's clean malachite (the watermarked sets are not shipped). The form around it is the CRM's too: tab-label inputs whose label becomes the error message while the field is wrong, the one full-width submit with a spinner while busy and a lock when ready, the "Secure checkout" line. The gateway is a **provider** the island is configured with (`provider: "stripe"` from the server; the island's tokenize / next-action steps are looked up by provider), so a second gateway is a second entry, not a second widget. Everything REQ-213 says about where the money goes is unchanged.

**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/pay-card.test.ts` (the pure `shared/payments/pay-card.ts`: the number cells with and without the mask, Amex's 4-6-5, the holder cells, the expiry halves, which cells changed, the mark's anchor/size/opacity fallbacks, the focus ring's transform, the field→zone map), `jest/unit/stripe-card-pay.test.ts` ("REQ-216 …": the island carries the per-cell card, the ring, the mask, the fade, the animation classes, the provider table; the CSS carries the keyframes and the tab-label field; the art ships; the server names the provider) · integration n/a — the widget is browser motion; the charge path is REQ-213's `card-pay.e2e.test.ts` · e2e `e2e/stripe-card/stripe-card.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-213 … / REQ-216": the ring is on while the number has focus; the number prints one digit per cell and masks to `4242 **** **** 4242` when focus leaves; the holder prints in cells, uppercase; the Visa mark appears; the malachite art is the card's face).

**Evidence (2026-11-06, local, REQ-216):** RED first — `jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'pay-card|stripe-card-pay'` → "Test Suites: 2 failed · Tests: 4 failed, 9 passed" (`shared/payments/pay-card.ts` did not exist; the island had no cells, ring, mask, provider table; the sheet had no keyframes). GREEN — `cd jest && jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 104 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 939 passed, 940 total" (two REQ-213 regexes retargeted: the flip is now `focused === "cvc"` and the publishable key is read off the provider's config); `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller` → "ok | 27 passed | 0 failed"; `shots run e2e/stripe-card e2e/invoice-polish e2e/linked-documents` → "9 pass · 0 fail" (the story 3.3 s: the malachite face, 19 cells, the ring on while the number has focus, the Visa mark, the mask `4242 **** **** 4242` once focus leaves, 10 holder cells and "ANA TORRES", then REQ-213's pay / decline / disconnect unchanged). Two things the lanes caught: the container-query blocks were ABOVE the base rules, so on a phone-wide card the later base rules won and the number row overflowed (reordered, plus the back face in container units); the production build appends `?__frsh_c=<build>` to static `src` attributes, so the story's `src` match missed the Visa mark that was on screen (`src*=`). `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint`, `deno check` clean on every touched file. Screenshots (scratchpad `shot2-desktop-number-focused.png`, `shot3-phone-front.png`, `shot3-phone-back.png`): a seeded "Red Roof Pros" with a Flaticon roof icon as its logo — the ring on the number, the Visa mark, the logo printed into the malachite as the issuer mark; the phone card with the masked number, the uppercase holder in cells, the ring on the expiry; the back with three `*` on the CVV band. Not carried from the CRM, on purpose: the two-field holder (an NMI rule), the month/year dropdowns and the billing-address step (Stripe takes MM/YY and no address), the existing-card tab (no card on file for a one-off invoice), the watermarked art sets.

(b) Settings → "Other payment links": the business adds any number (up to 10) of payment links by NAME + URL (e.g. "Extra Pay", Square, a bank portal); each is a branded button on the invoice. URLs are https only — `http://`, `javascript:`, `data:`, credentials-in-URL and host-less links are refused on save (400 `pay_link_url_not_https` / `pay_link_url_invalid`, nothing stored) and filtered again when projected. Tell us how"), where a payment link can be claimed too (as `other`, its name as the reference). With the card connected and no other method, no "reach out" fallback shows. (e) The invoice email carries a "Ways to pay" block — "Pay by card" to the invoice page when Stripe is connected, then the app links with the amount, the custom links, Zelle to copy (none on the "paid" email); the invoice text adds one line naming the online ways ("Pay online by card, Venmo, Cash App, Zelle or Extra Pay — all at the link."). The pure rules live in `shared/payments/pay-links.ts` (`projectPayMethods`, `payButtons`, `payWayNames`, `checkPayLinks`, `safeHttpsUrl`, the three deep-link builders) for any other surface (e.g. the invoice PDF's "How to pay").

## REQ-625 — A full customer form everywhere a customer is created, and an Edit for an existing one
**Source:** A2Z Landscape feedback relayed by Raphael, 2026-11-12 ("They tried to do a new customer and it only allows them to add the name and phone").
**Cause, from the code at `53f3cfc`:** the backend customer already took `address` and `notes`, but no form asked for them — the Clients page's Add client had name, business, phone, email; the new invoice's "New client" name, phone, email; the assistant's customer step name, business, phone, email. No form could edit a customer at all, though `PUT /customers/:id` existed. The as-you-type phone mask cut every number to ten US digits.
**Requirement:** ONE customer form (`front-end/components/CustomerForm.tsx`, rules in `shared/customer-form`) — name, company / business name, phone, email, street, city, state, zip (the shape of A2Z's QuickBooks export), notes — used by every new-customer entry point: the Clients page (a dialog), the new invoice's "New client" (the fields inline; blank bill-to fields and the service address fall back to what was typed), and the assistant's customer step (the same fields in the assistant's own look). The same dialog, prefilled, edits a customer from the client sheet (REQ-626) and saves through `PUT /customers/:id`; the sheet and the board show the change at once. The address is stored in parts (`street`, `city`, `state`, `zip`) AND as the one composed `address` string ("4410 Ranch Rd, Austin, TX 78735") every existing reader uses (invoice bill-to and service address, quotes, field tasks/subscriptions, the CSV export, search): the store recomposes it on every write that carries a part; a write carrying only a free-text `address` (older writers) keeps working and drops the parts; a customer saved before the parts existed prefills the edit form by splitting its address (unreadable text stays whole in Street). Validation is lenient: the name is required; any phone format with at least 7 digits (spaces, dots, dashes, parens, +country, ext) is accepted and kept as typed — the mask formats a plain US number only; email must look like `a@b.c`. Both languages; on a 390px phone the paired rows stack, nothing clips or overlaps.
**Also fixed on the way:** the assistant's "send the accepted quote" step read the customer from `clientsClient.list()` as if it were an array (it is the REQ-135 page envelope), threw, and never found the customer's email/phone — it now reads `GET /customers/:id`.

## REQ-626 — Every "Open" and card button does something
**Source:** A2Z Landscape feedback relayed by Raphael, 2026-11-12 ("How will they edit things because the open card does not work").
**Cause, from the code at `53f3cfc`:** the client card's "Open card" and "Message" buttons and its CTA had no `onClick`; its sort button ("Warmth") had none either (the API orders by name); the quote card's front CTA and "Resend" only called `stopPropagation()`; the invoice card's "Open" opened the customer's page `/i/:id` in a new tab instead of the editable panel; the payment card's front CTA, "Receipt", "Match invoice" and "Text client" only called `stopPropagation()`; the field task's "Invoiced" chip went to the whole invoice list.
**Requirement:** client card — "Open card" opens the client's sheet (`front-end/components/ClientSheet.tsx`, also `/customers?open=<id>`, read by id so any page links to it): name, company, number, phone, email, service address (a map link), notes, with Edit (REQ-625, the one solid primary) and Message; "Message" is a text to the client's phone (`sms:`), an email when there is no phone, and with neither it opens the edit form to add one (there is no in-app customer messaging thread: `/messages` is the assistant, and REQ-175's customer threads have no screen — the native compose is the working path); the CTA does what its label says — "Send a kind reminder" / "Send progress update" / "Follow up" / "Send a hello" open that message pre-filled, "Open card" opens the sheet; the panel's address row opens the map (or the edit form when there is none); the sort button switches Name A–Z ↔ Warmth. Quote card — the front CTA: a draft's "Finish + send" resumes the draft in the newest assistant conversation holding it (the quote's panel when none is left); "Friendly nudge" (opened, cooling) and "Win it back" (stale) send the quote again; everything else reads "Open quote" and opens the quote's panel; "Resend" on the back sends it again by email and text and says on the card what happened; a new "Open quote" on the back opens the panel. Invoice card — "Open" opens the EDITABLE detail panel in-app (`?open=`, no new tab); "View as customer" is its own link to `/i/:id` on the card's back and in the panel. Payment card — the front CTA: "View receipt" opens the invoice, "View timeline" flips to the trail, "Text client" opens the client's sheet; "Receipt" is the customer's copy `/i/:id`, "Match invoice" opens the invoice's panel, "Text client" the client's sheet. Field tasks — "Invoiced" opens that invoice. Work orders and the other field pages were audited: no dead controls.
**Decision, mine (not asked for):** "Send the offer" (an opened quote, 3+ views), "Trim & re-send" (cooling) and "Set a reminder" (sent) promised things the app cannot do in one click (there is no offer, trim or quote reminder flow), so those cards now read "Friendly nudge" (a resend) or "Open quote" — a label that says what the click does.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/card-actions.test.ts` ("REQ-626 …": the Message href — phone first, `+1` for US numbers, international kept, the email fallback, the pre-filled body, none without a contact; the client CTA's action per label; the quote CTA's label + action per stage; the newest conversation holding a draft; the wiring — no button whose only handler is `stopPropagation` in QuoteCard and PaymentsPage, Open card / Message / CTA / sort handlers on the client card, the sheet's Edit + Message, the invoice card's in-app Open and its separate `/i/` link, the payment card's four targets, the field task's invoice link; every new key in both languages) · integration n/a — no new endpoint: Open/Edit read and write through `GET`/`PUT /customers/:id` (REQ-625's integration test), Resend through the existing `POST /quotes/:id/email|text` · e2e `e2e/open-cards/open-cards.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-626: client card → Open card …": the panel's Message is `sms:+15125550142`, the sheet with the address, the link `?open=`, Edit opens the form, the deep link reopens it; "quote card …": the front CTA opens the quote's panel, Resend answers visibly on the back, the back's Open quote; "invoice card …": Open opens `invoice-detail` in the same tab with a live Edit, View as customer is `/i/<id>`; "payment card …": Match invoice / Text client / Receipt hrefs, Match invoice opens the invoice's panel).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, local, REQ-626):** RED first — `jest --testPathPattern card-actions` → "Cannot find module '../../shared/card-actions/mod'"; the stories on a detached worktree of `53f3cfc` → all four fail (the Message / View as customer / Match invoice `getAttribute` timed out — the attributes do not exist; the quote CTA "the click never took"). ## REQ-627 — Removing an invoice, with a clear process (Delete / Void / Void & duplicate / locked), bulk Delete/Void, and the assistant's invoice no longer auto-sends
**Source:** A2Z Landscape feedback relayed by Raphael, 2026-11-12 ("They cannot delay the invoice and if you make a mistake... they want to be able to remove invoices (BUT WHAT IS THE PROCESS?)").
**Requirement:** One process, enforced by the server (`shared/documents/removal.ts` → `removalFor`) and shown by the app as the one button it allows. Never sent (draft / scheduled / no status, no `sentAt`) and no payments → **Delete** (gone; inline confirm). Sent (the customer may have seen it) or any payment on it → **Void**: `POST /invoices/:id/void { reason? }` sets `status: "void"`, `voidedAt`, `voidedBy {userId, name}`, `voidReason`; it stays in the list in a new **Cancelled** track with who/when/why; the customer's `/i/:id` says "<business> cancelled this invoice on <date>. Nothing is due on it — please don't pay it.", shows $0.00, and offers no pay UI (the claim endpoint already answers 409 `void`); payments stay attached and visible, and a note says refunds/credits are settled outside the app. **Paid** → locked: neither (the panel explains "a paid invoice is part of your records…"). **Void & duplicate** (`POST /invoices/:id/void-duplicate`) voids it and creates a fresh DRAFT copy of its content with a NEW number (`replaces` / `replacedBy` link them) and opens it. Refusals: DELETE on a sent / paid-into invoice 409 `must_void`; void on a never-sent draft 409 `must_delete`; paid 409 `locked_paid`; void twice / delete a void 409 `already_void`; `PUT status:"void"` 409 `use_void`; the void bookkeeping fields are never accepted from a PUT/POST body. Field batches (REQ-142): a voided invoice frees its tasks for the next pull; a void-&-duplicated one keeps them on the live copy (never billed twice). **Bulk:** the invoices list gets "Select" → a checkbox per card and a sticky bar (n selected · Select all in view · Clear · **Print / Download PDF** (solid primary, REQ-629) · Delete · Void (outlined) · Cancel (ghost)); Delete/Void preview what they will do and which are skipped and why, then `POST /invoices/bulk-remove { action, ids, reason? }` (≤ 500 ids, 400 `too_many`) applies the per-invoice rules and reports `{results, done, skipped}`; another owner's id is skipped as `not_found`, never touched. **Delay:** the assistant's invoice flows end at a review step — the invoice is created as a DRAFT and the card offers **Send now** (one tap, solid), **Save as draft**, **Schedule** (date → `status: "scheduled"` + `scheduledFor`, as InvoicesPage's "Send on").
**Decision, mine (not asked for):** the customer's link shows only the cancellation date — never who voided it or the internal reason.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/invoice-removal/test.ts` (the rules, the duplicate's fields, the 500 cap), `jest/unit/invoice-removal-print.test.ts` (bulkPlan / summarizeBulk; the page wiring — void, void & duplicate, Cancelled track, multi-select bar; the `/i` cancelled note; every key in both languages), `jest/unit/invoice-review-step.test.ts` (the review step: draft body, send-now / draft / schedule, keys) · integration `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/invoice-controller/removal.int.test.ts` (booted app: delete/void/locked rules and codes, who/when/why, the public projection says void and the claim is 409, a paid-into draft is voided with its payment kept, void & duplicate's new number, bulk with skips / foreign ids / >500), `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-627 void frees the batch's tasks…; void & duplicate keeps them on the corrected draft") · e2e `e2e/invoice-removal-print/invoice-removal-print.e2e.test.ts` (void with a reason → Cancelled note with the name and reason → `/i` says cancelled with no pay button; Void & duplicate lands on the new draft; bulk delete reports "sent — void instead (1)"), `e2e/invoice-review-step/invoice-review-step.e2e.test.ts` (the assistant card stops at review; draft until Send now; Schedule picks the day); `e2e/invoice-polish` REQ-167 (draft delete) still green.
**Evidence (2026-11-12, local, REQ-627):** RED first — `deno test` on `invoice-removal/test.ts` → "Type checking failed" (TS2307, `#documents/removal.ts` missing); `removal.int.test.ts` → "FAILED | 0 passed | 6 failed"; the field REQ-627 test failed with the old controller; jest `invoice-removal-print` → "Test Suites: 1 failed" (Cannot find module `front-end/lib/invoice-bulk`), then "Tests: 3 failed, 5 passed" (the page wiring) before the UI; jest `invoice-review-step` → "Test Suites: 1 failed" (module missing). ## REQ-631 — Language is per person: an invited editor's EN/ES is hers; the owner's and what the business sends its customers never move
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-12 — "Language is per person and invite could be required in the UI and the API." (A2Z Landscape: Alexander's daughter edits his account, REQ-146/190/191/624.)
**Requirement:** The signed-in person's language — the actor's own while a session acts for someone else's account, else the account's — drives the UI: every SSR route's language, the dashboard seed that sets the islands' `langSignal` and writes `pm_lang` + `pm:lang`, the sidebar, Settings' language row, `<html lang>`. Toggling EN/ES while acting (topbar or Settings → `PUT /me { language }`) writes HER own User record and never the owner's; `/me` and `/profile` carry it as `actor.language` (her record's, the account's while she has none). The app's own words TO the person follow it too: the sign-in code text when the page names no language (the phone's own saved language), the in-app notification feed, the assistant's server-authored replies and the stored phase divider, the insight cards. What the business sends ITS customers is unchanged and stays on the business: quote/invoice email + SMS, public pages, PDFs read the business identity's `commsLanguage` (+ the visitor's own `pm_lang`); the few customer-facing reads of the owner's own record (receipt PDF, change-order alert data, `send-paperwork-sms`'s error reason) keep reading HIS record — which only his own toggle changes.
**Decisions, mine:** (1) This supersedes REQ-624's decision (2) ("`language` on `PUT /me` while acting still writes the account"). (2) The owner's own toggle still writes the account record, because that record IS his person — so for the owner nothing changes; his UI language is also what the receipt PDF and the owner-addressed alerts use, as before (the business's customer language is `commsLanguage`, set in Settings' "send in" languages, and no person's toggle touches it). (3) An editor with no saved language falls back to the account's. (4) Left on the account on purpose: job-details/price generation, new-quote job names, the sample quote and the field batch pull — those write BUSINESS content (quotes/invoices) and stay in the business's working language.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/account-admins/test.ts` ("REQ-631 actorPatch …" — name, email AND language go to her, nothing to the account; "REQ-631 personLanguage …"), `jest/unit/person-lang.test.ts` (`shared/person-name` personLanguage; 22 SSR routes read through it and no island/component/lib/route reads `user.language`; dash-cache seeds `setLang` with it; sidebar + Settings; the /me + /profile types; the backend's `uiLangOf` is read by the notification feed, both insight controllers, the conversation divider and the chat controller → `HandleChatMessage.uiLang`; customer sends never read it) · integration `backend/src/users/entrypoints/me-controller/person-lang.int.test.ts` (four, the app booted on an in-memory KV: the editor's PUT writes her record "es", `actor.language` on /me + /profile, the owner's record + /me stay "en", the identity's `commsLanguage` stays "en"; the owner's own toggle still writes his record and leaves hers; the sign-in code is texted in her saved Spanish and his English; the notification feed renders the same row in Spanish for her, English for him) · e2e `e2e/person-lang/person-lang.e2e.test.ts` (the owner in English with an invoice; his editor flips the topbar to ES — "Hola, Daughter", her record "es", the owner's "en"; her `/dashboard` SSR is Spanish with no `pm_lang` sent and `<html lang="es">`; the owner then signs in on the same browser — English SSR and "Hey, Alexander", `<html lang="en">`; the customer's `/i/<id>` page language + title and the business's `commsLanguage` unchanged).
**Evidence (2026-11-12, local):** see the REQ-632 entry below (one run for both).

## REQ-192 — Timeclock: workers clock in and out from their own screen; the office reads the timesheet, fixes punches
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-05/06 ("were is the mallard group timeclock?" → "yes, fold in the time clock here. that way we have a timeclock feature."). The Mallard Group timeclock (`programming/timeclock/employee-timeclock-system`, its REQ-001…010/013/019) folded into this app as a feature of every account. Folded: the one button that flips, the immutable server-timestamped punch log, this week's shifts and totals on the worker's screen, the office timesheet by week, void a punch with a reason, add a manual punch with a reason (must alternate with its neighbours; an out needs an in before it). NOT folded (they belong to the other product or are already here another way): the personal kiosk link and device trust (a worker here signs in with cell + PIN, REQ-138), the Google Form / Sheet outbox, and jobs / runs / checklists / locations / schedules (this app's Recurring folder covers that ground).
**Requirement:** (a) A signed-in worker's /worker screen shows a clock card: one big button reading Clock in or Clock out by their current state, since when, today's and this week's totals, and this week's shifts (Mon–Sun, each with its day, in, out and hours; an open shift ticks). Pressing it records a punch at the server's time; a second press that would not flip the state (two taps at once) is refused, never doubled. (b) Every punch is an immutable record owned by the account (userId) and the worker; a void is a correction appended to it, never a delete; both carry a reason when the office makes them. (c) The office page /field/timesheet (Roles folder, "Timesheet", between Workers and Editors) shows a week at a time — each worker with their shifts, total and anomalies (an in without an out, an out without an in) — with the punch log for that week (voided ones struck through), Void with a reason, and Add punch (worker, in/out, time, reason). (d) The API: worker side `GET /timeclock/worker/status`, `POST /timeclock/worker/punch` behind pm_worker; office side `GET /timeclock/report`, `GET /timeclock/punches`, `POST /timeclock/punches`, `POST /timeclock/punches/:id/void` behind the owner's session; every record is the calling account's. Weeks are the account's field time zone (FIELD_TZ, America/New_York by default) on the server; the worker's screen sends its own local week bounds.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/timeclock/domain/business/shifts/test.ts` (the pure rules, ported), `jest/unit/timeclock-feature.test.ts` (nav entry, both dictionaries, route → island, client), `jest/unit/sidebar-root-folders.test.ts` (Roles folder order) · integration `backend/src/timeclock/entrypoints/timeclock.int.test.ts` (flip, refusals, manual, void, report, account isolation) · e2e `e2e/timeclock/timeclock.e2e.test.ts` (worker clocks in and out on /worker; the office sees the shift on /field/timesheet, adds a manual punch, voids one), `e2e/sidebar-folders/root-folders.e2e.test.ts` (the Roles folder reads Workers | Timesheet | Editors).

## REQ-192 — AMENDMENT (2026-11-06): a whole forgotten shift is added in one go
**Source:** building the browser story: with single manual punches the office could never add yesterday's in + out before today's punches — the alternation rule refuses an "in" whose next punch is an "in", and an "out" with no "in" before it, so a pair can never be opened in front of an existing one.
**Requirement:** `POST /timeclock/shifts {workerId, start, end, reason}` writes the in and the out together; the pair must sit in a gap (no punch inside it, an "out" or nothing before, an "in" or nothing after), must not end in the future, and carries the reason on both. The timesheet's Add form offers Shift (in + out) first, then a single In or Out.
**Tests:** integration `timeclock.int.test.ts` (third test) · unit `jest/unit/timeclock-feature.test.ts` (strings, client) · e2e `e2e/timeclock/timeclock.e2e.test.ts` (the office adds yesterday 8–12 as one shift, then voids its out).

## REQ-195 — Page transitions and motion all over the app
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-06 ("i want page transitions and animations all over the fucking app").
**Research applied:** cross-document View Transitions (Chrome docs: `@view-transition { navigation: auto }`, Chrome 126+ / Safari 18.2+, Firefox falls back to a plain navigation; the `pagereveal` tagger must be a classic parser-blocking script in `<head>`); motion guidance distilled from Emil Kowalski's and Material 3's published rules — ease-out by default, UI animation under ~300 ms, exits faster than entrances, animate only transform and opacity, press feedback at scale .97, reduced motion keeps a gentle fade rather than removing everything.
**Requirement:** `static/motion.css` is linked on every page by `_app.tsx`: duration/easing tokens (120/200/320 ms; ease-out, emphasized, iOS sheet curve); every same-origin navigation cross-fades and slides the page up (forward), down (back — a history traversal backwards) or just fades (same path: reload / query change), the dashboard rail (`.sb`) is a named element that stays put; `[data-stagger] > *` and `main.main > *` rise in staggered 40 ms apart; a `[data-pane]` replays its entrance when shown; buttons/links/inputs get transitions and a .97 press; `prefers-reduced-motion` keeps fades and drops movement. A classic head script tags each transition's direction.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/motion-system.test.ts` · integration n/a · e2e `e2e/motion/motion.e2e.test.ts` (tokens resolve, opt-in + press + rail rules loaded, tagger ran, first child rises, reduced motion → fade).

## REQ-784 — A sent-messages outbox: every email and text that went to a customer is listed — when, customer, channel, language, subject or first line, sent / not sent and why — and opening one shows it as sent (demo-loop cycle dv1, issue d12; cycle 1 m33)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Product decision, Raphael: "And yes to a sent message outbox." Demo-loop cycle dv1, issue d12 "A sent-messages outbox shows every email and text that went to customers". Cycle 1 m33: "/messages redirects to /assistant; no way to check what was sent or in which language." The merged RCA for d12 was empty (`[{}]`), so the cause below was established in this worktree (demo-fixes 0b909555).
**Why there was none:** `front-end/routes/messages/index.tsx` only 302s to `/assistant?from=messages` (P6.14). The backend keeps a comms trail, but only of DELIVERED quote / invoice dispatches, in the customer's conversation thread (`LogPaperworkMessage.run`, called on `result.ok` in `send-paperwork-email/mod.ts` and `send-paperwork-sms/mod.ts`), with no language. A failed or skipped send leaves nothing: `SendQuote` / `ChatBilling` skip a 555 text before dispatch (REQ-764 / REQ-770), and the trail must hold real deliveries only because `GET /messages` is the receipts strip's source (REQ-403, `failed-sms-truth.int.test.ts`). The change-order request (`SendChangeOrderAlert`), the overdue reminders (`SendPaymentReminder`) and the signed-copy email (`SendSignedConfirmation`) are not recorded at all.
**Requirement:** Every email and text that goes, or was meant to go, to a customer is recorded in the business's outbox. That covers the quote, invoice (and paid invoice), change order, payment receipt, signed copy, overdue reminder and inquiry reply. Each entry records the time, the customer (named as at send time), the channel (email / text), the language it went out in, the document it carried (Quote Q-001, Invoice INV-001, Change order CO-001…), the subject (email) or first line (text), and the status: sent, or not sent with the reason (no email / phone on file, a 555 test number that can't receive texts, an invalid number, the provider refused). It also keeps the full content as sent: the email's HTML, or the text's words. The owner's own heads-ups (accepted / inquiry / change-order alerts to the contractor) are not customer messages and stay out. The page is `/messages`, labelled "Outbox" in the sidebar root (es "Bandeja de salida"). It lists the entries newest first, and opening one shows the email exactly as rendered (sandboxed) or the text's words, with the reason when it did not go. It reads in en and es. The API is `GET /outbox` and `GET /outbox/:id`, scoped to the signed-in account. The conversation trail (`GET /messages`) is unchanged.
