## REQ-785 — a job that runs several days is scheduled as ONE job: it shows on every day it covers for the owner and on the worker's screen, its dates can be edited, and it is done once (demo-loop cycle dv1, issue d11; first seen cycle 3, M42)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none". Demo-loop cycle dv1, issue d11 "A job that runs several days can be scheduled as one job" (cycle 3, M42: the field area only modelled subscriptions, zones and rounds, so a 3-day job took three one-off tasks). Raphael's decision as product owner: "Yes, multi-day jobs." The verifier's check: Field → schedule a 3-day fence install as ONE job; it appears on each of the 3 days (owner and worker view); edit its dates; complete it. The RCA handed over for this id was empty (`[{}]` at 0b909555). The cause below comes from reading the code at 0b909555.
**Cause (at 0b909555):** a field task (`FieldTask`, `backend/src/field/dto/field.ts`) had one `date` and one `workerId`. `FieldTaskStore` keyed it under that one day only (`["field_task_by_day", userId, date, id]`), so `GET /field/tasks?date=` and `GET /field/worker/tasks?date=` could list it on that day and no other. `POST /field/tasks` (REQ-164) took one day and one worker, and `PUT /field/tasks/:id` could not change a task's day. The worker API showed a worker only the tasks with `t.workerId === w.id`, and `inActionWindow` counted back from the task's one day. "Add task" on /field/tasks had one Day field and one Worker select. /worker grouped visits by `subscriptionId`, so every one-off of a day (subscriptionId "") fell into one card.
**Requirement:**
- A one-off task (REQ-164) can be a job of several days. `POST /field/tasks` takes its first day (`date`) and its last day (`endDate`, or a number of `days`), at most 31 days. Blank, null or the first day itself means one day. The job is ONE record. It is keyed under each day it covers (`FieldTaskStore.extraKeys`) and lists once on each of those days, in the office's day and on each worker's screen, and on no other day. A range read answers it once. `putMany` keeps every commit under KV's 1000-mutation cap.
- "Assign workers": the job has its worker (`workerId`) and more workers (`crewIds`). The crew must be the account's own workers and never includes the lead. The crew sees the job on each of its days and may check it off (`onTask` in `canAct`). On a day the job covers, everyone on it gets the REQ-171 "new job today" text, once each.
- The office edits a one-off's days and crew with `PUT /field/tasks/:id`: `date`, `endDate` (null = one day) or `days`, and `crewIds`. The new days and crew are checked before anything on the task changes. A move drops the day keys the job left. The refusals: a subscription's visit belongs to its schedule (400 `not_one_off`); an invoiced task is 409; a last day before the first is 400 `end_before_start`; more than 31 days is 400 `job_too_long`.
- Done once: one check-off (the office's REQ-159 check or the worker's) completes the whole job on all its days. A worker may act on a job from its first day until two days after its LAST day (a foreman fourteen). A job of several days is never deferred: the worker API answers 409 and the office changes its days. It bills once: a pull that reaches any of its days takes it as ONE line ("Nov 16 – Nov 18 — Fence install — <address>", unit "job" / "trabajo"), and the draft's service period runs from the job's first day to its last.
- /field/tasks: "Add task" has First day and Last day, which shows "3 days · Nov 13 – Nov 15", and "More workers" checkboxes. A job's card reads "Day 2 of 3 · Nov 13 – Nov 15" and "With Pedro". "Edit dates" opens First day, Last day and More workers on the card; Save re-reads the day and flashes "Dates saved — <range>". Delete on a job asks "Delete this job — all 3 days?".
- /worker: a job is its own visit (`visitKey`: a one-off's customer + first + last day). It shows "Day 2 of 4 · Nov 13 – Nov 16" and "With Luis", lists for its crew too, and has no Defer. A one-off visit no longer offers the services "add" row, which always failed because there was no subscription to add to. A worker's note stays on its own visit (`sameVisit`) and no longer lands on every one-off of that day.
- Every new string is in en and es. `field.tk.addHint` says a job can run several days.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/job-span/test.ts` ("REQ-785 …" ×6: the days a job covers; `spanFrom` with endDate / days / one day and the refusal codes; `onTask` / `crewList` / `canAct`; `inActionWindow` counted from the last day; `oneOffTask` / `sameVisit` / `officeService` keep the span and the crew; `linesFor` / `lineText` / `batchTitle` bill once and name the range) · unit `jest/unit/field-multi-day-job.test.ts` ("REQ-785 …" ×28: `front-end/lib/field-job.ts` — `jobDayOf`, `jobRange` en/es, `jobSpanProblem`, `onJob`, `workMates`, `crewChoices`, `visitKey`; every new key in en + es with its placeholders; the client types; the wiring of Add task, the card, Edit dates and /worker) · integration `backend/src/field/domain/data/field-stores/job-days.int.test.ts` ("REQ-785 FieldTaskStore …" ×3: one key per day, a re-put drops the days it left, 40 jobs of 31 days in one putMany) · integration `backend/src/field/entrypoints/multi-day-job.int.test.ts` ("REQ-785 …" ×4 over HTTP: the 3-day job lists once on each of its days for the office, the lead and the crew, and not the day before or after, plus `days: 3`; editing the days, the last day alone and back to one day, and the refusals; Pedro (crew) checks it off and it reads complete on all 3 days, defer is 409, one invoice line names its days, billed once; a plain worker completes a job that started 4 days ago and ends today, the lead and the crew are each texted once, a note stays on its job) · e2e `e2e/field-multi-day-job/field-multi-day-job.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-785 (demo dv1-d11) …": the verifier's walk in a real browser — Add task with a last day and Pedro on the crew; "Day 1/2/3 of 3" on each day and nothing on the 4th; Edit dates to 4 days; Pedro on /worker sees "Day 1 of 4" today, "Day 2 of 4" tomorrow and "With Luis", and has no Defer; one check-off; the owner's day 3 reads complete).
**Evidence (2026-11-13, branch fix/cdv1-d11-multi-day-jobs off demo-fixes 0b909555):**
- RED: `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/field/entrypoints/multi-day-job.int.test.ts` gave "FAILED | 0 passed | 4 failed". The POST answered no `endDate` and no crew (`[true, "2026-11-13", undefined, …, undefined, undefined]`); the job listed on day 0 only (`[0]` against `[0, 1, 2]`); Pedro's complete gave `404 {"message":"not found"}`; the job that started 4 days ago gave `409 "outside the days you can edit"`. `field-stores/job-days.int.test.ts` gave "FAILED | 0 passed | 3 failed": the job was keyed under its first day only, a re-put kept 2026-11-16 and never added the 18th and 19th, and the 40 jobs listed 0 on Dec 15. `job-span/test.ts` failed type-checking: the module was missing and `FieldTask` had no `endDate` / `crewIds` (13 errors). Jest: "Cannot find module '../../front-end/lib/field-job'". E2E on the unfixed code (a throwaway detached worktree of origin/demo-fixes with only the story copied in, removed afterwards): "✗ REQ-785 … locator.fill: Timeout 15000ms exceeded … waiting for locator('[data-cy='tk-add-form']').locator('[data-cy='tk-add-end']')", because Add task had no last day.
- GREEN: `deno test -A --unstable-kv` on the three new files plus `tasks/test.ts` and `batch-lines/test.ts` gave "ok | 38 passed | 0 failed". `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/field/` gave "ok | 124 passed | 0 failed (9m28s)". After the PUT's checks moved ahead of its writes, `multi-day-job.int.test.ts` + `field.int.test.ts` gave "ok | 30 passed | 0 failed" and `src/field/domain/business/` + `src/field/domain/data/` gave "ok | 71 passed | 0 failed". The jest file gave "Tests: 28 passed"; `npx jest --selectProjects unit` gave "Test Suites: 498 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 5086 passed". The front-end deno tests (`lib/field-ssr`, `field-add-task`, `field`, `worker-*`) gave 10 + 32 passed. `shots run e2e/field-multi-day-job` gave "✓ REQ-785 (demo dv1-d11) … 248.7s" (1 pass · 0 fail), and on the final code (after the PUT change) "✓ REQ-785 … 60.2s". The neighbouring stories, `shots run e2e/field-tasks e2e/worker-tomorrow -- --filter "/REQ-(164|526|611|362)/"`, gave 4 pass · 0 fail. The e2e runs used `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-test-dummy-not-real` so the backend boots without the real .env (the stories use no LLM), plus `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1` and `SHOTS_SERVE_TIMEOUT=300000` (the host's load average was about 100). `deno lint` is clean on every touched file. `deno check` is clean on the islands, the two routes, the client, the lib, the backend modules and the tests. `deno fmt --check` is clean on every created file and on the touched files that were clean before. `tasks/`, `batch-lines/`, `field-stores/`, `field-views/` and `worker-controller/` were not fmt-clean before and keep their style.

## REQ-782 — Card payment on an invoice is a "Pay by card" link that opens a separate payment portal (demo-loop cycle dv1, issue d10)
**Source:** the user: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none" — demo-loop cycle dv1, issue d10 ("Card payment on an invoice is a link that opens a separate payment portal"), with the product owner's decision quoted by the RCA: Raphael: "Card payments should be a link to a separate portal." (Earlier cycles 3/4: "card means a payment link the contractor supplies".)
**Cause, from the code at `0b909555`:** a business could only take cards two ways — connect its own Stripe (REQ-212/213/216), which drew the card form INLINE on `/i/:id`, or switch on "Credit card" with free-text instructions, which was only a manual "I sent it" chip ("Your contractor will share a secure way to pay by card."). There was nowhere to give a card payment page, and no card way was a link to a separate portal.
**Requirement:** (a) Settings → Payments → Credit card has a **Card payment link** field (`acceptedPaymentMethods.card.url`): the business's own card payment page (a Stripe Payment Link, Square, PayPal checkout). https only — `http://`, `javascript:`, host-less are refused on save (400 `card_url_not_https` / `card_url_invalid`, nothing stored), `""` clears it; the field explains what it does and shows the error inline. A link pasted into the old instructions field (its placeholder said "Payment link, or …") counts too. (b) On `/i/:id`, "Pay $X by card" is the solid primary, first, above the app buttons and "I sent it": a link (`target=_blank`, `rel=noopener noreferrer`) to the business's **separate card portal** — with the business's own Stripe connected, our card page `/i/:id/pay` (the business's name, the invoice number, the amount due and the REQ-216 pay card, charged on their key; it is no longer drawn inline on the invoice); otherwise the card payment link, with a line naming the business, the portal's host, the amount and the invoice number to enter. (c) With neither, the customer sees no card button (never a dead end); the business's own view of the invoice says how to set it up and links to Settings → Payments. (d) The invoice text and email name "card" as an online way (the email's "Pay by card" row to the invoice page) when a card link is set, as they already did for Stripe. English and Spanish throughout. The shared rules live in `shared/payments/pay-links.ts` (`checkCardPayUrl`, `hasCardPayLink`, `cardPayWay`).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/card-pay-link.test.ts` ("REQ-782 …": the https rule, the projection's card row, `cardPayWay` portal / link / none, the text names; the wiring — `/i` mounts `PayByCard` and not the inline widget, the button's new tab + `rel`, the owner's setup hint, the `/i/:id/pay` portal page, the Settings field, the controller's refusal, every key in both languages), `backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/pay-ways/test.ts` ("REQ-782 …": a card link names card in the en/es text and puts the card row first in the email); the REQ-213/REQ-630 wiring pins in `jest/unit/stripe-card-pay.test.ts` and `jest/unit/pay-links.test.ts` amended to the portal · integration `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/card-pay-link.int.test.ts` (booted app: PUT `/profile/identity` refuses http / javascript: / host-less card links with 400 and stores nothing, stores a good one trimmed; `/invoices/:id/public` carries the link on the card row) · e2e `e2e/card-pay-link/card-pay-link.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-782: …" — the owner's view says how to set card up and the customer sees no card button; Settings refuses http and saves the https link, which reads back after a reload; the customer's `/i/:id` shows "Pay $65.00 by card" before "I sent it", `href` = the link, new tab, `noopener noreferrer`; clicking opens the portal in its own tab; Spanish "Pagar $65.00 con tarjeta"); `e2e/stripe-card` and `e2e/pay-links` amended: "Pay by card" → `/i/:id/pay`, the card pays there.
**Evidence (2026-11-13, local, branch fix/cdv1-d10-card-pay-link off demo-fixes 0b909555):** RED first (tests committed alone, c6af4f62) — `deno test` on `card-pay-link.int.test.ts` + `pay-ways/test.ts` → "FAILED | 3 passed | 3 failed" (the http link stored with 200; the card row without `url`; "Pay online by Venmo" with no card); jest unit lane → "Test Suites: 3 failed … Tests: 12 failed" (`card-pay-link`, `pay-links`, `stripe-card-pay`: `cardPayWay` / `checkCardPayUrl` missing, no `PayByCard`, no `/i/[id]/pay.tsx`). GREEN — the same backend files "ok | 6 passed | 0 failed"; neighbours `deno test src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller src/paperwork/domain/business/pay-ways src/users/entrypoints/business-identity-controller` → "ok | 88 passed | 0 failed"; `shots run e2e/card-pay-link e2e/stripe-card e2e/pay-links` → REQ-782 ✓ and REQ-212/213/216 ✓; REQ-630 failed once on the Zelle "Copied" click (a click before the claim island hydrated, now that the page's first wait is the server-drawn link — the story clicks until it answers) and then ✓ alone. `deno check` + `deno lint` clean on the touched front-end files.

## REQ-781 — No empty strip is kept for the customer's demo pill: it floats over the page, never over a control (demo-loop cycle dv1, issue d7)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dv1, issue `d7` — "No empty strip is reserved for the demo pill". Raphael's decision on it: "the gap reserved for the demo pill ... that's not a decision" (fix it). Merged RCA fix direction (at `0b909555`): REQ-379 / REQ-440(b) gave the pill a full-width band (cycle 4 p4-p8b).
**Cause:** `DemoModeOverlay.tsx` place() reserved REQ-379's band whenever the pill sat home — `room(home.room)` → `setPillRoom` set `--demo-pill-h` (64 px at 1280×720) and the body's bottom padding, every app shell subtracted it (`dashboard.css`/`assistant-page.css` `.app` height), and REQ-440's `data-cy="demo-band"` painted it in the page's colour. REQ-643 kept that room while the pill sat home, which at 1280×720 is nearly always (the shells shrink to leave the strip, so home is always clear): an empty ~64 px band under /dashboard, /quotes and the quote page.
**Requirement:** no room and no band are ever kept for the pill (`--demo-pill-h` unset, no body padding, no painted band; the app reaches the window's foot). The pill floats over the page (`placePill`, `shared/demo-mode/pill.ts`):
1. whole, in the first spot with nothing of the page under it — home (bottom-left), bottom-right, bottom-centre, top-right, top-left (`pillSpots`, under the impersonation banner);

## REQ-780 — the send dialog's email preview is visible on the presenter's stage (demo-loop cycle dv1, d6)
Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." His decision on this one: "The email preview should not be blank on the presenter screen."

Demo issue d6, cycle dv1. Earlier it was cycle 5 m18. The RCA: SendLangPreview renders "What they'll get" as `<iframe sandbox="" srcdoc=EMAIL>`. The REQ-242 mirror recorder dropped every embedded page's srcdoc, and the replay refused it, so the stage showed an empty box.

Now an iframe's srcdoc crosses the mirror. It is cleaned on both ends by `cleanEmbedDoc` (shared/demo-mode/mirror.ts), which removes:
- scripts, `<noscript>`/`<template>` and comments
- nested frames, objects and embeds
- `<base>` and http-equiv metas
- event handlers, nested srcdoc and integrity/nonce attributes
- `javascript:`/`vbscript:` URLs and scripting `data:` URLs

It is not sent under `data-demo-mask` or over 512 000 characters. The stage builds it in a frame with `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` and never `allow-scripts`. That sandbox is set before the srcdoc, and no frame can change or remove it. The frame sits inside the stage frame and inherits its sandbox and CSP (`script-src 'none'`), so nothing in the email runs. A frame's `src` still never crosses, and nothing of a frame/object/embed does. This amends REQ-242: its snapshot expectation now shows the sample frame's srcdoc, cleaned and sandboxed.

**Tests:**
- unit: jest `unit/demo-stage-email-preview.test.ts` (REQ-780: cleaning, snapshot, language-switch op, forged ops) and `unit/demo-mode-mirror-dom.test.ts` (the REQ-242 expectation, amended)
- integration: n/a — the mirror is browser-to-browser; the backend only relays opaque chunks (`backend/src/demo-mode/entrypoints/demo-mode-controller/int.test.ts` still green)
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-email-preview.e2e.test.ts`. In real Chromium, the real recorder and replayer inside MIRROR_SRCDOC show the Spanish email on the stage within 1 s (styled, at the customer's size), then the English one after the switch, and no script runs.

## REQ-779 — the assistant keeps every job detail the contractor typed: "on Shoal Creek" is the job address, and an incomplete email ("tom@reyes") is kept and flagged, never dropped (demo-loop cycle dv1, issue m7)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." On this issue, Raphael's decision: "fix all of these." Demo-loop cycle dv1, issue m7 "Assistant keeps every job detail the contractor typed (address, email)". Verify round 6: help-me-price with "Bathroom floor for the Hendersons on Shoal Creek: porcelain 12x24, recessed niche, before Thanksgiving, email tom@reyes" opened the customer step with the address empty, and "tom@reyes" left Email empty with no warning. The RCA handed over was empty (`[{}]`), so the cause below was traced in the worktree at 0b909555.
**Cause:** (1) `extractServiceAddress` (`shared/quote-flow/quick-quote-prefill.ts`) reads a number-less "on <Street>" only when a street-type word follows (St / Dr / …, REQ-331/435). "on Shoal Creek:" has none, so the help-me-price quote (`AsstChat.startQuoteFromRaw`) and the chat's `create_quote` (`handle-chat-message`) were both stored with no `serviceAddress`, and the step's address box (`initialServiceAddress={quote?.serviceAddress}`) stayed blank. (2) `extractEmail` (`quote-facts.ts`) needs a full address with a TLD. "tom@reyes" read as no email, and unlike the phone (REQ-575 `unusablePhone`), nothing named it.
**Requirement:**
- As a last resort, the job address is one to three Capitalized words right after a lower-case "on" / "en", closed by `:` `,` `;` `.` or the end of the text: "on Shoal Creek:" becomes "Shoal Creek", and "en Shoal Creek" works the same way. A day, a month, a holiday or a payment app is never an address ("on Monday", "on Thanksgiving.", "en Navidad", "on Zelle"). The earlier forms still win.
- If the quote has no address, the customer step's address box falls back to the address read from the typed text.
- An "@" word that is not a full email ("tom@reyes", "carl@", "ana@gmail") is the new fact `unusableEmail`. The Email box is pre-filled with it. While the box still holds that value, or is empty, the form shows `asstChat.customerStep.emailIncomplete`: en "The email in your message (tom@reyes) looks incomplete — type the full address, like name@example.com.", es "El correo de tu mensaje (tom@reyes) parece incompleto — escribe la dirección completa, como nombre@ejemplo.com.". Next stays disabled until the email is fixed or cleared.
- The earlier parts of the sentence are unchanged: the porcelain correction, the niche (REQ-575/653) and the deadline term (REQ-771).
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/dv1-m7-address-email.test.ts` ("REQ-779 …" ×28). Covers the demo sentence → "Shoal Creek" and the other "on/en <Street>" forms; days, holidays and apps are refused; the earlier forms still win; `extractUnusableEmail` and `unusableEmail` for incomplete emails, and none for full ones; AsstChat wiring; the en and es key.
- integration: `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/int.test.ts` ("REQ-779 dv1 m7 …"). The verifier's sentence through the chat's `create_quote` stores `serviceAddress` "Shoal Creek".
- e2e: `e2e/dv1-m7-address-email/dv1-m7-address-email.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-779 dv1 m7: …"). In a browser on the seeded customer step:
  - the address box reads "Shoal Creek" and the Email box reads "tom@reyes";
  - the "looks incomplete" note names it, and Next is disabled;
  - typing "tom@reyes.com" hides the note and enables Next.
**Evidence (2026-11-13, branch fix/cdv1-m7 off demo-fixes 0b909555):**
- RED, all on the original source:
  - jest `--testPathPattern dv1-m7-address-email` gave "Tests: 17 failed, 11 passed, 28 total"; every positive case failed.
  - `deno test … int.test.ts --filter REQ-779` gave "FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed" (`- undefined + "Shoal Creek"`).
  - `shots run e2e/dv1-m7-address-email/…` gave "✗ … expectation failed: the job address typed 'on Shoal Creek' is in the address box — expected "Shoal Creek", got """.
- GREEN:
  - jest file "Tests: 28 passed".
  - int "ok | 1 passed".
  - `shots run` "✓ REQ-779 … · 47.6s" (1 pass · 0 fail). The screenshot shows Hendersons, tom@reyes with the note, Shoal Creek, and Next disabled.
- Neighbours:
  - `npx jest --selectProjects unit` gave "Test Suites: 498 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 5086 passed".
  - `deno test -A --unstable-kv --parallel` over handle-chat-message/ and business/openai-tools/ gave "ok | 306 passed | 0 failed".
  - `deno lint` is clean on the touched files, and `deno check islands/AsstChat.tsx` is clean.
  - `deno fmt --check` is clean on the new files and on the two shared files. AsstChat.tsx (known-unformattable) and int.test.ts (already unformatted at HEAD) were not run through fmt.

## REQ-777 — "Job done, invoice her" keeps the customer that was set through the quote's own setup questions (wizard), en + es (demo-loop cycle dv1, M9 verify round 6; amends REQ-768 / REQ-772)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Raphael's decision on the dv1 RCA: "fix all of these." Demo-loop cycle dv1, issue M9 "'Job done, invoice them' keeps the customer even when it was set through the quote's setup questions". Verify round 6: draft Q-001 "Bathroom Tile Installation · Ana Diaz" (customer set via the wizard) lost the customer on "Job done, need to invoice her".
**Cause (reproduced at demo-fixes 0b909555):** (1) the wizard's customer step (`HandleWizardAnswer.persistAnswers`) binds the customer to the quote by id only — `QuoteStore.update` writes `customerId` and no `customerSnapshot` (the snapshot is taken at create only). `billingReply`'s job-done offer (`backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-answers/mod.ts` `jobDoneInvoiceOffer`, REQ-768/772) named the customer from the snapshot, the signer or the summary's "— Name" tail — none present — so the reply said "…started an invoice for $1,450: pick who it's for…" and the offer carried no `customerName`. `AnswerBilling` never read the bound customer. The thread's title ("Bathroom Tile Installation · Ana Diaz") comes from the bound customer, which is why the verifier saw her name there. (2) On the front end, the offer's name (`prefillCustomerName`) only reached the hidden create form's input; the customer step's known-customer match and prefill read `stepFacts`, which had no name — so "Who is this for?" showed the bare pick list.
**Requirement:** (a) `AnswerBilling` reads the customer the quote is bound to (`quote.customerId`, else the thread's) and passes it to `billingReply` (`opts.customer`); a job-done offer on a never-signed quote names that customer first (it is also who the quote points at after a swap), with her email, then the snapshot / signer / summary tail as before. (b) The invoice wizard's customer step takes the flow's name into its facts (`withOfferedCustomerName` in `shared/quote-flow/customer-dedupe.ts`, applied to AsstChat's `stepFacts` after the summary tail): a saved customer is offered in one tap ("Use Ana Diaz ✓" / "Usar a Ana Diaz"), a new one opens the create form already filled. Typed in the thread's composer or in the wizard step's "Tell the assistant…" box; English and Spanish.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-answers/test.ts` ("REQ-777 M9 billingReply: …" ×2: the wizard-bound Ana Diaz names the offer + email in en + es; the bound customer wins over a stale snapshot) · unit `jest/unit/invoice-offer-customer-step.test.ts` ("REQ-777 M9 …" ×4: `withOfferedCustomerName` rules; with it `knownCustomerForStep` offers the saved Ana Díaz, without it nobody; AsstChat wires it into `stepFacts`) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/billing-actions.int.test.ts` ("REQ-777 M9 (dv1): …" ×5: draft Q-001 with nobody named, the real TransitionToTerms + HandleWizardAnswer customer step create Ana Diaz, then "Job done, need to invoice her" / "Trabajo terminado, necesito facturarle" / "The job is finished, please bill her" in Q-001's thread — in the composer and in the wizard step's box — → the offer for Ana Diaz, ana.diaz@example.com, $1,450; no model call; no invoice) · e2e `e2e/chat-invoice-intent/chat-invoice-intent.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-777 M9 (dv1): …" en + es: Q-001 created, Ana Diaz set through the wizard's customer step over HTTP, the sentence typed in the step's "Tell the assistant…" box on /assistant/<Q-001 thread> → the pad opens at 1450, the reply names Ana Diaz, Continue → "Who is this for?" / "¿Para quién es esto?" offering Ana Diaz).
**Evidence (2026-11-13, branch fix/cdv1-m9 off demo-fixes 0b909555):**
- RED: `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check …/billing-actions.int.test.ts --filter REQ-777` → "FAILED | 0 passed | 5 failed": "Expected actual: "Job's done — let's bill it. The quote was never signed, so I've started an invoice for $1,450: pick who it's for, check the details and send it." to contain: "Ana Diaz"" (es: "…empecé la factura por $1,450: elige a quién va…"); `deno test …/chat-answers/test.ts --filter REQ-777` → "Type checking failed" ('customer' does not exist in the opts type); `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern invoice-offer-customer-step` → "Tests: 4 failed" ("dedupe.withOfferedCustomerName is not a function"; the AsstChat wiring regex unmatched); `shots run e2e/chat-invoice-intent/… -- --no-check --filter REQ-777` → "✗ … expectation failed: the reply names Ana Diaz (got: … Job's done — let's bill it. The quote was never signed, so I've started an invoice for $1,450: pick who it's for…)" en and es; with only the server fix: "✗ … the customer step carries Ana Diaz (offered: "")" (bare pick list).
- GREEN: int filter → "ok | 5 passed | 0 failed"; chat-answers test.ts → "ok | 39 passed"; jest file → "Tests: 4 passed"; `shots run e2e/chat-invoice-intent/chat-invoice-intent.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` → "ok | 6 passed | 0 failed" (REQ-656, 752, 768, 772 and REQ-777 en + es ✓; the screenshot shows "¿Para quién es esto? · Usar a Ana Diaz ✓ ana.diaz@example.com" on Q-002's thread).
- Neighbours: `deno test -A --unstable-kv --parallel` over handle-chat-message/, answer-billing/, chat-billing/, transition-to-terms/, handle-wizard-answer/, business/ → "ok | 859 passed | 0 failed"; jest `--testPathPattern "invoice-offer-customer-step|c4-summary-customer|chat-invoice-flow-offer|customer-dedupe|customer-step"` → "Tests: 75 passed"; `deno check` + `deno lint` clean on AsstChat.tsx and customer-dedupe.ts; `deno fmt --check` clean on every touched file except AsstChat.tsx (known-unformattable, not run).

## REQ-778 — Free plan: five quotes a month, enforced and stated — the New quote path and /quotes say the limit and how to upgrade, and the pricing page says "Up to five quotes a month" (demo-loop cycle dv1, issue d8; amends REQ-109's second line and follows REQ-766)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dv1, issue d8 "Free plan: five quotes a month, enforced and stated". Raphael's decision (the product owner): **"The free plan limit is five quotes."** DONE MEANS: a Free account can make five quotes in a calendar month; the sixth is refused with a clear message (en/es) naming the limit and how to upgrade, both on /quotes and in the assistant chat; the pricing page says "up to five quotes a month" for Free.
**What already existed (REQ-766, at 0b909555):** the cap itself — `QuoteAllowance` refuses the sixth quote of the calendar month on Monster Free: `POST /quotes` answers 402 `{ ok:false, reason:"quote_limit", limit:5, used:5 }` and the chat's `create_quote` replies `chatCoordinator.quoteLimit`. Its tests (unit, int, e2e) were re-run green here.
**Gaps found (RCA, file:line at 0b909555):** (1) /quotes "New quote" (`front-end/components/QuotesSections.tsx` `data-cy="quote-new"` → `/assistant`) makes the quote through the wizard's `startQuoteFromRaw` (`front-end/islands/AsstChat.tsx` `api.post("/quotes", quoteFields)`), whose catch showed `err.message` — "POST /quotes failed: 402" — not the limit. (2) /quotes said nothing about the cap. (3) Free's card and the landing blurb said "Up to five quotes and contracts a month" (`shared/quote-flow/pricing-plans.ts`, `front-end/lib/landing-dict.ts`), not "up to five quotes a month"; a quote IS the agreement since the quote+contract merge. (4) The chat's reply sent the user to "Settings → Plan"; the tab is "Billing" ("Facturación").
**Requirement:**
- `GET /quotes/allowance` (QuoteController, declared before `:id`, needs a session) returns the same `QuoteAllowance` answer: `{ ok:true }` or `{ ok:false, reason:"quote_limit", limit, used }`.
- /quotes reads it (SSR seed `loadQuotesSeed` → `quoteLimit`, and the island's periodic `loadPipeline`). At the cap the hero shows `data-cy="quote-limit-note"`: `quoteLimit.message` + a "See plans" / "Ver planes" link to `/settings?tab=billing`. en: "You've made your 5 quotes for this month on Monster Free. Monster has unlimited quotes: upgrade in Settings → Billing, or your 5 new quotes start again on the 1st." es: "Ya hiciste tus 5 cotizaciones de este mes en Monster Free. Monster tiene cotizaciones ilimitadas: mejora tu plan en Configuración → Facturación, o tus 5 cotizaciones nuevas vuelven a empezar el día 1."
- The assistant's New quote wizard reads a 402 quote_limit from `POST /quotes` (`quoteLimitFromError`, `front-end/lib/quote-limit.ts`) and shows that message, in the UI language.
- `chatCoordinator.quoteLimit` (REQ-766's chat reply) names Settings → Billing / Configuración → Facturación.
- Free's second line and its blurb are "Up to five quotes a month" / "Hasta cinco cotizaciones al mes" (plan card, settings plan cards, landing blurb, /landing2). This amends REQ-109's dictated "Up to five quotes and contracts a month" per Raphael's decision above; the other two lines stay word for word.
**Tests:**
- unit: `front-end/lib/quote-limit.test.tsx` (deno, "REQ-778 dv1 d8: …" ×6 — a 402 quote_limit is read as the limit and other errors are not; the message en/es names five quotes, Monster Free and Settings → Billing; the /quotes hero at the cap shows the note and the plan link, en + es, and none under the cap; the /quotes seed reads GET /quotes/allowance and the seeded page shows the note on first render) · `jest/unit/dv1-free-quote-limit.test.ts` ("REQ-778 dv1 d8 …" ×4 — the Free card and blurb say "Up to five quotes a month" / "Hasta cinco cotizaciones al mes"; the en/es message keys; the wizard's catch uses `quoteLimitFromError` + `quoteLimitMessage`). REQ-109/REQ-733 pins amended to the new line: `jest/unit/plan-copy-truth.test.ts`, `jest/unit/landing2-page.test.ts`, `jest/unit/pricing-plans.test.ts`, `e2e/landing2/landing2.e2e.test.ts`.

## REQ-787 — Repeat visits can be Annual: pick a month from a dropdown, then the day(s) on that month's calendar (2026-11-13, hotfix)
**Raphael:** "in recurring visits i need to add an anual where i can select a month from a dropdown to select the month and have the month view. this way we can define an annual recurring visit. this is a hotfix as soon as you finish and verify it push it."
**What it does:** Cadence on /field/subscriptions offers Weekly, Monthly and **Annual**. Annual shows a **Month** dropdown (January–December, starts on the first visit's month) and that month's **calendar** (title "March 2027", a week header, day 1 under its real weekday, as many days as that month has in the year it first falls). The owner picks the day(s) on it; the card reads "Annual · March 5" / "Anual · 5 de marzo"; Edit reopens on the same month and day. The visit is due once a year in that month on the picked day(s), never before the first visit; 29 in February falls on the 28th in non-leap years. Data: `Subscription.cadence = "annual"`, `month` (1–12), `daysOfMonth`. An annual visit is never read as a weekly charge (`subscriptionBilling` → undefined). **REQ-157 AMENDMENT:** the cadence list is now Weekly | Monthly | Annual.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/schedule/test.ts` ("REQ-787 isDue — annual …", "REQ-787 scheduleText — annual …") · unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/quote-subscription/test.ts` ("REQ-787 subscriptionBilling: an annual visit is never read as a weekly charge …") · integration `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-787 an annual subscription keeps its month and day(s) …; month 0 or 13 is 400; a PUT changes the month") · e2e `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-787: Annual shows a Month dropdown and that month's calendar …"; REQ-157's story amended to expect "Weekly|Monthly|Annual").
**Evidence (2026-11-13):** RED — unit: `TS2322 Type '"annual"' is not assignable to type 'Cadence'`; int: `400` instead of `201`; billing unit: returned a weekly term instead of `undefined`; e2e: `locator.selectOption: Timeout 15000ms exceeded` (no Annual option). GREEN — schedule unit `10 passed`, quote-subscription unit `8 passed`, `field.int.test.ts` `27 passed`; `deno task test:unit` → `1658 passed | 0 failed` + jest `5176 passed, 1 skipped`; `shots run e2e/field-tasks` → `19 pass · 1 fail` — `✓ REQ-787 · 24.9s`, `✓ REQ-157`; the one red, REQ-143 ("1 of 1 tasks done" never shows), fails identically on an untouched origin/develop worktree (pre-existing, not this change).

## REQ-793 — Demo mode follows the customer into the worker view (AMENDS REQ-217)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13, mid-demo: "my demonee switched to the worker view and the demo is not showing his screen as a matter of fact its showing this [stage pill: 'Esperando la app de Alexander Jerez…' · 'La pantalla de Alexander Jerez, 2828 × 1666'] fix it, verify its fixed and push it as a hotfix to main so that it reflects on prod."

## REQ-788 — Recurring visits: an "Overhead" toggle in the subscription form's upper right adds the overhead cost set in Settings to every visit
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13 ("in recurring visits there needs to be a toggle button in the upper right that adds an overhead cost. that overhead cost is defined in settings. the toggle button is in the same style as the weekday selection button. hotfix so push it as soon as its verified by you").
**Requirement:** Settings → Business carries "Overhead cost per visit", a dollar amount (`fieldOverheadCents`, a whole number of cents ≥ 0; 0 or unset = none). The New / Edit subscription form on /field/subscriptions carries a toggle chip in its upper right, styled as a weekday chip (`.days .day`, teal when on), reading "Overhead · $25.00" with the Settings amount; it is off on a new subscription and remembers its state on an edit (`overhead: boolean` on the subscription). When it is on, every visit of that subscription bills one more line — "Overhead" / "Gastos generales", on the visit's date and address, priced at the Settings amount as it stands when the batch is pulled — so the draft's total is the visit's services plus the overhead. A visit of a subscription with the toggle off, or an account whose overhead is 0, bills exactly as before. The subscription card lists the overhead under its services when the toggle is on. The overhead line is no task: it is never stamped on a task, never shown to a worker, and never counts as a $0 line.
**Assumption (mine):** "overhead cost" is a flat dollar amount per visit, not a percentage.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/batch-lines/test.ts` ("REQ-788 …": one overhead line per visit of a subscription with the toggle on; none when off or when the amount is 0; the line has no task and totals in), `backend/src/field/domain/business/invoice-terms/test.ts` ("REQ-788 parseOverheadCents"), `jest/unit/overhead-toggle.test.ts` (the form's chip in the modal head with the weekday chip's class, the Settings input, the client fields, both languages' labels) · integration `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-788 …": the Settings amount, a subscription created with the toggle on and one without, the day generated and completed, the pull: the first draft bills services + overhead with an Overhead line, the second bills services only; the toggle flips on an edit; a bad amount is refused) · e2e `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-788: …": the amount set in Settings, the chip in the form's upper right styled as a weekday chip, toggled on, saved; the card shows the overhead; the pulled draft totals services + overhead).
**Evidence (2026-11-13, local, REQ-788):** RED first — `deno test` on batch-lines / invoice-terms → "Type checking failed" (`parseOverheadCents`, `overhead` did not exist); `jest --testPathPattern overhead-toggle` → "Test Suites: 1 failed · Tests: 5 failed". GREEN, on origin/develop (63b657ad) — `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field` → "ok | 131 passed | 0 failed"; `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/users/entrypoints src/users/dto` → "ok | 124 passed | 0 failed"; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 509 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 5181 passed, 5182 total" (the first run caught REQ-522: the Spanish hint said "Ajustes" — now "Configuración"); `SHOTS_JOBS=4 shots run e2e/field-tasks e2e/settings-one-net-days e2e/settings-field-validate e2e/settings-editcard-feedback` → 22 pass · 1 fail (the REQ-788 story 120.6 s under a host load of 40–75: the chip's computed radius/height/weight equal the weekday chip's, the chip to the right of the title on its row, "Overhead · $25.00", toggled on and saved, the card's overhead row, the draft `Lawn cut=6500,Overhead=2500`, amount 9000, zeroLines 0). The one fail was REQ-143 and it fails on origin/develop untouched: its story waits for "1 of 1 tasks done" while the worker screen has said "1 of 1 task done" (`worker.today.one`) since 2026-11-12 — see the REVISION below. `deno fmt --check`, `deno lint`, `deno check` clean on the touched front-end files; `deno lint` clean on the touched backend files. **Requirement:** Wherever a batch invoice renders (the public page, the invoice PDF, the batch print PDF, the email), its visits sit under their address: the address is the heading (with that address's subtotal when the bill has several addresses), under it one row per visit by date, "Oct 2 · Lawn · $65.00", the amount at the end. Now (a) a line saved without them is read back from its own text ("Oct 2 — Lawn — <address>", "2 oct — …", "Nov 16 – Nov 18 — …"), its year taken from the bill's service period (else the day it was made; a period across new year puts January in the later year), so invoices already stripped group again; (b) the editor keeps a visit's date / service / address whenever the line's text is unchanged (a rewritten or new line is no longer that visit).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/visit-groups.test.ts` ("REQ-791 groupVisits reads a batch line back from its text …", "REQ-791 keepVisitFields …") · integration `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-invoice-pdf/int.test.ts` ("REQ-791 render-invoice-pdf: a batch draft whose lines lost their visit fields is drawn grouped by address, then date — no flat paragraph") · e2e `e2e/invoice-polish/invoice-polish.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-791: a batch draft's visits read as address → date → amount in the Job details section, after an edit too").

## REQ-798 — The dashboard's money widget is the star: one segmented bar of the business's money, five buckets, click a segment to see its documents one by one
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13 (two screenshots: the current "Money owed to you" card and QuickBooks' money bar — "this widget shows peoples business details we actually want to make this widget needs to be the star of the show and adhere more to the example … when you click on the share of the bar it details what invoice one by one"), then "i asked you to hotfix it".
**Requirement:** The "Money owed to you" card leaves the bottom-right corner and becomes a full-width band at the top of the dashboard, right under the setup checklist and above the KPI tiles. It keeps its label, its big number (the balance of every open invoice by the REQ-397 open-receivable rule, overdue or not), the "Nudge all" button when something is overdue, REQ-473's "Upcoming: $925 bills Nov 26" line and empty texts, and REQ-728's skeleton while the lists load. Under that, five stat columns in QuickBooks' order, each an amount over a caption with its count: estimates out (sent quotes), unbilled income (won jobs' agreed total minus what has been invoiced or scheduled against them), overdue invoices (open, past due), open invoices (open, not yet due), recently paid (paid in the last 30 days). Under the columns one segmented bar, one colour per bucket, each segment's width its share of the five amounts; a column or its segment is a button. One bucket is always selected — by default the first non-empty of overdue, open, unbilled, estimates, paid — and the selected segment is lifted while the others dim. Below the bar the selected bucket's documents are listed one by one: the customer and job, a meta line (the overdue days / due date / paid date / sent date, and the document's number), the amount; every row is a link that opens that quote or invoice. A bucket with nothing in it says so in one line. Amounts are INTEGER CENTS end to end and render through `fmtMoney`. The old three-legend aging bar is gone. ## REQ-788 — AMENDMENT (2026-11-13): the overhead is a percentage OR a dollar amount
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13 ("we want it in percentage, or in dollars, push as a hotfix.").
**Requirement:** Settings → "Overhead cost per visit" carries a `$ | %` switch (`fieldOverheadMode`: "flat" | "percent", flat by default) beside the amount: in `$` the field is a dollar amount per visit (`fieldOverheadCents`, as before); in `%` it is a percentage of the visit's services (`fieldOverheadPct`, 0–100, up to two decimals). The subscription form's chip reads "Overhead · $25.00" in `$` and "Overhead · 10%" in `%`. A percent visit bills `round(services × pct / 100)` cents on its Overhead line, where services is the sum of that visit's service lines on the invoice; the card shows the computed amount and the percentage ("$6.50 · 10%"). ## REQ-807 — HOTFIX: a customer's card sheet opens in view, wherever the page is scrolled (fixed overlays inside the content pane)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13, a screen recording (`Screen Recording 2026-11-13 at 1.20.04 PM.mov`): on /customers, "Open card" on the last card of the page (scrolled to the bottom) — nothing appears; the sheet is only found after scrolling all the way back to the top. "this should not happen … fix, verify and push to prod as a hotfix."
**Requirement:** "Open card" opens the client sheet over the screen where the person is — the pane does not have to be scrolled to the top to see it, and the pane's own scroll position is untouched. In general: a `position: fixed` overlay inside the content pane is fixed to the viewport, never to the pane.
**Cause:** REQ-195's motion system (released 2026-11-12) gives `main.main > *` — which is `.content`, the scrolling pane — the `pm-rise` entrance with `animation-fill-mode: both`; a finished animation with a transform keeps the effect applied (an identity matrix), and a transformed element is the containing block for every `position: fixed` descendant, so the sheet's backdrop sat at the top of the pane, ~5000 px above the viewport. `backwards` keeps the from-state through the delay and applies nothing after the end.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/motion-system.test.ts` ("REQ-807 …": every `pm-rise` entrance fills `backwards`, never `both`/`forwards`) · integration n/a — a stylesheet · e2e `e2e/customer-sheet-in-view/customer-sheet-in-view.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-807: …": 24 customers, the pane scrolled to the last card, Open card → the sheet's backdrop covers the viewport (top 0, the window's height), the sheet is visible, the pane's scrollTop is unchanged).
**Evidence (2026-11-13, hotfix off main b786734e):** reproduced first with a probe story (plain and inside a live demo, both the same): after Open card, `[data-cy=client-sheet]` is in the DOM and the URL carries `?open=…`, but the backdrop's rect is `top=-4964 h=684` with `.content` reporting `transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)` from `pm-rise:finished` (`animation-fill-mode: both`). RED — `npx jest unit/motion-system.test.ts` → "Tests: 1 failed, 4 passed" (`REQ-807 …`: the rule says `both`); `shots run e2e/customer-sheet-in-view -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-807 … expected 0, got -4964`. GREEN — `motion.css` fills `backwards` on both `pm-rise` rules; jest → "Tests: 5 passed, 5 total" (REQ-195's own tests included); `shots run e2e/customer-sheet-in-view e2e/motion -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-807 … · 3.5s`, `✓ REQ-195 … · 1.7s`. The recording's slow "scroll to the top" was the person scrolling up by hand to find the sheet, not the app scrolling.

## REQ-806 — The approve-link door: Claude views one account read-only after a one-time tap on the super-admin phone
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13, after Claude would not sign in to prod with a texted code ("how can we setup a door for you that you are willing to walk through"), rejecting a standing secret ("a random key that can be leaked") in favour of a one-time approval: "yes do the approve link then as a separate endpoint so it doesnt break everyone elses access."
**Requirement:** Separate endpoints under `/api/ops/*` — sign-in, `/admin` and every other session unchanged. `POST /ops/requests { account, reason }` (anyone; at most 10 an hour) matches exactly one account by phone, name, email or business and texts the always-super-admin phone (+1 843-855-7133) "Claude asks to view <business> (<phone>) (read-only, 30 min). Reason: … Approve or deny: <link>"; no single match texts nobody, and the answer is the same either way. The asker gets an id and a poll token only. The link opens `/ops/approve/:token`, which shows the ask; reading it changes nothing (a link preview never approves); Approve (the one solid button) or Deny (outlined) decide it once, within 10 minutes. Approve mints a session for that one account that is read-only (every non-GET is 403 `read_only_session`), dies after 30 minutes (401), and carries the approver as `impersonatorId`; `GET /ops/requests/:id` with the poll token hands it over once. Tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes; every ask is kept 30 days as the audit trail. Off the real deploy (no text goes out) the approve token rides the ask's reply, as REQ-082's code does. `deno task ops ask "<account>" --reason "<why>"` waits for the tap and keeps the session in `~/.config/documonster-ops/view.json` (0600, never printed); `deno task ops view <path>…` opens each path in its own headless browser as that view — every write aborted — saving a screenshot and the page text (a `/pdf` path as the PDF); `deno task ops end` forgets it.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/business/ops-access/test.ts` (4: tokens, status, the text, `sessionRefusal`), `jest/unit/ops-tool.test.ts` (3: args, the write block, names + cookie) · integration `backend/src/users/entrypoints/ops-access-controller/int.test.ts` (4: the whole approve flow incl. read-only + once + single use; the dev token; deny + expiry + other sessions untouched; no match + rate limit) · e2e `e2e/ops-approve/ops-approve.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-806: Approve on /ops/approve/:token gives the asker a read-only view of that one account, once; Deny opens nothing").
**Evidence (2026-11-13):** RED — unit `Module not found …/ops-access/mod.ts`; int `404 Not Found` (no /ops routes); jest `Cannot find module '../../shared/ops/tool'`. ## REQ-803 — A business connects its OWN Square in Settings, the way it connects its own Stripe, and its customers pay invoices by card on Square's checkout
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13: "do you see stripe? we want to also add square in the same way." (Stripe: REQ-212/213/216/630, the portal rule REQ-782 — Raphael's D10: "Card payments should be a link to a separate portal".)
**Requirement:** (a) Settings gets a "Card payments (Square)" card under the Stripe one. The business pastes its Square **access token** and, optionally, a **location ID** (blank = the first ACTIVE location). The backend checks the token with `GET /v2/locations` (`Authorization: Bearer`, `Square-Version: 2025-01-23`), refuses a malformed token or an application id/secret (422 `token_invalid` / `app_id_not_token`, before Square is asked), a token Square rejects (422 `square_rejected` with Square's words), a location that is not one of the seller's ACTIVE ones (422 `location_not_found`), an account with none (422 `no_location`), a non-USD location (422 `currency_unsupported`). The token is stored SEALED with the secret-box (AES-GCM under SECRETS_KEY, REQ-212) and never returned; the status shows the seller's name, the location's name and id, the environment and the masked token (`EAAA••••WXYZ`), plus the same merchant preview as Stripe's and the line "Payments go straight to your Square account. DocuMonster never holds your money." Disconnect forgets it. No OAuth platform app, no application fee — every call runs on the business's own token, so the money settles in the business's Square balance. (b) On `/i/:id`, with Square connected and a balance, "Pay $X by card" is the solid primary in the same place as Stripe's (REQ-782), with "Secure checkout by Square — you pay {business} directly."; the manual card chip is dropped while Square is connected, as it is for Stripe. Tapping it POSTs `/invoices/:id/square/checkout` with the balance and version the page showed; the server creates a Square payment link on the business's token (`POST /v2/online-checkout/payment-links`: `idempotency_key`, `quick_pay { name: "Invoice INV-001 · <business>", price_money { amount: <balance cents>, currency: USD }, location_id }`, `checkout_options.redirect_url: <origin>/i/<id>?square=return`, `payment_note: <number>`), stores the pending checkout (invoice, version, amount, link id, order id, url) and answers the URL; the browser goes there in the same tab. A stale balance or version is 409 `stale_balance` with the current ones, before Square is asked; the button takes the new amount and says so. A paid invoice is 409 `already_paid`; no Square is 404 `card_unavailable`. The same balance at the same version reuses the link already made. `/i/:id/pay` offers the same Square button (the no-script way). (c) No webhook, like Stripe: when the customer comes back (`?square=return`, forced) and whenever the public invoice loads while a checkout is pending (at most every 10 s per checkout, so the page's own polling does not hammer Square), the server reads the order (`GET /v2/orders/{id}`) on the business's token. Paid = state COMPLETED with a tender, or tenders covering it with nothing left due (`net_amount_due_money` 0); it is recorded through the SAME `RecordCardPayment` path Stripe uses — a Payment with method card, reference = the tender's Square `payment_id`, idempotent on it (never twice), the balance, the PAID stamp, the receipt — and the page renders paid on that very load. Unpaid → nothing recorded, the button stays, and a return says "Your card payment wasn't completed, so nothing was charged." A canceled order closes the checkout. (d) The invoice email's "Pay by card" row and the text's "Pay online by card, …" count Square as they count Stripe. (e) Off the real deploy a token `EAAAfake_<name>` talks to an in-process fake Square (two locations, one INACTIVE then one ACTIVE; payment links point at a dev-only checkout page `/api/dev/square/checkout/:linkId` naming the invoice, the business and the amount, with Pay — completes the fake order with one card tender — and Cancel, both heading back to the redirect). On the real deploy a fake token is refused (422 `fake_token_refused`) and the dev routes 404, exactly like dev-stripe-controller. English and Spanish throughout.
**Decisions:**
- **One card provider at a time — connecting one is refused while the other is on.** PUT `/me/square` while Stripe is connected is 409 `stripe_connected`; PUT `/me/stripe` while Square is connected is 409 `square_connected`; nothing is stored either way. The Square card says so ("You take cards through Stripe right now. To use Square instead, disconnect Stripe above first") instead of showing its form, and the two Settings cards re-read each other's status when either connects or disconnects (`pm:card-provider` event). Chosen over "most recently connected wins" because nothing is ever silently replaced and there is never a question which one charges. Should both records ever exist anyway, Stripe wins (`cardPayWay` and `ConnectSquare.tokenFor`), so Stripe's behaviour is exactly as before.
- **Environment is inferred, not a toggle:** the token is sent to production (`connect.squareup.com`) first; a 401 there sends it to the sandbox (`connect.squareupsandbox.com`). The environment found is stored and every later call (payment link, order) goes to that host. The card shows "Live" or "Sandbox" (+ "no real card is charged"). The fake token is "sandbox".
- **The return address:** on the real deploy always the site's own origin (APP_URL, else documonster.com) — never the caller's `Origin` header, so no one can mint a checkout on a business's Square that sends the customer elsewhere; off the real deploy the page's own origin (dev boxes, the e2e runner's port).
- **The amount recorded** is the order's total WITHOUT any tip (a tip on Square's page is the business's, not the invoice's).
- **The fake checkout returns with a page that moves on by itself, not a 303** — the dev front-end's `/api` proxy follows redirects server-side and would serve the invoice under the checkout's URL.
- **Test seam:** the Square code reads the real-deploy switch through `squareEnv.reader` (process env by default) so the int tests pin "off the real deploy" for Square without flipping the process-wide DENO_DEPLOY that parallel test files share.
**Data (all user-owned):** `["square_settings", userId]` → `{ userId, tokenSealed, tokenMasked, environment, fake, locationId, locationName, sellerName, merchantId?, connectedAt, updatedAt }`; `["square_checkout", invoiceId, paymentLinkId]` → `{ userId, invoiceId, version, amountCents, paymentLinkId, orderId, url, redirectUrl, status: pending|paid|closed, paymentId?, createdAt, checkedAt? }`. Pure rules in `shared/payments/square.ts` (`squareTokenInfo`, `maskSquareToken`, `squareApiBase`, `squareCheckoutName`, `squareReturnUrl`, `squareOrderPayment`); `cardPayWay` gains `square` → `{ kind: "square", href: "/i/:id/pay" }`.
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/square-pay.test.ts` ("REQ-803 …": the API hosts and Square-Version; token shapes incl. the fake and app ids; the mask; the checkout name and return URL; when an order is paid — COMPLETED, OPEN with nothing due, tip excluded, tender id fallback, open, canceled, partial, no tender; `cardPayWay` square and Stripe-first; the wiring of the client, the settings card, the checkout island, `/i` and `/i/:id/pay`; every key in en and es), `backend/src/core/data/square-gateway/test.ts` (the fake's locations and 401; a fake token refused on the real deploy with nothing sent; the payment link, idempotency, the order OPEN then COMPLETED with the payment id, another seller's token 404, a foreign location 400; the real HTTP calls with `fetch` stubbed — production first, sandbox on 401, Square's words when neither accepts, the headers, the payment-link body, the order read on the same host), `backend/src/users/entrypoints/dev-square-controller/test.ts` (the fake page, Pay completes, Cancel pays nothing; on the real deploy all three routes 404). Amended: `jest/unit/owner-cannot-claim.test.ts` (REQ-479's pin on the `/i` read now allows the `?square=return` suffix).
- integration: `backend/src/users/entrypoints/square-settings-controller/int.test.ts` (connect with the fake token: the status without the token, the first ACTIVE location, the token sealed at rest; a pasted location used, a foreign or inactive one 422 with nothing stored; a rejected token 422, a malformed token / app id 422; one provider at a time both ways; DELETE forgets; no session 401; the fake checkout page), `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/square-pay.int.test.ts` (GET `/invoices/:id/square` off then on, no token, the Stripe config off, the manual card chip dropped; the checkout is a link for the exact balance on the business's token and location back to `/i/:id?square=return`, reused for the same balance; stale amount / version 409 with nothing asked of Square, no Square 404, bad body 400, unknown invoice 404; the return — unpaid records nothing, paid records exactly one card Payment with the Square payment id, a second return and a reload record nothing more, a paid invoice refuses a new checkout; a customer who paid and never came back is recorded on the next plain load; the return origin rule; the invoice email and text name card first once Square is connected).

## REQ-809 — Focusing a field keeps the modal where it is; clicking a client picks it and closes the list (hotfix)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13, right after REQ-801 shipped: "now when i focus the field, the thing scrolls all the way down, if i focus the field it should stay in view." → "when i click a client, the pick box stays open, no reason for that it should pick and close both fixes."
**Cause, proved in a probe story on main:** (1) the scroll is not the picker's: focusing ANY field of the New invoice modal (the job name too) jumped the modal's scroll container to its bottom (`scrollTop` 0 → 1052 = max) about 60 ms after focus, even with `focus({ preventScroll: true })`, and opening the list without focus did not scroll. The global `MobileViewport` island's `focusin` reveal (there to keep a field and its submit button clear of the iOS keyboard) finds the last button after the field in the same form — "Issue invoice", at the bottom of the modal — and `scrollBy`s the scroll container to show it, on a desktop where there is no keyboard. (2) the list staying open: the box sat inside the `<label>` — a click on a row is a click on the label, which re-focuses the input, and the box opens on focus. Moved out of the label in the probe, the pick closed the list.
**Requirement:** Focusing a field never scrolls the page or modal on its own on a desktop: the keyboard reveal only corrects while the on-screen keyboard overlaps the visual viewport (`innerHeight − visualViewport.height > 2`), checked on every pass so it still kicks in the moment the keyboard opens on a phone. The New invoice client box is a `<div>` with a `<span>` caption, not a `<label>`; clicking a client picks it, the box reads the pick, the list closes, nothing scrolls.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/invoice-client-pick-focus.test.ts` ("REQ-809 …": MobileViewport declares `keyboardOpen` and `correct` returns on it first; the client caption is a `<div>`+`<span>`, no `<label>` around the box) · integration n/a — no server change · e2e `e2e/invoice-client-pick/invoice-client-pick.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-809: …" in a browser with 13 customers: the modal opens at scrollTop 0; clicking the client box leaves it at 0 after 700 ms with the box in view and the list open; "Ann" + click "Ann Lee" → the hidden `customerId` is the customer's id, no list, the box reads "C-001 · Ann Lee", scrollTop still 0; clicking the job name box leaves scrollTop 0).
**Evidence (2026-11-13, Mac host, worktree hotfix-invoice-client-focus off origin/main 24ef9f9c):** RED first — jest "Tests: 2 failed, 2 total"; `shots run e2e/invoice-client-pick` → "✗ … expectation failed: focusing the client box does not scroll the modal — expected 0, got 1052". GREEN — jest unit lane `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 516 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 5242 passed, 5243 total"; `shots run e2e/invoice-client-pick e2e/invoice-numbering e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check` → 24 pass · 0 fail (REQ-809 4.5 s; REQ-152/144 — the repeat-visit picker — unchanged). One race hardened on the way: the REQ-206 quote-prefill story read the hidden pick the instant the ledger showed and once lost to the customers fetch (3/3 green alone) — it now waits for the value. `MobileViewport.tsx` was not `deno fmt`-clean on main, so the diff carries its reformat (11 real lines, `git diff -w`). `deno lint`, `deno check` clean on the touched files.
**Prod (2026-11-13, main 404890f1, pushed 18:40Z; carried by the later release 1f7a03b5):** live by 18:47Z — `/login` lists `fresh-island__MobileViewport-CUz4y0Z5.js` (was BhbTPRIJ) and the chunk carries the `innerHeight-…height>2` keyboard guard. On develop as 48cbf48c.

## REQ-803 — A business connects its OWN Square in Settings, the way it connects its own Stripe, and its customers pay invoices by card on Square's checkout
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13: "do you see stripe? we want to also add square in the same way." (Stripe: REQ-212/213/216/630, the portal rule REQ-782 — Raphael's D10: "Card payments should be a link to a separate portal".)
**Requirement:** (a) Settings gets a "Card payments (Square)" card under the Stripe one. The business pastes its Square **access token** and, optionally, a **location ID** (blank = the first ACTIVE location). The backend checks the token with `GET /v2/locations` (`Authorization: Bearer`, `Square-Version: 2025-01-23`), refuses a malformed token or an application id/secret (422 `token_invalid` / `app_id_not_token`, before Square is asked), a token Square rejects (422 `square_rejected` with Square's words), a location that is not one of the seller's ACTIVE ones (422 `location_not_found`), an account with none (422 `no_location`), a non-USD location (422 `currency_unsupported`). The token is stored SEALED with the secret-box (AES-GCM under SECRETS_KEY, REQ-212) and never returned; the status shows the seller's name, the location's name and id, the environment and the masked token (`EAAA••••WXYZ`), plus the same merchant preview as Stripe's and the line "Payments go straight to your Square account. DocuMonster never holds your money." Disconnect forgets it. No OAuth platform app, no application fee — every call runs on the business's own token, so the money settles in the business's Square balance. (b) On `/i/:id`, with Square connected and a balance, "Pay $X by card" is the solid primary in the same place as Stripe's (REQ-782), with "Secure checkout by Square — you pay {business} directly."; the manual card chip is dropped while Square is connected, as it is for Stripe. Tapping it POSTs `/invoices/:id/square/checkout` with the balance and version the page showed; the server creates a Square payment link on the business's token (`POST /v2/online-checkout/payment-links`: `idempotency_key`, `quick_pay { name: "Invoice INV-001 · <business>", price_money { amount: <balance cents>, currency: USD }, location_id }`, `checkout_options.redirect_url: <origin>/i/<id>?square=return`, `payment_note: <number>`), stores the pending checkout (invoice, version, amount, link id, order id, url) and answers the URL; the browser goes there in the same tab. A stale balance or version is 409 `stale_balance` with the current ones, before Square is asked; the button takes the new amount and says so. A paid invoice is 409 `already_paid`; no Square is 404 `card_unavailable`. The same balance at the same version reuses the link already made. `/i/:id/pay` offers the same Square button (the no-script way). (c) No webhook, like Stripe: when the customer comes back (`?square=return`, forced) and whenever the public invoice loads while a checkout is pending (at most every 10 s per checkout, so the page's own polling does not hammer Square), the server reads the order (`GET /v2/orders/{id}`) on the business's token. Paid = state COMPLETED with a tender, or tenders covering it with nothing left due (`net_amount_due_money` 0); it is recorded through the SAME `RecordCardPayment` path Stripe uses — a Payment with method card, reference = the tender's Square `payment_id`, idempotent on it (never twice), the balance, the PAID stamp, the receipt — and the page renders paid on that very load. Unpaid → nothing recorded, the button stays, and a return says "Your card payment wasn't completed, so nothing was charged." A canceled order closes the checkout. (d) The invoice email's "Pay by card" row and the text's "Pay online by card, …" count Square as they count Stripe. (e) Off the real deploy a token `EAAAfake_<name>` talks to an in-process fake Square (two locations, one INACTIVE then one ACTIVE; payment links point at a dev-only checkout page `/api/dev/square/checkout/:linkId` naming the invoice, the business and the amount, with Pay — completes the fake order with one card tender — and Cancel, both heading back to the redirect). On the real deploy a fake token is refused (422 `fake_token_refused`) and the dev routes 404, exactly like dev-stripe-controller. English and Spanish throughout.
**Decisions:**
- **One card provider at a time — connecting one is refused while the other is on.** PUT `/me/square` while Stripe is connected is 409 `stripe_connected`; PUT `/me/stripe` while Square is connected is 409 `square_connected`; nothing is stored either way. The Square card says so ("You take cards through Stripe right now. To use Square instead, disconnect Stripe above first") instead of showing its form, and the two Settings cards re-read each other's status when either connects or disconnects (`pm:card-provider` event). Chosen over "most recently connected wins" because nothing is ever silently replaced and there is never a question which one charges. Should both records ever exist anyway, Stripe wins (`cardPayWay` and `ConnectSquare.tokenFor`), so Stripe's behaviour is exactly as before.
- **Environment is inferred, not a toggle:** the token is sent to production (`connect.squareup.com`) first; a 401 there sends it to the sandbox (`connect.squareupsandbox.com`). The environment found is stored and every later call (payment link, order) goes to that host. The card shows "Live" or "Sandbox" (+ "no real card is charged"). The fake token is "sandbox".
- **The return address:** on the real deploy always the site's own origin (APP_URL, else documonster.com) — never the caller's `Origin` header, so no one can mint a checkout on a business's Square that sends the customer elsewhere; off the real deploy the page's own origin (dev boxes, the e2e runner's port).
- **The amount recorded** is the order's total WITHOUT any tip (a tip on Square's page is the business's, not the invoice's).
- **The fake checkout returns with a page that moves on by itself, not a 303** — the dev front-end's `/api` proxy follows redirects server-side and would serve the invoice under the checkout's URL.
- **Test seam:** the Square code reads the real-deploy switch through `squareEnv.reader` (process env by default) so the int tests pin "off the real deploy" for Square without flipping the process-wide DENO_DEPLOY that parallel test files share.

## REQ-808 — Settings: Square | Stripe | Custom button — the online-payment setup is one section with three tabs (hotfix)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13: "make 3 tabs, one for square, one for stripe and one for custom button. ship this as a hotfix." Clarified from his prod screenshot (via the coordinator): the Custom button tab is the "Other payment links" card (name + https link rows, Add link / Remove — e.g. "Xpress") together with the single "Card payment link" field (REQ-782); the three tabs replace the Stripe card (REQ-212), the Square card (REQ-803) and the Other payment links card (REQ-630), and the links' copy stops calling Square a link now that Square is a real connection.
**Requirement:** Settings → **Online payments** ("Pagos en línea") is ONE section under the manual methods with three real tabs — **Square | Stripe | Custom button** ("Botón propio" in Spanish): `role=tablist/tab/tabpanel`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls` / `aria-labelledby`, a roving `tabIndex`, ←/→ (wrapping), Home / End. Each panel is that provider's EXISTING setup, moved, not rebuilt: the Square card (REQ-803), the Stripe card (REQ-212), and the Custom button = the card payment link (REQ-782, moved out of the Payments card's Credit card row, which now points to the tab: "Your card payment link is set in Online payments. Open the Custom button tab") plus the Other payment links card (REQ-630). All three panels are mounted, the inactive ones hidden. Each tab label carries a small "✓ Connected" (Square, Stripe) / "✓ On" (Custom button: a card payment link or any payment link) mark. The tab that opens is the ACTIVE one — the one the customer pays through, in `cardPayWay`'s order: Stripe, else Square, else the Custom button; Square when none is set — decided once both gateways have answered; connecting or disconnecting afterwards never moves the person off the tab they are on. One provider at a time (REQ-803) is said inside the tabs: with Square connected the Stripe tab says "You take cards through Square right now. To use Stripe instead, disconnect Square on the Square tab first — one card account at a time." (and the Square tab says the same of Stripe). Your other payment links below always show as their own buttons." (Stripe likewise). Saving a card payment link from the tab turns Credit card on (the link has always ridden on it — `projectPayMethods` projects it only for an enabled card); Remove clears the link and leaves Credit card as it was.
