## REQ-809 — Focusing a field keeps the modal where it is; clicking a client picks it and closes the list (hotfix)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13, right after REQ-801 shipped: "now when i focus the field, the thing scrolls all the way down, if i focus the field it should stay in view." → "when i click a client, the pick box stays open, no reason for that it should pick and close both fixes."
**Cause, proved in a probe story on main:** (1) the scroll is not the picker's: focusing ANY field of the New invoice modal (the job name too) jumped the modal's scroll container to its bottom (`scrollTop` 0 → 1052 = max) about 60 ms after focus, even with `focus({ preventScroll: true })`, and opening the list without focus did not scroll. The global `MobileViewport` island's `focusin` reveal (there to keep a field and its submit button clear of the iOS keyboard) finds the last button after the field in the same form — "Issue invoice", at the bottom of the modal — and `scrollBy`s the scroll container to show it, on a desktop where there is no keyboard. (2) the list staying open: the box sat inside the `<label>` — a click on a row is a click on the label, which re-focuses the input, and the box opens on focus. Moved out of the label in the probe, the pick closed the list.
**Requirement:** Focusing a field never scrolls the page or modal on its own on a desktop: the keyboard reveal only corrects while the on-screen keyboard overlaps the visual viewport (`innerHeight − visualViewport.height > 2`), checked on every pass so it still kicks in the moment the keyboard opens on a phone. The New invoice client box is a `<div>` with a `<span>` caption, not a `<label>`; clicking a client picks it, the box reads the pick, the list closes, nothing scrolls.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/invoice-client-pick-focus.test.ts` ("REQ-809 …": MobileViewport declares `keyboardOpen` and `correct` returns on it first; the client caption is a `<div>`+`<span>`, no `<label>` around the box) · integration n/a — no server change · e2e `e2e/invoice-client-pick/invoice-client-pick.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-809: …" in a browser with 13 customers: the modal opens at scrollTop 0; clicking the client box leaves it at 0 after 700 ms with the box in view and the list open; "Ann" + click "Ann Lee" → the hidden `customerId` is the customer's id, no list, the box reads "C-001 · Ann Lee", scrollTop still 0; clicking the job name box leaves scrollTop 0).
**Evidence (2026-11-13, Mac host, worktree hotfix-invoice-client-focus off origin/main 24ef9f9c):** RED first — jest "Tests: 2 failed, 2 total"; `shots run e2e/invoice-client-pick` → "✗ … expectation failed: focusing the client box does not scroll the modal — expected 0, got 1052". GREEN — jest unit lane `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → "Test Suites: 516 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 5242 passed, 5243 total"; `shots run e2e/invoice-client-pick e2e/invoice-numbering e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check` → 24 pass · 0 fail (REQ-809 4.5 s; REQ-152/144 — the repeat-visit picker — unchanged). One race hardened on the way: the REQ-206 quote-prefill story read the hidden pick the instant the ledger showed and once lost to the customers fetch (3/3 green alone) — it now waits for the value. `MobileViewport.tsx` was not `deno fmt`-clean on main, so the diff carries its reformat (11 real lines, `git diff -w`). `deno lint`, `deno check` clean on the touched files.
**Prod (2026-11-13, main 404890f1, pushed 18:40Z; carried by the later release 1f7a03b5):** live by 18:47Z — `/login` lists `fresh-island__MobileViewport-CUz4y0Z5.js` (was BhbTPRIJ) and the chunk carries the `innerHeight-…height>2` keyboard guard. On develop as 48cbf48c.

## REQ-810 — Remove an invoice from a batch, and a line from a batch invoice (inline buttons)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-13: "i need a way to remove invoices from a batch and a way to remove a row from batch. i think a button inline would work in each case."
**Decisions:**
- **Remove from batch** — a quiet outlined-danger button in the footer of every DRAFT card on /field/batches ("Remove from batch" / "Quitar del lote"), confirmed inline in the card (no browser dialog; danger-outlined "Remove" + ghost "Cancel", as REQ-163's task delete). The draft is DELETED (InvoiceStore.delete — the same never-sent delete REQ-627 uses), it leaves `batch.invoiceIds`, and its tasks get `invoiceId` cleared, so a later pull of that range bills them. `DELETE /field/batches/:id/invoices/:invoiceId` → the updated BatchView.
- **Remove a line** — an inline "×" on each line of a DRAFT card (accessible name "Remove this line" / "Quitar esta línea"). The line leaves the invoice; `amount`, `description`, `lineItems` and the title + service dates (REQ-703 `batchTitle`, re-derived from the lines left) are recomputed; the line's task is un-invoiced. The overhead line (REQ-788) just leaves. Removing the last TASK line (only an overhead line left, or nothing) removes the whole invoice as above. Removing a visit leaves that visit's overhead line in place (the owner × it too if wanted). `DELETE /field/batches/:id/invoices/:invoiceId/lines/:index?key=<taskId, else the line's description>` → the updated BatchView.
- **Which task a line frees** — `lineItem()` now writes `taskId` (and `overhead: true` on the overhead line). A line pulled before this change is matched to the invoice's own tasks (tasks of the batch range with `invoiceId === invoice`) by date + service + address, the price breaking a tie; only a UNIQUE match frees a task. No match: the line still leaves, nothing is freed, the server logs it. A `taskId` that is not one of the invoice's tasks frees nothing. An old overhead line is known by its label ("Overhead" / "Gastos generales").
- **Guards** — `key` must equal the row's taskId or description, else 409 `stale_line` with `detail.invoice` = the invoice as it is now (the page swaps it in and says so inline); a bad index is the same 409. A sent / paid / void invoice: 409 `not_draft` and no buttons on its card (its own page voids it). Another account's batch, or an invoice not in the batch: 404.
- **Page** — updates in place from the answered batch (card totals, the batch total, the "N invoices" count, the Earlier-batches row, the send ticks); a busy state on the button that runs ("…" on the ×, "Loading…" on Remove) with every other remove disabled meanwhile; errors inline in the card. **A batch left with no invoices** keeps its record but shows "No invoices left in this batch." while open and drops off Earlier batches (the list already showed only batches with invoices).
- Line titles are recomputed in the draft's language (read from its line units, visit/visita), not the owner's current UI language.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/batch-lines/test.ts` ("REQ-810 lineItem …", "REQ-810 taskForItem …" ×2, "REQ-810 withoutLine …" ×3; REQ-173's lineItem expectation now includes `taskId`) · integration `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-810 remove an invoice from a batch …" — deleted, out of invoiceIds, tasks un-invoiced, re-pull bills them, sent 409, another account 404; "REQ-810 remove a line …" — exactly its task freed and the amount drops, overhead line just leaves, stale guard / bad index / no guard 409 with the current invoice, last task line removes the invoice, sent 409; "REQ-810 remove a line of an invoice pulled before …" — old lines without taskId matched to the right task, an unmatched line frees nothing) · e2e `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-810: a batch of two customers — × a line and the totals drop in place; Remove from batch → confirm → the card is gone and the counts update; a sent invoice shows no remove buttons").
**Evidence (2026-11-13, Mac host, worktree batch-remove, branch feat/batch-remove off origin/develop 268e95c9):** RED first — `deno test … batch-lines/test.ts` → 16 TS errors (no `taskForItem` / `withoutLine`, no `taskId` on lineItem), `--no-check` → "FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed"; `deno test … field.int.test.ts --filter REQ-810` → "FAILED | 0 passed | 3 failed" (each "404 Not Found" — no route); `shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check --filter REQ-810` → "✗ REQ-810 … locator.innerText: Timeout 15000ms exceeded" (no batch total hook, no buttons). GREEN — batch-lines + job-span "ok | 26 passed | 0 failed"; field.int.test.ts "ok | 32 passed | 0 failed"; `deno task test:unit` → deno "ok | 1680 passed | 0 failed", jest "Test Suites: 518 passed · Tests: 1 skipped, 5264 passed, 5265 total"; `deno task test:int` → "ok | 1237 passed | 0 failed"; `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check` → 22 pass · 0 fail (REQ-810 3 s; REQ-143 passed in this run). Front-end touched files `deno fmt --check` + `deno lint` + `deno check` clean. Backend touched files `deno check` clean and `deno lint` clean except the pre-existing `any` on field.int.test.ts:34 (same 1 problem at HEAD); e2e file lint has the same 3 pre-existing problems as HEAD. The backend batch files and the two test files were not `deno fmt`-clean before this change (house long lines) and were not reformatted.

## REQ-811 — A checklist a repeat visit can reference, instead of listing the same task types again
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-15: "sometimes recurring has the same thing over and over and over again. So what I would like is to be able to optionally associate A checklist to recurring. That way it's a reference and instead of having a bunch of different line items, I can have a single checklist that's associated and not have to associate multiple line items with the same thing."
**Decisions:**
- **A checklist** is a named, account-owned list of task types with a price each (`Checklist` in `field_checklist`, `/field/checklists`: GET, POST `{name, items}`, PUT `:id`, DELETE `:id`). The name is required, at most 80 characters, and unique in the account (case- and accent-insensitive; 409 `checklist_name_taken`). Its items are parsed exactly as a repeat visit's (by id or by name, found in any case or created); at least one with a price (400).
- **The association is optional and a reference.** A repeat visit may carry `checklistId` (POST / PUT `/field/subscriptions`; `null` clears it; another account's or an unknown one is 404 `checklist_not_found`). A repeat visit needs a checklist OR at least one task type of its own (400 otherwise — and clearing the checklist of a visit with none of its own is the same 400). Its effective services are the checklist's items followed by its own; a type in both takes the visit's OWN price (the per-customer override). The day's generation (REQ-141/170), the worker's and the office's "add a service" pricing (REQ-141/165), the per-visit total (overhead REQ-788, the quote billing line REQ-699) all read the effective list.
- **Editing the checklist changes every repeat visit using it.** Its open future tasks (from today on, not done, not invoiced) are dropped and re-derived on the next read, as a schedule change does (REQ-170). **Deleting a checklist in use is refused**: 409 `checklist_in_use`, `detail.subscriptions` = how many; the page says so with the count. The account wipe (REQ: /me/wipe) sweeps by userId, so the new store needs nothing.
- **The view.** GET `/field/subscriptions` (and the zone's members) answers `checklistId`, `checklistName`, and `items` = the EFFECTIVE list, each checklist-contributed row flagged `fromChecklist: true`. GET `/field/checklists` answers each checklist with `taskTypeName` on its items and `usedBy` (how many repeat visits reference it), sorted by name.
- **Pages.** `/field/checklists` — a new entry in the Field folder ("Checklists" / "Listas de tareas", right after Repeat visits): cards with the items and their prices and "Used by N repeat visits"; New / Edit modal (name + the same task-type combobox and price rows as the repeat-visit form); Delete with inline confirm; the in-use refusal reads inline on the card. `/field/subscriptions` — the form gains a **Checklist** select above the task types (None / each checklist by name / a "Manage checklists" link to the new page); with a checklist picked, the task types block reads "Extra task types" with the hint that the checklist's services are included and may be left empty; the Edit form lists only the visit's own rows. ## REQ-839 — A service catalogue: task types carry a description, can be archived, and are managed on /field/services
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-16: "We also need a place to define line items. Things that can be chosen in line items and things that can be chosen in checklist. So basically one of those tasks becomes an ID, a description, and then the price can be set wherever it's set because it might be different sizes."
**Decisions:** a task type (`TaskType`) gains `description?` (≤ 300), `archived?: true` and `updatedAt`. No price on the type — the price lives where the type is used (a repeat-visit row, a checklist row, a one-off task, an on-site add). `GET /field/task-types?q=` keeps its search and now hides archived types unless `?all=1`; each row carries `usedBy: { subscriptions, checklists }`. `POST /field/task-types { name, description? }` → 201 (409 `task_type_name_taken` on the same name in any case; a name matching an ARCHIVED type restores it, 200). `PUT /field/task-types/:id { name?, description?, archived? }` (409 on a taken name). `DELETE /field/task-types/:id` → 409 `task_type_in_use` with `detail { subscriptions, checklists, tasks }` while a repeat visit, a checklist or a task references it, else gone. Every combobox (repeat visit, checklist, one-off task, office add-service, the worker's `GET /field/worker/task-types`) offers only un-archived types; typing an archived type's name restores it (`findOrCreateTaskType` answers `restored: true`). Page `/field/services` (nav "services" in the Field folder after Checklists): cards with the name, the description, "Used by N repeat visits · M checklists", Edit (name + description), Archive / Restore, Delete when unused; a New modal.

## REQ-840 — Crews: a worker belongs to one crew; a crew has a foreman, its members and the services it does — all on /field/workers
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-16: "The worker belongs to a crew. Inside the worker, each crew has a foreman, and then however many workers. And then that's clearly shown and chosen inside the worker view."
**Decisions:** `Crew { id, userId, name, color, foremanId?, taskTypeIds: string[], coversAll?: true, createdAt, updatedAt }` in KV prefix `field_crew`; `FieldWorker.crewId?` — a worker is in at most ONE crew. `GET /field/crews` (sorted by name; each with `members [{ id, name }]`, `foremanName`, `taskTypeNames`, `zones` = the zones listing it), `POST /field/crews { name, color?, foremanId?, memberIds?, taskTypeIds?, coversAll? }` → 201, `PUT /field/crews/:id` (same fields; `memberIds` REPLACES the membership — a worker named leaves their old crew), `DELETE /field/crews/:id` (409 `crew_covers_zones` with the zone names while a zone lists it; else its members are freed and its open generated tasks from today re-derive). Rules: the name is unique per account in any case (409 `crew_name_taken`); the foreman must be a member (400 `foreman_not_member`); the services must be the account's types (400) and a type claimed by another crew is 409 `task_type_claimed` with `detail { crew }`; an empty `taskTypeIds` means "does any service". `PUT /field/workers/:id { crewId: string | null }` moves one worker. The crew's foreman (`crew.foremanId`) sees and acts on every task of the crew (`canAct`); the legacy account-wide `role: "foreman"` keeps seeing everything. `GET /field/worker/me` and the login answer add `crewName`, and `role` reads "foreman" for a worker who leads their crew. `GET /field/workers` rows carry `crewId`, `crewName`. Page: a Crews panel on /field/workers — cards (colour dot, name, foreman, members, services or "any service", "covers every zone", zones count), New / Edit modal (name, colour, members as checkboxes, foreman select among the picked members, services as checkboxes, the covers-every-zone toggle), Delete with an inline confirm; each worker row shows its crew chip and a Crew select.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/crews/test.ts` ("REQ-840 crewMembers / leadOf / crewNameTaken / claimedBy / canActOn") · integration `field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-840 crews — …") · e2e `field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-840: a crew made on /field/workers …") · jest `field-services-copy.test.ts` covers the `field.crew.*` keys too.

## REQ-841 — A zone is staffed by crews; each service on a visit goes to the crew that does it, so one house can split across crews
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-16: "Let's say I have a mulching crew and a grass cutting crew. They go to some houses that are different to each other, but then there's one house that they have in common. How would that be addressed?" + "We could pick different task IDs or worker crews."
**Decisions (this REPLACES the "one map per crew" idea of the scoping note — once a crew owns a service type, a per-crew map decides nothing; the shared house is decided by the service, and a crew covering the whole town is one flag, not a zone list):** zones stay geographic (REQ-140 unchanged); `Region.crewIds?: string[]` joins the legacy `workerId`. `PUT /field/regions/:id/worker { workerId?: string | null, crewIds?: string[] }` — `crewIds` replaces the zone's crew list (each the account's; 404 otherwise); the zone's open generated tasks from today re-derive. The generator (`staffFor`, pure): for a visit's service, the candidates are the zone's crews in order, then every crew marked `coversAll` (by name) — the first that lists the service's type takes it; else the first that lists no types (does anything); else the zone's legacy worker; else the service is UNCOVERED and reported. A crew with no members is skipped. A crew's task carries `crewId`, `workerId` = the crew's foreman (else its first member by name), `crewIds` = the other members, so every member sees it on /worker and may check it off (REQ-785's rule). `GET /field/tasks/unstaffed` rows gain `taskTypeNames` (the uncovered services; the whole visit when its zone has no staff). Views: a task carries `crewName`; `GET /field/regions` rows carry `crews [{ id, name, color }]`. Assignments page: with crews on the account the zone head shows a crew picker (checkbox chips, saved on change) and the workload strip counts per crew; without crews, today's worker select. Tasks page: the card shows a crew chip; the groups read "Crew · Zone" for a crew's task.
**Tests:** unit `crews/test.ts` ("REQ-841 staffFor — the claiming crew, the catch-all crew, coversAll, order, no members, legacy worker, uncovered") + `tasks/test.ts` ("REQ-841 generateTasks — the shared house splits across the two crews; a grass-only house reaches only the grass crew") · integration `field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-841 the shared house — …") · e2e `field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-841: two crews on one zone …").
**Evidence (2026-11-16, same run as REQ-839):** RED first — `crews/test.ts` staffFor tests → module missing; `tasks/test.ts` "REQ-841 generateTasks — the shared house splits" → `AssertionError: Values are not equal` (one task per type on the zone's single worker, no `crewId`); the int test → `"400 Bad Request"` on PUT /field/regions/:id/worker { crewIds }; the e2e story → `Timeout … waiting for locator('[data-cy=asg-region-crew]')`. GREEN — unit + int inside the lanes above; the e2e story (9.1 s: "1 zones with no crew" → both crew toggles on the zone → the banner gone → /field/tasks with two tasks in two groups, "Ana Ruiz · Zona A" wearing the Grass crew chip holding Lawn cut and "Pedro Gil · Zona A" wearing Mulch crew holding Mulching). Two e2e fixes along the way, both in the stories and the page, not the rule: the zone's crew toggles are controlled inputs that flip once the server has answered (click + wait, not `check()`), and "Move all to…" moved out of the group's `<h3>` so a title's text is the group's name alone (REQ-166's story counts titles by name).

## REQ-842 — Absences: a worker or a crew is out for a date range; their work is covered, deferred or skipped — recorded now or in advance
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-16: "What if so-and-so goes on vacation? How will we be able to schedule it so that if a crew goes on, or somebody goes on vacation or misses a day, we can change the assignment now or in advance."
**Decisions:** `Absence { id, userId, workerId? | crewId?, from, to, disposition: "cover" | "defer" | "skip", coverCrewId?, coverWorkerId?, note?, createdAt }` in KV prefix `field_absence`. `GET /field/absences` (from today on, sorted by `from`, with `name`, `coverName`), `POST /field/absences` → 201 (400: dates not YYYY-MM-DD, `to` before `from`, a range over 366 days, neither or both of worker/crew, `cover` without a target, a target that is the absent crew itself; 404 an unknown worker/crew), `DELETE /field/absences/:id`. Both writes drop the open generated tasks of the affected staff from max(from, today) to `to`, so the next read re-derives them. Generation on a day: an absent worker is left out of their crew's members for that day (the foreman out → the first available member leads); a crew with no available member, a crew-level absence, or an absent legacy solo worker is OUT that day and the disposition applies — cover: the task goes to the cover crew (its lead and members) or the cover worker, with `coverFor` = the absent crew's or worker's id (the view names it `coverForName`); defer: the task is made `deferred` with `deferredTo` = the first later day (≤ 31) the staff is available, and a copy holds that day (same stable-id rule, never overwriting a record already there); skip: the task is made `skipped` (not done, never billed). `POST /field/tasks/reassign { date, fromWorkerId? | fromCrewId?, toCrewId? | toWorkerId? }` moves that day's open, un-invoiced tasks of one worker or crew at once (the unplanned sick day; REQ-166 for a whole day). Page: on /field/workers each worker row and each crew card has "Mark out" → a modal (from, to, what happens: Cover by [crew | worker], Defer, Skip; a note); an "Away" panel lists current and upcoming absences with Remove. Tasks page: a covering task shows "Covering for X"; the day's group header offers "Move all to…".
**Tests:** unit `crews/test.ts` ("REQ-842 availableMembers / isOut / nextAvailableDay") + `tasks/test.ts` ("REQ-842 generateTasks — cover, defer (copy on the next available day), skip; the foreman out → the next member leads") · integration `field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-842 absences — …") · e2e `field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-842: a crew marked out on /field/workers …").
**Evidence (2026-11-16, same run as REQ-839):** RED first — `crews/test.ts` availableMembers/isOut/nextAvailableDay → module missing; `tasks/test.ts` "REQ-842 generateTasks — cover, defer, skip" → `AssertionError` (no `coverFor`, no deferred copy); the int test → `"404 Not Found"` on POST /field/absences; the e2e story → `Timeout … waiting for locator('[data-cy=away-empty]')`. GREEN — unit + int inside the lanes above (the int test proves cover / defer-with-copy / skip / the foreman out → the next member leads / a member's absence changing only the lead / 400 on bad ranges / `POST /field/tasks/reassign` moving a whole day); the e2e story (23.1 s: Ana's task today → "Grass crew is out" from the crew card, covered by the Mulch crew, note Vacation → the Away row "covered by Mulch crew" → /field/tasks on Pedro Gil with "Covering for Grass crew" → Remove → Ana's again, no cover line). ## REQ-880 — Reduced motion must settle the landing's looping animations, not strobe them (the shaking hero phone)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-16: "For some reason, the phone is shaking on the landing page."
**Cause (proved):** macOS Reduce Motion is on, so Chrome matches `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. `landing.css` line 265 handled it with the common shortcut `*, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important }` — but left `animation-iteration-count` at each element's own `infinite`. `phoneFloat` (6s, ±10px), `docFloat` and `blobDrift` therefore looped once every 0.01ms forever, and every rendered frame sampled a random phase: the hero phone jumped between translateY(0) and translateY(-10px) frame after frame. Measured in the installed Google Chrome (GPU, 1280×900), frame-to-frame mean absolute pixel difference over the phone region, 25 fps for 6 s: motion on 1.33 (0 of 149 frames over 5); Reduce Motion on 15.16 (130 of 149 frames over 5). `getBoundingClientRect` could not see it (the main thread reads a constant 245.09), which is why the first geometry probes were clean — the compositor thread does the strobing. The same shortcut block is in `dashboard.css`, `assistant.css` and `assistant-page.css` (×2).
**Decision:** every blanket reduced-motion block also sets `animation-iteration-count: 1 !important`, so a shortened animation runs once and rests at its end state. Targeted one-shot shortenings (motion.css view transitions, paycard entrances) are left alone. Motion on is unchanged: the phone still floats `infinite`.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/landing-reduced-motion.test.ts` (every static sheet's blanket `*` reduced-motion block that shortens `animation-duration` also caps the iteration count; the hero float stays infinite with motion on) · integration n/a — a static stylesheet, no server logic · e2e `e2e/landing-reduced-motion/landing-reduced-motion.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-880: under reduced motion the hero phone, document and blobs run once and settle; with motion on the phone floats" — `animationIterationCount === "1"` and every `getAnimations()` entry `finished` under reduce; `phoneFloat … infinite` without).
**Evidence (2026-11-16):** RED first — unit: `Expected pattern: /animation-iteration-count\s*:\s*1\s*!important/ … Received: "*, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; …"`; e2e: `expectation failed: hs-blob hs-blob--mint: reduced motion runs the animation once — expected "1", got "infinite"`. GREEN — unit `Tests: 4 passed, 4 total`; e2e `✓ REQ-880 … · 2.2s · 1 pass · 0 fail`. Visual proof after the fix, same Chrome recording with Reduce Motion: phone-region diff/frame mean 0.05, max 0.43, 0 of 149 frames over 5 (the phone sits still).

## REQ-884 — Hires: intake, roster, detail, the signing link by text + email, expiry and re-issue, offboarding
**Source:** the prototype's Roster, New-hire intake, Hire detail and Send-link modal.
**Requirement:** (a) `POST /hr/hires { firstName, lastName, email, phone, departmentId, startDate }` → 201: the packet is minted from the department's docIds at that moment and frozen onto the hire (a later department edit never changes an in-flight packet), the department's systemIds are snapshotted, a random token is minted with `tokenExpiresAt = now + settings.linkExpiryDays`, status `invited`; with `settings.autoSend` on, the link is sent at once. 400 `name_required` without a first name, 400 `department_required` / 404 `department_not_found`, 400 `phone_invalid` when the phone is not a usable number. (b) `POST /hr/hires/:id/send` texts and emails the link again (SMS "Hey {first}! 🐋 Welcome to {company}. Tap to sign your new-hire paperwork before Day 1: {url}"; email with the Open signing link button); on an `expired` hire the token is rotated (the old link is dead) and the hire returns to `invited`. `mail.sentAt` records it. (c) `GET /hr/hires` (sortable by the page: status asc floats unfinished hires — expired, opened, invited, signing — above signed, provisioning, active; secondary by start date) and `GET /hr/hires/:id` (profile, pipeline, packet with per-doc done/proof, provisioning results); both apply lazy expiry: an `invited|opened|signing` hire whose `tokenExpiresAt` has passed reads back `expired`. (d) `POST /hr/hires/:id/offboard` → status `offboarded`, with the provisioning teardown of REQ-888. (e) Every hire endpoint is the calling account's: another account's hire is 404. (f) Pages: /hr/hires (search box, sortable table — New hire, Department, Start, Progress, Status, Resend/Re-issue/View; empty state with "Add your first hire"), /hr/hires/new (the intake form with the department picker and the live "Packet they'll sign" preview; Create & send link opens the send-link modal showing the real link and the text), /hr/hires/:id (profile card, the pipeline Invited → Link opened → Signing in progress → All documents signed → Accounts provisioned, the welcome-email delivered/opened line, the signing link with Copy + Open, the text and email previews, the Accounts & systems cards, the Signing packet table whose rows open the proof — REQ-885).

## REQ-885 — Phone signing by token: open, acknowledge or sign each document, finish MONSTERIZED; a proof per document
**Source:** the prototype's phone flow (Step n of N, the document, the "I have read and understand" box, printed name + the signature pad, Continue / Sign & finish, the completion screen) and the detail's "View a signature" modal.
**Requirement:** (a) `GET /hr/sign/:token` (public) → the packet for the phone: the hire's first name only, the department name, the company name, the documents in packet order (label, category, kind, content HTML or the PDF's field list, creds flag, done) — and flips `invited` → `opened` the first time (`mail.openedAt`). An unknown token is 404 `link_not_found`; a lapsed one is 410 `link_expired`; a finished packet still opens (read-only, all done). (b) `POST /hr/sign/:token/docs/:docId { printedName, consent: true, signaturePng? }` → 201 with the proof: `consent` is required (400 `consent_required`); a `sign` document needs a `printedName` and a `signaturePng` (400 `signature_required`); an `ack` document needs only the consent. The proof records who (printed name), the document and its version at signing, the kind, the signature image, the consent text, the IP and user agent, and the time. The packet doc is marked done; status becomes `signing`, and `signed` (with `signedAt`) once every doc is done — then REQ-889's notify-on-completion and auto-provision run. A doc already done is 409 `already_signed`. (c) `GET /hr/sign/:token/pdf/:docId` streams an imported PDF to the phone. (d) `GET /hr/hires/:id/proofs/:docId` (admin) → the proof, or 404 `not_signed_yet`. (e) The page /sign/:token renders phone-first: the progress bar and Step n of N, the eyebrow + title, the scrollable document, the credentials box when the document carries them, the acknowledgment checkbox, for a signature document the printed name and a draw-with-your-finger pad with Clear, Continue disabled until acknowledged (and signed); the last step reads Sign & finish and lands on "You're officially MONSTERIZED!". (f) In hire detail, clicking a packet row opens the proof modal: the handwritten mark (the image), printed name, date signed, the audit line (device, IP, token) — or "Not signed yet".
**Tests:** unit `onboarding/test.ts` ("REQ-885 packetProgress / allDone") · integration `hr.int.test.ts` ("REQ-885 …") · e2e `hr-onboarding.e2e.test.ts` (the hire signs on /sign/:token in the browser).
**Evidence (2026-11-16, same run as REQ-883):** inside the int test — first name only on the phone, `opened` on first GET, 400 `consent_required` / `signature_required`, 409 `already_signed`, the proof's ip/user-agent/consent text, status signing → signed + `signedAt`. The e2e story's step 5 (no session: "Hi Dani!", Step 1 of 2 refused without the box, acknowledged, Step 2 of 2 printed name + a drawn signature → "You're officially MONSTERIZED!") and step 6 (the proof modal: printed name "Dani Reyes", an `<img>` of the drawn signature, "Signed on mobile …").

## REQ-888 — Systems and provisioning: the connected-systems registry; MONSTERIZED — per-system results, retry, manual completion, teardown on offboarding
**Source:** the prototype's Systems tab (connected systems + the System integrator catalog) and the detail's "Build in CRM & create accounts" moment; spec §6 (partial success, per-system results, manual retry, no rollback) and M6 offboarding.
**Requirement:** (a) `GET /hr/systems` → `{ systems, catalog }` (the account's attached systems; the catalog entries not yet attached: Quickbase CRM, Readymode, Five9, Paychex, Email (Google), DocuSign, Salesforce, Slack, ADP, Twilio, Okta); `POST /hr/systems { key }` attaches a catalog entry as `connected` (or `{ name, kind, desc }` a custom one; 409 `system_exists`); `PUT /hr/systems/:id { status?: connected|available, webhookUrl?: string|null }`; `DELETE /hr/systems/:id` removes it and drops it from every department. (b) An arm is how a system gets built: a system with a `webhookUrl` is provisioned by POSTing `{ event: "hire.provision", hire, system }` to it — a 2xx is `ok`, anything else `fault` with the reason; a system without one is `manual` — the admin marks it `done` from hire detail. (c) `POST /hr/hires/:id/provision { systemId? }` runs every arm in the plan (the department's current connected systems, else the hire's snapshot) or re-runs one; each arm's result `{ systemId, name, state, detail, at }` is kept on the hire; status is `provisioning` while any arm is `fault` or `manual`, `active` (with `activeAt`) once every arm is `ok|done` — or at once when the plan is empty; 409 `not_signed` before the packet is complete. `POST /hr/hires/:id/provision/:systemId/done` marks a manual arm done. (d) `POST /hr/hires/:id/offboard` tears down in reverse: every `ok|done` arm with a webhook gets `{ event: "hire.offboard", … }` → `torn_down` / `teardown_fault`; manual arms become `torn_down` with the note; status `offboarded`. (e) Pages: /hr/systems (Connected systems cards with Connect/Disconnect and a webhook URL field, the System integrator catalog with Attach); hire detail shows a card per arm (Created / creating… / Queued / Waiting on signatures / Manual — Mark done / Failed — Retry) and, once active, "{first} is officially MONSTERIZED!".
**Tests:** unit `onboarding/test.ts` ("REQ-888 aggregateProvisioning") · integration `hr.int.test.ts` ("REQ-888 …" — a local webhook server answering 200 then 500; manual arms; retry; mark done; offboard) · e2e `hr-onboarding.e2e.test.ts`.
**Evidence (2026-11-16, same run as REQ-883):** inside the int test — the catalog minus the attached, 409 `system_exists`, the webhook URL validated, a local `Deno.serve` webhook answering 200 ×2 → `ok` arms and a no-webhook system → `manual`; 500 → `fault` → Retry → `ok`; `…/provision/:systemId/done` → `done` → the hire `active` with `activeAt`; offboard → `torn_down` / `teardown_fault`, status `offboarded`. The e2e story's steps 2 and 6 (Attach Quickbase CRM from the catalog; after the packet completes the hire is Provisioning with the Quickbase arm MANUAL STEP → Mark done → Active, "Created (manual)").

## REQ-910 — A sent invoice's Edit can add and remove lines, add "n % of the lines above" as an Overhead line, and says the customer still sees the published version until Publish
**Source:** Johanna (A2Z), 2026-11-16, WhatsApp video 3 + the two invoice photos: "Este invoice le faltó agregar el 10% y no tenemos la opción de editarlo" — she expects to add the charge and the customer's copy to follow, "como en QuickBooks".
**Found (develop `6fc0bd4c`):** the detail panel's Edit form (`InvoicesPage.tsx`, `invoice-edit-form`) lists the existing lines (description, qty, price) with no add, no remove and no percentage helper — and renders no lines block at all for a one-amount invoice; `EditableLine` drops the REQ-788 `overhead` flag so a save would strip it from the batch's line; after Save on a sent invoice the panel shows the pending bar but says nothing about what the customer sees. The design (agreed 2026-11-16): the surcharge is a plain line item flagged `overhead: true`, priced when added — no stored percentage, no dynamic recomputation (the batch's own overhead is REQ-788).
**Requirement:** (1) The Edit form's lines block always renders (`invoice-edit-lines`): each line has description/qty/price, an Overhead checkbox (`invoice-edit-line-overhead-i`) and Remove (`invoice-edit-line-remove-i`); "+ Add line item" (`invoice-edit-line-add`) appends an empty line. (2) A number box (`invoice-edit-pct`, default 10) and "Add as Overhead line" (`invoice-edit-pct-add`) append a line named Overhead / Gastos generales priced at `percentOfLinesCents(lines, pct)` (round(subtotal × pct / 100), 0 for ≤ 0 / NaN / no lines), flagged overhead; the amount follows the lines. (3) Save sends every line's `overhead` flag; on an issued invoice the save keeps REQ-201's pending revision and the panel says "Saved. {customer} still sees the published version until you publish the revision." (`invoice-published-note`); Publish (quiet or notify) makes Version n+1 and the customer's page shows the new total.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/invoice-edit-lines.test.ts` ("REQ-910 …": `percentOfLinesCents`; the form's add/remove/pct/overhead controls; `lineItemsOf` keeps the flag and the save emits it; the saved note; both languages) · integration `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/revisions-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-910: an added Overhead line on a sent invoice is pending until published …": PUT 6 lines on a 5-line sent invoice → live amount unchanged, `pendingRevision` 6 lines with the flag, public $350; publish → version 2, $385, public $385) · e2e `e2e/req-910-invoice-add-line/req-910-invoice-add-line.e2e.test.ts` (Edit a sent 5 × $70 invoice → 5 removable lines + add → 10 % → a sixth "Overhead" line at $35 checked → Save → pending bar + the note, public still $350 → Publish quietly → "Version 2" → /i/:id reads $385.00).
**Evidence (2026-11-16, same run as REQ-909):** RED — the unit file in the 18 failures above; the story on the unfixed code → `expectation failed: every line can be removed — expected 5, got 0`. The Deno case passes on the unfixed backend too (the backend already took `overhead` on a line and queued an issued invoice's PUT as the pending revision — REQ-788/REQ-201; the case is the regression guard for the flow the new UI drives, not a backend change). ## REQ-824 — The stage shows the customer's hover and focus: the field they type in looks focused, what their mouse is over lights up, and the search box's × shows (demo-loop cycle dm1, issue m2)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm1 (run r83b6287b, demo-report.md), issue m2 "Hover and focus styling are not mirrored": demo 2 "focused: green border on the customer, unfocused pink fill on the stage"; the top search's native "×" shows only on the customer (every other child identical); calendar day "19" and the "2–3 days" chip light up under her mouse only on the customer (fleet-1 stdout:39, :67); demo 3 the /welcome business-name focus ring (fleet-2 stdout:81); demo 5 the composer and the signing page's typed-name field (fleet-4 stdout:52-55). RCA at cbcae62d: analyst FEATURE_GAP, skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_POLISH ("the stage misstates which field is active").
**Cause (RCA):** the REQ-242 mirror copies the DOM: nodes, attributes, values, checked state, scrolls and canvases. `:hover`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible` and `:focus-within` are browser state, never attributes, so they never crossed. The recorder (`front-end/lib/demo-mode/mirror-record.ts`, its listeners at :727-736) had no focus or hover tracking. The stage's replica can never be in those states itself: its frame is `inert`, `tabindex=-1` and `pointer-events:none` (REQ-293, `front-end/islands/DemoStage.tsx`:1806-1815). Chromium shows a search box's native cancel button only while the box is focused or hovered (its UA rule; measured here: 80 dark pixels idle, 127 focused or hovered, on both sides of a real frame), so the stage's copy never showed it.
**Requirement:**
- The recorder marks what the customer's browser says matches, with `Element.matches`, as REQ-638 marks an open select: `data-mirror-focus` on the element that matches `:focus` (value `visible` when it also matches `:focus-visible`, else empty), `data-mirror-focus-within` on every element that matches `:focus-within`, and `data-mirror-hover` on every element that matches `:hover` (the element under the pointer and its ancestors). Only elements that cross get a mark. A snapshot carries the marks, and they move, appear or go within one frame of a focus change, a pointer crossing or a key. The page's own attributes with these names never cross, and the customer's own DOM is never touched.
- No hover marks when the customer's pointer cannot hover (`(hover: none)`, a phone). There a tap leaves a sticky `:hover`, which the page's `@media (hover: hover)` rules ignore on the customer's screen but would apply on the presenter's desktop stage.
- The stage rewrites the customer's style rules in place to read the marks. In every same-origin sheet of its frame (links, `<style>`s, the REQ-547 bridge copies, `@media`/`@supports`/`@layer` blocks, nested rules, imports), `:hover` becomes `[data-mirror-hover]`, `:focus` becomes `[data-mirror-focus]`, `:focus-visible` becomes `[data-mirror-focus="visible"]` and `:focus-within` becomes `[data-mirror-focus-within]`. Specificity and cascade position stay the customer's, and a `:not(:hover)` rule stops matching on the stage when the customer hovers. A pseudo-class after a pseudo-element (`::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover`), escaped colons and attribute values stay as they are.
- The UA's own state rules that no page sheet carries are the stage's own: an adopted sheet in a cascade layer, so every rule of the page beats it, as a UA rule is beaten. It draws Chromium's focus ring on `[data-mirror-focus="visible"]` (`outline: auto 1px -webkit-focus-ring-color`, offset 1px on links and 2px on checkboxes and radios) and shows a search box's × while it is marked focused or hovered.
- Not mirrored, by design: `:active` (a press lasts a moment), theme-painted native controls (a default button's hover is painted by the platform, not a CSS rule), and a touch customer's sticky hover (above).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-mirror-focus-hover.test.ts` ("REQ-824 …": the selector rewrite, the in-place rules walk, the recorder's marks on the fake DOM (record → JSON → replay) for focus, focus-visible, focus-within, hover, moves, blur, a late snapshot, a fresh subtree, the page's own attributes, skipped subtrees, no hover on a `(hover: none)` device, the customer's DOM untouched), and the replay's in-place restate and UA sheet. The fake DOM gains `matches()` for the four pseudo-classes and `activeElement` (`jest/unit/support/fake-dom.ts`). `jest/unit/demo-replay-still.test.ts` (REQ-547) is amended: once a page's own links are in, no bridge copy is left, and only the stage's REQ-824 UA sheet stays adopted. · integration n/a — the mirror runs browser to browser and the backend only relays opaque chunks. The marks cross as ordinary attributes and `a` ops, already pinned by REQ-242's relay tests. · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-mirror-focus-hover.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-824 … the real recorder and replayer …": in real Chromium, with MIRROR_SRCDOC's inert sandboxed frame and the app's own `assistant-page.css`, the stage's composer computes the customer's border and background when idle, when focused (green border, white) and when blurred again; the hovered `.dur__chip` gets the same border; a search box focused with a value shows the × (the same ink on both sides); a keyboard-focused button draws the same focus ring and a mouse-focused one draws none, on both sides. "REQ-824 … during a demo …": a full two-browser demo, where the customer's click into the real /assistant composer gives the stage frame's composer the customer's focused border and background within 1.5 s).
**Evidence (2026-11-15, branch fix/cdm1-mirror-focus-hover off demo-fixes cbcae62d):** Probes first, in Chromium 156 (Playwright's headless shell). The search box's × counted 80 dark pixels idle and 127 when focused or hovered on the customer's side, 80 on the inert stage copy, and 127 with MIRROR_UA_CSS adopted and the mark set. `CSSStyleRule.selectorText` can be set on the sandboxed srcdoc frame's same-origin sheets, and an invalid value leaves the selector unchanged. A keyboard-focused button and the stage's marked button gave byte-identical screenshots. The one pass is the guard "the marks never touch the customer's own page". The failures were `Expected ".composer__inner[data-mirror-focus-within]" Received ".composer__inner:focus-within"`; no marks on the stage, while the page's own `data-mirror-*` crossed ("- Expected - 1 + Received + 3"); no frame after focusin, pointerover, keydown or focusout ("Expected: true, Received: false"); and an empty MIRROR_UA_CSS. `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-mirror-focus-hover.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` failed both stories with the same values: "✗ … real recorder and replayer … REQ-824: focused, the stage's composer computes the customer's green border and white fill within 1 s — expected "rgb(81, 152, 67) | rgb(81, 152, 67) | rgb(255, 255, 255)", got "rgba(100, 69, 54, 0.16) | rgba(100, 69, 54, 0.16) | rgb(242, 235, 232)"", and the same pair for "✗ … during a demo …". ## REQ-823 — A same-tab navigation is never shown as "the other tab", and a customer who signs out is said to have signed out — the stage never goes Live on another tab of the dead session (demo-loop cycle dm1, issues m8 + M2)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm1 (run r83b6287b), Demo-mode-only test, five testers. Issue `m8` — "Stage banner says 'Now showing …'s other tab' after a navigation in the same tab" (fleet-3: after a second tab existed, every `goto` in tab 1 — /customers, '/'→/dashboard, /i/abc123 — showed "Now showing +15125550403's other tab (…)"). Issue `M2` — "After the customer logs out with a second tab open, the stage shows 'Live' on the background /quotes tab" (fleet-3: "Loading their next page… 3/4/5 s behind", then Live on tab 1's stale /quotes). RCA (analyst + skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_POLISH, at demo-fixes `cbcae62d`).
**Cause (RCA):** (m8) an address-bar navigation, `page.goto` or the browser's reload button fires no Navigation API `navigate`, so the leaving page says "closing" (leave-hint.ts). `transport.ts` `tabLeft` held the followed browser tab only for "navigating"; on "closing" with another tab connected, `follow()` switched to that tab at once, then back when the same tab's new page claimed ~1 s later. DemoStage's `followTabs` counted A→B→A as a tab switch and raised the "Now showing {name}'s other tab" banner for the stage's own unrequested detour. (M2) DashSidebar's `logout()` fires `pm:logout`, POSTs /api/auth/logout and sets `location.href = "/"`. Demo mode never heard of it: the overlay ignored `pm:logout`, the leave went out as "navigating" (a 5 s "Loading their next page…" for a page that never comes, because "/" has no session and mounts no overlay), and `follow()` then fell back to the customer's other tab. That tab's session was already dead, but the backend `Logout` only deletes the session record and leaves its demo sockets open. In headless every tab reports visible, so the background tab still had a link. In a real browser the same thing happens with two visible windows.
**Requirement:**
1. (m8) When the followed browser tab's page goes "closing" or says nothing while another of the customer's tabs is connected, the stage keeps following that browser tab ("between") for SILENT_GRACE_MS. A page with the same tab key that claims inside that window is the same tab: the stage goes back to it and never offers, syncs or names (onPeerOnline) the other tab. A real close falls over to the other tab once the grace ends, or at once when the customer really uses the other tab (a newer claim). With no other tab, a closing page is still "waiting" at once (REQ-391 m21).
2. (m8) The stage's tab tracker (`followTabs`) weighs a follow against the browser tab whose page was last ON SHOW (`shown()`, from the replay's onShown). A→B→A, where B's page never showed, is not a tab switch: no "Now showing {name}'s other tab" banner, and a pending tab notice is dropped. A→B shown→A is still a switch and is said.
3. (M2) A page can say it is going because the customer signed out: LeaveWhy `"signout"` on the wire (`leaving`, and the departure's `why`). After the app's sign-out event (`pm:logout`) the leave hint says "signout". The customer's overlay hears `pm:logout` (`onSignout`, signout-signal.ts), sends `leaving("signout")`, closes its link before the redirect and drops the demo. It tells the browser's other tabs on a BroadcastChannel so their overlays do the same.
4. (M2) A stage whose followed tab signs out says so at once: "waiting" (never "between"), with "{name} signed out" / "{name} cerró sesión" in the pill and on the waiting banner. It falls back to none of the customer's other tabs (the same dead session). A tab claimed since the sign-out (her phone, used) or a page of that browser tab signed in again is followed, and the words go back to normal. No page clock is started.
5. (M2) Backend: a customer (viewer) demo socket closes when its sign-in session is gone (logout, account closed, wipe). The demo hub announces the departure with why "signout". A dead session can never rejoin the hub (the socket upgrade is refused). Another session of the same customer (another device) stays.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-stage-tab-leave-follow.test.ts` ("REQ-823 …": transport closing/silent hold with another tab, same key back within SILENT_GRACE_MS → no onPeerOnline to the other tab, real close falls over after the grace, a newer claim during the hold, the only tab closing still waits at once; signout → waiting at once, no fallback even long after, onSignedOut, no onPageGone, a claim since / the same tab signed in again is followed; followTabs A→B unseen→A no switch, A→B shown→A a switch, late keys; the wire parses `signout`; leave hint says "signout" after `pm:logout`; signout-signal hears this tab and the browser's other tabs; overlay and stage wiring; en + es words) · amended REQ-436 test in `jest/unit/demo-stage-tab-follow.test.ts` (a keyed followed tab that says it is closing with /q open falls over after SILENT_GRACE_MS, not at once) · integration `backend/src/demo-mode/entrypoints/demo-mode-controller/int.test.ts` ("REQ-823 …": `leaving signout` crosses on the departure; POST /api/auth/logout closes every demo socket of that session with why signout, her other session stays, the dead session's socket is refused) · e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-tab-leave.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-823 m8 …": two customer tabs, `goto` in the followed tab, never the "other tab" banner and the stage stays on that tab; "REQ-823 M2 …": sign out from the sidebar with a second tab open, the stage says "Ana Torres signed out" and never goes Live on the other tab).
**Evidence (2026-11-15, Mac host, worktree fix-cdm1-stage-tab-leave-follow, branch fix/cdm1-stage-tab-leave-follow off origin/demo-fixes cbcae62d):** RED first. jest `npx jest unit/demo-stage-tab-leave-follow.test.ts unit/demo-stage-tab-follow.test.ts --selectProjects unit` gave "Tests: 19 failed, 17 passed, 36 total". The failures: the immediate fallback (`followed.length` "Expected: 3 Received: 4", the onPeerOnline("q1") behind the banner, in the amended REQ-436 test too); "t.shown is not a function"; `leaving` signout parsed to `null`; the hint said "closing" after pm:logout; "Cannot find module '../../front-end/lib/demo-mode/signout-signal'"; the overlay and stage wiring absent; `demoMode.signedOut` undefined. Backend `deno test -A --unstable-kv …/demo-mode-controller/int.test.ts --filter REQ-823`: type check "TS2322 Type '"signout"' is not assignable to type 'LeaveWhy | undefined'". With `--no-check`: "FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed" — the departure had no `why: "signout"`, and "timed out waiting for a laptop tab goes (1 of 2)" (logout left her sockets open). e2e on demo-fixes (a detached worktree at cbcae62d with the story copied in), `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-tab-leave.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check`: "0 pass · 2 fail". m8: "expectation failed: m8: the stage never said it shows the other tab". The stage put tab 2 on ("640 × 760", /settings, "Now showing Ana Torres's other tab (/settings)"), then "Now showing Ana Torres's other tab (/customers)" after a `goto` in tab 1. M2: "timed out: M2: the stage says Ana Torres signed out". The stage counted "Loading their next page… 2 s … 7 s behind", then "Waiting for Ana Torres's app…". An earlier run of the same story went "Live" on "640 × 760" /quotes after "Loading their next page… 5 s behind": the tester's own M2. GREEN. jest: the two files "Tests: 36 passed". The whole unit project (`npx jest --selectProjects unit`) gave "Test Suites: 520 passed, 520 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 5290 passed, 5291 total". The 9 neighbouring demo suites gave "Tests: 222 passed". Backend: REQ-823 "ok" ×2. `deno test -A --unstable-kv --parallel src/demo-mode/ src/users/domain/coordinators/logout/ src/users/domain/data/session-store/ src/users/domain/coordinators/require-user/` gave "ok | 75 passed | 0 failed". e2e: `SHOTS_JOBS=1 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=~/Library/Caches/deno/npm/registry.npmjs.org/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-tab-leave.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` gave "2 pass · 0 fail" three runs in a row (M2 24–26 s, m8 32–48 s). The neighbouring `e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-live.e2e.test.ts` (REQ-391's closing path) gave "1 pass". ## REQ-822 — The stage's copy of the customer's pill shows End's question (demo-loop cycle dm1, m1)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none" — demo-loop cycle dm1 (run r83b6287b), issue **m1** "Stage pill ghost does not copy customer's pill state (End question open; folded vs expanded on a second demo)", BUG_CONTRADICTION of REQ-540 ("the ghost draws the whole pill, word for word"). Demo agents saw, while the customer's pill asked "End the demo with Alex? Yes, end it / Keep going", the stage's ghost read "Demo mode / Alex is guiding you / Connected / End demo / …"; and on demo 3's second demo the ghost showed the whole pill while the customer had the folded mini-pill.
**Cause (RCA at cbcae62d, analyst + skeptic UPHELD):** `PillFace` (shared/demo-mode/protocol.ts) had no field for "End is asking"; the overlay's `asking` state (DemoModeOverlay.tsx) never went into `faceRef` / `sendPill`, so `ghostWords` (shared/demo-mode/pill.ts) always drew End and only the `clipped` "…" leaked through; `place()` returned early while the question was up. Introduced by 1fab11dd (REQ-540) and 07947c3d (REQ-637). Second-demo part (unproven in the RCA): after a follow switch the stage shows its own guess (`pillFaceAwaiting`, untucked) while the new page's real pill waits in the REQ-636 hold (`createPillSync`) for its frame.
**Requirement:** The customer's pill face carries `asking` and the question with both answers in the customer's words (`ask`, `yes`, `no`; parsed and length-capped). While End asks, the stage's ghost draws that question in End's place with "Yes, end it" / "Keep going" as disabled chips (no End chip; an older page without the words: "Wants to end the demo" in the stage's words), and the stage's own pill says "{name} is deciding whether to end the demo" (es: "{name} está decidiendo si terminar la demo") wherever the ghost is. Keep going puts End back on both. `place()` still sends the face while the question freezes the pill. A face whose only change from the one on the stage is End's question (plus the `clipped` it causes) shows at once, not held for a frame; right after a follow switch the new page's first face replaces the stage's guess at once when it differs from it only in status / label / tucked (the folded mini-pill shows, not the guessed whole pill). A tuck, opened pill or new words otherwise still wait for their frame (REQ-636). A new page's awaiting face is never asking.
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-stage-pill-asking.test.ts` ("REQ-822 …": the wire keeps asking/ask/yes/no and drops junk; ghostWords with the question, the fallback words, not asking, ended; pillFaceAwaiting drops the question; pillShowsAtOnce — the question up/down at once, a tuck or new words held; the second-demo sequence through createPillSync (follow switch → guess → the new page's folded face shows at once → a later tuck waits for its frame); an instant pill supersedes what was held; the islands' wiring; the lang keys in en and es).
- integration: n/a — no server change: the pill face rides the existing peer link untouched by the backend (the demo-hub/demo-role deno tests still pass).
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-ghost-asking.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-822 …": a super admin opens a demo on a 1280×800 customer; the customer taps End (or the mini-pill's ×); their pill asks "End the demo with Alex?"; the stage's ghost shows that question, "Yes, end it" (aria-disabled) and "Keep going", and no End chip; the stage's pill says "Ana Torres is deciding whether to end the demo"; Escape (Keep going) puts End back on the ghost and the badge goes).
**Evidence (2026-11-15, Mac host, worktree fix-cdm1-stage-pill-asking-face off origin/demo-fixes cbcae62d):**
- RED first. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-stage-pill-asking` → "Tests: 13 failed, 1 passed, 14 total" (`pillShowsAtOnce is not a function`, no asking on the wire, no lang keys, no wiring). The e2e on the base source → "✗ REQ-822 … timed out: the stage's ghost draws the question — {"ask":null,…,"end":true,"text":"Demo modeAlex is guiding youConnectedEnd demo…"}" — the reported ghost, word for word.
- GREEN. The same jest run → "Tests: 14 passed, 14 total"; `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo` → "Test Suites: 64 passed · Tests: 779 passed"; `deno test` demo-hub + demo-role → "ok | 28 passed | 0 failed"; `SHOTS_JOBS=1 shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-ghost-asking.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` → "✓ REQ-822 … 49.6s — 1 pass · 0 fail"; with the neighbour `e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-folded-label.e2e.test.ts` → "✓ REQ-637 …".
- `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on the touched islands and shared modules; `deno fmt` on every touched file (all were clean at the base) and the new tests.
**Known limits:** on a 1280 px customer window the widened asking pill runs past the window's right edge (the "Keep going" button is off-screen, so the e2e answers with Escape) — the customer-side placement while asking is not changed here. The second-demo folded/expanded mismatch was not reproduced live; the fix covers the RCA's candidate path (follow-switch guess + hold) and is proved at unit level only.

## REQ-818 — The demo pill's last resort is the spot with the fewest controls, never the sidebar's Log out; a peeked pill slides off a control (demo-loop cycle dm1, m5)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none" — demo-loop cycle dm1 (run r83b6287b), issue m5 "Demo pill covers page content (sidebar Log out, phone headings, footer) and changes corners between pages". Demo 3: "demo-pill at 0,760 (96×32) covers the sidebar "Log out" button (16,742, 196×42)" on desktop /customers at 1280×800. RCA (analyst + skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_CONTRADICTION, at cbcae62d): `placePill`'s last line `return fold(tab() ?? tabs[0])` (and the same in its dialog branch) put the mini-pill on tabs[0] — the bottom-left edge, a spot already known to hold a control (at 1280×800 that is exactly `.nav-item--logout`) — which breaks REQ-781's "never over a control"; and the pill shown out of its mini-pill (the peek) was placed flush with the tab's edge with no controls check (the footer's "Términos y condiciones de SMS" link).
**Requirement:** When no spot is free of controls, the customer's pill goes to the mini-pill or whole spot with the FEWEST controls under it (a tie keeps REQ-781's order, mini-pill first) — under a dialog with nowhere to dock, the mini-pill spot with the fewest. The mini-pill's spots also run along the bottom edge (a tab's width and a gap at a time, after both side edges), so a page with controls up both edges still has a place; a tab there is fully round. The whole pill shown out of a mini-pill sits flush with the tab's edge (centred over a bottom-edge tab) unless a control is under it there: then it slides along the tab's row to the place with the fewest controls, nearest that edge first, always inside the window (measured only while it is out). Covering text and changing corners between pages stay allowed (REQ-781).
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-pill-control-fallback.test.ts` ("REQ-818 …": tabs[0] at 1280×800 is 0,760 over Log out; bottom-edge tab spots, all inside the window, side edges first; every spot holds a control except one partly clear tab spot → that spot, never tabs[0]; a partly clear whole spot → the whole pill there; a dialog with nowhere to dock → the tab spot with the fewest; a /customers-like layout (Log out, sidebar, right rail) → the mini-pill lands along the bottom off Log out; peekBox flush when clear, a peek box over a footer link slides off it inside the window, the fewest along a crowded row; the overlay places the peek through `peekBox` with `countControls`).

## REQ-821 — A first join shows the customer's whole pill ("{name} is guiding you" with End) for a few seconds before it yields (demo-loop cycle dm1, issue m9)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm1 (run r83b6287b), issue m9: on a dense page (/assistant, /customers) the customer's pill opened already folded to its "Demo ×" mini-pill, so the REQ-153 amendment's join line was never seen. RCA (analyst + skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_CONTRADICTION, at cbcae62d): the placement effect runs `place()` as soon as the pill shows and every 700 ms; with page content under every spot `placePill` folds (REQ-545/637/781); `yieldsRef.current = !(compact && open) && !fresh` kept the whole pill only for a RESTART (REQ-298's `fresh`), never for a first join. requirements.md contradicted itself: REQ-153 AMENDMENT ("it joins: the pill says \"{name} is guiding you\" with End") vs REQ-545/637/781 (fold whenever content is under it).
**Requirement (reconciles REQ-153's amendment with REQ-545/637/781):** a first join gets the grace a restart gets. When a demo id first reaches the customer's tab, the WHOLE pill (status, "{name} is guiding you", End) shows from that moment — "Connecting…" included — until `JOIN_SAY_MS` (5 s) after the link is up (or 5 s after arrival if the link never comes up), or until the customer presses or types in the page after `RESTART_MIN_MS` (2 s; REQ-647's touched rule; a press on the pill itself does not count); then it yields to the page as REQ-545/637/781 say. Once per demo id: a page load that carries the demo in (REQ-535 — every link is a full load) is not a join and folds as before. The pill is re-placed at once when the grace starts or ends. A restart keeps REQ-298's "started a new demo" line as before.
**Implementation:** `shared/demo-mode/restart.ts` `JOIN_SAY_MS` + `joinGrace()` (`arrived` / `live` / `seen` / `touched` / `dispose`); `front-end/islands/DemoModeOverlay.tsx` — a `joined` state, `seen` for the carried demo, `arrived`/`live` on `[demo.id, status]` for a viewer, the REQ-647 input listener also ends the join grace, `placeRef.current()` on `joined`, and `yieldsRef.current = !(compact && open) && !fresh && !joined`.
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-pill-join-grace.test.ts` ("REQ-821 …": the grace is 4-6 s and longer than RESTART_MIN_MS; whole from arrival, yields JOIN_SAY_MS after live; a link that never comes up still yields; the same id again says nothing; `live` for another id or with no arrival does nothing; a carried (`seen`) demo gets no grace; a new id gets its own; REQ-647's input rule; dispose; the overlay's wiring).
- integration: n/a — front-end only: no endpoint, store or protocol change.
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-join-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-821 …": a contractor on /customers with 24 rows at 1280×800, the pill sampled every 100 ms on the page's own clock; a first join shows the whole pill with "Alex from DocuMonster is guiding you" and End for its first 2.5 s live, then folds to the mini-pill within JOIN_SAY_MS + 3 s; a second contractor's demo (opened from a fresh admin session) — a key press in the page 2.3 s after live folds it within 1.5 s, before the grace ends).
**Evidence (2026-11-15, Mac host, worktree fix-cdm1-pill-join-grace off origin/demo-fixes cbcae62d):**
- RED first. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-pill-join-grace` → "Tests: 1 failed, 7 passed" (the overlay's wiring: no `!joined` in yieldsRef). `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-join-grace.e2e.test.ts` on the untouched cbcae62d tree → "✗ REQ-821 … expectation failed: first join: the pill shows whole with \"Alex from DocuMonster is guiding you\" and End for its first 2500 ms live — [\"0:folded:Demo ×\",\"260:folded:Demo ×\"]".
- A first cut started the grace only when the link went live: the pill was folded through "Connecting…" and unfolded ~2 s later (sampled "0:folded … 2055:whole"); the grace now starts on arrival and restarts once at live, and the pill is re-placed at once.
- GREEN. jest `--testPathPattern 'demo-pill-join-grace|demo-mode-restart|demo-pill|demo-ended|demo-mode-protocol'` → "Test Suites: 16 passed · Tests: 162 passed". `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-join-grace.e2e.test.ts` (with its type check) → "✓ REQ-821 … · 25.8s — 1 pass · 0 fail". Neighbours `shots run e2e/demo-mode/{demo-pill-yield,demo-pill-folded-label,demo-restart,demo-pill-reload,demo-end-ask-compact,demo-pill-no-gap,demo-pill-clear}` → "7 pass · 0 fail" (REQ-222/298, 228/291, 535, 545, 548, 637, 781). `demo-pill-home` (REQ-379) passed with the change and fails on cbcae62d; `demo-mode.e2e` (REQ-153 … its 1 s "Opening…" wait) fails on cbcae62d as well as here — pre-existing, host load ~30.

## REQ-820 — A pointer resting on the customer's demo pill keeps it whole: no refold after 6 s, no slide past the window's edge (demo-loop cycle dm1, m6 + test-setup-m4)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none" — demo-loop cycle dm1 (run r83b6287b), issues **m6** ("Customer pill jumps half off-screen every ~6 s while idle on /dashboard with coach-mark") and **test-setup-m4** ("Demo 1 'element detached from the DOM' on pill-tab hover"); RCA LIKELY / skeptic UPHELD (reproduced in Chromium), judge BUG_POLISH + BUG_CONTRADICTION.
**Cause (RCA, at cbcae62d):** the folded pill's tab opened the whole pill on `mouseenter` and armed `unpeekIn(PILL_PEEK_MS = 6000)`; the only thing that cleared that timer was `holdPeek` on the persistent pill div's `mouseenter`, which fires before the tab's (outer → inner) while `peek` is still false, and never again while the pointer stays inside. So after 6 s the pill folded under a resting pointer; the tab re-mounted under it, Chromium's post-layout hover update gave the new button a `mouseenter` (probe here: pointerenter/mouseover/mouseenter on every re-mounted node, no mousemove), and it opened again. Each opening went from `tabStyle` (left 0, translate 1184 px) to `pillStyle` with `transition:transform 250ms`, so the whole pill slid in from x 1196 — half off-screen on the right edge. The tab's swap for the whole pill (Playwright's "element was detached") is by design (REQ-545) and unchanged.
**Requirement:** while a mouse or pen pointer is on the customer's pill (folded or whole) it stays whole however long it rests; it folds only once the pointer leaves it (after a 300 ms wait), or — opened by a tap with no pointer on it — after PILL_PEEK_MS. End's question up holds it as before. The tab opens on real pointer movement over it (mousemove), a focus or a tap — never on a bare mouseenter. The frame that turns the tab into the whole pill has no transform transition: it appears at its box and never slides in from the tab's translate; later moves glide as before. Implementation: `peekTimer({ held, fold })` in `shared/demo-mode/pill.ts` (re-arms while held); `DemoModeOverlay` tracks `overPillRef` from the pill div's pointerenter/pointerleave (touch excluded — its :hover sticks after a tap), the tab's `onMouseMove={openPeek}`, and a one-frame `noGlide` (`transition:none`).
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-pill-peek-hold.test.ts` ("REQ-820 …": not held → folds once after the wait; a pointer resting 20 s → never folds, leaving folds after 300 ms; held when it fires → folds at the next wait; re-arm replaces, cancel drops; the island folds through `peekTimer` held by a mouse/pen pointer or End's question; the tab opens on mousemove/focus/click, no mouseenter; `noGlide ? "transition:none"`). Amended: `jest/unit/demo-pill-yield.test.ts` (REQ-545's tab-wiring check now expects `onMouseMove`, says REQ-820).
- integration: n/a — front-end only: no endpoint, store or message changed.
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-peek-hold.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-820 …": a demo on a contractor with 24 customers; the customer at 1280×800 on /customers scrolled mid-way, the pill folded to its tab; a real pointer moves onto the tab and rests 8 s while every animation frame is sampled — never folded again, no frame past 0..view.w; the pointer leaves → folded).
**Evidence (2026-11-15, Mac host, worktree fix-cdm1-pill-peek-hover-hold off origin/demo-fixes cbcae62d):**
- RED first. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-pill-peek-hold` → "Tests: 7 failed, 7 total" (`peekTimer is not a function`; no `overPillRef`, `onMouseMove`, `noGlide`). `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-peek-hold.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` (PORT=5737 serve) → "✗ REQ-820 … expectation failed: no frame of the whole pill is past the window's edge (vw 1280) — 1006:1196-1720 7276:1196-1720 7368:1196-1720 7384:943-1467 …" — the opening slide from 1196, and again ~6.3 s later (the refold-and-reopen loop).
- GREEN. jest unit `--testPathPattern 'demo-'` → "Test Suites: 64 passed · Tests: 772 passed". `SHOTS_JOBS=1 shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-peek-hold.e2e.test.ts e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-yield.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` → "✓ REQ-545 · 95.7s", "✓ REQ-820 · 38.5s" — 2 pass · 0 fail; `e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-folded-label` "✓ REQ-637" and `demo-pill-no-gap` "✓ REQ-781" (the first parallel run under host load average ~45 timed out REQ-545's waitFor and REQ-820's screenshot; both green serially).
- `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on `islands/DemoModeOverlay.tsx`; `deno fmt --check` clean on every touched and new file (all were clean at the base).

## REQ-819 — The send dialog's email preview has no scroller of its own: scrolling it is mirrored, and the customer's pointer over it keeps moving on the stage
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm1 (run r83b6287b), demo issue **M3** (CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_CONTRADICTION against REQ-242/REQ-780): the customer scrolled 500px inside "What they'll get"; the stage still showed "Hi John 👋" at the top (the stage frame's `contentWindow.scrollY` was 0) and the customer's "ML" marker froze at the frame's edge.
**Cause (RCA at cbcae62d):** `SendLangPreview.tsx` rendered the email as `<iframe sandbox="" srcdoc=…>` at a fixed 320px (`static/assistant-page.css`, `static/quotes.css`), so it scrolled inside its own, opaque-origin document. The mirror recorder listens for scroll on the top document only (`mirror-record.ts` capture listener; its scroll ops read window and top-document elements only), and the overlay tracks the customer's pointer with a top-document `pointermove` (`DemoModeOverlay.tsx`), so neither ever saw the email's scroll or the moves over it.
**Requirement:** The email preview never scrolls on its own: the frame is sized to its email's height (re-fitted on every load — the language switch — and when its width changes; a shorter email shrinks it), so the send dialog's own `max-height` + `overflow-y: auto` scroll — already mirrored — is what moves. The frame is `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` (so the page can measure it; never `allow-scripts`, nothing in the email runs) with `scrolling="no"` and `pointer-events: none`, so the wheel over it scrolls the dialog and every pointer move over it reaches the top document. REQ-780's srcdoc path (cleaned srcdoc, the stage's `allow-same-origin` frame) is unchanged and still carries the content; the fitted height crosses as the frame's style.
**Tests:**
- unit: `front-end/lib/email-frame-fit.test.ts` ("REQ-819 …" ×4: the frame takes its email's full height; a shorter email shrinks it; border-box adds the borders so the viewport is the email's height; an unreadable document leaves the frame alone) · `front-end/lib/send-lang-preview.test.tsx` (REQ-461 SSR test, revised: `sandbox="allow-same-origin"`, no `allow-scripts`, `scrolling="no"`).
- integration: n/a — front-end only; no endpoint, store or projection changed (the preview data is REQ-461's unchanged `GET /quotes/:id/send-preview`).
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-email-preview-scroll.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-819 …": the REAL `SendPreviewBody` bundled with preact, under the app's own quotes.css + assistant-page.css, in a send dialog streamed by the real recorder into the real replayer: the frame is as tall as its email; the customer wheels 500px over the preview → the dialog scrolls, the email's frame stays at 0, and within 1 s the stage shows the same email line at the dialog's top; a mouse move down across the preview is heard by a top-document `pointermove` at every step to where it rests; the English email re-fits and reaches the stage; no email script runs). REQ-780's `demo-stage-email-preview.e2e.test.ts` still green.
**Evidence (2026-11-15, Mac host, worktree fix-cdm1-email-preview-scroll off origin/demo-fixes cbcae62d):**
- RED first. `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-email-preview-scroll.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` → "✗ REQ-819 … expectation failed: REQ-819: the email preview has no scroller of its own (frame 150 / email undefined) — expected \"fits\", got null" (the `sandbox=""` frame's document is unreadable and keeps its fixed height). `deno test lib/send-lang-preview.test.tsx` → "FAILED | 2 passed | 1 failed" (sandbox `""` ≠ `"allow-same-origin"`). `deno test lib/email-frame-fit.test.ts` → Module not found `email-frame-fit.ts`.
- GREEN. `deno test -A lib/send-lang-preview.test.tsx lib/email-frame-fit.test.ts` → "ok | 7 passed | 0 failed". `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-email-preview-scroll.e2e.test.ts e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-email-preview.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` → "✓ REQ-780 …" and "✓ REQ-819 …". `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'demo-stage-email-preview|send-dialog-lang-preview'` → "Test Suites: 2 passed · Tests: 11 passed". `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on every touched TS file; `deno fmt` clean on the new files, `SendLangPreview.tsx`, `quotes.css` (`assistant-page.css` was not fmt-clean at the base).

## REQ-813 — Demo mode: after a page load the stage's own pointer marker shows what the customer has (dimmed "not shown" / "pointing…"), and the customer's "pointing…" ends when the stage stops looking
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm1 (run r83b6287b), issue **m4** (BUG_CONTRADICTION, RCA confirmed + skeptic upheld at cbcae62d): after a customer page load the customer showed nothing (fleet-4/stdout:49) or a short "Alex is pointing…" chip (fleet-1/stdout:73), while the stage drew a full-strength green "You" arrow under its own "Your pointer isn't on Maria's screen" banner. Cause: REQ-642's OwnPointer is drawn from `ownAt(h)`, which ignores alive/absent, and the stage had no pending state; REQ-645's `seekAgain` gave up after REANCHOR_CAP_MS without telling the customer, whose chip ran its own PENDING_MS.
**Requirement:** The stage's own marker (`demo-pointer-own`) says what the customer has (`ownLook`): **absent** while `pointerAbsent` holds — dimmed to `OWN_ABSENT_OPACITY` (0.4), hollow and dashed, tagged "You · not shown" / "Tú · no se ve" even while a ghost exists, `data-absent`; **pending** while the stage's pending window runs (started when `resendPointer` sends `{k:"pending"}`, PENDING_MS at most, ended by a move, a drop, or the give-up) — "You · pointing…" / "Tú · señalando…" with the same pulsing dot as the customer's chip, `data-pending`; else **live** at full strength. When `seekAgain`'s look by the print gives up (`seekGaveUp`: REANCHOR_CAP_MS passed, no match) after a `pending` was sent, the stage sends `{k:"leave"}` so the customer's chip ends at the same moment. The old spot is never re-sent on the new page (REQ-645 rule kept).
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-stage-own-pointer-absent.test.ts` ("REQ-813 …": `ownLook` absent for a dead node anchor, live when drawn, pending over absent; `OWN_ABSENT_OPACITY` ≤ 0.5; `seekGaveUp` only past the cap on a styled replay with a printable print; wiring — OwnPointer gets `look={ownLook(absent, pending)}` and both labels, resendPointer calls `startPending(` after sending pending, seekAgain sends leave + `endPending(` on `seekGaveUp(`, data-absent/data-pending in OwnPointer, keys in en + es). `front-end/components/demo-mode/OwnPointer.test.tsx` (deno, renders `OwnMarker`: live full strength/filled/"You"; absent dimmed `opacity:0.4`, `fill="none"`, "You · not shown", data-absent, tagged even when `tagged=false`; pending data-pending + "pointing…"). Amended: `jest/unit/demo-stage-presenter-pointer.test.ts` (REQ-393's "the only leave" now excludes seekAgain's give-up leave).
- integration: n/a — front-end only: no endpoint, store or wire type changed (`leave` and `pending` already existed).
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-scroll-pointer.e2e.test.ts`, the "next page" story (now names REQ-813): after the customer goes to /q under his still mouse, the stage's `demo-pointer-own` carries `data-absent` (no live own marker) while the customer has no `demo-pointer`; after his move the marker is live again.
**Evidence (2026-11-15, Mac host, worktree fix-cdm1-stage-own-pointer-absent off origin/demo-fixes cbcae62d, serve on PORT=5813):**
- RED first: jest `--testPathPattern demo-stage-own-pointer-absent` → "Tests: 12 failed, 12 total"; `deno test components/demo-mode/OwnPointer.test.tsx` → TS2305 no exported member `OwnMarker` / `OWN_ABSENT_OPACITY`; `shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-scroll-pointer.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check --filter REQ-813` → "✗ … timed out: REQ-813: the stage's own marker is absent while the customer has no presenter pointer (last error: Error: stage own marker absent=0 live=1 · customer demo-pointer=0)".
- GREEN: jest `--testPathPattern demo-` → "Test Suites: 64 passed · Tests: 777 passed"; deno `OwnPointer.test.tsx` + `demo-pointer-off-mark.test.tsx` → "ok | 9 passed | 0 failed". e2e: the REQ-813 step (and the "move brings it back, live" check) passes in every run; the story as a whole did not finish green on this host — under load 23–50 it fails later at the REQ-645 reload step ("no presenter arrow on the customer's screen") or the REQ-451 scroll-ride step, and the untouched base cbcae62d fails the same story at the same two steps under the same load (2/2 base runs), so those are pre-existing and not caused by this change.
