## REQ-858 — /admin's guide gate loads the app's stylesheets (dashboard.css, public-lang.css) and the shell's motion.css: every stylesheet link in a <Head> is keyed, components and islands included (demo-loop cycle dm4, issues m7 + setup-4) — REGRESSION of REQ-855, AMENDMENT of REQ-055 / REQ-195
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm4 (run rf5fcb8b9, `demo-loop/runs/rf5fcb8b9/demo-report.md`), issues **m7** "/admin gate card during a demo has no app styling (only public-lang.css, fallback font instead of Nunito)" and **setup-4** "Fallback/monospace font on /admin gate card attributed partly to headless font set" (fleet-rf5fcb8b9-0/stdout:85: "Only public-lang.css is loaded (`document.styleSheets` = public-lang.css + 2 inline); body font-family is 'ui-sans-serif, system-ui…'"). RCA (analyst + skeptic UPHELD for both, judge BUG_POLISH, at demo-fixes 7401e980): not a headless artifact.
**Cause (RCA):** Fresh 2's head dedupe key for a `<link>` is `vnode.key ?? type + sorted props` with `href` left out (`@fresh/core` preact_hooks.ts ~L390-437). `components/AdminGuideGate.tsx` had two unkeyed `<link rel="stylesheet">` in its `<Head>`: dashboard.css (REQ-376, e2c927b9) and public-lang.css (REQ-855, 2b511ab1). Both keyed "link::stylesheet", so the last, public-lang.css, won. The shell's unkeyed motion.css link (`routes/_app.tsx`, REQ-195) has the same key and was swapped for it. The gate page ended up with public-lang.css alone: no Nunito, no app styling, no motion. REQ-055's guard (`jest/unit/head-stylesheet-keys.test.ts`) only walked `front-end/routes`, and REQ-855's tests asserted only the toggle's markup, so the regression passed green.
**Requirement:**
1. The gate's links are keyed (`key="css-dashboard"`, `key="css-public-lang"`); rendered inside the real app shell, the /admin gate's HTML links /dashboard.css, /public-lang.css and /motion.css.
2. The shell's motion.css link is keyed (`key="css-motion"`), so no page's lone unkeyed `<Head>` stylesheet link can take its place (this also gives motion.css back to every page with one unkeyed link, e.g. /dashboard, /admin, /assistant).
3. REQ-055's guard reads `front-end/routes`, `front-end/components` and `front-end/islands`: a file with two or more stylesheet links keys each one; `_app.tsx`'s stylesheet links are all keyed. Reviewed hits: LegalPage (2 links, both keyed); SiteFooterView, AsstThreads, DemoStage, MoneyInput and FieldAssignmentsPage mention "stylesheet" only in comments or DOM code, no `<link>` in a `<Head>`.
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/head-stylesheet-keys.test.ts` (REQ-055 guard extended to components + islands, and "REQ-858 (dm4 m7) the app shell's own stylesheet links are keyed …"). Amended pin: `jest/unit/motion-system.test.ts` (REQ-195) now expects `<link key="css-motion" rel="stylesheet" …>`.
- integration: `front-end/lib/admin-gate.int.test.ts` "REQ-858 (dm4 m7): the guide gate's page links dashboard.css, public-lang.css and the shell's motion.css" (real /admin middleware + real `_app.tsx` via `appWrapper`, backend in process).
- e2e: n/a — the demo loop does not run the browser lane per fix; the integration test renders the real middleware, gate and shell through Fresh's own head dedupe, which is where the bug lived, and the next demo cycle re-checks `document.styleSheets` live.
**Evidence (2026-11-16, Mac host, worktree fix-cdm4-admin-gate-css-keys off origin/demo-fixes 7401e980):**
- RED first. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern head-stylesheet-keys` gave "Tests: 2 failed, 1 passed, 3 total": offenders `components/AdminGuideGate.tsx: <link rel="stylesheet" href={asset("/dashboard.css")} />` and `… "/public-lang.css" …`, and the unkeyed `_app.tsx` motion.css link. `cd front-end && deno test -A --unstable-kv lib/admin-gate.int.test.ts` gave "FAILED | 6 passed | 1 failed": `AssertionError: /dashboard.css is linked: ["/public-lang.css"]` — the page carried exactly the one sheet the demo measured.

## REQ-879 — A stale logged-out /login tab rejoins the demo once the customer has signed in again in another tab: it goes to `?next=`, mounts the overlay, and the stage follows it (demo-loop cycle dm5, issue m3)
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm5 (run r38fa8936 on demo-fixes `abbf6bc3`, the fifth run, after cycles dm1–dm4), Demo-mode-only test, five testers. Issue `m3`: "Stage stays Live on the old /settings tab while the customer looks at a stale logged-out /login tab" (fleet-3/stdout N3: the customer logs out in tab 0, tab 1 lands on /login?next=/quotes, she logs back in on tab 0 and opens /settings, then selects tab 1 and clicks inside it; the stage log stays at "Configuración · DocuMonster|0|Live|" and tab 1 has no pill). RCA (analyst + skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_CONTRADICTION against REQ-232 "the stage follows the tab the customer is using … says plainly whether it is live", at `abbf6bc3`).
**Cause (RCA):** `front-end/routes/_app.tsx` mounts the early demo script and `DemoModeOverlay` only when the request carried a session (`hasSession`). A /login page rendered without one (client.ts's 401 redirect to /login?next=…, a tab left over from REQ-823's sign-out) runs no demo code: no socket, no claim, nothing said to the stage. Nothing on that page noticed that a login in another tab put a live session back in the browser's shared cookie, so the stage kept following the last tab that claimed. A /login reloaded with a session also ignored `?next=` and went to /dashboard.
**Requirement:**
1. A /login page watches for the customer coming back to it: window focus, the tab shown again (`visibilitychange` → visible), a page restored from the back-forward cache, a click or a key in it. Each asks GET /api/me with the browser's cookie (one ask at a time, at most one a second; the body is never left open). Once it answers 200, the page replaces itself with `?next=` (or /dashboard). That page loads with the session, mounts the overlay, claims on input, and the stage follows it, Live, on that page.
2. `?next=` is followed only when it is a path on this site: it must start with `/`, never `//`, never contain a backslash, and never be /login or /verify. Anything else goes to /dashboard.
3. The /login handler sends a visitor who already has a session to the same `?next=` (same rule), not always /dashboard.
4. Not built: the RCA's optional part (b), a "hidden" presence bit from the followed tab that has the stage say "{name} is on another page". The judge marked it optional, and the RCA notes it does nothing in headless runs, where every tab reports visible. Part (a) is the root-cause fix: the stale tab picks the session up again.
**Implementation:** `front-end/lib/login-rejoin.ts` (`rejoinTarget`, `signedInNow`, `watchLoginRejoin`, `REJOIN_GAP_MS`); `front-end/islands/LoginForm.tsx` (a mount effect that installs the watcher with `rejoinTarget(location.search)` and `location.replace`); `front-end/routes/login.tsx` (an authed visitor goes to `rejoinTarget(search)`).
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-login-tab-rejoin.test.ts` ("REQ-879 …", 6 cases: `rejoinTarget` on site paths, foreign/`//`/backslash/`javascript:`/sign-in targets; `signedInNow` asks /api/me with credentials, 200/401/failure, the body cancelled; focus after a login elsewhere goes to next; visible, pointerdown, keydown, and pageshow(persisted) ask too, while hidden does not; one ask in flight, at most one a second, goes once, `stop()` removes every listener; LoginForm wiring).
- integration: `front-end/lib/login-rejoin.int.test.ts` ("REQ-879 …", 3 cases: the real /login handler with the backend answered in process. A session with `?next=/quotes` → 302 /quotes; no next, or a foreign or sign-in next → /dashboard; no session or a dead one → the sign-in page).
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-tab-leave.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-879 (demo-loop cycle dm5, m3) …": demo on tab 1 (1100 × 780), she signs out (the stage says "Ana Torres signed out"), a second tab opens /login?next=%2Fquotes with no session and no pill, she signs in again and tab 1 is Live; the stale tab is brought to front and clicked, it goes to /quotes and shows the pill, a key there, and the stage shows 640 × 760, Live, /quotes).
**Evidence (2026-11-16, Mac host, worktree fix-cdm5-login-tab-rejoin-demo, branch fix/cdm5-login-tab-rejoin-demo off origin/demo-fixes abbf6bc3; its own server `PORT=58791 deno task serve`, host load 80–95):**
- RED first. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-login-tab-rejoin` gave "Tests: 6 failed, 6 total": "Cannot find module '../../front-end/lib/login-rejoin'" ×5, and the LoginForm wiring was absent. `cd front-end && deno test -A --unstable-kv lib/login-rejoin.int.test.ts` gave "FAILED | 2 passed | 1 failed": `/login?next=/quotes` with a session went to "/dashboard", where "/quotes" was expected. e2e `SHOTS_JOBS=1 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:58791 shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-tab-leave.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check --filter REQ-879` gave "✗ … m3: the stale /login tab never went to /quotes after the re-login (still http://localhost:58791/login?next=%2Fquotes)". That is the tester's m3. (Two earlier runs died in set-up on host load: REQ-823's known 90 s `page.screenshot` stall after the navigating Demo click. The story now clicks Demo by mouse, as REQ-834's sibling stories do, and waits for tab 1 to leave /dashboard instead of the `/` URL.)
- GREEN. The same jest run gave "Tests: 6 passed, 6 total". The whole unit project (`npx jest --selectProjects unit`) gave "Test Suites: 556 passed, 556 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 5610 passed". The int test gave "ok | 3 passed | 0 failed". The e2e story gave "✓ … 23.3s" and "✓ … 33.9s" in two runs in a row.
- `deno lint` and `deno check` (lib/login-rejoin.ts, islands/LoginForm.tsx, routes/login.tsx) are clean. `deno fmt --check` is clean on the new files, LoginForm.tsx and the e2e file. `routes/login.tsx` was already not fmt-clean at base and was not reformatted.

## REQ-878 — The stage's file chip sits by the button the customer used, never over the row's hint or the button's label (demo-loop cycle dm5, issue p2) — AMENDMENT of REQ-827 / REQ-862
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm5 (run r38fa8936, `demo-loop/runs/r38fa8936/demo-report.md`), issue **p2** "Stage file-picker chip is centred on the whole settings row, so it covers the helper text and the 'Subir certificado' label" (seen by demos 2, 4 and 5: fleet-r38fa8936-1/stdout:73 button 271–379, hint 391–800, chip 653–855; fleet-r38fa8936-3/stdout:140 chip x955 over "certificado" and its hint). RCA CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_POLISH at abbf6bc3. REQ-862's fix held only for the shape its tests used.
**Cause (RCA):** /settings (`front-end/islands/SettingsPage.tsx`, logo row ~853, insurance certificate row ~1365, W-9 row ~1485) opens each file input from a SIBLING button: a full-width `display:flex` row holds `<button>`, `<input type=file style="display:none">` and a hint `<span>`. REQ-827's `chipAnchor` (`front-end/lib/demo-mode/mirror-replay.ts`) walked up to the first ancestor with a box, i.e. the whole row; REQ-862's `placeChip` saw the chip fit inside that row and centred it there, over the hint (logo) or the button's label plus hint (certificate). REQ-862's unit and e2e fixtures only had the hidden input INSIDE its label button, where the nearest box is the button.
**Requirement:**
1. A hidden file/date input's chip anchors on the control the customer used: the input when it has a box; else its boxed `<label for=id>`; else its nearest sibling button / `[role=button]` / label / input[type=button|submit]; only then the nearest boxed ancestor.
2. The chip never covers what the customer can read in the frame. `placeChip` tries spots in order — on the control (centred, when it fits), right of it, left of it, past the text beside it in its row (SettingsPage's hint), under it, over it — and takes the first that fits the frame and intersects no text run (Range line boxes) or control/picture other than the anchor; a spot inside the control's own row (its parent's box) wins over one outside it (never the sidebar while the row has room). Only when no spot is free does REQ-862's rule (on / right / left / centred, clamped) apply. A row-wide ancestor anchor is therefore never centred over its own children's text.
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-mirror-picker-open.test.ts` — new block "REQ-878 (cycle dm5, p2) …" with SettingsPage's sibling markup and the demo's boxes: logo (row 271–1236, button 271–379, hint 391–800) — the chip is not centred on the row (652), clears the hint and the button, stays vertically centred on the button and inside the row; certificate (narrow card row, hint to the frame edge, text to its left) — the chip clears the button, the hint and the left text, inside the frame. Amended: REQ-862's "no room anywhere" test now also puts fields right over and under the button so its centred-clamped fallback is still what it pins.
- integration: n/a — front-end replay geometry only; no endpoint, store or protocol change.
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-picker-open.e2e.test.ts` "REQ-878 (cycle dm5, p2): a file chooser opened from a SIBLING button …" — real Chromium, real recorder → real replayer frame, SettingsPage's logo and certificate rows (button + display:none input + hint span in a flex row, onClick → input.click()): each chip is visible, inside the frame, and its rect intersects neither the button, the button's text (Range) nor the hint (Range line boxes).
**Evidence (2026-11-16, Mac host, worktree fix-cdm5-picker-chip-anchor off origin/demo-fixes abbf6bc3):**
- RED: `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-mirror-picker-open` → "Tests: 2 failed, 22 passed, 24 total" (logo: `Expected: not 652` — centred on the row; certificate: chip intersects the button/hint, `Expected: false, Received: true`). `SHOTS_JOBS=1 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… shots run e2e/demo-mode/demo-picker-open.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` → "FAILED | 1 passed | 1 failed": `REQ-878: the logo chip … expected …"clearOfHint":true… got …"clearOfHint":false`.
- GREEN: the same jest run → "Tests: 24 passed, 24 total"; `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'demo-'` → "Test Suites: 97 passed · Tests: 1092 passed". The same shots run → "ok | 2 passed | 0 failed" (REQ-827/862 story and REQ-878 story; screenshot: the certificate chip sits under "Subir certificado", clear of its hint). `e2e/demo-mode/demo-select-open.e2e.test.ts`'s REQ-638 send-menu story fails identically with mirror-replay.ts at abbf6bc3 (`locator.waitFor: Timeout 20000ms exceeded`, pre-existing, unrelated). `deno lint`, `deno check` (mirror-replay.ts, islands/DemoStage.tsx) and `deno fmt --check` clean on the touched files.

## REQ-876 — End's question opens near where End was pressed: among the boxes with no control under them, the one whose answers are nearest the press (demo-loop cycle dm5, m2) — AMENDMENT of REQ-852 / REQ-866
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm5 (run r38fa8936, `demo-loop/runs/r38fa8936/demo-report.md`), issue **m2** "Opening End's question moves the customer pill ~630 px from where End was clicked (x823 y12 -> x12 y63)" (fleet-r38fa8936-3/stdout:92-101: before x823 y12 444×43, after x12 y63 671×43, click at (1199,34); fleet-r38fa8936-0/stdout:19 the same box). RCA CONFIRMED (high), skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_POLISH, at abbf6bc3.
**Cause (RCA):** a side effect of REQ-852/REQ-866. `placeAsk` (front-end/islands/DemoModeOverlay.tsx) passed `askSpot` (shared/demo-mode/pill.ts) only the view, dock, size and controls; `askSpot` took the FIRST box with no control under it in a fixed order (here, the opposite edge, the bottom row, centred, then the rows between at whole-pill-width x steps). On /welcome at 1280×800 the 671 px asking pill covers the brand in every top-row box, the footer's phone link in both bottom-row boxes, and the wizard's right-aligned EN | ES switch at the right of row 63 — so (12,63) won, its answers ~630 px from the press. How far the answers land from End played no part.
**Requirement:** REQ-852/866's rule stays: no control of the page under the asking pill when a box without one exists, else the fewest; a clear current anchor keeps its dock (REQ-300). When the island knows where End was pressed (`near`: the last press on the pill — End or the mini-pill's × — within 5 s; the keyboard keeps REQ-866's order), every box — REQ-852/866's, rows a third of a step (pill height + gap) apart at both edges and centred, and the anchor's row and the rows within a step of it slid from the anchor's edge in PILL_TAB.w/2 steps — is ranked by the gap between its answers ("Yes, end it" + "Keep going", measured in the asking pill; absent, its right end ASK_ANSWERS_W = 150 px wide) and the press, and counted nearest first: the first with no control wins, else the fewest (a tie: the nearest). ## REQ-877 — With his mouse beside the frame, the stage draws a faint ghost of the customer's off marker (chevron + his initial) on the frame's same edge, fading out when hers does (demo-loop cycle dm5, issue m1)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm5 (run r38fa8936, `demo-loop/runs/r38fa8936/demo-report.md`), issue **m1** "Off-frame presenter pointer: the customer sees a clamped edge mark with an 'A' initial, while the stage says 'off' and draws no ghost of it" (fleet-r38fa8936-4/stdout:57: customer `demo-pointer-off-mark` 1264–1278×784–798 and `demo-pointer-off-initial` 'A' 1247–1263×767–783, a second case at (640,775) over 'Todas las facturas'; the stage showed only the banner). RCA CONFIRMED (transient, ~2.9 s per move), skeptic CORRECTED (the customer's mark fades: pmDemoOffFade 2500 + 400 ms), judge BUG_POLISH, option (a), at abbf6bc3.
**Cause (RCA):** beside the frame `anchorOf` (DemoStage.tsx) sends an o:1 edge anchor (REQ-393/451); the customer's DemoPointer draws `offMark` + `offBadge` (his initial) and fades it out over OFF_MARK_SHOW_MS + OFF_MARK_FADE_MS (REQ-635). The stage's `reportedGhost` returned null for every held o:1 anchor (51a8c3ca, REQ-642), and OwnPointer draws no tag off the frame (REQ-860), so the stage drew nothing of what her screen showed for those ~2.9 s.
**Requirement:** for a customer report of his held o:1 anchor, `reportedGhost` returns an edge ghost (`off: { key }`): the edge is read in HER px (the frame's `s`), the ghost sits against that edge of the frame at the same point along it, and `key` is her marker's rounded spot (DemoPointer's `markKey`). It is never dropped as "under his cursor" (GHOST_GAP_PX), and never held back for REQ-789's rest (hers shows at once). PointerGhost draws it as her marker — the chevron (`offMark`) and his initial on a dot (`offBadge`), faint, no "You" tag — keyed on `off.key`, with the same `pmDemoOffFade` (`OFF_FADE_KEYFRAMES`, now one shared definition used by DemoPointer too) over OFF_MARK_SHOW_MS + OFF_MARK_FADE_MS, `forwards` to 0: a new spot restarts both fades, and it is gone when hers is. **Tests:**

## REQ-870 — "Return to your account" on /admin's guide gate, when it ends the demo, lands on /admin saying "You ended the demo"; the leave reports whether it ended the demo (demo-loop cycle dm5, issue p7)
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm5 (run r38fa8936, `demo-loop/runs/r38fa8936/demo-report.md`), issue **p7**: "'Return to your account' from the gate card lands on /admin with no 'You ended the demo' notice, unlike End from the pill". In fleet-r38fa8936-0/stdout:84-92 the gate warned "You are the only presenter — leaving ends the demo for Maria Lopez." and /admin then loaded with no notice. RCA CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_CONTRADICTION (against REQ-235 and REQ-855), at abbf6bc3.
**Cause (RCA):** `front-end/lib/return-to-account.ts` (REQ-376, e2c927b9) POSTed the leave, stopped impersonating and navigated to `withLang(ADMIN_PATH, lang)`. That is a bare /admin with no `?demo=ended&by=you`, which is the only thing that makes /admin show the notice (`endedHref`/`readEndedNotice` → DemoModeOverlay `endedNotice`). The client could not know better: `POST /demo-mode/sessions/:id/leave` returned only `{ ok: true }`, while `leaveDemo` ends the demo only when no presenters remain.
**Requirement:**
1. `POST /demo-mode/sessions/:id/leave` answers `{ ok: true, ended: boolean }`. `ended` is true only when this leave ended the demo (the last presenter left). `leaveDemo` returns that flag. The client type in `front-end/clients/demo-mode.ts` carries it.
2. `returnToOwnAccount` lands on `returnedHref(ended, lang)` (`shared/demo-mode/ended.ts`). When the demo ended, that is `endedHref({ by: "you" }, lang)`, the same /admin the pill's End lands on, saying "You ended the demo". Otherwise it is the plain console `withLang(ADMIN_PATH, lang)`. That covers a colleague still presenting, a failed leave, and no demo to leave. It never claims an end that did not happen. The leave still comes before the account is handed back (REQ-232).
3. Scope: the gate's Return only. The impersonation banner's Return (`ImpersonationBanner.stop`) and the stage's Leave are unchanged.
**Tests:**
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-gate-return-ended.test.ts` ("REQ-870 (dm5 p7) …": `returnedHref` equals `endedHref({ by: "you" })` when ended, in each language, and the plain console otherwise; pins on return-to-account, the client type and the controller's `{ ok: true, ended }`). `front-end/lib/return-to-account.test.ts` (4 × "REQ-870 (dm5 p7) …": real `returnToOwnAccount` with fetch and `location` stubbed; ended → `/admin?demo=ended&by=you&lang=es`, leave before stop-impersonating; not ended → `/admin?lang=en`; leave 500 → `/admin?lang=en`; no demo → `/admin`, no leave call). AMENDMENT of the REQ-855 pin in `jest/unit/demo-presenter-chrome.test.ts`: `location.href = returnedHref(ended, lang)`.
- integration: `backend/src/demo-mode/entrypoints/demo-mode-controller/int.test.ts` "REQ-870 (demo-loop dm5, p7) POST /demo-mode/sessions/:id/leave says whether the leave ended the demo …" (composed router, real KV: a colleague's leave → `{ ok: true, ended: false }`; the last presenter's → `{ ok: true, ended: true }`).
- e2e: `e2e/admin-impersonate-gate/admin-impersonate-gate.e2e.test.ts` "REQ-870 (demo-loop dm5, p7): as the only presenter, Return to your account from /admin's gate ends the demo and lands on /admin saying 'You ended the demo' …". It runs in real Chromium: start the demo from /admin, open a second tab on /admin and get the gate, click Return. `[data-cy=demo-ended]` then says "You ended the demo", and Demo can be started again.
**Evidence (2026-11-16, Mac host, worktree fix-cdm5-gate-return-ended-notice off origin/demo-fixes abbf6bc3):**
- RED first. `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/demo-mode/entrypoints/demo-mode-controller/int.test.ts --filter REQ-870` gave "FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed": actual `{ ok: true }`, expected `+ ended: false`. `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/return-to-account.test.ts` gave "FAILED | 3 passed | 1 failed": actual `/admin?lang=es`, expected `/admin?demo=ended&by=you&lang=es`. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern demo-gate-return-ended` gave "Tests: 4 failed" (`returnedHref is not a function`, and the pins unmatched). The e2e ran with `PORT=5617 deno task serve` and `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… BASE_URL=http://localhost:5617 shots run e2e/admin-impersonate-gate/admin-impersonate-gate.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check`. ## REQ-871 — The box the customer's pill sends to the stage is never smaller than her measured pill, so the resting ghost never cuts "… is guiding y…" (demo-loop cycle dm5, issue p1) — AMENDMENT of REQ-835 / REQ-865
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm5 (run r38fa8936, demo-report.md), issue **p1** "Stage ghost of the customer pill cuts off 'Alex is guiding y…' / 'Alex te está guian…' (1 px short); the dm4 fix (REQ-865) did not hold" (fleet-r38fa8936-0/stdout:21/68: span scrollWidth 116 > clientWidth 115 at 1280, "The ghost of the open question was not truncated"). RCA CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_CONTRADICTION, at abbf6bc3. (The task text called the failed fix REQ-861; REQ-861 is the /settings address autocomplete, the dm4 ghost fix is REQ-865.)
**Cause (RCA):** `pillRestBox` (shared/demo-mode/pill.ts, added by 47413066, REQ-835) sent `width: Math.round(box.width)` and `height: Math.round(box.height)`. Her pill is shrink-to-fit, so its width has a fraction (Ana 404.25, Maria 414.44, Jo 395.48). A fraction under .5 lost up to half a pixel. REQ-865 lays the ghost out at exactly `g.width / fit.s` with her own metrics, so nothing absorbed the deficit, and the one-row ghost's text span (`min-width:0; text-overflow:ellipsis`) drew "… is guiding y…". REQ-865's e2e only measured the pill with End's question open, never the resting pill every tester looks at. Which presenter name gets cut depends on the host's fonts.
**Requirement:** `pillRestBox` rounds the width and height UP (`Math.ceil`), never to the nearest: the box sent is never smaller than the measured box and at most 1 px larger. Left and top still round to the nearest. With her resting pill shown whole ("Demo mode · {name} is guiding you · Connected · End demo"), at 1280 and 700 wide, in EN and ES, for presenters Ana, Maria, Jo and Alex, the stage's ghost says the same "{name} is guiding you" and no element of it has scrollWidth > clientWidth.
**Tests:**

- integration: n/a — front-end geometry only; no endpoint, store or wire-format change (the rect field stays a number).
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-ghost-no-truncation.e2e.test.ts` (8 new stories "REQ-871 (demo-loop cycle dm5, p1): EN|ES — presenter "Ana|Maria|Jo|Alex": at rest, at 1280 and 700 …": a super admin named the presenter presents to Sam; the pointer on her folded tab shows her whole resting pill (REQ-545/820); her pill's words are whole, and the stage's ghost says the same phrase with no element cut; then at 700 the same).

## REQ-872 — The stage's customer cursor tag stays off the replay's drawn select list and picker chip (demo-loop cycle dm5, issue p12) — AMENDMENT of REQ-848
**Source:** Raphael: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm5 (run r38fa8936, `demo-loop/runs/r38fa8936/demo-report.md`), issue **p12** "Stage's customer cursor tag 'ML' is placed over a row of the drawn native select list" (fleet-r38fa8936-4/stdout:34,59: the 'ML' tag sat over the 'Español' option). RCA CONFIRMED, skeptic UPHELD, judge BUG_POLISH, at demo-fixes abbf6bc3.
**Cause (RCA):** the stage places the customer's tag with `tagPlacement` scored by `frameCoverage` (DemoStage.tsx `coversFrame`), which hit-tests the replay with `elementFromPoint` (DemoPointer.tsx `contentAt`). The replay draws an open select's list (`[data-mirror-listbox]`, REQ-638, ca9e5616) and the picker chip (`[data-mirror-picker]`, REQ-827) with `pointer-events:none` (mirror-replay.ts LIST_CSS / CHIP_CSS), so hit-testing sees through them to the dialog under them and every slot over the list scored clean.
**Requirement:** `pointer-events:none` stays on the drawn list and chip (anchorAt relies on it, mirror-replay.ts). `frameCoverage` also reads those boxes by geometry: a point on a drawn list row other than the one the arrow is on, or on the picker chip, counts as a control (cost 3 per sample, like any other control); the row the arrow is on and the list's padding count as text (1). `tagPlacement` therefore picks a side off the list when one is free.
**Tests:**
- unit: `front-end/lib/demo-stage-tag-drawn-list.test.tsx` ("REQ-872 (demo dm5 p12) unit: …" — a tag over a drawn list row costs > 0; another row costs as a control and the arrow's own row does not; the picker chip costs as a control; `tagPlacement` with the frame covers picks a free side, not the tail over the list; the attribute names match mirror-replay's `LISTBOX_ATTR` / `PICKER_ATTR`).
- integration: n/a — no endpoint, store or protocol change; the scoring is a pure function over the replay document, covered at unit level, and DemoStage's wiring of `frameCoverage` is already pinned by REQ-848's `front-end/lib/demo-stage-covers-frame.test.tsx`.
- e2e: n/a here — the demo loop does not run the browser lane per fix; the next demo cycle re-checks the tag with a select list open.

## REQ-873 — A peeked customer pill whose whole row holds controls opens on another row: /customers at 700 wide no longer puts it over the filter tabs (demo-loop cycle dm5, p5) — AMENDMENT of REQ-818 / REQ-849
**Source:** Raphael, the demo loop: "fix every issue the demo found, loop until there are none." Demo-loop cycle dm5 (run r38fa8936, `demo-loop/runs/r38fa8936/demo-report.md`), issue **p5** "Hover-opened customer pill covers the list filter tabs on /customers at 700 wide" (fleet-r38fa8936-1/stdout:79-85: the peek at 12-513 × 549-592 over Todos 261-342, Nuevos 346-436 and En curso 440-535 × 551-581, ES, 700×800, tab at 0,560). RCA CONFIRMED (high), skeptic UPHELD; judge BUG_CONTRADICTION (REQ-818 "a peeked pill slides off a control"; REQ-228 AMENDMENT / REQ-781: the customer's pill stays off controls).
**Cause (RCA, at abbf6bc3):** `peekBox` (shared/demo-mode/pill.ts) fixed `top = tab.top + tab.height - home.height` and only varied x, from PILL_MARGIN to view.w - margin - w. A 501 px pill at 700 wide can only range over 12..187, so every box spans the filter tabs; each try counted 3 controls and `fewest`'s tie kept flush, {12,549,501,43}. Unlike `placePill` / `askSpot` (REQ-866 rows), it had no other row to try.

None clear: the row's fewest, flush on a tie (REQ-818 unchanged). A clear tab row keeps the old place. Wherever it opens, `peekHolds` still counts the tab's box as the pill's (REQ-849), so the pointer that opened it keeps it whole.
**Implementation:** shared/demo-mode/pill.ts `peekBox` (new optional `top`, the row/spot search after the row's fewest); front-end/islands/DemoModeOverlay.tsx passes `top: bannerH()` to it.
**Tests:**

- integration: n/a — front-end placement geometry only; no endpoint, store or wire message changes.
- e2e: n/a — the demo loop does not run the browser lane per fix; the unit case is the demo's measured geometry, and the next demo cycle re-checks /customers at 700 wide live.

## REQ-881 — the stage's drawn select list closes when the popup is gone, even with no event (AMENDMENT of REQ-638)

**Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 6, issue m5; "you personally go fix the polish problems"):** the stage kept drawing a native select's list after the customer closed it with Escape; a second Escape cleared it.

Why: a real browser's native popup swallows the Escape (and the click outside) that closes it, so the page receives no keydown/mousedown and the recorder (REQ-638) keeps the select marked open until some other event.

Requirement:
1. While a select is marked open, the recorder reads the browser's own state with `select.matches(":open")` on every frame pass (the 500 ms sweep included). Once `:open` has read true for that select, a false reading closes the mark, with no event needed. A `:open` that never read true (a browser without a picker, a headless one) is not trusted: the REQ-638 events still decide.
2. Where `:open` is unsupported (matches throws), a pointer move that reaches the page more than 400 ms after the opening and at least 4 px from the opening point closes the mark: an open native list captures the pointer, so a move means it is gone. A date input's picker is not closed this way (REQ-827 keeps its own rules).

Tests: `jest/unit/demo-mirror-select-open.test.ts` ("REQ-881 — …", 4 tests: `:open` true→false clears on the next frame; a never-true `:open` is not trusted; a pointer move closes it after the grace and not on a jitter; a date picker is untouched). e2e: n/a — the fix is in the recorder's event/state logic, covered end to end on the fake DOM through the replayer; a real popup's swallowed Escape cannot be driven from Playwright (its key events bypass the native popup).

## REQ-890 — a crowded tab row opens the compact pill before the peek moves away; the pointer's travel to it is not a leave (AMENDMENT of REQ-818 / REQ-849 / REQ-873)

**Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 6, issues m1 + m2; re-check 11 of REQ-873 did not hold):** "you personally go fix the polish problems" — the hover-opened customer pill at 700 px still covered the /customers filter chips (ES) or opened 250 px away over the empty-state line and folded under the pointer (EN).

Reproduced by hand at 700×800 (EN, 405 px pill, tab at (0,560)): the tab's row has a control under every x (sidebar buttons to x 212, filter chips from x 261), so REQ-873 moved the peek to the nearest control-free box, (252,702), three rows down. The pointer then crossed a gap `peekHolds` does not count and the peek folded on the way. In ES (501 px) no control-free box exists for the whole pill, so it fell back to the tab's row over the chips.

Requirement:
1. `peekBox` takes the pill's compact size (the ≤640 px form). When no box of the whole pill on the tab's row is control-free, it tries the compact size at the same x's — on the tab's row first, then the other rows and spots — before moving the whole pill away, and returns the compact box flagged `compact`. The overlay shows the compact form while such a peek is out and goes back to the whole form when it folds; the stage's ghost follows (`face.compact`).
2. When neither form has a control-free box, the row's fewest is returned flagged `crowded`; an overlay still showing the whole form switches to compact and measures again (the compact size is only known once rendered).
3. `peekHolds` counts the corridor (the union of the tab's box and the pill's) for PEEK_TRAVEL_MS (1.5 s) after the pointer was last on the tab or the pill (the opening counts), so a pointer travelling from the tab to a peek that opened away from it does not fold it, however long it rested on the tab first; after that, REQ-849's rule alone.

Tests: `jest/unit/demo-pill-peek-compact.test.ts` (9 tests: the bug's geometry; compact on the tab's row; whole fits → unchanged; crowded flag with and without a compact size; corridor held within the travel time, not after, not outside, and the REQ-849 rule alone). The overlay side is exercised by `jest/unit/demo-mirror-select-open`-style fake-DOM tests: n/a — the overlay's compact switch is a one-line state change exercised by the e2e `e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-peek-compact.e2e.test.ts` (customer at 700×800 on /customers hovers the tab: the pill opens compact on the tab's row, over no control, and stays while the pointer moves onto it).


**REVISION (2026-11-16, same day, headless re-check):** on the real /customers at 700×800 the "Export customers" link ends 3 px into the tab's row, so no 43 px box with its foot on the tab's foot is control-free; the compact pill takes the next clear row (REQ-873's order), 8 px under the tab, flush with its edge, and the corridor hold carries the pointer across the gap. The e2e asserts "on the tab's row or the row next to it, flush with the tab", not feet-level. Also fixed: the overlay's `place()` closure is the mount's, so it read a stale `peekCompact` and stored the compact peek's size as the whole pill's (`fullRef`); it now reads the rendered form off the pill (`data-compact`) and the window width directly.
## REQ-892 — A tab whose demo a sign-out dropped rejoins from ANY session-less page (the landing a sign-out lands on, a public page), not only from /login (demo-loop run 6, dm6, issue m3; AMENDMENT of REQ-879)

**Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 6, issue m3):** "you personally go fix the polish problems" — tester 4: customer tabs A (/customers) and B (/settings); log out in B (lands on "/"); log in again in A → /dashboard; select B and click its h1. For 10+ s the stage shows /dashboard and "En vivo" while B — the landing, no session — has no demo elements. Expected: B rejoins like the /login fix, or the stage stops saying Live.

Cause: REQ-879's watcher is installed only by `LoginForm` (/login). DashSidebar's logout sends the tab to "/", and `_app.tsx` mounts no demo code on a page rendered without a session (`hasSession` gates the overlay and the early script), so no session-less page but /login ever noticed the shared cookie coming back to life.

Requirement:
1. When the overlay's signout gate drops a page's demo (`out`: a link or a demo was there), the tab keeps a mark in its sessionStorage (`pm:demo-rejoin`, `markDemoRejoin`), fresh for REJOIN_MARK_MS (30 min). A sign-out in a tab with no demo marks nothing.
2. Every page rendered WITHOUT a session carries a module script of its own (`lib/demo-mode/demo-rejoin.ts`, served like REQ-648's early script: `DEMO_REJOIN_SRC` from the same stand-in, a second input `pm-demo-rejoin` of the browser's build). While the mark is fresh it watches as /login does (`watchLoginRejoin`: focus, the tab shown, a click, a key; one ask a second, GET /api/me) and once signed in again goes to the dashboard from "/" or reloads its own page elsewhere, clearing the mark. That page has the session, mounts the overlay and claims the stage. Without the mark nothing is installed and nothing is asked (an ordinary anonymous visitor). /login, /verify (REQ-879's own watcher) and the stage are left out.

Tests:
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-landing-tab-rejoin.test.ts` ("REQ-892 …", 6 cases: the mark set/fresh/stale/cleared, garbage, a refused store; not on the sign-in pages or the stage; the target ("/" → /dashboard, else itself); startDemoRejoin with and without the mark, the mark cleared on the go; another page reloads itself; wiring of the overlay, the entry script, `_app.tsx`'s `!hasSession` tag, the stand-in and the plugin's two entries in dev and in a build). REQ-648's plugin tests amended for the second input.
- integration: n/a — the stand-in is `null` outside Vite (the plugin writes the URLs), so a Fresh-handler test cannot see the tag; the plugin's dev/build output is asserted directly in the unit wiring test, and the HTTP side (GET /api/me) is REQ-879's unchanged.
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-tab-leave.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-892 …": demo on tab 1 at 1100×780 → Log out → the stage says she signed out, tab 1 is on "/" with no pill → she signs in again in tab 2 (640×760), Live there → tab 1 brought back and clicked goes to /dashboard, shows the pill, and the stage follows it, Live).

## REQ-895 — The stage's last frame after an end mirrors the customer's notice (title · text · ×, nothing cut) and drops the off-frame outline (demo-loop run 6, dm6, issue m6; AMENDMENT of REQ-540 / REQ-838 / REQ-393 / REQ-868)

**Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 6, issue m6):** "you personally go fix the polish problems" — tester 5: the customer presses × then "Sí, terminar"; within 0.5 s the stage's ghost read "Modo demo · Ter… · La demo terminó" while her pill read "Modo demo · Terminaste la demo · ×", and the dashed off-frame outline was still drawn in that last frame.

Cause: (1) the overlay's ended-notice face carried `label` ("La demo terminó"); `ghostWords` drew it as a status chip beside the text, and the chip squeezed the text to "Ter…" (the notice itself has no chip, only a ×). (2) The frame's outline (`mirrored && off`, REQ-393) had no `ended` gate; the chrome-row badges got theirs in REQ-868.

Requirement:
1. The ended-notice face says `notice: true` (PillFace, on the wire: `parsePillFace` keeps the boolean; the overlay's sender and the stage's `faceOf` copy it — both build the face field by field). `ghostWords` on a notice face: the title (not on the compact phone pill), the whole text (also on the compact pill: never the guide's short name), a `dismiss` "×" — no status chip, no End. `pillFaceOffline` keeps the flag, so the ghost stays the notice after her page goes. The stage draws the × (`data-cy=demo-pill-ghost-dismiss`).
1b. The notice reaches the stage. (a) It shows AT ONCE (`pillShowsAtOnce`): it is the overlay's own render, which the page observers ignore, so no mirror frame follows to release a held face (it waited PILL_HOLD_MAX_MS). (b) It is SENT before this side's end: `end()` and `presenterOut()` call `sayEnded` (one face source, `noticeFaceOf`) before `link.end()` / the server call — the stage's socket closes on the server's `ended`, and the face sent after the next render (place() samples the page first) lost that race by ~100 ms in the headless re-check. A layout effect on `notice` re-places the notice element too.
2. The frame's dashed off-frame outline is gone once the demo has ended (`!ended && mirrored && off`).

Tests:
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-stage-ended-frame.test.ts` ("REQ-895 …", 3 cases: ghostWords on a notice face (whole and compact), a status face unchanged; the flag through parsePeerMessage, junk dropped, kept offline; wiring — the overlay's face, the stage's × and the outline gate).
- integration: n/a — pure face logic and a render gate, no request/response.
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-ended.e2e.test.ts` (REQ-235/300 story, added: while the server's answer is held after her Yes, the stage's ghost says "You ended the demo" whole with a × and no status/End chip; after the answer, every sampled frame whose status reads "The demo ended" has `outline-style: none`, until the hop to /admin).

## REQ-896 — The stage knows WHY the customer's page went: a closed tab's hold is "One moment…" (never "Loading their next page…"), and no ghost of her pill is drawn while waiting after a close (demo-loop run 6, dm6, issues p1 + p7; AMENDMENT of REQ-838 / REQ-875 / REQ-391)

**Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 6, issues p1 + p7):** "you personally go fix the polish problems" — p1 (testers 2, 4): closing the customer's only tab showed "Cargando su siguiente página…" for up to 2 s before "Esperando la app de Maria Lopez…" — the label said she was loading a page when the tab was gone. p7 (tester 4): the stage's dimmed ghost of her pill read "Conectando…" under the waiting banner after her page was gone.

Cause: transport.ts `tabLeft` knows the leave's `why` (closing / navigating / signout / nothing said) but `hold`, `startGrace` and `refresh` dropped it, so the stage could not word a closed page differently from a navigation, and `pillFaceOffline(face, "waiting")` made the ghost say "Connecting…".

Requirement:
1. The link carries the reason with every status: `onStatus(s, leave?)` — the followed (or last) tab's leave reason, cleared the moment a tab of hers is here again (`tabSeen`).
2. `stageStatus` takes `leave`: a "between" hold over a mirrored screen is "Loading their next page…" only for a navigation; a close, or nothing said, is the neutral "One moment…" (`pageGone`, `demoMode.pageGone` in en and es). A new tab awaited (`awaiting`) still loads its page; not mirrored is still connecting. The frame is held for `pageGone` as for `loadingNext` (dimmed, his pointer not sent).
3. While waiting after anything but a navigation the stage draws no ghost of her pill (`pillShown`): nothing is connecting; the banner says it is waiting.

Tests:
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-stage-leave-reason.test.ts` ("REQ-896 …", 5 cases: the transport's statuses carry closing / navigating / nothing through between → waiting and clear on her next page; stageStatus's words per reason, with awaiting / not mirrored / waiting / ended unchanged; the two words in en and es; the stage's wiring). REQ-391 (`demo-stage-live.test.ts`) and REQ-648 (`demo-stage-page-latency.test.ts`) tests amended: their "Loading their next page…" cases name a navigation, and a close is pageGone.
- integration: n/a — the hub relays `why` unchanged (REQ-823's int tests); this is client-side wording and a render gate.
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-status-words.e2e.test.ts` — REQ-875 p4 story amended (her only tab closes: the hold says "One moment…", never "Loading their next page…"; once waiting, no ghost of her pill at all) and REQ-838 m5 story amended (an address-bar navigation / reload says "closing": "Un momento…", never "Cargando su siguiente página…"). `e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-live.e2e.test.ts` (REQ-391: an in-app page change still says "Loading their next page…") unchanged, re-run.

## REQ-897 — The folded demo chip's last resort is the control-free spot with the LEAST of the page under it (a heading weighs more than a line), and it holds its spot through a scroll (demo-loop run 6, dm6, issues p4 + p5; AMENDMENT of REQ-853 / REQ-781 / REQ-818)

**Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 6, issues p4 + p5):** "you personally go fix the polish problems" — p4 (tester 4): at 390×844 in Spanish the folded "Demo ×" chip sat at (0,644) over the start of the dashboard's "Termina la configuración — faltan 5 cosas" heading ("Term" hidden). p5 (tester 5): scrolling /settings at 390 px the chip hopped (0,324) → (294,604) → (294,444) → (0,764) → … as text came and went under it; it never covered a control.

Cause: `placePill`'s `tab()` kept the current spot only while NOTHING was under it, and its last resort took the FIRST tab spot with no control under it — never the one with the least of the page under it, and a heading weighed no more than a line of text (`pageUnder` counted distinct pieces).

Requirement:
1. With no tab spot clear of the page, the chip takes, among the spots with no control under them, the one with the least of the page under it (`fewest(open, blocked)`; a tie keeps the spots' order — REQ-853's first-with-no-control when all are equal); the kept spot stays while it is as clear as that. The overlay's `pageUnder` weighs a heading (`HEADING_SELECTOR` = h1, h2, h3, role=heading) `HEADING_WEIGHT` (3): a title is never the first thing covered. A spot with nothing under it still wins outright (REQ-853 unchanged).
2. While the page scrolls (`scrolling`: a scroll event under `PILL_SCROLL_SETTLE_MS` = 500 ms ago, any scroller, `scrollingRef` in the overlay) the kept spot HOLDS — the first cut moved it when a control came under it, and on /settings a field sits in every row, so it hopped on every 40 px step (seen in the e2e); a finger on the page is scrolling, not tapping. Once the events have stopped for PILL_SCROLL_SETTLE_MS the overlay places the pill once more (`scrolling: false`) against what is under it now, so a settled chip is off every control and heading as before.

Tests:
- unit: `jest/unit/demo-pill-tab-spot-choice.test.ts` ("REQ-897 …", 10 cases: the 390×844 fixture; the least-covered control-free spot, not the heading's; a tie keeps the order; a clear spot still wins; the weight and selector; settled vs scrolling with text, with a control, with no kept spot; the overlay's wiring — heading weight in pageUnder, scrollingRef set on scroll and cleared with a final place() after PILL_SCROLL_SETTLE_MS, `scrolling:` passed to placePill). `demo-pill-peek-edge-margin.test.ts` (REQ-849) and `demo-pill-status-words.test.ts` (REQ-838) wiring regexes reconciled with REQ-890 / REQ-896 (the measurement goes through `size`; `pillShown` has REQ-896's waiting gate).
- integration: n/a — pure placement geometry and a scroll flag in the browser; no request/response.
- e2e: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-pill-tab-spot-choice.e2e.test.ts` (new, 390×844 ES, five setup items deferred so the checklist heading is on /dashboard: the folded chip covers no heading and no control there; on /settings a continuous wheel scroll of 30 × 40 px — the chip's box changes zero times during it, and settled it covers no control; `chip-log.json` in the evidence). REQ-853 (`demo-pill-tab-spot`), REQ-545 (`demo-pill-yield`), REQ-866 m2b and REQ-890 (`demo-pill-peek-compact`) re-run green. (REQ-228/291 `demo-pill-clear` and REQ-866 m2 / REQ-876 on /welcome fail on this branch with REQ-897 set aside too — pre-existing, taken up next.)

**Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 6):** "you personally go fix the polish problems" — while re-running the pill lane after REQ-897, REQ-228's e2e (the whole pill covers no control on /dashboard at 1280×800) was red; a bisect through scratch worktrees showed it red at every branch point back to origin/develop. ## REQ-539 AMENDMENT — a `pointerover` the stage gets at load, under a still mouse, is where the mouse was — never a move of his (2026-11-16)

**Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 6):** "you personally go fix the polish problems" — the REQ-539 m24 story (`e2e/demo-mode/demo-presenter-rest.e2e.test.ts`) and REQ-645's "M2, start" / "M2, page change" stories (`demo-pointer-identity.e2e.test.ts`) were red on demo-fixes and at the pre-cycle commit 454b6433 alike: on a desktop customer, the click on Demo lands on the fitted frame and her screen showed his arrow at once (1041, 366 — his mouse at 1030, 478 on the stage), with no move of his; the stage never asked him to "move to show it".
**Cause (probe, headless shell 1208 / Playwright 1.58):** the stage's handler counted every `pointermove` / `pointerover` / `pointerdown` as "a real event says where the mouse is" (REQ-451), on the premise that a page loaded under a still mouse gets no pointer event at all. Chromium DOES fire a trusted `pointerover` (with `pointerenter` and `mouseover`) at the mouse's spot ~40 ms after the stage loads (a throwaway story recorded them: `pointerover` trusted at 1031, 479 at t=43 ms, no `pointermove`), so /admin's hand-off hint was dropped and the spot was pushed as his pointer.
**Requirement:** `pointerCounts(type, moved)` (`front-end/lib/demo-mode/cursor-handoff.ts`): `pointermove` and `pointerdown` always count; `pointerover` counts only once he has moved or pressed on this stage (`movedRef`, reset when the demo changes). Before that, a `pointerover` is where the mouse already was — a hint, as REQ-539 makes /admin's hand-off — and nothing of his reaches her screen until he moves. REQ-539 / REQ-645 (M2) otherwise unchanged.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-stage-pointerover-load.test.ts` ("REQ-539 pointerCounts …", "REQ-539 wiring …") · integration n/a — browser event semantics, no server part · e2e `demo-presenter-rest.e2e.test.ts` "REQ-539 (demo m24)" and `demo-pointer-identity.e2e.test.ts` "REQ-645 (demo cycle 5 M2, start)" / "(M2, page change)" (red → green; m24's wait for `demo-status` also follows REQ-890's compact pill: `pillUp`).
**Evidence (2026-11-16):** RED — `npx jest unit/demo-stage-pointerover-load` → 2 failed (`pointerCounts` not exported; no wiring); the three stories red (m24: "the presenter's arrow showed with no move {x:1041.28,y:366.303}"). GREEN — jest 12 passed (with demo-pointer-seed-origin); `shots run demo-presenter-rest demo-pointer-identity demo-pointer-above-pill` on :5601 → m24 12.9 s ✓, M2 start 7.5 s ✓, M2 page change 9.1 s ✓, c4-M6 ✓, M8 ✓ (REQ-393 M2 tab switch, REQ-645 M1 twin and REQ-831 still red — separate causes, see their entries).

## REQ-907 — Signing out lands on the landing page: a poll's 401 during the sign-out never bounces the tab to /login?next=…

**Source:** Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 6): "you personally go fix the polish problems" — the REQ-834 story (`e2e/demo-mode/demo-stage-tab-leave.e2e.test.ts`) was red on demo-fixes and at the pre-cycle commit 454b6433: after Log out, tab 1 never rested on "/". A throwaway probe with the tab's requests recorded showed the chain: `POST /api/auth/logout` → the overlay's held `GET /api/demo-mode/active?wait=` answered 401 the moment the session died → `GET /` (the sidebar's own navigation) → 9 ms later `GET /login?next=%2Fdashboard`, which replaced it. The user who signs out lands on the login page with a "next", not on the landing.
**Cause:** `front-end/client.ts` patches `fetch` so any 401 from a same-origin /api/* request on an authed app route sends the tab to `/login?next=<here>` (an expired session). A sign-out is not an expired session, and any poll in flight (the demo overlay's /active ask, a topbar count) loses the race to the sidebar's navigation.
**Requirement:** `bounceToLogin({ status, api, authed, signingOut })` (`front-end/lib/signout-bounce.ts`) bounces only when no sign-out has been announced in this tab: client.ts hears `pm:logout` (DashSidebar fires it BEFORE the session dies — its logout and its account switch) and from then on lets every 401 through; the sign-out owns the navigation. An expired session's 401 bounces as before.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/signout-no-login-bounce.test.ts` ("REQ-907 bounceToLogin …", "REQ-907 wiring …") · integration n/a — one tab's fetch patch, no server part · e2e `demo-stage-tab-leave.e2e.test.ts` "REQ-834 / REQ-823 AMENDMENT (dm2, M1)" (red → green: tab 1 rests on "/" after the sign-out).
**Evidence (2026-11-16):** RED — `npx jest unit/signout-no-login-bounce` → Cannot find module `lib/signout-bounce`; the REQ-834 story red at `waitForURL("/")` (20 s), the probe's tab on `/login?next=%2Fdashboard`. GREEN — jest 2 passed; `shots run demo-stage-tab-leave --filter REQ-834` 23 s ✓ on :5601; the probe's tab rests on `http://localhost:5601/` with the stage saying "Ana Torres signed out".

## REQ-908 — Starting or ending an impersonation clears the tab's dash cache

**Source:** Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 7, m4): "you personally go fix the polish problems" — the dm7 testers saw the staff member's own name/profile flash on the first paint of the customer's pages after Demo started (and the customer's on the staff's pages after End), before the real profile replaced it.
**Cause:** `front-end/lib/dash-cache.ts` (REQ-624) keeps the signed-in person's profile in sessionStorage so a page paints from it before `/api/me` answers; an impersonation (`adminClient.impersonate`) and its end (`stopImpersonating`) swap the session but left the previous person's cache in place, so the next page's first paint was the last person's.
**Requirement:** `adminClient.impersonate` and `adminClient.stopImpersonating` (`front-end/clients/admin.ts`) call `clearDashCache()` once the server has answered, so the next page paints the next person's profile from its first frame. Nothing else of REQ-624 changes.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/impersonation-dash-cache.test.ts` ("REQ-908 wiring …") · integration n/a — one tab's client cache, no server part · e2e: covered by the demo-mode lane's stage stories (the staff's /admin after End shows the staff's own name — `demo-viewers` M21, re-run green).
**Evidence (2026-11-16):** RED — `npx jest unit/impersonation-dash-cache` → 1 failed (admin.ts imports no `clearDashCache`); GREEN — 1 passed; `deno lint` / `deno check` clean on clients/admin.ts.

## REQ-451 AMENDMENT 2 — when the page moves under the presenter's still pointer (a scroll, a resize, a layout change) the arrow is drawn WITH its element in that frame — never a glide from where it was (demo-loop run 9, p5)

**Raphael (2026-11-16, demo loop run 9, p5):** two testers scrolled the customer's page with the presenter resting on a field: the arrow trailed its field by up to 85 px through the wheel burst and caught up over ~250 ms — REQ-180's glide (tau 50 ms) was applied to a re-placement that is not a move of his hand.
**Requirement:** `PointerCmd.snap?: boolean` (PeerPointer.tsx); the overlay's `replace()` (every re-placement of a resting anchor after the page moved) calls `place(pid, a, "move", /*shift*/ true)`, which puts `snap: true` on that command only; PeerPointer passes `cmd.snap === true` to `glide.glideTo(at, outside, rect, snap)`; `useGlide.glideTo(…, snap)` cancels any glide in flight and paints the target at once (as a first sight does). His hand's moves and clicks glide as before.

**Raphael (2026-11-16, "you personally go fix the polish problems"):** the REQ-890 story (700×800 on /customers) was red in the lane and alone, at HEAD and at 588005ea: hovered, the chip at (0,560) opened the compact pill flush for one frame at (12,549), then `peekBox` moved it to (252,702) — three rows down, 240 px right, over the empty-state text — the REQ-890 complaint again. The overlay offers `[fullRef, compactSizeRef]` while the pill is folded and NOT during a peek (the open pill's tab never hops from under the pointer).

## REQ-379 AMENDMENT 2 — the customer's pill is compact when the WHOLE pill would be wider than two thirds of the window (not only at or under 640 px); a pill not yet in the window's form is never placed or folded as it is, so the compact form's size is learnt while it is still out; the whole's size rides to the next page (demo-loop lane, REQ-890; by hand)

**Raphael (2026-11-16):** at 700×800 the whole pill is 501–514 px — 72 % of the window: no row of such a window has room for it beside the page's controls (the survey above: a control under the whole's flush box at every tab spot), so every peek had to fall to the compact form, whose size the overlay only learns once a crowded row has shown it. Worse, the switch to the compact form happened inside the same placement that folded the pill in its old form: folded, the compact form was never measured, so the whole's 514 px stood for the pill's size on every page after (carried as REQ-830's `full`), and REQ-890 AMENDMENT 2's choice judged the peek by a form the window would never show.
**Requirement:** `pillCompactForm(viewW, whole)`: compact at or under PILL_COMPACT_MAX_W (REQ-379), or when the whole pill's measured size (`whole`, null until it has rendered once) is wider than PILL_WHOLE_MAX_SHARE = 2/3 of the window — judged on the WHOLE's size only (judged on the compact's it would flip back and forth: `wholeSizeRef` is written by the whole form alone). The overlay's `isNarrow()` is that function over the window and `wholeSizeRef`. `place()`: when the window's form differs from the base form as rendered (`compactBaseRef`), it sets the form and returns — the switch renders first, and that render places the pill (the `[compact]` effect), measured in its new form while still out. REQ-830's carried place gains `whole` (the whole's size), restored before paint, so a reload at 700 px starts compact with the compact's size as its base (`full`).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-pill-tab-peekable.test.ts` describe "REQ-379 AMENDMENT 2 — pillCompactForm" (640 → compact; 700 with 501 → compact, with null or 400 → whole; 1280 with 501 → whole) + wiring (`pillCompactForm(globalThis.innerWidth, wholeSizeRef.current)`, `if (!compactNow) wholeSizeRef.current = size`, the bail-out `const n = isNarrow(); if (n !== compactBaseRef.current) { setCompact(n); return; }`, the carried `whole` restored and written); `jest/unit/demo-pill-carry-place.test.ts` "REQ-379 AMENDMENT 2: the whole pill's size rides along" (+ a malformed `whole` dropped). The three REQ-379/835/852 wiring suites that sliced the island at `setCompact(narrow())` / `useState(narrow)` now slice at `isNarrow` (the same switch under its new name). E2e: the REQ-890 story (above). Integration: n/a.
**Evidence (2026-11-16):** a placement log in the overlay (throwaway, removed) on the reloaded page: before — `rec 67ms tucked=true compact=true … at 604,680` then `(0,560)`, `carried … "full":{"w":514,"h":43},"whole":{"w":514,"h":43}`, `peek=[{"w":514,"h":43}]`; after — `rec 55ms tucked=false compact=true 297x43`, `carried … "full":{"w":297,"h":43},"whole":{"w":514,"h":43}`, `peek=[{"w":297,"h":43}]`, the chip at (604,480), the story ✓. jest green (577 suites).

**Requirement:** `ghostFade(f, at, now)` (shared/demo-mode/presenter-anchor.ts): a move of at least `GHOST_FADE_MOVE_PX` (2) while the fade is still running (`now - f.since < GHOST_FADE_MS`, 250 — pmDemoGhostIn's length) gives a new `key` and resets the fade's clock at the new spot; after the fade a move keeps the key (the drawn ghost slides, no flash); a sub-pixel jitter is not a move. PointerGhost keeps that state in a ref and keys its fading element by it, so a mid-fade move remounts the element and its animation at the new spot.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/demo-stage-ghost-rest.test.ts` describe "REQ-789 AMENDMENT (demo-loop run 12, p1)": the tester's numbers (545.9 → 469.3 at +83 ms → key 1, clock reset; → 462.4 → key 2); a move after the fade keeps key 0 and the clock; a 1.1 px jitter returns the same state; wiring — `fadeRef.current = ghostFade(…)` and `key={fadeRef.current.key}` on the ghost's element. Integration: n/a. E2e: n/a — a 250 ms opacity ramp under headless frame pacing (~6 fps with two pages open, the house note) cannot be sampled faithfully; the unit cases carry the tester's own numbers.
**Evidence (2026-11-17):** RED — jest with presenter-anchor.ts / PointerGhost.tsx at HEAD (8f331add): `TypeError: ghostFade is not a function` ×3 and the wiring pattern missing. GREEN — jest 578 suites, 5795 passed.

## REQ-890 AMENDMENT 3 — a peek opens with its details closed; "more" during a peek opens them for that peek; a peek takes a box clear of controls AND words when one exists (demo-loop run 14, m2 + p1; by hand)

**Raphael (2026-11-17, demo loop run 14, tester 4):** m2 — the pill the customer opened from its folded "Demo" tab at 390 px was the two-row (73 px) form with its details and sat at (12,115) over "Step 2 of 10" (143–163) and the card's top edge for 3 s and more; p1 — "once the customer opens the pill at 390, it stays in the two-row form (73 px) on every later page". ## REQ-890 AMENDMENT 6 — REVISION: Keep going's guard goes with the mouse on a whole pill too (demo-loop run 17, m2; by hand)

**Raphael (2026-11-17):** tester 5 (×4) and tester 3: after Seguir the first click on End was swallowed even after the mouse had left the pill and come back — on a WHOLE pill (1280 px, no peek). Two causes: the pointer-move listener that clears the approach was the peek's alone, and the pointer's position (`pointRef`) on a whole pill was only the one seen entering it, so the guard's point was stale (on the Mac the in-place click asked again instead). The Keep going effect now installs its own document pointermove listener until the approach ends, and the pill keeps `pointRef` current on every pointer move over it.
**Tests:** unit (run 17 block: the listener; `onPointerMove` on the pill); e2e `demo-pill-approach-guard` (1280×800 ES /dashboard, the whole pill: Seguir → the click in place does not ask; away to (700,300), back onto End in 5 steps, 1.2 s rest, click → asks).
**Evidence (2026-11-17):** story ✗ at 9e649768 (scratch worktree :5611): `the click where the mouse rests after Seguir is not End's ({"box":[597,418,671,43],…,"under":"demo-end-cancel","asking":true})` → GREEN at the fix (3 pass).

### REQ-235 AMENDMENT — Yes counts at once when the press that asked is not on it (demo-loop run 18, m1; 2026-11-17)
In the owner's words (the loop): "Customer's first click on 'Sí, terminar' does nothing after opening the question from the folded tab's ×" — at 1280×800 the × asked, the mouse travelled ~820 px to Sí and clicked ~400 ms later; nothing happened, 2 of 2. Cause: Yes waits END_ARM_MS (400 ms) so a double click on End never ends a demo — measured from the question's effect (~480 ms after the × click, the arming clock starting in the mounted question's effect), while a double click's second click lands where the first did, never 820 px away. Rule: a Yes farther than END_PRESS_NEAR_PX (12 px) from the press that asked arms at once (`yesArmsAtOnce`, `EndConfirm.arm()`); a press on or near Yes, no press known (the keyboard, a stale one) or Yes not laid out keeps the clock. EndDemo records End's own press; the customer's pill hands it the ×'s press (REQ-876's `endPressRef`, fresh within 5 s) as `pressedAt`.
- Unit: `jest/unit/demo-run18-polish.test.ts` (yesArmsAtOnce cases, endConfirm.arm(), EndDemo + overlay wiring). RED→GREEN: 6 of 583 suites red on the stale regexes (run15/run16/leave-reason/actor-name/end-ask-compact; REVISION notes added) → 583/583 green.
- Integration: n/a — the arming is the pill's own component state.
- E2E: `e2e/demo-mode/demo-run18-polish.e2e.test.ts` "REQ-235 AMENDMENT (demo-loop run 18, m1)". RED at 964a2df9 (the click 385 ms after the ×: Yes still disabled, the pill asking, the stage "En vivo"); GREEN after the change (the demo ends on the first click).

### REQ-890 AMENDMENT 6 REVISION 2 — an approach is over once the pointer has rested a second (demo-loop run 18, m2; 2026-11-17)
The tester (demo 4): the mouse reached the tab in five steps, the peek opened with End under it, five more small steps (~5 px) and a full second's rest — the click was still "the tab's" (nothing visible happened; the second click asked). AMENDMENT 6 judged only by distance (within PEEK_HOVER_CLICK_PX of where the approach ended). Rule: an approach carries `since` (its last continuous move, or Keep going) and is over once the pointer has rested PEEK_APPROACH_REST_MS (1000 ms) there — `approachRested`; the pill's End guard and the peek's tab-click guard judge a click by `approachClaims` (not rested, within the tolerance). ## REQ-899 — `communications` module: texting on the business's own Twilio line (send, receive, delivery status, threads)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-16 ("I just added a new Twilio account … implement the feature for texting and the feature for voice into v2 … put it in a module called communications"). Context from the same conversation: he wants his own application shell instead of Quo, on Twilio, with his own voice agent.
**Requirement:** A new backend module `backend/src/communications/` (a sibling of `communication`, deliberately not merged into it) on a NEW Twilio account read from `COMMS_TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` / `COMMS_TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` / `COMMS_TWILIO_FROM` (never the OTP account's `TWILIO_*`). `POST /communications/texts` sends an SMS from the line to an E.164 peer and records it; Twilio's inbound-message webhook (`POST /communications/twilio/sms`) records an inbound text and answers empty TwiML; the status webhook (`POST /communications/twilio/sms-status`) updates delivery state (queued → sent → delivered | undelivered | failed, with the Twilio error code). `GET /communications/threads` lists one thread per peer number, newest first, with the last preview and an unread count; `GET /communications/threads/:peer` returns the thread's texts and calls and marks it read. Every Twilio webhook is unauthenticated for sessions but refuses (403) any request whose `X-Twilio-Signature` does not validate (HMAC-SHA1 of the public URL + sorted form params with the auth token); the public URL is rebuilt from `COMMS_PUBLIC_URL` because the app sits behind a proxy. Without `COMMS_TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` the sender runs in dev mode (logs, no dispatch), like the OTP `SmsService`.
**Decision, mine (not asked for):** v1 is one line for the whole business: threads and calls carry `line` (our E.164) and are visible to every authenticated user; per-user lines are additive later. Phone numbers are normalized with the existing `normalizePhone`.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/communications/domain/business/twilio-signature/test.ts` (Twilio's published vector `0/KCTR6DLpKmkAf8muzZqo1nDgQ=`, tamper → false, missing header → false); int `backend/src/communications/domain/coordinators/*/int.test.ts` (send records + dispatches through a capturing Twilio seat; receive/status with a signed and an unsigned request; thread listing/unread); e2e `backend/src/communications/entrypoints/e2e.test.ts` (booted app: login, send in dev mode, signed inbound webhook, thread shows both, unsigned webhook → 403).

## REQ-900 — `communications` voice: a browser softphone on the line (token, outbound dial, inbound ring, status, recordings, call log)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-16 (same request: "the feature for voice").
**Requirement:** `POST /communications/voice/token` mints a Twilio Voice access token (HS256 JWT, `cty: twilio-fpa;v=1`, `iss` = `COMMS_TWILIO_API_KEY_SID`, `sub` = account SID, voice grant with `incoming.allow` and `outgoing.application_sid` = `COMMS_TWILIO_TWIML_APP_SID`, identity = the user's id, TTL 1 h) so the front-end can run Twilio's Voice JS SDK. Twilio webhooks: `POST /communications/twilio/voice/outgoing` (the TwiML App URL: the softphone dialed a number → `<Dial callerId=line><Number>`, call recorded as outbound); `POST /communications/twilio/voice/incoming` (the line was called → thread upserted, call recorded as inbound, TwiML rings the softphone identities for 20 s with `action` → unanswered); `POST /communications/twilio/voice/unanswered` (the Dial result: an answered call hangs up; otherwise exactly one fallback arm per `COMMS_FALLBACK` — `agent` → `<Connect><ConversationRelay>`, `voicemail` → `<Record>`, `forward` → `<Dial>` to `COMMS_FORWARD_TO`, `hangup`; default voicemail; `forward` without a number degrades to voicemail); `POST /communications/twilio/voice/status` and `/voice/recording` patch the call (status, duration, recording SID/URL). `GET /communications/calls` is the log newest first, `GET /communications/calls/:id` one call with its transcript. Every webhook is signature-checked as in REQ-899.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/communications/domain/business/voice-token/test.ts` (header/claims/grant shape, HMAC verifies, TTL, identity charset), `backend/src/communications/domain/business/twiml/test.ts` (every verb builder, XML escaping), `backend/src/communications/domain/business/fallback/test.ts` (the one-arm rule); int `backend/src/communications/domain/coordinators/*/int.test.ts` (incoming/outgoing/unanswered/status/recording against an in-memory KV); e2e `backend/src/communications/entrypoints/e2e.test.ts` (token endpoint returns a decodable JWT; signed incoming webhook answers Dial/Client TwiML and the call appears in the log).

## REQ-901 — `communications` voice agent: the line's own AI receptionist over Twilio ConversationRelay
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-16 ("do my own voice agent").
**Requirement:** `GET /communications/voice/relay` is the ConversationRelay WebSocket. Twilio sends JSON frames (`setup`, `prompt{voicePrompt,lang,last}`, `interrupt{utteranceUntilInterrupt}`, `dtmf{digit}`, `error`); the server answers `{"type":"text","token":…,"last":true}` and `{"type":"end"}`. The brain is the module's `LLMClient` (the agents module's seam: OpenAI when `AGENTS_LLM_CLIENT=openai`, the stub otherwise) with a system prompt from `COMMS_AGENT_PROMPT` (default: a receptionist for the business that takes the caller's name, number and reason and promises a call back). A finished caller turn (`last:true`) asks the LLM once; partial prompts are ignored; an interrupt truncates the stored assistant turn to what was actually heard; a DTMF digit is a turn ("pressed 1"); the reply token `[END_CALL]` ends the session; a session ends itself after 40 caller turns. Every turn is appended to the call's transcript in KV; `POST /communications/twilio/voice/relay-done` (the `<Connect>` action) stores the session status/handoff and hangs up.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/communications/domain/business/relay/test.ts` (the pure protocol state machine: setup, partial vs final prompt, interrupt truncation, dtmf, end marker, turn cap, unknown frames); int `backend/src/communications/domain/coordinators/relay-session/int.test.ts` (a scripted socket + stub LLM: tokens sent, transcript persisted, end frame); e2e n/a — Twilio must originate the websocket; verified by hand on the first real call (log the evidence here).

## REQ-903 — `communications` lines: every customer gets their own number on a Twilio subaccount we create for them, bought from inside the app
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-16 ("let's do sub-accounts, but they won't have to make accounts, will they?" — no: we create the subaccount by API under our main Twilio account; the customer never sees Twilio, and all usage bills to us).
**Requirement:** `GET /communications/numbers/available?areaCode=843` (or `contains=`) lists purchasable US local numbers with voice + SMS from Twilio's inventory. `POST /communications/numbers` `{phoneNumber, friendlyName?}` provisions the signed-in user's LINE in one coordinator: create a subaccount named for the user, create an API key and a TwiML App (Voice URL → our `voice/outgoing` webhook) inside it, buy the number into it with Voice URL → `voice/incoming`, SMS URL → `twilio/sms`, status callback → `voice/status`, and store the line `{userId, subaccountSid, number, numberSid, apiKeySid, twimlAppSid, friendlyName, status}` with the subaccount auth token and the API key secret SEALED with the repo's secret-box (REQ-212's AES-GCM under `SECRETS_KEY`) — never in clear in KV, never in any response. A user has at most one active line (409 on a second buy). `GET /communications/line` returns the user's line, redacted (no secrets), or 404. If a step after the subaccount fails, the coordinator closes the subaccount it created and reports the Twilio reason (502).
**Decision, mine (not asked for):** one line per user for now (a second line is a later product decision); numbers are US local only; the subaccount's friendly name is `documonster:<userId>` so the Twilio console stays searchable.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/communications/domain/business/numbers/test.ts` (the search query and the mapping of Twilio's inventory rows; the redaction of a line); int `backend/src/communications/domain/coordinators/lines/int.test.ts` (provision through a capturing Twilio seat: the four calls in order with the right URLs, secrets sealed in KV and absent from the result, second buy → 409, a failed buy closes the subaccount); e2e `backend/src/communications/entrypoints/e2e.test.ts` (search + buy against the local Twilio stand-in; `GET /communications/line` is redacted).

## REQ-904 — Every communications request resolves to ONE line: the signed-in user's for the app, the subaccount's for Twilio's webhooks
**Source:** same conversation (multi-tenant follows from subaccounts).
**Requirement:** Authenticated endpoints (texts, threads, calls, the softphone token) act on the user's active line; with no line they answer 409 `no_line` (texts) or an empty list / 503 (token). Twilio webhooks resolve the line from the request's `AccountSid` (a subaccount SID → that line; the main account SID → the env line) BEFORE the signature check, and verify the signature with THAT line's auth token; an unknown AccountSid is 403. The softphone token is minted with the line's API key and `sub` = the subaccount SID; inbound calls ring the line owner's identity (their user id). The env line (`COMMS_TWILIO_*`, Mallard's recruiting number today) belongs to the user named by `COMMS_ENV_LINE_OWNER`; nobody else can use it. The single-line behaviour of REQ-899/900 is preserved for that owner.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/communications/domain/business/line-resolution/test.ts` (which AccountSid maps to which line, env owner rule); int `backend/src/communications/domain/coordinators/line-context/int.test.ts` (user→line, webhook→line with the right token, unknown → forbidden, no line → `NoLineError` 409); e2e `backend/src/communications/entrypoints/e2e.test.ts` (a second user cannot see the first user's threads; a webhook with the subaccount's SID verifies with the subaccount token, not the main one).

## REQ-920 — Texting registration (A2P 10DLC) from the Phone page
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-17: "there's no place to do the A2P 10DLC registration … I just don't know that this is complete." Facts read from the Twilio account (read-only, 2026-11-17): the main account's business profile "MONSTER RESERVATIONS GROUP" is twilio-approved as a `direct_customer` (not ISV); it has an APPROVED STANDARD brand and VERIFIED campaigns (CUSTOMER_CARE on the "Monster Recruiting" service, MARKETING on another); his new number sits in a subaccount, which has no registration of its own. Twilio's rules: a number on a subaccount needs its own brand + campaign through the ISV flow (a secondary customer profile under an ISV-type primary profile), and a number moved to the main account can join a main-account messaging service whose campaign is verified.
**Requirement:** (a) **Customers (ISV path):** the Phone page's **Texting registration** panel takes the business's details once — legal name, EIN, business type, industry, website, address, authorized representative, use case, how people opt in, 2–5 sample messages, opt-in/opt-out/help copy — and the backend walks Twilio's ISV API on the line's subaccount: secondary customer profile (policy `RNdfbf3fae0e1107f8aded0e7cead80bf5`: business EndUser, representative EndUser, Address → supporting document, assignment to the primary profile, evaluation, submit), A2P trust product (policy `RNb0d4771c2c98518d916a3d4cd70a8f8b`), brand registration, a messaging service (inbound URL = our SMS webhook), the campaign (`Compliance/Usa2p`), and the number added to the service. The panel shows each step's status (profile → brand → campaign, with Twilio's `errors` when a step fails), refreshes on open and on "Check status", and texting from a subaccount line is allowed only once the campaign is VERIFIED (a text before that is refused with one line saying so). (b) **The platform's own line (house path, super admins only):** instead of a new brand, the number moves to the main account (Twilio's AccountSid transfer with the main credentials), gets a main-account API key + TwiML App for the softphone, and joins one of the main account's messaging services with a VERIFIED campaign (picked from a list); its webhooks are set on the number; the line record becomes `kind: "main"` and webhooks for the main account resolve by the `To` number before falling back to the env line. (c) When the primary profile is not ISV-type, the customer panel says so in one line — "Twilio has to mark the platform's business profile as ISV Reseller or Partner before customer lines can be registered" — and the form stays usable up to that step. (d) The Systems tab's Phone & text card shows the registration state (Not registered / In review / Registered). (e) Both dictionaries. Fees: Twilio bills brand and campaign registration to the platform's account; the panel says so before submit.
**Decision, mine:** registration state lives in KV per line (`comms_a2p`, by line id) with every Twilio SID; statuses are polled through Twilio's GETs (Event Streams later). The house path is super-admin only because only Monster's own business may text under Monster's brand.
**Tests:** (a) unit `backend/src/communications/domain/business/a2p/test.ts` (form → Twilio attributes, status reduction, the gate), int `backend/src/communications/domain/coordinators/a2p-registration/int.test.ts` (the walk against a TrustHub/Messaging stand-in, statuses, failures mid-way, refresh), e2e `e2e/communications/a2p.e2e.test.ts` (the panel: fill, submit, statuses, the ISV-prerequisite line), `jest/unit/a2p-panel.test.ts`; (b) int `backend/src/communications/domain/coordinators/house-line/int.test.ts` (transfer + key + app + service join against the stand-in; non-admin 403), unit `line-resolution/test.ts` AMENDED (main-account webhook by `To`); (d) `jest/unit/settings-systems-tab.test.ts` AMENDED.

The by-hand registration check is the Prod line below.

**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-18: "on the invoice it says 'check accepted' it should say 'send to' <address>". Cause: `payOptionLines` (REQ-629) printed "Check accepted" whenever checks were on and the check's own "mail to" was blank, and printed "Mail to: …" when it was filled.
