## REQ-925 — English only in Settings means nothing goes out in Spanish: no invoice, quote, page or message
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-18: "if i send an invoice, sometimes its in spanish. if in settings english is only selected it should not be possible to get an invoice quote or comunication that is in spanish. because only english is selected. hotfix plz."
**Cause (read from the code, reproduced RED below):** the one outbound resolution, `resolveCommsLanguage` (`shared/quote-flow/comms-language.ts`), went per-send pick → the customer's own language (REQ-715) → the stored default `commsLanguage` → en, and never looked at Settings → "Languages you send in" (`identity.commsLanguages`). So a customer marked Spanish, a Spanish pick in the send sheet, a stale `commsLanguage: "es"` left behind after Spanish was unticked, or an invoice's stored `lang` sent Spanish from an English-only account. The send sheet's "Sends in" also always offered the app language and the customer's language (REQ-715 / `sendLangChoices`), and the public pages /i, /q, /co followed the visitor's `?lang=` / `pm_lang` cookie / browser language and always showed EN | ES.
**Requirement:** When the account has stored send-in languages, every customer-facing output uses only those: (a) `resolveCommsLanguage` takes `sendLanguages` and never returns a language outside them (a disallowed pick, customer language or default falls through; else the set's first). Every dispatcher passes the identity's set: quote/invoice email + text, both send previews, overdue reminders, payment receipts (email + PDF), change-order requests, the signed confirmation (email + PDF), Field customer texts and inquiry replies. (b) `BusinessIdentityStore` reads and writes `commsLanguage` clamped to the set, so every direct `ident.commsLanguage` reader (PDF renderers, job details) follows. (c) The public projections clamp `docLang` (invoice + quote) and the change order's language, and hand the pages `sendLanguages`; /i, /i/:id/pay, /co and /q render only in the set (whatever `?lang=`, `pm_lang` or Accept-Language say) and show no EN | ES switch when there is one language. (d) The app's send sheets (quote + invoice) and the assistant's "Preview in" offer and start on only the set's languages. With both ticked, or no set stored, REQ-715 / UX-28 behave as before.

Each row bills that service once (quantity 1) at its price. Saving with a row that has no service, or no price above $0, is refused with one line ("Pick a service on every line." / "Give every service a price above $0."). ## REQ-927 — Services migrate into another service as a segment that can be undone, redone or moved on — so a service can be deleted without breaking anything
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-18: "in services we need a way to migrate services to another and segment it out so we can undo redo or move that segment to another spot, this way we are able to delete services without fucking up the integrity of the system." Asked and answered the same day: everything moves, history included ("Everything, incl. history"); a segment "means that if something used to be x and we migrate to y we mark records as belonging to x before"; undo after the old service was deleted brings it back ("Yes, undo brings A back").
**Requirement:** (a) On /field/services every card has **Move to…**: pick another live service; every record on the old one moves to it — repeat-visit rows, checklist rows, every task (done and invoiced ones too) and the crews' service lists — and "Delete <old> once nothing uses it" (on by default) deletes it. (b) Each moved row carries a mark `migratedFrom: [{ typeId, migrationId }]` (a stack — the last is the latest), and the move is saved as a segment (`ServiceMigration`, KV `field_service_migration`) listing the exact records, the rows merged away (a record that already had the target keeps its own row; the old row is kept on the segment and comes back on undo, at its place) and what happened to each crew ("replaced" / "dropped"). (c) A **Moves** list on the page shows each segment (old → new, "deleted" when the old one is gone, what it holds in singular/plural) with **Undo** (the records go back; a deleted old service comes back under its own id and name), **Redo** (the same records move again) and **Move to…** (the same records go on to another service; they stay marked as the old one). (d) Integrity: all-or-nothing per action; a crew whose only service would vanish (the target belongs to another crew) refuses the move (`migration_crew_conflict`, with the crew's name); a segment whose records were moved again by a later one refuses undo until that one is undone (`segment_superseded`); a deleted old service whose name was taken since refuses undo (`undo_name_taken`); same service 400, archived target 400, nothing to move 409; editing a repeat visit or a checklist keeps its rows' marks; open generated work from today on the services involved re-derives so a day never doubles. DELETE of a service now also counts the crews that list it (`detail.crews`), and the in-use message points at Move to…. (e) Both dictionaries. API: `POST /field/task-types/:id/migrate { toId, deleteAfter? }` → 201, `GET /field/service-migrations`, `POST /field/service-migrations/:id/undo|redo`, `POST /field/service-migrations/:id/move { toId }`.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/service-migration/test.ts` (6: migrate / crews / undo + redo / only the segment's records / move from applied and from undone / superseded) · int `backend/src/field/entrypoints/service-migration.int.test.ts` (the full HTTP walk: in-use counts with crews, migrate, marks kept through a PUT, delete, undo restores the deleted service by id, redo, move, no doubled day, migrate + delete, another account 403/empty); `field.int.test.ts` REQ-839 AMENDED (`detail.crews: 0`) · jest `jest/unit/service-migration-page.test.ts` (keys en/es, no jargon, singular counts, the client's five calls, the page's controls and refusal codes) · e2e `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` "REQ-927: Move to… …" (and REQ-839's story AMENDED: "or archive it").

## REQ-926 — Chargeback a payment (with a fee, its default in Settings); no more "In transit"
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-18, on A2Z in prod: a payment recorded on a Paper invoice (REQ-922) "says its in transit, but there is no way to mark it as delivered." Then: "lets remove the in transit, add to the payment a 'chargeback' button … add a default fee in the settings and a modal when the chargeback is clicked to add a fee with the default populated. hotfix this. we can then delete in transit." Found (develop `43a515f2`): `front-end/islands/PaymentsPage.tsx` `deriveStatus` made every check "In transit" for 5 days and every ACH for 2, from the method and the age alone — nothing was stored, and nothing could clear it.
**Requirement:** (a) /payments has no In transit: every recorded payment is Landed. (b) Every payment card has **Chargeback** (`pay-card-chargeback`). It opens a modal (`chargeback-modal`) with a fee box (`chargeback-fee`) prefilled with Settings' **Chargeback fee** and an optional reason; Confirm (`chargeback-confirm`) calls `POST /payments/:id/chargeback { feeCents, reason? }`. (c) The server keeps the payment, stamped `reversedAt` / `reversedReason` / `reversedFeeCents`. A reversed payment counts toward no balance, total or report: the invoice's balance is recomputed, so a paid invoice reopens and goes back to owing on its own number and link. A fee > 0 is added to that invoice as its own line ("Chargeback fee" / "Cargo por contracargo", flagged `chargebackFor: <paymentId>`, untaxed): subtotal and amount rise by the fee, and an amount-only invoice first gets its amount as one line. The customer is not notified. A second chargeback on the same payment → 409 `already_reversed`; another owner's payment → 404. (d) `POST /payments/:id/chargeback/undo` takes the stamp and the fee line away and recomputes the balance. ## REQ-924 — Customer workspace: the Customers menu lists the customers, each customer is a full page where everything is done
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-18, for a client: "what he would like to see is that you can do everything in the customer tab. meaning that send invoice, see how much they owe etc. so on the left side there are customers on the context aware menu. then each is a full page on the main screen." — then "what about recurring services?", then "remove the search … the app layout is a left bar, a top bar, and a main screen, cannot edit this layout … you cannot remove the search [in the top bar] but everything else. that is a context aware search so use the search bar there." Approved mockup: `customer-workspace-mock` (2026-11-18), "love it, build it into the app".
**Requirement:**
(a) **Left bar — the Customers context.** On `/customers` and `/customers/<id>` the sidebar shows the Customers context instead of the root: **Back** (to the root menu), the label "Customers" with the count, **All customers** (`/customers`, the existing board), **New customer** (`/customers?new=1`, opens the existing customer form), then one row per customer → `/customers/<id>`: the customer's initials, name, and a status line — "$X overdue" (pink) when an invoice is past due, else "Owes $X", else "🔁 <schedule>" when a repeat visit is active, else "Paid up". Rows are ordered most overdue first, then most owed, then by name. The open customer's row is the active (green) row. The root's Customers row stays a link to `/customers`. No search box in the sidebar. Collapsed rail: initials only.
(b) **Top bar.** The layout is unchanged (left bar, top bar, main screen). On customer pages the top bar shows the menu button, the search and the EN/ES switch — no greeting, no activity ticker. The search is context-aware: a **Customers** chip sits in it (× or Backspace on an empty box searches everything again); results for the open customer come first under "In <name>"; a customer result opens `/customers/<id>` (outside the Customers context the search is unchanged).
(c) **Main screen — `/customers/<id>`**, one customer, everything on one page: a header (initials, name, phone, email, address) with **Send invoice** (the one solid primary), **Record payment**, **New quote** (outlined) and **More** (Send a text, Start recurring service, Edit details). A money summary on every tab: **They owe you** (with the overdue part and a Remind button, or "All paid up"), **Billed** (lifetime, issued invoices), **Paid to you** (with the last payment), **Recurring** ($/month of active services, next visit, done-but-unbilled amount) and **Open quotes**. Tabs: **Overview** (unpaid invoices, recurring services, open quotes, details, activity, notes), **Invoices**, **Quotes**, **Payments**, **Recurring** (each service: services + prices per visit, schedule, address, ≈$/month, terms, the next visits from the schedule, recent visits, done-not-billed with **Bill now**, Pause/Resume, Edit; then the visit history), **Jobs** (work orders), **Messages** (the phone thread with the customer, compose a text; a link to set up the line when there is none).
(d) **Actions reuse the app's flows, never a copy:** Send invoice = the Invoices page's new-invoice form with the customer chosen; Record payment / Mark paid = the payment form on the chosen open invoice; Remind = the invoice send sheet for that invoice (AMENDED by REQ-1031: Remind = the invoice's reminder nudge (REQ-021/477)); New quote = an assistant conversation bound to the customer; Start recurring service / Edit = the Repeat visits form, prefilled with the customer (`/field/subscriptions?new=1&customerId=<id>`); Bill now = the visits batch pull for this customer only, then send its draft; Pause/Resume = the subscription's active flag; Edit details = the customer form. After an action the page re-reads the workspace.
(e) **API.** `GET /customers/:id/workspace` (the owner's session; 404 for another account's or a deleted customer) returns the customer's card plus `summary` (owedCents, overdueCents, billedCents, paidCents, lastPayment, openQuotes + openQuotesCents, recurringMonthlyCents, activeServices, nextVisit, unbilledVisits + unbilledCents), `invoices`, `quotes`, `payments`, `services` (with perVisitCents, monthlyCents and the next visits by the schedule), `visits` (the last year and next 60 days) and `workOrders`. `POST /field/batches/pull` takes an optional `customerId` and then drafts only that customer's visits.
(f) Both dictionaries carry every string (`customerWs.*`).
**Decision, mine:** `/customers` keeps the existing board as "All customers" (its tests stand); the stories that used `/customers` only as a shell page to exercise the root menu start from `/dashboard` instead (AMENDMENT to their setup, not their intent). Monthly ≈ weekly × weeks-per-month ÷ interval, monthly × days, annual ÷ 12. Skipping or moving one visit stays on the Tasks page.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/analytics/domain/business/customer-workspace/test.ts` (summary math, monthly estimate per cadence, next visits by the schedule, unbilled visits, overdue) · unit `jest/unit/customer-workspace.test.ts` (sidebar rows: order + status line; scoped search ordering and customer-hit url; the route → island wiring; the client paths; both dictionaries) · int `backend/src/analytics/entrypoints/clients-controller/workspace.int.test.ts` (the workspace of a seeded customer; 404 for another account) · int `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field-controllers/pull-customer.int.test.ts` (pull with customerId drafts only that customer) · e2e `e2e/customer-workspace/customer-workspace.e2e.test.ts` (sidebar lists the customers with their balances, a row opens the full page with the money summary, Record payment lowers what they owe, the top-bar search is scoped and puts the open customer first; Recurring: the service with its price and next visits, a done visit not billed, Bill now sends her invoice, Pause/Resume, Start recurring service opens the prefilled form).

## REQ-929 — Settings: sign out after inactivity
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-18: "in settings add an inactivity timer, this way it logs the user out if they are not using it."
**Requirement:** (a) Settings → Account has a **Security** card with "Sign out after inactivity": Never, 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 2 hours, 4 hours. It saves on change through `PUT /me { idleLogoutMinutes }` (one of 0, 15, 30, 60, 120, 240; anything else is a 400). It is the person's own setting: an editor acting in someone's account writes her record, never the owner's, and `/me` / `/profile` carry hers on `actor.idleLogoutMinutes`. Unset reads as Never, so no existing account changes until someone picks a time. (b) On every signed-in app page, when the person's setting is above 0 and nobody has touched the app (pointer, key, touch, scroll, wheel) in ANY of the browser's tabs for that long, the tab signs out the way the sidebar does (`pm:logout`, the dash cache cleared, `POST /api/auth/logout`, so the server session is gone) and lands on `/login?idle=1`, which says "You were signed out after a period of inactivity." (c) One minute before, a banner says "You'll be signed out in 0:59 for inactivity" with a **Stay signed in** button; any activity resets the timer and hides it. (d) A change in Settings applies at once, without a reload. Both dictionaries.
**Decision, mine:** the default is Never (opt-in) so nobody already in the field is signed out mid-job by surprise. Activity is shared across tabs through `localStorage` (`pm:idle-last`), so a person working in one tab is not signed out of another.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/idle-logout.test.ts` ("REQ-929 …" — choices, the person's own minutes, the timer's phases, the countdown, the shared stamp; Settings card, shell mount, /login notice, both dictionaries) · int `backend/src/users/entrypoints/me-controller/idle-logout.int.test.ts` ("REQ-929 …" — PUT /me stores and /me + /profile read it; 45 / -15 / "30" / 15.5 / null → 400; an editor's is hers on `actor.idleLogoutMinutes`, the owner's untouched) · e2e `e2e/idle-logout/idle-logout.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-929 …" — Playwright's fake clock: pick 15 on Settings, PUT /me 200, no reload; at 14:01 the banner counts down, Stay signed in hides it; 15:01 later the tab is on /login?idle=1 with the notice and GET /api/me is 401).
**Evidence (2026-11-18):** RED — `npx jest unit/idle-logout.test.ts` → `Tests: 9 failed, 9 total`; `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/users/entrypoints/me-controller/idle-logout.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 3 failed` ("45 → 200", stored `undefined`). GREEN — jest file `Tests: 9 passed`; the users me-controller + account-admins files `ok | 42 passed | 0 failed`; `deno task test:unit` → deno `ok | 1778 passed | 0 failed`, jest `Tests: 1 skipped, 6050 passed, 6051 total`; `deno task test:int` → `1316 passed | 1 failed`, the one REQ-803 square-pay (the known parallel-lane flake; alone `ok | 7 passed | 0 failed`); `shots run` of REQ-929 + 16 Settings/login neighbours against `PORT=5441 deno task serve` → `21 pass · 1 fail`, the fail REQ-631 person-lang ("her dashboard is rendered in Spanish by the server"), which fails identically against a pristine origin/develop `8daa2268` server (:5445). ## REQ-942 — LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-1: two alternatives the contractor types are never added into one total the customer signs
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". Issue **q1-1** [major/BUG_HARM], cycle 1: QA2 asked for "two options: option A basic subway tile $9,800, option B large format porcelain + niche + glass door $13,450"; the draft added both lines into Total $23,250.00 (option A also read "porcelain"), the email and /q showed AGREEMENT VALUE $23,250.00 with no picker, and signing bound the customer to both, with the 20% deposit and INV-001 ($4,650) computed from the sum.
**Root cause:** nothing in the quote pipeline can represent "alternatives, the customer picks one". The chat model's only drafting tool, `create_quote` (backend/src/agents/domain/business/openai-tools/mod.ts), is a flat `lineItems[]` of `{description, amountCents}`; the quote prompt (`lang/en.json` `prompts.systemQuote`, used by `SYSTEM_PROMPT_QUOTE`) has no rule for customer-facing alternatives, and its "Tile bathroom 80 sqft" example answers "(80 sqft, porcelain)", teaching a default material; the coordinator's pre-save guards (`statedTotalCents` → undefined for this message, `settleCreateQuote`) do not recognise alternatives, so HandleChatMessage saves both lines on one draft; `quoteTotalCents` (shared/documents/ledger.ts) sums every line, and the agreement value, deposit and INV-001 all read that sum.
**Requirement:** a message that names alternatives (option A / option B, "two options", "dos opciones", "opción A/B") is never saved as one quote whose total adds them; the reply and card never name the summed total; the quote prompt says alternatives are never added together, and its examples put no material on a line that the contractor did not type.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/llm-prompts/alternatives.test.ts` ("REQ-942 …": the alternatives rule; the tile example without "porcelain") · int `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/alternatives.int.test.ts` ("REQ-942 …": the tester's exact en message and an es version, stub LLM answering two lines of 980000 + 1345000 → no saved quote totals 2325000, the reply/card never says $23,250) · e2e n/a — the trigger is the model's create_quote answer; the e2e server runs the echo stub LLM and a browser story has no hook to script the backend's model, and the customer-side harm (/q, deposit, INV-001) follows only from the saved total the int test pins.
**Evidence (red, 2026-11-18, at 16e7e33e):** `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/business/llm-prompts/alternatives.test.ts src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/alternatives.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 4 failed`: "the quote prompt has no rule that alternatives / options are never added together"; "the tile example injects a material nobody typed"; "a saved quote totals $23,250 — option A + option B added together (estimatedTotal 2325000 …)" (en and es).

## REQ-944 — Document and app dates follow the business's time zone; a batch-sent invoice email shows its issue date (LOOP-007 cycle 1: q1-10, q1-13)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." LOOP-007 cycle 1, issues **q1-10** [major/BUG_HARM] "Documents sent in the evening carry the next day's date (UTC, not the business time zone)" and **q1-13** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION] "Batch-sent invoice email shows a blank 'Issued —' and a 29-day due date".
**Root cause:** no document or app-chrome date path takes the business's zone (REQ-255 `businessTimezone` is used only by Settings and the field-notices sweep). The /q agreement page prints through `formatLongDate` (shared/quote-flow/format-helpers.ts), which reads `getUTC*`, so it always prints the UTC day; the email's `fmtDate(q.createdAt, lang)` (send-paperwork-email/mod.ts) never passes the `tz` that `fmtPaperworkDate` accepts, so it uses the process zone (UTC on Deno Deploy); the quote PDF's `fmtDate` pins `timeZone: "UTC"`; the seven app routes build the header from `new Date().getDay/getMonth/getDate()` in the server's zone; the chat/list clocks use the device's zone. An Austin, TX quote sent at 7:37 PM Central on Nov 18 (01:37Z) reads Nov 19 everywhere. For q1-13, `FieldBatches.send` emails the draft before it stamps `issuedDate` (and `asDelivered` never fills it), so the Issued row is "—", while "Drafted" formats `new Date()` in UTC and Due counts from `fieldToday()` — one day short on an evening send.
**Requirement:** (a) every date a document, email, PDF or app header prints for an instant is that instant's day in the business's time zone (`businessTimezone`: the picked zone, else the address's state, else New York); a bare YYYY-MM-DD keeps its calendar day in every zone. (b) The public /q payload carries that zone so the page renders in it. (c) A batch-sent invoice email shows the issue date it is issued with; Drafted = Issued; Due = Issued + its days to pay.
**Tests (RED at 16e7e33e, 2026-11-18):**
- unit `jest/unit/business-tz-document-dates.test.ts` ("REQ-944 …": `formatLongDate('2026-11-19T01:37Z','es','America/Chicago')` = "18 de noviembre de 2026" — got "19 de noviembre de 2026"; date-only strings keep their day (guard, green); the seven routes' header not built from `now.getDay/getMonth/getDate()`; AsstChat `fmtTime` and communications `shortTime` name a `timeZone`) — `cd jest && TZ=UTC npx jest unit/business-tz-document-dates.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 failed, 1 passed`.
- int `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/business-tz-dates.int.test.ts` (TX business, Spanish email, createdAt 2026-11-19T05:37Z → "Creada 18 de noviembre de 2026"; got "Creada 19 de noviembre de 2026").
- int `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/business-timezone.int.test.ts` (GET /quotes/:id/public carries `timezone` "America/Chicago" — got undefined; GET /quotes/:id/pdf contractor signature "Date: November 18, 2026" — got November 19).
- int `backend/src/field/entrypoints/batch-email-dates.int.test.ts` (pull + send a batch with FIELD_TZ = identity zone off the UTC day; the outbox email's Drafted/Issued/Due — got `drafted "November 19, 2026"`, `issued "—"`).
- Run: `cd backend && TZ=UTC deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check <the three int files>` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 4 failed`.
- e2e `e2e/batch-email-dates/batch-email-dates.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-944 q1-13": /field/batches → Pull → Send selected → the outbox email shows Drafted = Issued = the invoice's issuedDate and Due = issued + netDays) — `shots run e2e/batch-email-dates -- --no-check` → `got {"drafted":"November 18, 2026","issued":"—","due":"December 18, 2026"}`.
- e2e for the q1-10 /q page and header: n/a — the dates come from instants the server stamps (createdAt/publishedAt/now) and the shots lane has no server clock or KV seam to pin them to an evening; the /q formatter is pinned by the jest unit, its zone by the public-payload int test, the email and PDF by the int tests.
**Fix (2026-11-18):** one business zone (`businessTimezone`: picked → address state → New York) now reaches every date path. `formatLongDate(iso, lang, tz?)` takes an instant's calendar parts from `Intl…formatToParts({timeZone: tz})` (bare YYYY-MM-DD keeps its noon-UTC anchor); `fmtDate` (doc-parts), `quote-doc.tsx`, `/i`, `paidLine` and `receivedNoteBody` pass it. The public `contractor` projection (`/quotes|invoices|change-orders/:id/public`) carries `timezone`. `SendPaperworkEmail` resolves the zone once per send onto the identity and every renderer formats with it; the quote / invoice / print PDFs and the signed-confirmation PDF take it too. GET `/me` carries `businessTimezone`; the seven app routes build the header through `front-end/lib/greeting-date.ts` (`formatToParts` in that zone); `formatClockTime(when, lang, {timeZone})` + `shortTime(iso, now, timeZone)` drive the chat island and the Phone page's list clocks. q1-13: `FieldBatches.send` stamps `issuedDate` + `dueDate` (REQ-174) on the draft BEFORE it renders the message and puts the draft's own back on a failed send; `asDelivered(invoice, issuedDate)` / `stampInvoiceDelivered(…, issuedDate)` fill an unissued invoice's issue date (the business's day) on every email/SMS delivery, so no path prints "Issued —". The Settings zone hint (en/es) now says documents follow the zone.
**Test corrections (why):** (1) the jest chat-clock check read `front-end/ui-breakdown/…/AsstChat.tsx`, the design mock excluded in deno.json that no route serves; it now reads the live `front-end/islands/AsstChat.tsx` (and a behavioural case pins `formatClockTime('2026-11-19T01:32Z','es',{timeZone:'America/Chicago'})` = "7:32 p. m."). (2) `business-timezone.int.test.ts` built a line item without `unit`, a TS2741 that failed the whole type-checked `deno task test:int` lane; `unit: "ea"` added. (3) the e2e compared two objects with shots' `expect.eq`, which is `===`, so it could never pass ("expected {…} got {…}" with identical values); it now compares their JSON. (4) the REQ-915 wiring regex `<PhonePage />` now also accepts the `timeZone={…}` prop.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-18):** `cd jest && TZ=UTC npx jest unit/business-tz-document-dates.test.ts` → `Tests: 5 passed`; `cd backend && TZ=UTC deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check <the three int files>` → `ok | 4 passed | 0 failed`; `shots run e2e/batch-email-dates -- --no-check` (BASE_URL = this tree served on :47800/:47801) → `✓ REQ-944 q1-13`, and the same story against the pre-fix commit 9ce4182e served from a scratch worktree → `✗` ("issued":"—"). Neighbours: `deno task test:unit` → jest `Tests: 1 skipped, 6089 passed, 6090 total`, deno `1788 passed | 5 failed`, the 5 all `AddrInUse` in public-controller/e2e.test.ts (a parallel agent's port) — that file + me-controller alone `ok | 49 passed | 0 failed`; `deno task test:int` → `ok | 1334 passed | 0 failed`; shots over business-timezone, c4-batch-checks-note-flash, field-tasks, outbox, phone-drawer, timezone-select, topbar-chrome, topbar-page-title, customer-language → 5 fail (REQ-143, REQ-223, REQ-715, REQ-784, REQ-842), the same 5 failing identically against the pre-fix 9ce4182e server. `deno check` + `deno lint` clean on every touched front-end/shared file; touched backend modules `deno check` clean.

## REQ-1013 — LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-100: the Annual hint says "One visit a year" while the picker takes several days (failing tests)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." Issue q1-100 [polish/BUG_CONTRADICTION], LOOP-007 cycle 1.
**Root cause:** REQ-787 (commit 3b545b13) added `field.subs.annualHint` as "One visit a year, on the day(s) you pick in this month. …" (es: "Una visita al año, el día o los días que elijas en este mes. …"). The Annual month calendar in `front-end/islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx` is a multi-select (`daysOfMonth` checkboxes), and the hint sits right under it. `isDue` (`backend/src/field/domain/business/schedule/mod.ts`) is due on every picked day of the chosen month, and the customer workspace estimate counts `daysOfMonth.length / 12`. So days 5 and 20 in March give two visits a year, while the hint promises one. REQ-787 wanted multi-day on purpose ("on the picked day(s)"), so only the copy is wrong. It is an AMENDMENT to REQ-787's copy.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/annual-hint-copy.test.ts` ("REQ-1013 …": en and es `field.subs.annualHint` do not say one visit / una visita, and do say every year / each day, cada año / cada día) · unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/schedule/test.ts` ("REQ-1013 isDue — annual with two picked days …": over 2026, days [5,20] in March are due exactly on 2026-03-05 and 2026-03-20. This guard is already green and pins the behaviour the copy has to describe) · int n/a — the API and scheduler are right; the defect is only dictionary copy · e2e `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1013: Annual with two days checked (5 and 20) …": checks 5 and 20 in March and reads `[data-cy=subs-month-view] .hint`).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-18):** `npx jest unit/annual-hint-copy.test.ts` → `Tests: 2 failed, 2 total` (`Expected pattern: not /\bone visit\b/i … Received string: "One visit a year, …"`; `not /\buna visita\b/i … "Una visita al año, …"`). `shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check --filter REQ-1013` against `FRONTEND_PORT=5731 BACKEND_PORT=5732 deno task serve` → `✗ REQ-1013 … expectation failed: the hint does not promise one visit a year (got "One visit a year, on the day(s) you pick in this month. …")`, after "two days are checked" (5|20) passed.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** copy only — `lang/en.json` `field.subs.annualHint` → "Every year in this month, on each day you pick. 29 in February falls on the 28th in shorter years."; `lang/es.json` → "Cada año en este mes, en cada día que elijas. El 29 de febrero cae el 28 en los años que no lo tienen." The scheduler and picker were already right (multi-day annual is REQ-787's intent); no test was changed.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** RED at the base commit — `npx jest --selectProjects unit` with the base dictionaries → `Tests: 2 failed, 1 skipped, 6084 passed, 6087 total` (the two failures are this file's en/es tests). GREEN — `npx jest --selectProjects unit --runTestsByPath unit/annual-hint-copy.test.ts` → `Tests: 2 passed, 2 total`; `deno test -A src/field/domain/business/schedule/test.ts` → `ok | 11 passed | 0 failed`; `shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check --filter REQ-1013` against `FRONTEND_PORT=5841 BACKEND_PORT=5842 deno task serve` (this worktree) → `✓ REQ-1013 … · 124.8s`; neighbour `--filter "REQ-787: Annual"` → `✓ REQ-787: Annual shows a Month dropdown …`. Both dictionaries valid JSON, fmt-clean via stdin, same 6276 keys.

## REQ-1015 — Remove access refuses before the confirm step when the worker still covers zones (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-101)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." QA issue q1-101 [polish/BUG_POLISH] "Remove-access confirm comes before the refusal", cycle 1.
**Root cause:** on /field/workers the wk-delete button always runs `setRowErr(null); setConfirmId(w.id)`, so the owner answers "Remove {name}'s access?" and only then learns, from DELETE's 409 `worker_covers_zones`, that it can't be done. The row already knows the zones the worker covers (`mine = regions.filter((r) => r.workerId === w.id)`, drawn as the "Covers" chips), so the page can refuse first with the `field.wk.err.coversZones` wording. The server guard (REQ-421) is correct and stays as the backstop for a stale page.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/field-worker-remove-zones.test.ts` ("REQ-1015 …": the wk-delete handler checks `mine` and sets the coversZones row error instead of opening the confirm step) · int n/a — the server already refuses with 409 `worker_covers_zones` and names the zones, pinned by REQ-421 in `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` · e2e `e2e/field-worker-errors/field-worker-errors.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1015 …": a worker covering a zone → click Remove → no confirm step, "This worker still covers Zone A. Reassign those zones in Assignments first." on the row, no DELETE sent; a worker with no zones still confirms and is removed).
**Evidence (2026-11-18) RED:** `npx jest unit/field-worker-remove-zones.test.ts` → `Tests: 2 failed, 2 total` (`Expected pattern: /\bmine\b|\.workerId\s*===/`); `shots run e2e/field-worker-errors -- --no-check` against `PORT=5617 deno task serve` → REQ-421 ✓, REQ-1015 ✗ `expectation failed: no "Remove Luis Herrera's access?" confirm step for a worker who covers Zone A (row: …CoversZone A · 1…Remove Luis Herrera's access?ConfirmCancel)`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `front-end/islands/FieldWorkersPage.tsx` — the wk-delete button now calls `askRemove(w, mine)`. When the row's `mine` (the zones this worker covers) is non-empty, it clears any open confirm and sets the row error to `field.wk.err.coversZones` with the zone names (via `zoneName`, the same wording the 409 maps to), so no confirm opens and no DELETE goes out. A worker with no zones still gets the confirm step. The server's 409 stays as the backstop for a stale page. No lang changes: the key already existed in en + es.
**Evidence (2026-11-19) GREEN:** `npx jest --selectProjects unit --runTestsByPath unit/field-worker-remove-zones.test.ts` → `PASS`, `2 passed`. The 11 jest suites that read FieldWorkersPage.tsx (field-worker-errors, worker-covers-row, field-worker-form-hints, worker-language, …) → `Test Suites: 11 passed`, `Tests: 72 passed`. `deno lint` + `deno check islands/FieldWorkersPage.tsx` clean, and `deno fmt -` on the file leaves no diff. `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5627 shots run e2e/field-worker-errors -- --no-check` against `PORT=5627 deno task serve` → ✓ REQ-1015 (85s), ✓ REQ-421. shots also ran related field stories: REQ-842 (Away/Remove on /field/workers) ✓. The others marked ✗ were "did not finish" cutoffs under heavy host load (parallel fixers) or are known-red (REQ-555, REQ-799). None of them clicks wk-delete; it appears only in field-worker-errors.e2e.test.ts.

## REQ-1016 — Every customer email's `<html lang>` is the language it is written in (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-102)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-18: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q1-102** [minor/BUG_POLISH] "Spanish Paid email is marked <html lang="en">", LOOP-007 cycle 1.
**Root cause:** the generic email wrapper `shell()` in `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/mod.ts` takes `lang` and uses it for every translated string (the Drafted label, the kind label in `<title>`), but its root element is the fixed text `<html lang="en">` (line 726, from 30d70e55, before the emails were bilingual). The quote and itemized-invoice templates already write `<html lang="${L.docLang}">`. An amount-only invoice (no quote lines) goes `renderInvoiceHtml` → `renderInvoiceBasicHtml(…, lang, paid)` → `shell({…, lang})`, so a Spanish account's paid or sent amount-only invoice email reads Spanish (`<title>Factura INV-001</title>`) while declaring English, and screen readers and mail-client translation use the wrong language.
**Requirement:** every customer email built by `shell()` (amount-only invoice, its paid email, the batch invoice email) declares `<html lang="es">` when written in Spanish and `<html lang="en">` when written in English.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/html-lang.test.ts` ("REQ-1016 …": `renderInvoiceBasicHtml` in Spanish, paid and unpaid, is `lang="es"` with `<title>Factura`; `renderInvoiceHtml` for a quote-less invoice is `es` for an es-comms business and `en` for an en one) · int `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/invoice-controller/paid-email-lang.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1016 …": over HTTP, an es-comms account's amount-only invoice, a payment that closes it, and `GET /outbox/:id` of the paid email: the body opens `<!doctype html>\n<html lang="es">`) · e2e `e2e/outbox/outbox.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1016 …": the same on the dev stack, then the Outbox row opens the email and its frame's `<html lang>` is `es`). jest/unit n/a: no front-end logic is involved.
**Evidence (2026-11-18), RED:** `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/html-lang.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 3 failed` (`Values are not equal: the Spanish email's <html lang>` `- en` / `+ es`); `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/invoice-controller/paid-email-lang.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` (`- <html lang="en">` / `+ <html lang="es">`); `shots run e2e/outbox -- --no-check --filter REQ-1016` against `FRONTEND_PORT=47161 BACKEND_PORT=47162 deno task serve` → "the stored HtmlBody opens with a Spanish root element — expected `<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"es\">`, got `<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"en\">`". With the one-line fix applied temporarily (then reverted), the story got past that assertion; the host load (~140) then timed out its `page.goto`, so the frame step has not been seen green yet.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `shell()` in `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/mod.ts` now writes `<html lang="${lang}">` (`lang: Lang`, `"en" | "es"`) instead of the fixed `<html lang="en">`. Every email the wrapper builds (amount-only invoice, its paid email, the batch invoice email) now declares the language it is written in, the same way the quote and itemized-invoice templates already use `L.docLang`. One-line change. The file was already unformatted at the base commit and was not reformatted.
**Evidence (2026-11-19), GREEN** (host load ~165, so `--no-check`; typecheck done separately): `deno check src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/mod.ts` → `Check` clean; `deno lint` same file → `Checked 1 file`; `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/html-lang.test.ts` → the 3 REQ-1016 tests `ok`; `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/paperwork/entrypoints/invoice-controller/ src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/` (REQ-1016 int + every neighbour) → `ok | 80 passed | 0 failed (7m28s)`; `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:47171 shots run e2e/outbox -- --no-check --filter REQ-1016` against `FRONTEND_PORT=47171 BACKEND_PORT=47172 deno task serve` → `✓ REQ-1016 … opens in the Outbox as <html lang="es"> · 58.5s`. Shots also ran other workers' stories (REQ-786/810/811/839/840/842/921/927/995), which "did not finish" under that load; they cover worker, field and invoice-line UI that does not use `shell()`.

## REQ-1017 — The payment receipt email carries the customer's Reply-To, like the invoice emails (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-104; AMENDMENT to REQ-175)
**Source:** Raphael, LOOP-007: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". Issue q1-104 [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 1: "Payment receipt email has no Reply-To, unlike the invoice emails."
**Root cause:** Reply-To is added only inside `SendPaperworkEmail` (REQ-175, `replyAddress(await this.replyTokens.forCustomer(userId, customerId), inboundDomain())`) and `ReplyToInquiry`, not in the shared email path. `ConfirmPayment` (`backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/confirm-payment/mod.ts`) sends the "Receipt for INV-…" email by calling `EmailService.send` itself with to, subject, htmlBody, from, cc and attachments. It never builds or passes `replyTo` and has no `ReplyTokenStore`. `postmarkPayload` sets `ReplyTo` only when given `input.replyTo`, so the receipt goes out with none, and a customer who replies to it reaches the business's From alias instead of their Messages thread. REQ-175 ("every paperwork email … to a known customer carries Reply-To") was wired and tested on send-paperwork-email only.
**Requirement:** the receipt email to a known customer carries `Reply-To: reply+<token>@<inbound domain>`, with the same per-(contractor, customer) token the invoice emails use.
**Tests:** unit n/a — the bug is a missing call argument in a coordinator, not a pure function (`postmarkPayload` already maps `replyTo` → `ReplyTo`) · int `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/confirm-payment/reply-to.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1017 / REQ-175 confirm-payment: …": the real EmailService with a captured Postmark fetch; the receipt payload's ReplyTo matches `reply+<token>@inbound.documonster.com` and equals `ReplyTokenStore.forCustomer` for that customer) · e2e n/a — Reply-To is a mail header the app never shows, and the shots harness has no Postmark sink to read the payload from (no `POSTMARK_BASE_URL` mock anywhere in the repo), so the integration test on the real Postmark payload is the user-facing boundary.
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED):** `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/confirm-payment/reply-to.int.test.ts` → `AssertionError: Expected actual: "(no ReplyTo)" to match: "/^reply\+[a-z0-9]+@inbound\.documonster\.com$/"` · `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `ConfirmPayment` holds a `ReplyTokenStore` (as `SendPaperworkEmail` does) and, when the invoice has a customer, passes `replyTo: replyAddress(await replyTokens.forCustomer(userId, customerId), inboundDomain())` to the receipt's `EmailService.send`, so the receipt carries the same per-(contractor, customer) token as the invoice emails.

## REQ-940 — LOOP-007 q1, q1-11: the worker's "Today" is the business's day — Done on Today's visit saves, no 409
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". Issue q1-11 [major/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 1: "Worker can't complete a visit shown under 'Today': the server's field day is hard-wired to America/New_York".
**Root cause (RCA at 16e7e33e):** the app has three ideas of "today". The worker island replaces the SSR day with the browser's local date after hydration (`WorkerScreen.tsx` `const now = todayIso(); setToday(now)`), and /field/tasks starts from the browser date (`FieldTasksPage.tsx`). The backend gates every worker action with `inActionWindow(w, t.date, fieldToday(), …)` (`worker-controller/mod.ts` `actionable` and add-service), where `fieldToday()` is `todayIn(FIELD_TZ || "America/New_York")` (`schedule/mod.ts`) and a task dated after that day is refused with 409 "outside the days you can edit" (shown as "that day can no longer be edited", wrong for a future day). The timeclock week uses the same env var. The business's own zone (`businessTimezone({timezone, state})`, REQ-172/255) is read only by the 9 am notices. So whenever the business's (or device's) date differs from New York's, the worker sees a visit under Today, taps Done, and gets a 409; GET /field/worker/tasks with no date returns New York's round, not the business's.
**Requirement:** the field day (worker default round, action window, add-service, office day, timeclock week) is the business's day in its time zone (picked → state → FIELD_TZ → New York); Done on the visit under Today saves.
**Tests:** unit n/a — the pure helpers (`todayIn`, `inActionWindow`) are correct in isolation; the bug is which zone the controllers pass them, covered by int · int `backend/src/field/entrypoints/business-day.int.test.ts` ("REQ-940 (q1-11) GET /field/worker/tasks with no date is the business's day…", "REQ-940 (q1-11) the worker completes the visit on the business's today — 200, not 409…"; zone picked at run time so its date differs from New York's: Pacific/Kiritimati, else Pacific/Honolulu) · jest unit `jest/unit/worker-business-day.test.ts` ("REQ-940 WorkerScreen does not overwrite today/date with the browser's todayIso()…", "REQ-940 FieldTasksPage does not start the office day from the browser's todayIso()") · e2e `e2e/worker-business-day/worker-business-day.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-940 (q1-11): /worker in the business's time zone — Today's visit saves on Done (no 409)…"; browser timezone set via CDP to the business zone).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19 01:55Z, NY 2026-11-18, Kiritimati 2026-11-19):** int → `FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed`: `the default round is the business day 2026-11-19 in Pacific/Kiritimati, not New York's 2026-11-18 (ahead)` (`- []` / `+ ["2026-11-19"]`) and `completing today's visit (2026-11-19 in Pacific/Kiritimati) — got {"status":409,"name":"FieldError","message":"outside the days you can edit"}`; jest → `Tests: 2 failed, 2 total`; e2e → `expectation failed: Done on Today's visit saves (got 409 {"status":409,"name":"FieldError","message":"outside the days you can edit"}) — expected 200, got 409`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** one per-account field day. New `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/business-zone/mod.ts`: `businessZoneOf(userId)` = the business's picked zone (identity) → its address's state → `FIELD_TZ` → New York (`resolveBusinessZone`, pure), and `fieldTodayFor(userId)`. Every former `fieldToday()` call that serves an account now uses it: the worker controller (default round, the action window for complete/uncomplete/skip/defer/note, add-service), every `/field/*` office default day and `dropOpen` from-today (field-controllers), field-batches, field-quote-subscriptions, the customer workspace; the timeclock's worker + office week bounds use `businessZoneOf`. `fieldToday()` / `timeclockTz()` remain only as the server fallback (tests of zone-less accounts). The worker's `/field/worker/login` + `/me` answer `today` + `timeZone`; new `GET /field/tasks/today` → `{date, timeZone}` for the office. A refused day now carries `code: "future_day" | "too_old"` + `detail.today`, and the worker screen words a future day with the new `worker.err.future` ("that day hasn't started yet" / "ese día aún no empieza") instead of "can no longer be edited". Front end: `WorkerScreen` no longer replaces the day with the browser's `todayIso()` after hydration — "Today" is `ssr.today` (route: `/me`'s `today`) and then `/me`'s answer on every full load (a screen on Today follows it); `/field/tasks` seeds from the business day (`loadFieldTasksSeed(sid, undefined)` reads `/field/tasks/today`) and the island starts on the seed's day (or asks `fieldClient.today()`), and its Today button goes to that day; `/field/batches`' default range, a new subscription's start date, and `/field/workers`' "out today" absence dates start on the business day (`fieldClient.today()`). The last one also fixed a second instance of the same bug found by the neighbouring e2e run: `FieldWorkersPage` defaulted an absence to the UTC date (`new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)`), so after 7 pm in New York REQ-842's story marked tomorrow out and today's round never moved (red at 03:19Z, green after). `fieldTodayIso(now, zone?)` takes the zone. This amends REQ-141 ("Today is the company's day in FIELD_TZ") / REQ-193 / REQ-197: the company's day is the business's own time zone (REQ-172/255); FIELD_TZ is only the fallback for an account with no zone and no state. A deferred visit's copy is on a later day and stays a read-only preview until that day is the business's today (REQ-362), which is now the same day on the screen and on the server.
**Tests added with the fix:** unit `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/business-zone/test.ts` ("REQ-940 resolveBusinessZone…", "REQ-940 the field day at 2026-11-19T04:30Z is Nov 18 in Chicago and Los Angeles, Nov 19 in UTC"); int `business-day.int.test.ts` third test ("…a day after the business's today is refused as 'future_day'…, and /me carries that day"); front-end `front-end/lib/field-ssr.test.tsx` ("REQ-940 (q1-11) loadFieldTasksSeed with no date reads the business's day from /field/tasks/today"). `field.int.test.ts` REQ-138's exact login-answer assertion gains `today` + `timeZone` (the answer's new fields; nothing removed).
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19 ~03:10–03:30Z, NY 2026-11-18, Kiritimati 2026-11-19):**
- `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/entrypoints/business-day.int.test.ts src/users/domain/coordinators/business-zone/test.ts` → `ok | 5 passed | 0 failed`.
- `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/users/domain/coordinators/business-zone/test.ts src/field/domain/business/schedule/test.ts src/timeclock src/field/entrypoints src/field/domain/coordinators/field-quote-subscriptions src/field/domain/coordinators/field-notices src/analytics/entrypoints/clients-controller/workspace.int.test.ts src/communication/entrypoints/notification-controller/owner-activity.int.test.ts` → `ok | 91 passed | 0 failed`.

- `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/field-ssr.test.tsx` → `ok | 11 passed | 0 failed` (`--no-check`: the file's RegionView/FieldWorkersSeed fixtures are type-stale at HEAD, unrelated); `deno check` + `deno lint` (stdin) clean on every touched front-end file.
- `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> BASE_URL=http://localhost:57411 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… shots run e2e/worker-business-day -- --no-check` (serve on PORT=57411, fresh KV) → `✓ REQ-940 (q1-11): /worker in the business's time zone — Today's visit saves on Done (no 409) and the server's default day is that day`. Neighbouring stories (c4-batch-checks-note-flash, field-ssr-first-paint, field-tasks, timeclock, worker-ssr, worker-tomorrow, worker-top-actions, worker-view-owner, worker-office-link, worker-language, field-worker-errors) → 49 pass; REQ-842 green after the absence-date fix. ## REQ-938 — A manual nudge on an invoice well past due reaches the customer (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-14)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." QA issue q1-14 [major/BUG_CONTRADICTION], LOOP-007 cycle 1: "Overdue nudge and reminder send nothing for an invoice issued already past due."
**Root cause (at 16e7e33e):** `manualReminderDay` (`shared/quote-flow/reminder-settings.ts`) rounds UP to the next step (`d <= 3 ? 3 : d <= 7 ? 7 : d <= 14 ? 14 : 30`), so an invoice 15+ days past due gets day 30, the owner-only alert. The card and drawer post `{day: 30}` to `/cron/invoice-reminder`; `runForInvoice` emits `invoice:escalated`, sends the customer nothing, still records day 30 in the history, and answers `{channels: [], escalated: true}`, which `nudgeNote` (`shared/documents/delivery-truth.ts`) words as "Already nudged today" (contradicting REQ-556). The day-30 record then stops the daily sweep: `pickNextDay` never goes below the largest step fired, so day 14 never goes out. Introduced in ecaf8a82 (REQ-704).
**Requirement:** a manual nudge on a past-due invoice sends the customer the largest customer step already reached (never day 30, never a step not yet reached: 4 days late → 3, 18 → 14); a recorded day-30 alert never stops the 3/7/14 customer steps; an escalated reply that reached nobody is never worded "Already nudged".
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/nudge-past-due-q114.test.ts` ("REQ-938 …": 18 days → 14, 4 → 3, 15..45 → 14; `nudgeNote({channels: [], escalated: true})` ≠ alreadySent) · int `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-payment-reminder/past-due-nudge.int.test.ts` ("REQ-938 …": the card's day reaches the customer's email; nudge + sweep send the customer something; after a bell-only day 30 the sweep still picks 14) · e2e `e2e/nudge-past-due-q114/nudge-past-due-q114.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-938 …": invoice issued today due 18 days ago → overdue card "Send nudge" → reply carries `email`, note "Nudge sent", one new reminder in `/api/outbox`). Note for the fixer: `jest/unit/reminder-cadence-c5.test.ts:95` (REQ-704) pins `manualReminderDay("2026-10-01", "2026-11-12") === 30` and needs amending to 14.
**Evidence (RED, 2026-11-18):** jest `Tests: 3 failed, 3 total` (`Expected: 14 Received: 30`; `Expected: 3 Received: 7`; `Expected: not "invoicesPage.nudge.alreadySent"`); int `FAILED | 0 passed | 3 failed` (`the nudge reached the customer (day 30, {…"channels":[],"escalated":true})`; history `[{"day":30,…,"channels":[]}]`; `- undefined + 14`); e2e against `PORT=5731 deno task serve` → `✗ REQ-938 … expectation failed: the reminder went out by email ({…"day":30,"channels":[],"escalated":true})`.
**Fix:** `manualReminderDay` rounds DOWN to the customer step already reached (1-6 days late → 3, 7-13 → 7, 14+ → 14) and never returns 30; `pickNextDay`'s never-go-back rule ignores the bell-only day 30, so a recorded owner alert never stops 3/7/14; `nudgeNote` words an escalated reply as `invoicesPage.nudge.ownerAlertOnly` ("This step only alerts you — nothing was sent to the customer.", en + es), never "Already nudged".
**Amended older tests (they pinned the bug):** `jest/unit/reminder-cadence-c5.test.ts` (REQ-704) pinned 41 days late → 30 and 13 days late → 14 (a step not yet reached); now 14 and 7, plus 14 days → 14. `backend/…/send-payment-reminder/cadence.test.ts` (REQ-021) pinned history `[30]` at 31 days → `undefined`; now the sweep picks 14 after a bell-only 30, and `[30, 14]` → `undefined` (still never re-fires).
**Evidence (GREEN, 2026-11-18):** jest `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --runInBand unit/nudge-past-due-q114.test.ts unit/reminder-cadence-c5.test.ts unit/delivery-truth.test.ts` → `Test Suites: 3 passed, 3 total · Tests: 25 passed, 25 total`; int `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-payment-reminder/` → `ok | 26 passed | 0 failed` (the 3 REQ-938 tests ok); neighbours `public-controller/delivery-truth.int.test.ts`, `cron-controller/reminder-preview.int.test.ts`, `coordinators/outbox.int.test.ts` → 11 ok, 0 failed; `customer-branding`, `customer-language`, `send-languages-lock` int → `ok | 17 passed | 0 failed`; `deno lint` + `deno check` (shared files, InvoicesPage.tsx, send-payment-reminder/mod.ts) clean; e2e against `PORT=5947 deno task serve`: `SHOTS_JOBS=1 … shots run e2e/nudge-past-due-q114 -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-938 … · 4.1s — 1 pass · 0 fail` (a first try under host load ~90 timed out on a 15 s locator wait after a 171 s run; the rerun passed). en/es keys in sync, `comms.a2p.sys.house` still last.

## REQ-939 — LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-15: "invoice her the balance" after a deposit she already paid opens the invoice flow, never "INV-001 is already paid"
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". Issue **q1-15** [major/BUG_HARM], cycle 1: in a new /assistant chat QA typed "Job done for Dana Whitfield: repaired her backyard gate and replaced 2 posts, $850 total, plus a $200 deposit she already paid by Zelle. Invoice her the balance, due in 7 days." and got "INV-001 is already paid, so nothing new is recorded." (Dana's older, paid $2,489.75 invoice); no invoice was made.
**Requirement:** that message (and its Spanish equivalent, "…y ya pagó un anticipo de $200 por Zelle. Factúrale el resto, a 7 días.") is a billing ask, not a payment report: nothing is recorded, no "already paid" dead end, and the invoice flow opens for Dana Whitfield at the $850 job with the $200 deposit credited (`invoiceFlow.amountCents` 85000, `depositPaidCents` 20000) and the reply says $650 is due. A real payment report ("Linda paid the deposit $1,425 by Zelle today") still records (REQ-583).
**Root cause (RCA at 16e7e33e):** `handle-chat-message/mod.ts` runs `parsePaymentReport` on the raw text before the model and the invoice flow. In `chat-billing-intent/mod.ts` "paid" matches `PAID_RES`; the "already paid" negation in `NOT_A_PAYMENT_RES` only covers the subjects i/we, not she; `amountIn` takes the first amount ($850) and `DEPOSIT_RE` sets `which: "deposit"`. `parseJobDoneInvoiceAsk` bails whenever `PAYMENT_REPORTED_RE` matches "paid", so the REQ-656 invoice flow cannot win. `ChatBilling.recordPayment` pools all of the named customer's invoices (only the paid INV-001), `pickPaymentInvoice`'s `byWhich` returns a one-invoice job's only invoice for "deposit", `take()` makes it `already_paid`, and `chat-billing/mod.ts` answers `chatCoordinator.payment.alreadyPaid` even for a report read from free text (`fromWords`). Introduced by 88f5458ce (REQ-583); the exclusion from a3a423f85 (REQ-656).
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-billing-intent/test.ts` ("REQ-939 q1-15 …": `parsePaymentReport` is undefined for the en + es message; the REQ-583 Linda report still parses; `parseJobDoneInvoiceAsk` gives `{ amountCents: 85000, depositPaidCents: 20000, customerName: "Dana Whitfield" }` en + es) · int `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/billing-actions.int.test.ts` ("REQ-939 q1-15: …" en + es: Dana with a paid INV-001, new chat → no alreadyPaid reply, no payment, invoiceFlow for Dana $850 / $200 credited, reply says $650) · e2e `e2e/chat-invoice-balance-after-deposit/chat-invoice-balance-after-deposit.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-939 q1-15: …": seeded paid INV-001 via claim + confirm, /assistant new chat, the typed message → invoice flow on screen, no "is already paid", no new payment).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-18, branch fix/q1-q1-15 off qa-loop 16e7e33e):** unit `deno test -A --no-check src/agents/domain/business/chat-billing-intent/test.ts --filter REQ-939` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 3 failed` (parsePaymentReport actual `{ amountCents: 85000, method: "zelle", which: "deposit" }`; parseJobDoneInvoiceAsk actual `undefined`, en + es); int `deno test -A --unstable-kv …/billing-actions.int.test.ts --filter REQ-939` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed` (`the reply is the dead end "INV-001 is already paid, so nothing new is recorded."` / `"INV-001 ya está pagada, así que no registré nada nuevo."`); e2e `shots run e2e/chat-invoice-balance-after-deposit -- --no-check` against `PORT=5747 deno task serve` → `✗ … expectation failed: no "INV-001 is already paid" dead end (got: INV-001 is already paid, so nothing new is recorded.)`.
**Fix (2026-11-18):** `chat-billing-intent/mod.ts` — new `priorPaymentInBillingAsk`: a message that asks to bill the rest (a bill word + balance/rest/remaining in one non-question sentence, e.g. "Invoice her the balance" / "Factúrale el resto") and has a paid clause marked "already"/"ya" (or a deposit beside a "total") is money already taken, not a payment. `parsePaymentReport` returns undefined for it. `parseJobDoneInvoiceAsk` no longer bails on "paid" in that case: it returns the "total" clause's amount as `amountCents` and the paid clause's amount as `depositPaidCents`. `chat-billing/mod.ts` — a report read from free text (`fromWords`) that lands on an already-paid invoice falls through like `none`, so there is no "nothing new is recorded" dead end. `handle-chat-message/mod.ts` — a job-done ask that names a customer whose job is paid in full does not bind that job (nothing is left to bill on it, so it is new work). It gets the invoice flow, carrying `depositPaidCents`, with the new `chatCoordinator.jobDoneInvoice.startDeposit` reply ("$850 less the $200 already paid, so $650 is due"; en + es). `shared/quote-flow/chat-invoice-flow-offer.ts` carries `depositPaidCents`. `AsstChat.tsx` prefills the flow's price with the balance ($650).
**Test correction (e2e):** the story waited for a visible assistant `.msg` bubble before checking anything. When the invoice flow opens, its price pad covers the thread, so no bubble is visible and the story timed out even though the right screen was up (shots frame 017: "$650" pad, Dana's job details). It now waits for the bubble OR `.chat__price-capture`. Every assertion is unchanged.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-18):** unit `deno test -A --no-check src/agents/domain/business/chat-billing-intent/test.ts` → `ok | 28 passed | 0 failed` (incl. REQ-939 ×4 and REQ-583 Linda). int `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check …/billing-actions.int.test.ts --filter REQ-939` → `ok | 2 passed | 0 failed`. Neighbours: every `handle-chat-message/*.test.ts` file green (24 files, e.g. billing-actions 32/32, int 90/90); `chat-billing-intent/test.ts` + `billing-actions.int.test.ts` + `chat-answers/` → `ok | 102 passed | 0 failed`. jest `npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/chat-invoice-flow-offer.test.ts` → `Test Suites: 607 passed, 607 total; Tests: 6084 passed`. `deno check` on the 3 backend modules + AsstChat.tsx + chat-invoice-flow-offer.ts is clean, and `deno lint` on the front-end files is clean. e2e `shots run e2e/chat-invoice-balance-after-deposit -- --no-check` against `PORT=6131 deno task serve` → `✓ REQ-939 q1-15 … · 198.4s` (1 pass · 0 fail).

## REQ-935 — An explicit invoice ask typed in the chat opens the invoice flow, never a quote, even with no "done" word; "net 15" is kept (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-16)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". LOOP-007 cycle 1, issue `q1-16` [major/BUG_CONTRADICTION] "Assistant makes a quote when explicitly asked for an invoice". On /assistant, in a new chat, the tester typed "Make a new invoice for Priya Shah, priya.shah@example.com, 77 Oak Hollow Dr, Austin TX 78745: stained her 300 sq ft deck, $1,450, net 15." and got "Q-001 · QUOTE DRAFTED" (a Free-plan quote used, net 15 lost), then "When does the job start?".
**Cause (RCA at 16e7e33e):** the server treats a typed invoice ask as one only when it says the job is finished. `parseJobDoneInvoiceAsk` (`backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-billing-intent/mod.ts`) returns undefined unless a `DONE_RES` word (done / finished / completed / wrapped up / all set, terminado / acabé …) is present, and the tester's sentence has none ("stained" is plain past tense). `isInvoiceRequest` is true, but `namedCustomersJob` finds no job for a brand-new customer, and the REQ-656 invoice-flow offer in `handle-chat-message/mod.ts` is gated on `jobDoneAsk` only. So the message reaches the chat model, whose only drafting tool is `create_quote`. The `InvoiceFlowOffer` payload has no due-terms field either, so "net 15" would be dropped on that path too.
**Requirement:** (a) An imperative ask to make / create / write / send an invoice ("Make a new invoice for X …", "Invoice X $N", "Hazme una factura para X") is an invoice ask without a done-word; "when it's done, invoice her", a quote ask, a payment report and a question still are not. (b) In a chat with no job bound and no job for the named customer, the server answers it without the chat model with the `invoiceFlow` offer, prefilled with details, amount, customer, email and `dueDays` read from "net 15" / "due in 15 days" / "a 15 días"; no quote is drafted, so no Free-plan quote is used. (c) The chat keeps `dueDays` when it reads the offer and the invoice flow prefills its due date from it.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/agents/domain/business/chat-billing-intent/test.ts` ("REQ-935 q1-16 …": the exact sentence → `{ amountCents: 145000, customerName: "Priya Shah", customerEmail: "priya.shah@example.com", dueDays: 15 }`; create/make/write/invoice asks en+es; the rejections still hold) · unit `jest/unit/chat-invoice-flow-due-terms.test.ts` ("REQ-935 …": `invoiceFlowOfferOf` keeps dueDays, drops junk; `startInvoiceFlow` reads `prefill.dueDays`) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/billing-actions.int.test.ts` ("REQ-935 q1-16 …": the sentence in a new chat → invoiceFlow with dueDays 15, stub model never called, no quote stored) · e2e `e2e/chat-invoice-intent/chat-invoice-intent.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-935 q1-16 …": typed on /assistant → no "QUOTE DRAFTED" card, pad at $1,450, no quote, offer dueDays 15).
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED at 16e7e33e):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/agents/domain/business/chat-billing-intent/test.ts --filter REQ-935` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 2 failed` (the exact sentence: `- undefined`). `deno test … billing-actions.int.test.ts --filter REQ-935` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` ("the chat model answered", `- 1 + 0`). `cd jest && npx jest unit/chat-invoice-flow-due-terms.test.ts` → `Tests: 2 failed, 1 passed` (dueDays dropped; `startInvoiceFlow` has no `prefill.dueDays`). `BASE_URL=http://localhost:5737 shots run e2e/chat-invoice-intent/… -- --no-check --filter REQ-935` → `✗ REQ-935 q1-16 … expectation failed: no 'QUOTE DRAFTED' card for an invoice ask — expected 0, got 3`.
**Fix (2026-11-18):** `parseJobDoneInvoiceAsk` (`chat-billing-intent/mod.ts`) now passes an explicit make-an-invoice ask (`INVOICE_ASK_RES`: "make / create / write / draft / prepare … (a new) invoice", a sentence opening "Invoice <Name>", "hazme / crea / prepara … una factura", "Factúrale a <Name>") as well as a done-word; `NOT_DONE_RES`, the quote ask, the payment report and the question rejections still run after it. "Send the invoice" is deliberately not in the list (that is sending an existing one).
