## REQ-967 — The signed agreement PDF names the signer in the customer's signature box (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-44)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." QA loop LOOP-007, cycle 1, issue q1-44 [polish/BUG_CONTRADICTION] "Signed PDF labels the customer's signature 'YOUR SIGNATURE'".
**Root cause:** `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-quote-pdf/mod.ts:778` always draws the customer box title with `renderQuotePdf.sig.yourSignature` ("YOUR SIGNATURE" / "TU FIRMA"), even when `quote.acceptedName` / `acceptedSignature` are set and drawn in the same box. The line came from d0131e7f5 (REQ-032, NW-28), which matched the web's unsigned prompt. REQ-692 later gave the signed web card its own title, `t.signatureOf(signerName)` ("{name}'s signature" / "Firma de {name}", `front-end/components/quote-doc.tsx`), and never ported it to the PDF. So the countersigned PDF reads "YOUR SIGNATURE | Linda Park" while /q reads "LINDA PARK'S SIGNATURE", and on the contractor's copy "YOUR" points at the wrong person.
**Requirement:** Once the quote is signed, the PDF's customer box title is the signer's typed name: "LINDA PARK'S SIGNATURE" (en) / "FIRMA DE LINDA PARK" (es), the PDF's caps style. "YOUR SIGNATURE" / "TU FIRMA" stays only on the unsigned PDF (REQ-032).
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-quote-pdf/signed-label.test.ts` ("REQ-967 …": signed en → "LINDA PARK'S SIGNATURE" and no "YOUR SIGNATURE"; signed es → "FIRMA DE LINDA PARK" and no "TU FIRMA"; unsigned keeps both prompts) · int `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/signed-pdf-label.int.test.ts` ("REQ-967 …": unsigned GET /quotes/:id/pdf says "YOUR SIGNATURE"; after POST /quotes/:id/accept as "Linda Park" the PDF says "LINDA PARK'S SIGNATURE" and not "YOUR SIGNATURE") · e2e n/a — the defect is text inside the PDF bytes; the int test drives the same accept → download path the browser uses and reads the drawn text, a browser adds nothing a PDF text check can see.
**Evidence (RED, 2026-11-18, at 16e7e33e):** `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-quote-pdf/signed-label.test.ts` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 2 failed` (`"…FIRMA DEL CONTRATISTA\nTU FIRMA\n" to contain: "FIRMA DE LINDA PARK"`; en `"…YOUR SIGNATURE\n" to contain: "LINDA PARK'S SIGNATURE"`); `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/signed-pdf-label.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` (`"…YOUR SIGNATURE\nLinda Park\n" to contain: "LINDA PARK'S SIGNATURE"`).
**Fix:** `render-quote-pdf/mod.ts` picks the customer box title by state: unsigned → `renderQuotePdf.sig.yourSignature` (REQ-032 prompt, unchanged); signed (`acceptedAt`, `acceptedName` or `acceptedSignature`) with a typed name → new key `renderQuotePdf.sig.signatureOf` ("{name}'S SIGNATURE" / "FIRMA DE {name}", name upper-cased with `toLocaleUpperCase(lang)`); signed without a name → the existing `renderQuotePdf.sig.clientSigned` ("CLIENT SIGNED" / "CLIENTE FIRMÓ"). The title is truncated with "…" to fit `halfW - 24`. AMENDS REQ-692: the signed label now applies to the PDF as well as the web card.
**Evidence (GREEN, 2026-11-18):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-quote-pdf/signed-label.test.ts src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/signed-pdf-label.int.test.ts` → `ok | 4 passed | 0 failed`; neighbours `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-quote-pdf/ src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/` → `ok | 106 passed | 0 failed`; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → `Test Suites: 607 passed, 607 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6084 passed`; mod.ts `deno fmt` (stdin) clean, `deno lint` / `deno check` clean; lang/en.json + es.json valid JSON, 6277 keys each, same set, last key unchanged (REQ-920).

## REQ-968 — Quote PDF section numbers run without a gap (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-45)
**Source:** Raphael (QA loop): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". Issue **q1-45** [polish/BUG_POLISH], cycle 1: "Quote PDF section numbers skip 03". `GET /api/quotes/:id/pdf` numbered the sections 01, 02, 04, 05, 06, but the web page numbers them 01–05.
**Root cause:** `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-quote-pdf/mod.ts` hardcodes each section's number as a string literal: "01" Job details, "02" Payment schedule, "03" Schedule, "04" Terms, "05" Terms and Conditions, "06" Signatures. Payment schedule, Schedule and Terms only render when they have data. Schedule only renders `if (quote.startDate || quote.estimatedCompletionDate)`, so a quote with neither date skipped Schedule and its "03", and the later sections still printed 04–06. The web document (`front-end/components/quote-doc.tsx`, 4c45161b3) fixed the same gap with a running counter. The PDF renderer, whose literals were carried over from render-contract-pdf in 1a520814, never got that fix. `render-invoice-pdf` has no numbered sections.
**Requirement:** the quote PDF's section discs read 01, 02, … in drawing order with no gap, whichever sections are present.
**Tests:** int `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-quote-pdf/section-numbers.int.test.ts` ("REQ-968 …": a quote with no dates → 01–05 and no 06; with a start and completion date → 01–06) · unit: n/a, because the numbering is inline in the coordinator's draw sequence and the int test renders it directly · e2e: n/a, because the defect is in PDF bytes that the int test reads through the same renderer the `/pdf` route calls, and a browser story would add nothing.
**Evidence (RED, 2026-11-18):** `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-quote-pdf/section-numbers.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 1 failed`, with `section headers drawn: ["01 Job details","02 Payment schedule","04 Terms","05 Terms and Conditions","06 Signatures"]`.
**Fix:** `render-quote-pdf/mod.ts` now numbers its sections with a running counter (`let sec = 0; const sn = () => String(++sec).padStart(2, "0")`), the same one `render-invoice-pdf/mod.ts` already uses (line 171) and the web page uses. All six `drawSectionHeader` calls pass `sn()` instead of a "01"–"06" literal, so a skipped section uses no number. Correction to the root-cause note above: `render-invoice-pdf` does number its sections, but it already uses the counter, so it has no gap and needed no change.
**Evidence (GREEN, 2026-11-18):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-quote-pdf/section-numbers.int.test.ts` → `ok | 2 passed | 0 failed`. Neighbours: `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-quote-pdf/ src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-invoice-pdf/` → `ok | 35 passed | 0 failed`. `deno fmt -` (stdin diff empty), `deno lint` and `deno check` on `render-quote-pdf/mod.ts` are clean.

## REQ-969 — AMENDMENT to REQ-015 (LOOP-007 q1, cycle 1, q1-46): the onboarding state step does not promise a governing state the agreement never names
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." QA issue q1-46 [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], LOOP-007 cycle 1.
**Cause:** `welcome.state.why` ("It sets the governing state on your agreements." / "Define el estado que rige tus acuerdos.") was written in 69a72236 (2026-07-09), when the governing state was meant to be the business's. REQ-015 (2026-09-18) then fixed the clause (`quoteDoc.clause.governingLaw.body`, `renderQuotePdf.clause.governingLaw.body`) to the client's words, "the laws of the state where the work is performed", with no state in it, and nobody updated the onboarding line. The wizard's StateStep (`front-end/islands/WelcomeWizard.tsx`) saves the state only into the business address, and that address is the only place it is printed. `assistantDemo.continueCta.sub` ("… governing state — a few quick questions" / "estado regulador") makes the same stale claim, though no assistant step asks it any more.
**Requirement:** the state step's "why" line (en + es) says what the state is used for, which is the business address, and does not claim a governing state. `assistantDemo.continueCta.sub` does not list a governing-state question. REQ-015's clause wording stays as it is, with no state placeholder.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/i18n-dictionary-consistency.test.ts` ("REQ-969 …") · integration n/a, because this is copy only and no backend contract changes · e2e `e2e/welcome-state-why/welcome-state-why.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-969 q1-46 …": a new account with every question answered except state and address lands on the state step, and its why line makes no governing-state claim and mentions the address).
**Evidence (2026-11-18), RED:** `npx jest unit/i18n-dictionary-consistency.test.ts -t REQ-969` gives `Tests: 3 failed, 49 skipped, 3 passed`, with `Expected pattern: not /govern/i  Received string: "It sets the governing state on your agreements."` and `Expected pattern: not /governing state/i  Received string: "Payment, warranty, dispute, governing state — a few quick questions"`. `shots run e2e/welcome-state-why -- --no-check` against `PORT=26746 deno task serve` gives `✗ … expectation failed: REQ-969: the state step's why line makes no governing-state promise (got "It sets the governing state on your agreements.")`.
**Fix:** I changed the onboarding copy and left the clause alone, because REQ-015's clause is the client's fixed language. `welcome.state.why` now reads EN "It goes on your business address on quotes, invoices and agreements." and ES "Aparece en la dirección de tu negocio en cotizaciones, facturas y acuerdos.", using the app's settled Spanish term "cotizaciones". `assistantDemo.continueCta.sub` dropped the governing-state item: EN "Payment, warranty, disputes — a few quick questions", ES "Pago, garantía, disputas — unas pocas preguntas rápidas". `lang/en.json` and `lang/es.json` stay in sync, are valid JSON, and are fmt-clean. No key was added or moved.
**Evidence (2026-11-18), GREEN:** `cd jest && npx jest unit/i18n-dictionary-consistency.test.ts` gives `Tests: 55 passed, 55 total`. The full jest unit lane (`npx jest --selectProjects unit …`) gives `Test Suites: 607 passed, 607 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 6090 passed`. `shots run e2e/welcome-state-why -- --no-check` against `PORT=26111 deno task serve` gives `✓ REQ-969 q1-46: the onboarding state step says the state goes on the business address … · 44.7s` (1 pass · 0 fail). An earlier run hit `page.waitForURL` timeout at /verify because it started before the backend finished booting. It went green once the run waited for "backendv2 listening".

## REQ-973 — LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-47: a published revision of a Spanish quote reaches the Spanish reader translated
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." Issue **q1-47** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 1: "Spanish quote V2 gets an English line item; /q with no ?lang renders in English."
**Root cause:** An English chat edit on an issued Spanish quote (`apply-chat-change-order`, REQ-201 path) appends `{description: "Baseboards", quantity, unit, price}` with no `descriptionByLang` as the pending revision. `POST /quotes/:id/publish {notify:true}` (`RevisionsController.publishQuote`) makes it live and calls `notify()` → SendPaperworkEmail/Sms without running the quote translator. Only SendQuote, LockQuote, the chat's lock_quote and PreviewQuoteSend run it, so REQ-264's "before every dispatch" is broken. The /q?lang=es page and the Spanish e-mail fall back to the English "Baseboards". **Second layer (found writing the test):** calling the real `TranslateQuote` on publish is not enough. The quote's base is `es`, so REQ-333 fills the es slot with the typed text verbatim (`descriptionByLang {"en":"Baseboards","es":"Baseboards"}`), and `lineItemDescription(li, "es", "es")` returns the typed text. A line typed in a language other than the quote's base has to be translated into the base too. The bare-/q half is NOT_A_BUG under REQ-048/REQ-715 (a bare link opens in Customer.language, else English).
**Requirement:** Publishing a quote revision that notifies the customer translates its line items into every document language first (REQ-264 AMENDMENT: publish-and-notify joins SendQuote/LockQuote/lock_quote). A failed translation never blocks the publish. The Spanish e-mail and /q?lang=es show V2's new line in Spanish.
**Tests:** int `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/revisions-controller/translate.int.test.ts` ("REQ-973 (LOOP-007 q1-47): …": a Spanish quote, an English pending line "Baseboards", publish {notify:true, language:"es"}, with the real TranslateQuote on QuoteTranslatorPort and only the model scripted. Asserts the translator runs, `localizeLineItems(public.lineItems, "es", public.lang)` is ["Pintura de paredes", "Zócalos"], and the e-mail HTML has "Zócalos" and not "Baseboards") · unit n/a — the defect is a missing call in the publish wiring plus the base-language rule the int test runs for real; `lineItemDescription`'s fallback is correct as designed · e2e n/a — the browser lane runs the stub LLM, which echoes instead of translating (the reason REQ-264 gives), so a browser cannot tell a translated line from the fallback.
**Evidence (2026-11-18), RED at 16e7e33e:** `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/revisions-controller/translate.int.test.ts` → `AssertionError: REQ-973: publish-and-notify runs the quote translator (REQ-264 "before every dispatch") — translator calls: []` · `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed`. With a scratch (reverted) `translator.run` added after publishRevision, it still fails at `/q?lang=es renders V2's new line in Spanish (stored lang=es, … "descriptionByLang":{"en":"Baseboards","es":"Baseboards"})`.
**Fix:** (1) `RevisionsController` takes the optional `QuoteTranslatorPort` and `InvoiceTranslatorPort`. `publishQuote` runs `quoteTranslator.run({userId, quoteId})` (every language) right after `publishRevision` and before the revised event and `notify()`, then re-reads the quote. The port logs and swallows a failure, so the publish never blocks. `publishInvoice` does the same for a standalone invoice (REQ-497; a quote-linked invoice takes the quote's text). (2) `TranslateQuote.rebaseForeignLines`: on a quote an earlier run already based (`lang` set, no re-base), a line with no copies yet that the other language's translation gives back unchanged, and whose words do not read as the base (`messageLang`), was typed in that other language. It gets one more model call into the base. The line's `description` becomes the base-language text, and `descriptionByLang` becomes `{[base]: translation, [other]: typed}`. A new line typed in the base language is translated as before and stays verbatim (REQ-333). An extra int test pins this rule: `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-quote/int.test.ts` ("REQ-973 (LOOP-007 q1-47) a line typed in English on an already-translated Spanish quote is re-based into Spanish; a new Spanish line stays verbatim").
**Evidence (2026-11-18), GREEN:** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/revisions-controller/translate.int.test.ts` → `ok | 1 passed | 0 failed`. `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-quote/int.test.ts --filter REQ-973` → `ok | 1 passed | 0 failed | 14 filtered out`. Neighbours: `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/translate-quote/ src/paperwork/entrypoints/revisions-controller/ src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote/ src/agents/domain/coordinators/lock-quote/ src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/preview-quote-send/ src/agents/domain/coordinators/apply-chat-change-order/` plus `src/paperwork/entrypoints/invoice-controller/` → `ok | 137 passed | 0 failed`. `deno check` on both modules is clean. `deno lint` is clean on the touched files; its one finding is the unused `json` in the untouched `revisions-controller/job-details-revision.int.test.ts:57`, which was already there.

## REQ-971 — REQ-715 AMENDMENT (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-49): "Sends in" / "Preview in" starts on the document's own language when the customer has none
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." Issue q1-49 [minor/BUG_POLISH], cycle 1: "'Sends in' defaults to English for a customer the contractor described in Spanish" — the contractor must remember to switch to Español.
**Root cause (at 16e7e33e):** the assistant's "Preview in" / "Sends in" default is `defaultSendLang(customer, appLang, sendLanguages)` (front-end/lib/send-dialog.ts; AsstChat.tsx previewLang state + its effect), which reads only Customer.language and then the app language. It never reads the quote's own language, `quote.lang`, which QuoteStore stamps from the typed text (`quoteTextLang`, REQ-710). Customer.language is set only when the contractor says so outright (the create_quote prompt never infers it from the language the user writes in, REQ-715 c4-M34), so a quote typed in Spanish in an English app for a new customer opens on English. /quotes' `QuoteSendDialog` (QuotesPage.tsx) passes no `initialSendLang` / `loadDefaultLang` either, unlike the invoice sheet (REQ-727). Both came in with 8cbb491a (REQ-715); the REQ-925 clamp with ded78f72.
**Requirement:** with no language on the customer, "Sends in" (assistant review card and /quotes' send dialog) starts on the document's own language, else the app language; the customer's own language still wins, and REQ-925's Settings clamp still applies. Customer.language is still never inferred.
**Tests:**
- unit `jest/unit/q1-49-sends-in-doc-lang.test.ts` ("REQ-971 …": `defaultSendLang(customer, appLang, sendLanguages, docLang)` order customer → doc → app and the clamp; AsstChat passes the quote's language and its effect follows it; QuotesPage gives QuoteSendDialog the quote's language)
- integration: n/a — the bug is the front-end default; both dialogs send the picked language explicitly, so the backend's no-pick fallback (resolveCommsLanguage) is not on this path
- e2e `e2e/sends-in-doc-lang/sends-in-doc-lang.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-971 q1-49 …": English app, Spanish-typed quote for a new "Jose Martinez" with no language → the assistant's "Preview in" and /quotes?open → Send ▾ → Email "Sends in" start on Español)
**Evidence (RED, 2026-11-18):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/q1-49-sends-in-doc-lang.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 failed, 2 passed` (`Expected: "es" Received: "en"`; AsstChat `defaultSendLang` calls have 3 args; QuoteSendDialog has no initialSendLang/loadDefaultLang). `shots run e2e/sends-in-doc-lang -- --no-check` against `PORT=6871 deno task serve` → `expected "assistant es=true en=false · /quotes es=true", got "assistant es=false en=true · /quotes es=false"` (setup checks passed: quote.lang "es", Jose has no language).

**Fix (2026-11-18):** `defaultSendLang(customer, appLang, sendLanguages, docLang?)` (front-end/lib/send-dialog.ts) now orders customer.language → the document's language → app language, still clamped by REQ-925. AsstChat's "Preview in" / "Sends in" passes `quote?.lang ?? quoteTextLang(quote)` and its follow-the-default effect lists it, so a quote that turns Spanish before the contractor taps a pill follows. /quotes passes `initialSendLang={defaultSendLang(state.customer, lang, undefined, q.lang ?? quoteTextLang(q))}` to `QuoteSendDialog` (new pass-through prop to `SendDialog`; `QuoteCard.lang` typed). The SendDialog's profile clamp (REQ-925) still applies after mount. Customer.language is still never inferred (create_quote prompt untouched); the backend no-pick fallback (resolveCommsLanguage) is unchanged, since both dialogs send the picked language explicitly.
**Evidence (GREEN, 2026-11-18):**
- `cd jest && npx jest unit/q1-49-sends-in-doc-lang.test.ts` → `Tests: 5 passed, 5 total`
- `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit $(grep -rlE "send-dialog|defaultSendLang|QuoteSendDialog|QuotesPage|clients/quotes|previewLang|AsstChat" unit)` → `Test Suites: 608 passed, 608 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6089 passed, 6090 total`
- `cd front-end && deno check` + `deno lint` on islands/AsstChat.tsx islands/QuotesPage.tsx components/QuoteSendDialog.tsx lib/send-dialog.ts clients/quotes.ts → all Check OK, `Checked 5 files` (lint clean)
- `PORT=6873 KV_PATH=<fresh> deno task serve` + `BASE_URL=http://localhost:6873 shots run e2e/sends-in-doc-lang -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-971 q1-49: … start on Español in an English app · 6s`
- Neighbouring e2e on the same server: edit-job-details-lang ✓, review-card-chrome-lang ✓, send-dialog-pin-top ✓ ✓. `e2e/customer-language` REQ-715 m31 fails at line 218 (`send-lang-es` getAttribute timeout) — the SAME failure with the whole front-end reverted to HEAD (d3458616) on the same server, so it is pre-existing, not this change; its step-20 screenshot shows "Sends in" on Español.

## REQ-934 — A customer set to Español is invoiced in Spanish from her own page (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-5; amends REQ-715)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA loop LOOP-007, cycle 1, issue **q1-5** [major/BUG_CONTRADICTION] "Customer set to Español is invoiced in English from her own page (send dialog defaults to English)". REQ-715 promises every send to a customer with a language starts in it.
**Root cause:** On `/customers/<id>` → Send invoice → Issue invoice, `InvoiceSendDialog` starts "Sends in" on `invoiceSheetLang(invoice)` — the invoice's typed language only — which outranks the customer's language (the reverse of `invoiceDocLang`, which ranks the customer first). An invoice with a line is translated and stamped `lang: "en"`, so the sheet starts on English outright; an amount-only invoice (no `lang`) asks `GET /invoices/:id/send-preview` with no pick, and `PreviewInvoiceSend.run` resolves `resolveCommsLanguage({ override: input.lang ?? invoiceDocLang(stored, quote), … })` without the customer (no third argument, no `customerLanguage`, the customer loaded only after), so it answers the account default / `commsLanguages[0]` / "en", which replaces her language. Send then dispatches with `language: "en"`: `<html lang="en">`, `?lang=en`. Introduced by 69ba46ac (REQ-727) before REQ-715 (8cbb491a) added the customer slot; REQ-715's int test covered only `PreviewQuoteSend`.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/loop7-q1-5-invoice-sheet-customer-lang.test.ts` ("REQ-934 q1-5 …": `invoiceSheetLang(invoice, customer)` → the customer's language, else the invoice's typed language, else undefined; `InvoiceSendDialog` passes the customer) · int `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/customer-language.int.test.ts` ("REQ-934 q1-5 (REQ-715): the invoice send preview with no pick starts in the customer's language …": amount-only invoice for Carmen (es), account `commsLanguage: "en"`, `commsLanguages: ["en","es"]` → `lang "es"`, subject "Factura …", SMS `?lang=es`; the pick still wins; Bob → "en") · e2e `e2e/customer-invoice-lang/customer-invoice-lang.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-934 q1-5 (REQ-715): from a Spanish-speaking customer's own page …": `/customers/<id>` → Send invoice → one line at $1,250 → Issue invoice → open "What they'll get"; Español pressed and the subject "Factura …"; Send → the outbox invoice email is `language=es`, `<html lang="es">`, `?lang=es`).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-18, 16e7e33e):** int → `AssertionError: Values are not equal: no pick → Carmen's language, not the account's` (`- en + es`); jest → `3 failed, 1 passed` (`Expected: "es" Received: undefined`; `Expected: "es" Received: "en"`; the dialog wiring regex); e2e → `expected "es=true en=false", got "es=false en=true"` (invoice lang=en, preview subject "Invoice INV-001 from Ortega Handyman Services — due December 19, 2026").
**Fix (2026-11-18):** (1) `PreviewInvoiceSend.run` loads the customer BEFORE deciding the language and resolves `override: input.lang ?? invoiceDocLang(stored, quote, customer)` plus `customerLanguage: customer?.language`, so the no-pick preview (the sheet's `loadDefaultLang`) answers her language. (2) `invoiceSheetLang(invoice, customer)` ranks the customer's language over the invoice's typed language (invoiceDocLang's order) and `InvoiceSendDialog` passes the customer, so a known customer language never waits on, or is replaced by, the server. (3) A second defect the e2e exposed once the send went out with `language=es`: the shared email `shell()` in `send-paperwork-email/mod.ts` hard-coded `<html lang="en">` (since 30d70e55) for every quote/invoice email; it now writes `<html lang="${lang}">`. `SendPaperworkEmail`/`SendPaperworkSms` already rank `customerLanguage` (UX-28), so no change there.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-18):** int `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/customer-language.int.test.ts` → `ok | 9 passed | 0 failed`; neighbours `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork` → `ok | 624 passed | 0 failed`; unit `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → `Test Suites: 608 passed, 608 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6088 passed` (incl. loop7-q1-5, 4/4); `cd front-end && deno lint` + `deno check` on `lib/invoice-send-sheet.ts components/InvoiceSendDialog.tsx` → clean; backend `deno check`/`deno lint` on the two touched coordinators → clean; e2e `BASE_URL=<own serve> shots run e2e/customer-invoice-lang -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-934 q1-5 … · 14.5s`. Related lane (customer-invoice-lang, customer-language, invoice-lang, invoice-send-sheet, amount-only-invoice, quote-to-invoice-lang, send-languages-lock, invoice-english-lines, c5-invoice-dispatch-contact): 9 pass · 5 fail; the same 5 (REQ-695 M23/m55, REQ-715 m31, REQ-727 'Finish + send' opens the sheet, REQ-727 'Send now' on a scheduled invoice) fail identically with the fix reverted on the same tree (baseline serve, SHOTS_JOBS=1), so they are pre-existing and not caused by this change.

## REQ-970 — LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-51: the wizard's paid card must not promise the full price on the next 1st (AMENDMENT to REQ-725)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." Issue q1-51 [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], LOOP-007 cycle 1: "Plan card says '$99 on the 1st of each month' but the Dec 1 charge is a prorated $41.52".
**Root cause:** REQ-725 (b0d06efa) cut the paid card's note on /welcome step 4 to one line, `welcome.plan.note.paid` = "{due} today, then {monthly} on the 1st of each month — …", and `wizardPlanNote` (front-end/lib/plan-pick-note.ts) fills it with only `due` and `monthly` from `switchQuote`. The real first-pick schedule (REQ-129, `anchoredSchedule` in shared/quote-flow/plan-switch.ts) bills the full month today, then on the NEXT 1st a prorated catch-up for the days past paid-through ($44.71 Monster / $89.87 Assist for a Nov 18 pick; $41.52 for Dec 19–31 on a Nov 19 UTC pick), and the full price only from the 1st after. The "How billing works" body on the same screen and Settings' `billing.note.first` state the prorated bill, so the card contradicts them and REQ-356's promise that the card never names a different number than the CRM charges.
**Requirement:** a paid card's note never says {monthly} is charged on the next 1st when `anchoredSchedule(now, monthly).firstAmountCents` differs from {monthly}: it names that catch-up amount, or the date the full monthly price starts (the 1st after `firstBillAt`), and it agrees with the "How billing works" body on what the next 1st costs.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/plan-step-billing.test.tsx` ("REQ-970 (q1-51): a Nov 18 Monster pick's card note does not promise $99 on Dec 1 …", "REQ-970 (q1-51): every paid onboarding card's note agrees with anchoredSchedule …") · integration, same file ("REQ-970 (q1-51) rendered: … each paid card's note agrees with the 'How billing works' body …", server-rendered WelcomeWizard) · e2e `e2e/plan-picker/plan-picker.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-054 + REQ-970: in onboarding the person picks a paid plan …", reads the card and the disclosure on /welcome step 4). Backend int: n/a — the defect is front-end copy; the charge itself (`anchoredSchedule`) is correct and already pinned by REQ-129. Note for the fixer: REQ-725's tests pin the old exact line ("$99 today, then $99 on the 1st of each month — …") in the same unit file and in REQ-054's e2e `expect.eq`; they are amended by this REQ.
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED at 16e7e33e):** `deno test -A front-end/lib/plan-step-billing.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 4 passed | 3 failed`: `AssertionError: Monster (en): the next 1st bills $44.71, not $99 — the card must name $44.71 or that $99 starts Jan 1; it says "$99 today, then $99 on the 1st of each month — you'll pay on a secure payment page next"`. `shots run e2e/plan-picker -- --no-check --filter "REQ-970"` → `✗ REQ-054 + REQ-970 … expectation failed: REQ-970: the Monster card must not promise $99 on the 1st the disclosure bills $41.52 for — name $41.52 or that $99 starts Jan 1; it says "$99 today, then $99 on the 1st of each month — you'll pay on a secure payment page next"` (the disclosure check `we bill $41.52` passed).
**Fix (option A, copy — the schedule is unchanged):** `wizardPlanNote` (front-end/lib/plan-pick-note.ts) now reads `anchoredSchedule(now, monthly)` for a first pick. When the next 1st is the prorated catch-up (`firstAmountCents !== monthly`), the card says `welcome.plan.note.paid` = "{due} today, a smaller catch-up bill on the next 1st, then {monthly} on the 1st of each month from {steadyFrom} — you'll pay on a secure payment page next" (es: "… un cobro de ajuste menor el próximo día 1, luego {monthly} el día 1 de cada mes desde el {steadyFrom} …"), where {steadyFrom} is the 1st after `firstBillAt` ("Jan 1" / "1 ene"). A pick made ON a 1st (the next 1st IS the full price) and an upgrade/downgrade keep REQ-725's plain line, now the new key `welcome.plan.note.paidSteady`. No dated amounts went back on the card (REQ-725's rule holds); the exact amount stays in "How billing works".
**Tests amended (REQ-725's exact-copy pins, which pinned the contradicting line):** `front-end/lib/plan-step-billing.test.tsx` "REQ-725: a paid card's note is one plain line …" now expects the catch-up line for the Nov 12 pick and the plain line for a Nov 1 pick; `e2e/plan-picker/plan-picker.e2e.test.ts` REQ-054's `expect.eq` on `plan-note-monster` now compares with `wizardCardNoteToday()`, which builds the expected line from `anchoredSchedule` for today. REQ-970's own assertions are unchanged.
**Evidence (2026-11-18, GREEN):** `deno test -A front-end/lib/plan-step-billing.test.tsx front-end/lib/plan-pick-note.test.tsx front-end/lib/plan-schedule-note.test.ts front-end/lib/plan-cards-all-features.test.tsx front-end/lib/welcome-lang.test.tsx` → `ok | 20 passed | 0 failed`. `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5477 shots run e2e/plan-picker -- --no-check --filter "REQ-970"` → `✓ REQ-054 + REQ-970: in onboarding the person picks a paid plan …`; the whole file → 14 pass, 1 fail: REQ-106's "answers at once" timing (3753 ms with 15 stories in parallel), which passes on its own (`--filter "REQ-106"` → ✓ 5.3s) and does not touch the note. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → `607 passed`. `deno lint` + `deno check` (plan-pick-note.ts, plan-step-billing.test.tsx, islands/WelcomeWizard.tsx) clean; lang/en.json + es.json valid, 6277 keys each, last key still `comms.a2p.sys.house`.

## REQ-972 — Quotes are called Quote / Cotización everywhere (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-52)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." Issue **q1-52** [polish/BUG_POLISH], LOOP-007 cycle 1: mixed terms for quotes — 'presupuestos' / 'estimates' on the dashboard money bar, 'propuestas' (es) / 'bids' (en) in the onboarding insurance step.
**Root cause:** the wrong words are hard-coded in two dictionary entries. REQ-798's money bar (08b4524a) copied QuickBooks' column caption: `MoneyBar.tsx` renders `plural(lang, "moneyBar.bucket.estimates", n)`, which is "{n} estimate(s) out" (en.json) and "{n} presupuesto(s) enviado(s)" (es.json), though the bucket links to /quotes and the rest of the app says Quotes / Cotizaciones (`nav.quotes`). REQ-227's onboarding copy (3808f6ef) says `welcome.insurance.why` "…to your bids" / "…a tus propuestas". The tests only checked that the keys exist, not their wording.
**Requirement:** `moneyBar.bucket.estimates.one/other` = "{n} quote out" / "{n} quotes out" and "{n} cotización enviada" / "{n} cotizaciones enviadas"; `welcome.insurance.why` says "quotes" / "cotizaciones"; no Spanish UI string calls a quote a "presupuesto" or "propuesta" (the "budget" meanings, a proposed change-order invoice and the landing pricing tier are allow-listed).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/quote-terminology.test.ts` ("REQ-972 …": the four strings, and the es.json terminology guard) · e2e `e2e/money-bar/money-bar.e2e.test.ts` (REQ-798 story's estimates caption now "$1,200 1 quote out"; new "REQ-972 (q1-52) …" story: one sent quote, the column reads "1 cotización enviada" in Spanish and "1 quote out" in English) · integration n/a — copy-only, no server change.
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED at 16e7e33e):** `npx jest unit/quote-terminology.test.ts` → `Tests: 5 failed, 5 total` (`Expected: "{n} quote out" Received: "{n} estimate out"`; `Expected: "{n} cotización enviada" Received: "{n} presupuesto enviado"`; insurance why "…to your bids" / "…a tus propuestas"). `shots run e2e/money-bar -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-798 … expected "$1,200 1 quote out", got "$1,200 1 estimate out"` and `✗ REQ-972 … the Spanish estimates column reads "1 cotización enviada" ($1,200 1 presupuesto enviado)`.
**Fix:** copy-only, in `lang/en.json` + `lang/es.json` (kept in sync; the internal bucket key `estimates` is code, not copy, and stays): `moneyBar.bucket.estimates.one/other` -> "{n} quote out" / "{n} quotes out" and "{n} cotización enviada" / "{n} cotizaciones enviadas"; `welcome.insurance.why` -> "…proof of insurance to your quotes." / "…comprobante de seguro a tus cotizaciones."
**Evidence (2026-11-18, GREEN):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/quote-terminology.test.ts` → `Tests: 5 passed, 5 total`. Full jest unit lane (`npx jest --selectProjects unit …`) → `Test Suites: 608 passed, 608 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6089 passed, 6090 total`. `PORT=5733 deno task serve` + `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> BASE_URL=http://localhost:5733 shots run e2e/money-bar -- --no-check` → `tests finished rc 0`, `✓ REQ-798 … the estimates column lists the quote and opens it`, `✓ REQ-972 (q1-52) … 'quote out' in English and 'cotización enviada' in Spanish` — 2 pass · 0 fail. `deno fmt --ext=json - < lang/{en,es}.json` → unchanged.

## REQ-974 — LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-53: an optional setup-checklist item is never counted as a thing left
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." Issue **q1-53** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 1: "Setup checklist shows the optional insurance item as '1 thing left' with a red bar."
**Root cause:** `front-end/islands/SetupChecklist.tsx` has no notion of an optional item. The insurance item ("Insurance (optional but helps)" / "Seguro (opcional pero ayuda)") is built like the required ones, so `remaining = items.filter(i => !i.done)` counts it, the heading picks `setupChecklist.heading.one` ("Termina la configuración — falta 1 cosa"), the bar stops at 6/7 = 86%, and the coral alarm styling never goes away, because the card only hides at `remaining.length === 0`. REQ-227(5) decided the dashboard keeps insurance on the setup list, not that it counts as a missing task.
**Requirement:** Insurance (and any item marked `optional`) stays listed and links to `/settings#insurance`, but the heading count and the progress bar use the required items only. With only optional items open, the card reads as done (`setupChecklist.heading.optionalOnly` in both dictionaries, the bar at 100%). The counting lives in a pure helper `setupChecklistSummary(items)` in `front-end/lib/setup-checklist.ts` → `{ requiredLeft, optionalLeft, pct, headingKey }`.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/setup-checklist.test.ts` ("REQ-974 …": only insurance open → requiredLeft 0, pct 100, optionalOnly; logo + insurance → heading.one, pct over required; the island uses the helper and marks insurance optional; both dictionaries) · int n/a — front-end only, the profile API does not change · e2e `e2e/setup-checklist-optional/setup-checklist-optional.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-974 q1-53 …": all onboarding answered except insurance, /dashboard in es → heading not "falta 1 cosa", progressbar aria-valuenow 100, insurance listed → /settings#insurance). Note for the fixer: `e2e/settings-deep-links` (REQ-513) finds the insurance link by the name "Insurance (optional but helps)", so it needs updating if the label changes.
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED):** `npx jest unit/setup-checklist.test.ts` → `Tests: 5 failed, 5 total` (`Cannot find module '../../front-end/lib/setup-checklist'`; `Expected pattern: /setupChecklistSummary\(/`; optionalOnly key `Received: "undefined"`); `shots run e2e/setup-checklist-optional -- --no-check` against `PORT=35117 deno task serve` → `✗ REQ-974 … expectation failed: the heading does not count the optional item as a thing left (got "Termina la configuración — falta 1 cosa")`.
**Fix:** new pure helper `front-end/lib/setup-checklist.ts` `setupChecklistSummary(items)` → `{ requiredLeft, optionalLeft, pct, headingKey }`, counting and percenting over the non-`optional` items only. `front-end/islands/SetupChecklist.tsx` gives `Item` an `optional` flag, marks insurance `optional: true`, and takes the heading key, count and bar from the helper; the card hides only when nothing at all is open, and with only optional items open it switches from the coral alarm to a calm green panel + full green bar. New key `setupChecklist.heading.optionalOnly` ("You're set up — the rest is optional" / "Ya estás listo — lo que queda es opcional") in both dictionaries, before the trailing `comms.a2p.*` keys. The insurance label is unchanged, so REQ-513's `settings-deep-links` story still finds it.
**Evidence (2026-11-18, GREEN):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/setup-checklist.test.ts` → `Tests: 5 passed, 5 total`; the full unit lane `npx jest --selectProjects unit …` → `Tests: 1 skipped, 6089 passed, 6090 total` (incl. settings-deep-links, i18n-dictionary-consistency, pay-links, actor-name, staff-placeholder-c2); `cd front-end && deno lint islands/SetupChecklist.tsx lib/setup-checklist.ts` → `Checked 2 files`; `deno check` same files → ok; `shots run e2e/setup-checklist-optional e2e/settings-deep-links -- --no-check` against `PORT=36565 deno task serve` → `✓ REQ-974 q1-53 … · 5.5s`, `✓ REQ-513 p8-pair1-b … · 7.5s`.

## REQ-975 — LOOP-007 q1-55: the Danger zone wipe block has its own heading; no confirm field shows its keyword as a placeholder
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." Issue q1-55, cycle 1 [polish/BUG_POLISH]: "Danger zone: the account-wipe block has no heading; the confirm placeholder looks pre-filled."
**Root cause:** `DangerZoneCard` in `front-end/islands/SettingsPage.tsx` builds its two sub-blocks unevenly. REQ-199 (474f09dc) added the Reset sub-block (`data-cy="settings-reset"`) with a bold `t.resetTitle`, an intro and a bottom border, above the older wipe content (f04e001e). The wipe content was left as a bare `<p>{t.wipeIntro}</p>` + label + input + button with no title, so "This deletes your account…" reads as part of the Reset block, and the card's only heading ("Danger zone") sits above Reset. P-65 (0b4b2703) set the wipe input's `placeholder={keyword}` ("DELETE"/"ELIMINAR"), and the Reset modal input uses `placeholder={resetKeyword}` ("RESET"/"REINICIAR"). `inputStyle` has no placeholder styling, so the empty field looks already typed. No `settings.wipeTitle` key exists.
**Requirement:** (a) The wipe content is its own sub-block, `data-cy="settings-wipe"`, opening with a bold title from `settings.wipeTitle` (EN "Delete account", ES "Eliminar cuenta"), its confirm input `data-cy="settings-wipe-confirm-input"`. (b) Neither confirm input (wipe, reset) uses its keyword as the placeholder.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/settings-wipe-heading.test.ts` ("REQ-975 …": both dictionaries carry `settings.wipeTitle`; the `settings-wipe` block has `{t.wipeTitle}` before `{t.wipeIntro}` and holds the wipe input; neither confirm input has `placeholder={keyword}` / `placeholder={resetKeyword}`) · int n/a — front-end only, no backend path · e2e `e2e/settings-wipe-heading/settings-wipe-heading.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-975 …", ES and EN: `[data-cy=settings-wipe]` opens with "Eliminar cuenta"/"Delete account" and holds the wipe input, whose placeholder is not "ELIMINAR"/"DELETE"; the reset modal input's placeholder is not "REINICIAR"/"RESET"). Note for the fix: `e2e/settings-numbering` (REQ-199) reads the reset keyword from the placeholder; it needs another source (the label's quoted word) once the placeholder goes.
**Evidence (RED, 2026-11-18, at 16e7e33e):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/settings-wipe-heading.test.ts` → 4 failed (`Expected: "Delete account" Received: undefined`; `no data-cy="settings-wipe" in DangerZoneCard`; `Expected pattern: not /placeholder=\{\s*keyword\s*\}/`; same for `resetKeyword`). `shots run e2e/settings-wipe-heading -- --no-check` against `PORT=5617 deno task serve` → both ES and EN `✗ … expectation failed: there is no [data-cy=settings-wipe] block — the wipe content has no sub-block of its own`.
**Fix:** `DangerZoneCard` (`front-end/islands/SettingsPage.tsx`) now wraps the wipe content in its own `data-cy="settings-wipe"` sub-block that opens with a bold `{t.wipeTitle}` (same style as the Reset title) before `{t.wipeIntro}`. The wipe input carries `data-cy="settings-wipe-confirm-input"` and `autoComplete="off"`. Both confirm inputs (wipe and reset) now use `placeholder={t.typeToConfirm}`, a hint that can't be mistaken for typed text, where they used to show the keyword. New keys go in both dictionaries ahead of the `comms.a2p.*` tail: `settings.wipeTitle` (EN "Delete account" / ES "Eliminar cuenta") and `settings.typeToConfirm` (EN "Type the word above" / ES "Escribe la palabra de arriba"). Neighbour fix, as noted above: `e2e/settings-numbering` (REQ-199) used to read the reset keyword from the placeholder. It now reads the quoted word from the field's label, which is the same source the island takes the keyword from. No REQ-975 assertion was changed.
**Evidence (GREEN, 2026-11-18):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/settings-wipe-heading.test.ts` → 4 passed. Neighbours `npx jest --selectProjects unit <every unit test that reads SettingsPage.tsx or lang/*.json>` → Test Suites: 608 passed, 608 total; Tests: 6088 passed, 1 skipped. `cd front-end && deno lint islands/SettingsPage.tsx && deno check islands/SettingsPage.tsx` → clean; `deno lint e2e/settings-numbering/settings-numbering.e2e.test.ts` → clean. `PORT=5617 deno task serve` + `BASE_URL=http://localhost:5617 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… shots run e2e/settings-wipe-heading e2e/settings-numbering -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-975 … lang=en`, `✓ REQ-975 … lang=es`, `✓ REQ-199 …` (3 pass · 0 fail).

## REQ-977 — One browser-tab title format: "<Page> · DocuMonster" (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-56)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." QA issue **q1-56** [polish/BUG_POLISH] "Inconsistent browser tab titles", LOOP-007 cycle 1.
**Requirement:** every signed-in app page's tab title, in EN and ES, ends with " · DocuMonster" and uses no em/en dash separator. The pages the sidebar names lead with the sidebar's label: /dashboard → `nav.home` ("Inicio" in ES, not "Panel"), /communications → `nav.phone` or `nav.communications`, /messages → `nav.outbox`, /reports → `nav.reports`. A customer's page reads "<name> · Customers · DocuMonster" ("Linda Pérez · Clientes · DocuMonster"). Public pages outside the app shell (/q, /i, /co, /sign, /welcome, login/verify, contact, errors, demo stage, pay/plan test pages, ops approve) are out of scope and may keep their own titles.
**Root cause (at 16e7e33e):** there is no single title format. `DocTitle` (front-end/components/DocTitle.tsx) and lib/doc-title.ts (REQ-367) render whatever string a route's builder returns, so each page hand-writes its full title, brand included, in lang/*.json. Later modules did it differently: `comms.docTitle` "Phone"/"Teléfono" (ef665dbe, REQ-915/916), `outbox.docTitle` "Outbox"/"Bandeja de salida" (f3ba1da1, REQ-784), `reportsPage.docTitle` and `roof.docTitle` "… — DocuMonster" with an em dash (0c7e27ef, REQ-794/795), `hr.*.docTitle` "HR · Overview" etc. with no brand (a12a9135, REQ-883..889), `accountsManager.docTitle` "Accounts Manager" with no brand; customers/[id].tsx returns the bare customer name (1c0be6f7, REQ-924); the Spanish `dashboardPage.docTitle` "Panel · {brand}" differs from the sidebar's "Inicio". The only guard (jest/unit/brand-name.test.ts) checks that ≥10 titles contain DocuMonster.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/doc-title-format.test.tsx` ("REQ-977 (q1-56): …" — walks every in-app `<DocTitle title={(l) => …}>` call site under front-end/routes, evaluates the route's builder with the real tFor + lib/doc-title.ts exports, renders it through the real DocTitle and judges the painted title and both data-title-* attributes: brand suffix, no dash, sidebar label lead, customer page) · int `front-end/lib/route-doc-title-format.int.test.tsx` ("REQ-977 (q1-56): …" — the real middleware + page in a Fresh app for /dashboard, /communications, /messages, /reports, /hr, /customers/:id; checks the SSR `<title>` in EN and ES) · e2e `e2e/tab-title-format/tab-title-format.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-977 (q1-56): …" — a Spanish account opens /communications, /messages, /reports, /hr and a customer's page; reads document.title after hydration).
**Evidence (2026-11-18), RED:** `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/doc-title-format.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 4 failed` (no brand on customers/[id], tools/satellite, messages, hr ×7, accounts-manager, communications, reports; em dash on reports + satellite; "Panel · DocuMonster" should start with "Inicio · "; "Linda Pérez" ≠ "Linda Pérez · Customers · DocuMonster"). `deno test -A lib/route-doc-title-format.int.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 6 failed`. `shots run e2e/tab-title-format -- --no-check` against a worktree `PORT=7313 deno task serve` → ✗ with `/communications: "Teléfono"`, `/messages: "Bandeja de salida"`, `/reports: "Informes — DocuMonster"`, `/hr: "RR. HH. · Resumen"`, `/customers/<id>: "Linda Pérez"`.
**Fix:** one rule, in code: `appTitle(lang, ...parts)` in front-end/lib/doc-title.ts joins the non-empty parts with `TITLE_SEP` (" · ") and appends `tFor(lang, "brand.name")` itself, so a page supplies only its own name (most specific first, then its section) and never the brand. The non-conforming in-app routes now build with it, reusing the sidebar's own keys where one exists so tab and sidebar match by construction: /dashboard `appTitle(l, nav.home)` ("Inicio · DocuMonster"), /communications `appTitle(l, comms.docTitle, nav.communications)` ("Teléfono · Comunicaciones · DocuMonster"), /messages `appTitle(l, nav.outbox)`, /reports `appTitle(l, nav.reports)`, /tools/satellite `appTitle(l, roof.docTitle)`, /accounts-manager `appTitle(l, accountsManager.docTitle)`, /hr/* `appTitle(l, hr.<page>.docTitle, nav.hr)` ("Resumen · RR. HH. · DocuMonster"), /customers/:id `appTitle(l, name, nav.customers)` ("Linda Pérez · Clientes · DocuMonster"; "Clientes · DocuMonster" while the customer fails to load). The dictionaries lost the hand-written brand/em-dash/"HR · " prefix: `reportsPage.docTitle` "Reports"/"Informes", `roof.docTitle` "Satellite measure"/"Medición satelital", `hr.*.docTitle` "Overview"/"Resumen" etc.; ES `dashboardPage.docTitle` "Inicio · {brand}" (still read by ui-breakdown). Pages already in the "<Page> · DocuMonster" form keep their dictionary titles; the REQ-977 unit test now walks every in-app DocTitle call site, so a new page that skips the format goes red. Public pages keep their own titles on purpose (the customer sees the business there — `publicDocTitle`, shared/documents/public-brand.ts). Existing test touched: front-end/lib/route-doc-title-lang.int.test.tsx (REQ-709) expected /accounts-manager to read the brand-less `accountsManager.docTitle` and /dashboard `dashboardPage.docTitle`; both now expect the `appTitle` builder the routes use — the REQ-709 assertion (the tab follows `?lang=`) is unchanged.
**Evidence (2026-11-18), GREEN:** `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/doc-title-format.test.tsx lib/route-doc-title-format.int.test.tsx` → `ok | 11 passed | 0 failed`. `deno test -A lib/doc-title-format.test.tsx lib/route-doc-title-format.int.test.tsx lib/route-doc-title-lang.int.test.tsx lib/html-lang-title.test.tsx` → `ok | 25 passed | 0 failed`. `BASE_URL=http://localhost:47142 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/tab-title-format -- --no-check` against a worktree `PORT=47142 deno task serve` → `✓ REQ-977 (q1-56): … read '<Page> · DocuMonster' in the tab · 11.2s` (1 pass · 0 fail). Neighbours: `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit …` (brand-name, route-doc-title-lang, hr-module, reports-export, roof-copy, live-lang-switch, i18n-dictionary-consistency, ux-page-copy, …) → `Test Suites: 607 passed, 607 total; Tests: 6084 passed, 1 skipped`; `deno lint` + `deno check` on every touched front-end file → clean. Pre-existing reds not caused here (files untouched by this fix): front-end/lib/outbox.test.tsx "REQ-784 d12 … Outbox is a root row" (Outbox moved into the Communications folder in 3fe1df39, REQ-914); e2e/route-doc-title REQ-709 /quotes expects "Quotes · DocuMonster" but quotesPage.docTitle is "Quotes &amp; agreements · DocuMonster" (unchanged by this fix).

## REQ-976 — LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-57: the header search dropdown closes when focus leaves it
**Source:** Raphael (QA loop): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." Issue **q1-57** [polish/BUG_POLISH], LOOP-007 cycle 1: on /communications the header search "stays open with a stale "Nada coincide con “512”" after focus moves to another field".
**Root cause:** `front-end/islands/GlobalSearch.tsx` closes its panel in only three cases: a document `mousedown` outside the island, Escape, or picking a row. Nothing closes it when focus leaves by keyboard (Tab) or by a programmatic focus, because there is no blur/focusout handler. `showPanel = open && q.trim() !== ""` and the query is never cleared, so the "no match" line keeps rendering. On top of that, the debounced fetch callback calls `setOpen(true)` unconditionally. A `/search` answer that lands after an outside click has closed the panel re-opens it over the field the user moved to. The island shipped this way in 474f09dc (REQ-198..210), and the close logic is unchanged through REQ-799 and REQ-924.
**Requirement:** the search panel closes when focus moves out of the search island (Tab, programmatic focus, a click elsewhere), and a search answer that arrives after that does not re-open it. Picking a row still works.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/global-search-focus-close.test.tsx` ("REQ-976 q1-57 …": the real island compiled with the automatic JSX runtime and mounted in deno-dom with a stubbed `dashboardClient.search`; '512' → no match → focus moves to another input → the panel is gone; type '512' → outside mousedown + focus move → the held answer resolves → the panel stays closed) · int n/a — front-end only, the /search API is not at fault · e2e `e2e/global-search-focus-close/global-search-focus-close.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-976 q1-57 …": on /communications, '512' → "Nothing matches" → Tab, and later focusing the area-code field `comms-search`, closes the panel; type '512' and click the area-code field while the '512' answer is held in flight by `page.route` → after the answer lands the panel is still closed).
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED at 16e7e33e):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/global-search-focus-close.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed` (`REQ-976: focus left the search box but the panel still shows the stale 'no match' for '512'`, `REQ-976: the late /search answer re-opened the panel after focus had moved away`). `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… shots run e2e/global-search-focus-close -- --no-check` → both ✗ (`after Tab the search panel still shows the stale 'No match for “512”'`, `the late '512' answer re-opened the search panel … expected 0, got 1`). Sanity check: with a scratch fix (root `onFocusOut` closing when `relatedTarget` is outside, plus the callback's `setOpen(true)` dropped), applied and then reverted, both levels go green (unit `ok | 2 passed`, e2e 2 ✓).
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `front-end/islands/GlobalSearch.tsx`: the island root has an `onFocusOut` that closes the panel when focus moves to something outside the island. A null `relatedTarget` right after a mousedown inside the island (panel padding, scrollbar) does not count, and a focused related link inside the panel does not close it. The debounced fetch callback no longer calls `setOpen(true)`, because typing, focus, `/` and ArrowDown already open the panel. A row pick still works: its mousedown `preventDefault` keeps focus in the box. **Test change (e2e story 2 only, no assertion touched):** its `page.waitForResponse('512', 15 s)` was armed before the fill, the click, the held route and the 2 s `panelGoneWithin`. On a loaded host (load avg 150–200) that chain alone ran past 15 s, and the dangling rejection killed the module before `release()` ran (net.jsonl had no `q=512`). The wait is now armed right before `release()`, which is still before the held request can answer.
**Evidence (2026-11-19, GREEN):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/global-search-focus-close.test.tsx` → `ok | 2 passed | 0 failed`. `BASE_URL=http://localhost:5476 SHOTS_JOBS=1 shots run e2e/global-search-focus-close/global-search-focus-close.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` → `2 pass · 0 fail`. On the same server with the island reverted to 16e7e33e → `0 pass · 2 fail` (`after Tab the search panel still shows the stale 'No match for “512”'`, `the late '512' answer re-opened the search panel … expected 0, got 1`), so the edited story still catches the bug. Neighbours: `shots run e2e/global-search/global-search.e2e.test.ts` → `3 pass · 0 fail` (REQ-207+799, REQ-519, REQ-799 phone; their earlier red under parallel load was a post-navigation `waitFor` timeout and went green alone). `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit …search files…` ran the whole unit lane: `Test Suites: 607 passed`, `Tests: 1 skipped, 6084 passed`. `deno lint` + `deno check islands/GlobalSearch.tsx` clean, and `deno fmt -` on both touched files shows no diff. No lang keys touched.

## REQ-978 — Settings number fields refuse bad input with an inline message, never a silent revert (LOOP-007 q1, q1-58)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." LOOP-007 cycle 1, issue **q1-58** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION] "Invalid numbers in Settings are silently reverted".
**Root cause:** In `EditCard` (`front-end/islands/SettingsPage.tsx`) each number field's onBlur checks the value and, when it fails, puts the stored value back and returns: no error state, no save, no "Saved". "Days to pay an invoice" −5 fails `n < 0` and snaps back to `accountNetDays(invoiceNetDays)` (45); "Overhead per visit" in % mode 500 fails `pct > 100` and becomes `fieldOverheadPct ?? 0`; the $ overhead and the chargeback fee do the same for a negative or blank value. REQ-501 gave the email and business name inline errors (`emailErr`/`bizErr`, rules in `shared/quote-flow/settings-fields.ts`), but the number fields (REQ-174, REQ-788 + AMENDMENT, REQ-926) were left without that path, and the native `min`/`max` never show a bubble because no form is submitted — while the hero promises "saved instantly".
**Requirement:** `shared/quote-flow/settings-fields.ts` gains `netDaysError(raw)` (integer 0–365), `overheadError(raw, "flat" | "percent")` (≥ 0, not blank, ≤ 100 for %) and `moneyError(raw)` (≥ 0, not blank), each returning an en+es dictionary key or null. On a bad blur Settings shows the message under the field (`settings-net-days-error`, `settings-overhead-error`, `settings-chargeback-fee-error`, `aria-invalid`), keeps the typed value on screen, saves nothing; a valid value clears the error and saves.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/settings-number-validate.test.ts` ("REQ-978 …": the three rules with −5/366/1.5/blank, 500/101/−1 %, −1/blank $; keys in both dictionaries; the island calls the rules, renders the three errors with aria-invalid, and the silent reverts are gone) · int n/a — the backend already refuses these on `PUT /profile/identity` (`UpdateBusinessIdentity` DTO `@Min(0) @Max(365)` on invoiceNetDays, `@Min(0) @Max(100)` on fieldOverheadPct, `@Min(0)` on the cents fields; pinned for pct 101 in `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts:2240`); the bug is client-only · e2e `e2e/settings-number-validate/settings-number-validate.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-978 q1-58: …": −5 days, 500 %, −1 chargeback fee → inline error, typed value kept, stored 45 / 10 / 3500 unchanged; 30 then saves and clears the error).
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED at 16e7e33e):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/settings-number-validate.test.ts` → `Tests: 6 failed, 6 total` (`shared/quote-flow/settings-fields.ts has no netDaysError()`, `Expected pattern: /netDaysError\(/`, `Expected pattern: not /n > 365\)…setNetDays(String(accountNetDays/`); `shots run e2e/settings-number-validate -- --no-check` against `PORT=5733 deno task serve` → `expectation failed: days to pay -5: the typed value stays on screen (not silently put back) — expected "-5", got "45"`.
**Fix:** `shared/quote-flow/settings-fields.ts` gains `netDaysError` (`settings.netDaysInvalid`), `overheadError(raw, mode)` (`settings.overheadPctInvalid` in %, `settings.moneyInvalid` in $) and `moneyError` (`settings.moneyInvalid`), with en+es copy. `EditCard` in `front-end/islands/SettingsPage.tsx` keeps `netDaysErr`, `overheadErr` and `cbFeeErr` the way REQ-501 keeps `emailErr`: a bad blur sets the error, renders it under the field (`role=alert`, `aria-invalid`), keeps the typed value and saves nothing. Typing clears the error, a valid blur saves, and switching the overhead mode clears its error. The silent restores to the stored value are gone.
**Evidence (2026-11-18, GREEN on fix/q1-q1-58):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/settings-number-validate.test.ts` → `Tests: 6 passed, 6 total`; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit <the 38 suites naming SettingsPage/settings-fields>` → `Test Suites: 608 passed, 608 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6090 passed` (the path args matched the whole unit lane); `cd front-end && deno lint islands/SettingsPage.tsx ../shared/quote-flow/settings-fields.ts` → `Checked 2 files`; `deno check` on both → clean; `deno fmt -` on all 4 touched files → no change; `PORT=5947 KV_PATH=<scratch>.kv deno task serve` + `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> BASE_URL=http://localhost:5947 shots run e2e/settings-number-validate -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-978 q1-58 … · 2.5s — 1 pass · 0 fail`. Neighbouring stories `shots run e2e/field-tasks e2e/payment-chargeback e2e/settings-one-net-days` → 28 pass, 2 fail. REQ-143 passed on its own rerun (it failed only under load). REQ-842 (/field/workers → /field/tasks `tk-cover-for`; it never opens /settings) fails the same way against a server built from base 16e7e33e, so it was red before this change and is not caused by it.

## REQ-979 — AMENDMENT to REQ-921: a New invoice on an account with no services is not a dead end (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-59)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." QA issue q1-59 [minor/MISSING_IN_FLOW], cycle 1: "New invoice without saved services: Amount is read-only, there is no free-text line, and a typed price is ignored."
**Root cause:** two causes add up, both from REQ-921. (1) The line picker is select-only: `ServiceSelect` wraps `SearchSelect` without `onCreate`, so on an empty or non-matching catalogue it shows "No matches", and the only help is a link that leaves the form for /field/services. (2) The Amount box and the totals check different things. `InvoicesPage` locks `new-invoice-amount` on `lines.length > 0`, which counts raw rows, and the form always opens with one `emptyServiceRow()`. The totals come from `serviceRowsToLines(lines)`, which drops any row with no service name, so a row priced 65 with no service gives no lines, and `computeTotals` falls back to the empty, locked `amount`. The result is a Subtotal of $0.00 with no message, and Amount stays locked until the user finds "Remove this service" on the empty row.
**Requirement:** (a) With `allowCreate`, the service picker offers `+ Add "<typed>"` when the typed name matches no service. Choosing it creates a real catalogue service (POST /api/field/task-types) and picks it, so a line still bills a catalogue service. (b) Amount is locked only while some row bills a service (`amountLocked(rows) === serviceRowsToLines(rows).length > 0`). An untouched empty row leaves the one-amount bill editable. (c) A price on a row with no service shows "Pick a service on every line." inline, never a silent $0.00.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/new-invoice-no-services.test.ts` ("REQ-979 …": `amountLocked` exported from shared/documents/service-lines; empty row, or a price with no service → false; a picked service → true; it agrees with `serviceRowsToLines`) · int n/a — the form never calls the backend for this; the create call uses the existing task-types endpoint, which its own int tests already cover · e2e `e2e/new-invoice-no-services/new-invoice-no-services.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-979 q1-59 …": with no services, typing "Lawn mowing" offers a create row, which picks it, $65 gives Subtotal $65.00, and the task-types list now has it; the untouched empty row leaves Amount editable and 65 gives $65.00; a price with no service shows the hint or bills). The fix must AMEND the REQ-921 story `e2e/service-lines` ("Snow plowing" asserts no `search-select-create`).
**Evidence (2026-11-18), RED at 16e7e33e:** `cd jest && npx jest unit/new-invoice-no-services.test.ts` → `TypeError: amountLocked is not a function`, `Tests: 4 failed, 4 total`. `shots run e2e/new-invoice-no-services -- --no-check` against `FRONTEND_PORT=5637 BACKEND_PORT=5638 deno task serve` → `0 passed | 3 failed`: "the picker offers to add the typed service (create rows: 0, "No matches" rows: 1)"; "the Amount box is editable while no row bills a service (readonly="", rows: 1)"; "a priced row with no service either bills or says why (subtotal $0.00, hint shown: false)".
**Fix (2026-11-18):** `shared/documents/service-lines.ts` gains `amountLocked(rows)` (true only while a row names a service — the same test `serviceRowsToLines` uses), `touchedServiceRows` (a row with neither service nor price is an untouched blank and never blocks a save) and `pricedRowWithoutService`. `InvoicesPage` locks and fills `new-invoice-amount` from `amountLocked(lines)` instead of `lines.length > 0`, checks `serviceRowsError(touchedServiceRows(lines))` on save, and shows "Pick a service on every line." inline (`new-invoice-line-hint`) while a row has a price but no service (hidden once a refused save shows the same text, so it never appears twice). `ServiceSelect` takes an optional `onCreate` and forwards it to `SearchSelect` with the label `serviceLines.create` (`+ Add "{name}" as a service` / `+ Agregar "{name}" como servicio`); New invoice, the invoice edit lines and the repeat-visit form wire it to `fieldClient.createTaskType`, add the new service to the island's catalogue and pick it, so a line still bills a real catalogue service. The form still opens with one empty row (the REQ-979 e2e drives `new-invoice-line-price-0` on it). Amended REQ-921 tests: `jest/unit/service-lines.test.ts` now asserts ServiceSelect forwards `onCreate={onCreate}` with the `serviceLines.create` label (was `not.toMatch(/onCreate=/)`), and `e2e/service-lines` now expects the "Snow plowing" create row to read `+ Add "Snow plowing" as a service` (was 0 create rows) — both encoded the no-create rule this amendment replaces.
**Evidence (2026-11-18), GREEN:** `cd jest && npx jest unit/new-invoice-no-services.test.ts` → `Tests: 4 passed, 4 total`. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` (the whole unit project) → `Tests: 1 skipped, 6088 passed, 6089 total`. `cd front-end && deno check` + `deno lint` on InvoicesPage.tsx, FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx, components/ServiceSelect.tsx, shared/documents/service-lines.ts → `Checked 4 files`, no lint findings. ## REQ-933 — LOOP-007 q1-6: the "Paid" invoice email does not ask the customer to pay
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green".
