## REQ-998 — AMENDMENT to REQ-601: a worker add (or editor invite) that could not be texted says why (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-85)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." QA loop LOOP-007, cycle 1, issue **q1-85** [minor/BUG_POLISH] "Worker add failure for a reserved number gives no reason". The tester added a worker at 843-555-0142 (reserved 555-01XX, refused by design per REQ-523) and read only "We couldn't text Luis Ortega — share the link and PIN yourself."; the owner isn't told why and may think the worker's phone is broken.
**Root cause:** the reason is thrown away between the SMS service and the page. `SmsService.send` refuses the 555-01XX number before Twilio with `{ ok:false, failureCode:"fictional", reason:"sms.fictionalNumber" }`, but `welcomeWorker()` in `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field-controllers/mod.ts` only logs `sent.reason` and returns `{ ok, url, body }`; `POST /field/workers` answers `texted:false`, `signInUrl`, `shareText` with no failure code, and `FieldWorkersPage` keeps `{ name, texted, pin, share }` and renders the one generic `field.wk.notTexted` whatever the cause. The `/me/admins` invite (`AdminsPage`, `admins.notTexted`) drops it the same way. Came in with REQ-151; REQ-601 added the link/PIN but no reason.
**Requirement:** the add/invite answers `smsFailureCode` when the text did not go; /field/workers and /admins keep it and word the reason per code (`field.wk.notTexted.<code>` / `admins.notTexted.<code>` for fictional, invalid, notMobile, optedOut, missing; the old line stays the fallback for "other"), in en and es. A reserved number reads "… reserved test number (555-01XX …) …" / "… número de prueba reservado …".
**Tests:** int `backend/src/field/entrypoints/worker-share-link.int.test.ts` ("REQ-998 … smsFailureCode 'fictional'"), `backend/src/users/entrypoints/admins-controller/invite-share.int.test.ts` ("REQ-998 … editor invite …") · unit `jest/unit/invite-share-link.test.ts` ("REQ-998 …": per-code keys in en+es, the reserved-number wording, both islands keep `smsFailureCode` and render the per-code key) · e2e `e2e/invite-share-link/invite-share-link.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-998 …": /field/workers en + `?lang=es`, /admins).
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED at 16e7e33e):** int `FAILED | 2 passed | 2 failed` (`- undefined + "fictional"` on both); jest `Tests: 4 failed, 7 passed, 11 total`; shots against a `PORT=56923 deno task serve` → the 3 REQ-998 stories fail: got "We couldn't text Luis Ortega — share the link and PIN yourself.", "No pudimos mandarle el texto a Luis Ortega — compártele el enlace y el PIN.", "We couldn't text (830) 555-0103 an invite — … Let them know yourself."; the REQ-601 stories in the file stay green.
**Fix:** the reason is carried end to end. `welcomeWorker()` (`backend/src/field/entrypoints/field-controllers/mod.ts`) returns `failureCode` (the SmsService's, "other" when absent or on a throw) and `POST /field/workers` answers `smsFailureCode` when `texted` is false; `AccountAdmins.invite` (`backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/account-admins/mod.ts`) does the same for `POST /me/admins`. `front-end/clients/field.ts` + `clients/admins.ts` type it (the shared `SmsFailureCode`); `front-end/lib/invite-share.ts` `notTextedReason()` keeps the worded codes (fictional, invalid, notMobile, optedOut, missing — "other" → the plain line); `FieldWorkersPage` and `AdminsPage` keep it in their `added`/`sent` state and render `field.wk.notTexted.<code>` / `admins.notTexted.<code>` (with `{name}`/`{phone}`), the old line as the fallback. New en+es keys sit next to their base keys (not after `comms.a2p.*`). No test was changed.
**Evidence (2026-11-18, GREEN):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/field/entrypoints/worker-share-link.int.test.ts src/users/entrypoints/admins-controller/` → `ok | 10 passed | 0 failed`; neighbours `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/field/entrypoints/ src/users/entrypoints/admins-controller/ <account-admins tests>` → `ok | 69 passed | 0 failed`; `cd jest && npx jest unit/invite-share-link.test.ts` → `Tests: 11 passed, 11 total`; full unit lane `npx jest --selectProjects unit` → `Test Suites: 607 passed, 607 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6088 passed`; `cd front-end && deno lint` + `deno check` on the 5 touched front-end files → clean; `deno check` on the 2 backend files → clean; shots against `PORT=57613 deno task serve` → `shots run e2e/invite-share-link` 6 pass · 0 fail (the 3 REQ-998 stories + the REQ-601 ones).

## REQ-1000 — LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-86: the timesheet's first load never claims "No punches this week" before the week is loaded
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." QA issue q1-86 [minor/BUG_POLISH], LOOP-007 cycle 1: "Timesheet first load shows 'No punches this week' while a worker is clocked in" (/field/timesheet; a reload showed the punch).
**Root cause:** `front-end/islands/TimesheetPage.tsx` starts with `report = null` and `punches = []` and fetches report, punches and workers in a `useEffect` after mount, with no "loaded yet" flag. The server render and every client render before that `Promise.all` settles turn `punches.length === 0` into the log panel's count "0" and `ts.noPunches` ("No punches this week."), the same screen as a week that really is empty; the worker rows need `report` too, so none show. The backend's week window and range filter are correct (a reload shows the punch). Dates from REQ-192 (61c8f68a); REQ-786 left the initial state unchanged.
**Requirement:** until the week's data has loaded, the punch-log panel shows neither the empty-state copy nor a count of 0 (a loading state instead); once loaded, the punch rows show, and a week that really has no punches still says "No punches this week."
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/timesheet-first-load.test.tsx` ("REQ-1000 (LOOP-007 q1-86) [en|es] …": the island's render before any fetch has no `ts.noPunches` and no "0" count in `[data-cy=ts-log-panel]`) · e2e `e2e/timeclock/timesheet-first-load.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1000 (LOOP-007 q1-86) …": a worker clocks in through `/api/timeclock/worker/punch`, `/api/timeclock/punches` is delayed 2 s, every state of the log panel is recorded from the first parsed byte; none before the punch row may show the empty copy or a 0; the week before, really empty, still says "No punches this week.") · integration n/a — the backend returns the right data; the defect is client-only render state.
**Evidence (RED, 2026-11-18, cycle 1):** `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/timesheet-first-load.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed` (`not loaded yet, but the log panel already says "No punches this week.": <h3 class="panel__title">Punches <span class="count">0</span></h3>…`, and the same in Spanish "Sin marcas esta semana."). `shots run e2e/timeclock -- --no-check` against `PORT=5637 deno task serve` → REQ-192 ✓, REQ-786 ✓, REQ-1000 ✗ `the log panel said "No punches this week." before the punch loaded: ["count=0 rows=0 empty=true","count=1 rows=1 empty=false"]`.
**Fix (cycle 1):** `TimesheetPage.tsx` keeps `loadedWeeks` — the week offset whose report/punches/workers last settled (null before the first fetch). Until it equals the shown `weeks`, the log panel drops the count and shows `field.common.loading` ("Loading…" / "Cargando…", `data-cy=ts-log-loading`) instead of `ts.noPunches`; after load, the rows or the real empty copy show as before. No new lang keys.
**Evidence (GREEN, 2026-11-19, cycle 1):** `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/timesheet-first-load.test.tsx` → `ok | 2 passed | 0 failed`. `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on `islands/TimesheetPage.tsx`; `deno fmt -` leaves it unchanged. Jest neighbours `npx jest --selectProjects unit -i --runTestsByPath unit/timeclock-feature.test.ts unit/timeclock-worker-hours.test.ts unit/sidebar-root-folders.test.ts` → `Tests: 14 passed, 14 total`. `shots run e2e/timeclock/timeclock.e2e.test.ts e2e/timeclock/timesheet-first-load.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` against `PORT=5653 deno task serve` (fresh KV) → `2 pass · 0 fail` (REQ-192 ✓, REQ-1000 ✓); REQ-786 ✓ in the same server's earlier run.

## REQ-1001 — Worker view: tapping a service's name checks it off (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-87) — AMENDMENT to REQ-196 (row-wide check-off target)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." QA issue **q1-87** (LOOP-007, cycle 1, polish/BUG_POLISH): "Tapping the service name on the worker view doesn't check it off — only the small Done square works." (/worker at 390x844)
**Root cause:** in `WorkerScreen.renderVisit` each service row (`.svc`) is a flex row of two parts: a 46x46 `<button class="svc__check" data-cy="w-check">`, which alone carries the onClick that calls `workerClient.complete/uncomplete`, and a plain `<div class="svc__name">` with the service name (plus the added/deferred/lock extras) that has no handler, no role and no pointer cursor. A tap on "Lawn mowing" lands on that inert div and nothing happens. It came in with the first version of the screen (fd52cfa2, REQ-137..143), and neither the REQ-196 redesign ("large tap targets to check tasks off") nor the REQ-362 preview lock (63e78ef3) widened the target to the row.
**Requirement:** the whole service row is the check-off target: tapping the name toggles complete/uncomplete like the square does, the toggling element keeps `data-cy="w-check"`, it is disabled under the same locked / preview / busy conditions, the row shows `cursor: pointer` (default when locked), and the extras do not double-fire.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/worker-row-check.test.ts` ("REQ-1001 …": the complete/uncomplete onClick sits on an element wrapping `.svc__name`, with `data-cy="w-check"` and the locked/preview/busy guard; `.svc` has `cursor: pointer`, a locked row `cursor: default`) · int n/a — front-end only, the complete/uncomplete endpoints already work · e2e `e2e/worker-row-check/worker-row-check.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1001 …": 390x844, a worker with "Lawn mowing" today taps the `.svc__name` text → POST `/complete`, row `svc--done`, chip "Done", name cursor pointer; a second tap → POST `/uncomplete`; tomorrow's preview row's name posts nothing).
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED at 16e7e33e):** `npx jest unit/worker-row-check.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 failed, 3 total` (the onClick element is `<button class="svc__check">…</button>`, which closes before `.svc__name`; `.svc` has no `cursor: pointer`). `shots run e2e/worker-row-check -- --no-check` against `PORT=5733 deno task serve` → `expectation failed: tapping "Lawn mowing" posts /complete (requests seen: [])`, `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** in `front-end/islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` the `.svc` row itself is now the `<button type="button" data-cy="w-check" aria-pressed disabled={s.locked || preview || busy.has(s.id)}>` that runs `workerClient.complete/uncomplete`; the 46px square became a decorative `<span class="svc__check" aria-hidden="true">` and the name a `<span class="svc__name">` inside it, so a tap anywhere on the row — the name included — toggles it, and the row's accessible name is now the service name instead of "Done". CSS: `.svc` resets the button (no border/background, `font`/`color` inherit, left-aligned, full width) with `cursor: pointer`; `.svc:disabled` and `.svc--locked` get `cursor: default`; the square's fade moved to `.svc:disabled .svc__check`, and the square inherits the row's cursor. The extras are spans with no handlers, so nothing fires twice.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --runInBand unit/worker-row-check.test.ts unit/worker-screen-redesign.test.ts` → `Tests: 7 passed, 7 total` (worker-row-check alone at the base file: `Tests: 3 failed, 3 total`). `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5761 shots run e2e/worker-row-check e2e/worker-tomorrow e2e/worker-ssr e2e/field-multi-day-job -- --no-check` against `PORT=5761 deno task serve` → `4 pass · 0 fail` (REQ-1001, REQ-362/528, REQ-197, REQ-785; the w-check neighbours still click and read `aria-pressed`/`disabled` on the row). `deno lint` + `deno check islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` clean; `deno fmt -` leaves the file unchanged.

## REQ-1003 — The new-hire email names the business that is hiring, not DocuMonster (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-88)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue q1-88 [minor/BUG_POLISH]: "New-hire email is DocuMonster-branded with no business name" (Outbox 005-email: From "DocuMonster" <hello@documonster.com>, subject "You're almost MONSTERIZED 🦷 — sign your new-hire paperwork", body "Welcome aboard, Jose!", and Reyes Lawn & Landscape is never named).
**Requirement:** The signing-link email `HrNotices.sendLink` sends to a new hire (the invite and the 24-hour reminder) comes From the business: `businessFrom({ alias, name })` (REQ-628), with the business's name as the display name, never the house "DocuMonster" From. The subject, the headline and the body say which business is hiring, in both dictionaries (`hr.email.inviteSubject`, `inviteHeadline`, `inviteBody`, `reminderSubject` carry `{company}`).
**Root cause:** `HrNotices.sendLink` (a12a9135, REQ-883..889) works out `company` (`settingsFor` → HR companyName → businessName → legalName → user name) and the text message uses it, but the email drops it twice. (1) Of `hr.email.*`, only reminderBody has a `{company}` slot (lang/en.json and es.json 5508-5511), and the headline's `t()` gets no vars. (2) The private `mail()` calls `email.send({ to, subject, htmlBody })` with no `from`, so `postmarkPayload` falls back to `HOUSE_FROM` = `"DocuMonster" <hello@documonster.com>`.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/hr/domain/coordinators/hr-notices/test.ts` ("REQ-1003 <lang> <key> names the hiring business": the four strings render the company, en + es) · int `backend/src/hr/entrypoints/hr-email-sender.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1003 the new-hire invite email is From the business and names it in subject + body": POST /hr/hires with autoSend, the EmailService input's Postmark payload) · e2e n/a: the HR email shows on no app page (HrNotices doesn't write it to the /messages outbox, and the hire's file doesn't show its From or subject), so the email boundary the int test reads is the only place to see it. NOTE for the fixer: `backend/src/hr/entrypoints/hr.int.test.ts:383` asserts the email contains "MONSTERIZED". That pins the old wording, so amend it to the new subject.
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED):** `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/hr/domain/coordinators/hr-notices/test.ts src/hr/entrypoints/hr-email-sender.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 9 failed`. Unit: e.g. `Expected actual: "You're almost MONSTERIZED 🦷 — sign your new-hire paperwork" to contain: "Reyes Lawn & Landscape"`. Int: `From="DocuMonster" <hello@documonster.com>`, `- fromName: "DocuMonster", htmlNamesBusiness: false, subjectNamesBusiness: false`.
**Fix (2026-11-18):** `HrNotices.mail()` now takes the sender. `sendLink` (invite + reminder) sends `from: businessFrom({ alias: identity.emailAlias, name: companyName })` with `replyTo` = the HR address, and `notifyComplete` uses the business From too. The dictionaries (en + es): `inviteSubject` "{company}: sign your new-hire paperwork before Day 1", `inviteHeadline` "Welcome to {company}", `inviteBody` names {company}, `reminderSubject` "Reminder from {company}: …". A new `reminderHeadline` means the reminder no longer reuses the invite's headline, and the headline's `t()` now gets the vars. The "MONSTERIZED 🦷" email wording is gone. The signing page's "You're officially MONSTERIZED!" screen is untouched. The hire's page email preview (`HrHireDetailPage`) passes `company` to the subject so it doesn't show a raw `{company}`. Amended, as the test writer flagged: `hr.int.test.ts` pinned the old subject (`"MONSTERIZED"`), and now asserts `from="Monster Reservations Group"` and the new subject.

**User's words:** "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green"

"inbound" : "outbound"`). This amends REQ-887: a department is a name + packet + accounts; division is no longer asked for or forced.

## REQ-1004 — A repeat visit can end on a date, and Pause asks first (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-90)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-18: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q1-90** [minor/MISSING_IN_FLOW] "Repeat visits lack an every-2-weeks cadence and an end date", LOOP-007 cycle 1.
**Root cause:** the repeat-visit form on /field/subscriptions (`front-end/islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx`) has no end-date field, and `POST` / `PUT /field/subscriptions` (`backend/src/field/entrypoints/field-controllers/mod.ts` create()/update()) never read `endDate` from the body, so a seasonal visit can't be given an end even though `isDue` already stops after `Subscription.endDate` (REQ-699, set today only by quote-made subscriptions). `scheduleText` never mentions an end. `toggle()` sends `{active: !s.active}` on the first click of Pause, with no confirmation (and no "pause until"). Every 2 weeks is NOT in scope here: REQ-157 removed it on Raphael's word ("cadence should be weekly or monthly"); the backend already accepts intervalWeeks 2, so re-adding the option is an owner call and needs a REQ-157 AMENDMENT.
**Requirement:** (a) POST and PUT /field/subscriptions take an optional `endDate` (YYYY-MM-DD, not before the first visit, else 400; null on PUT clears it); it is stored and returned, and no task is generated after it. (b) The schedule text appends "· until Mar 31" / "· hasta el 31 mar". (c) The New/Edit repeat visit form has an optional "Ends on" date (`data-cy=subs-end`) next to First visit. (d) Pause on a card opens a confirmation (`data-cy=subs-pause-confirm`); nothing is paused until it is confirmed.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/schedule/test.ts` ("REQ-1004 scheduleText — an end date appends …") · int `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1004 subscriptions — an endDate is kept on create, refused before the start or malformed, set and cleared on edit, and no task is generated after it") · e2e `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1004 (LOOP-007 q1, q1-90): a weekly repeat visit with Ends on set saves …" and "REQ-1004 (LOOP-007 q1, q1-90): Pause on a repeat-visit card asks for confirmation first …"). jest/unit n/a — the island's behaviour is pinned by the e2e stories and the text by the backend unit test.
**Evidence (2026-11-18), RED:** `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/domain/business/schedule/test.ts src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts --filter REQ-1004` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed` (`- Every week · Mon / + Every week · Mon · until Mar 31`; "the end date is kept on create" `- undefined / + "2026-11-25"`); `shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check --filter REQ-1004` → "the form has an 'Ends on' date next to First visit — expected 1, got 0" and "one click on Pause does not pause the visit — expected true, got false".
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `POST`/`PUT /field/subscriptions` read `endDate` through a new `parseEndDate` (`field-controllers/mod.ts`): YYYY-MM-DD, not before the first visit, else 400; absent keeps it, null/"" clears it; on PUT it is re-checked whenever either end moves. `isDue` already stops after `endDate`, so generation needed no change. `scheduleText` appends `untilText` ("· until Mar 31" / "· hasta el 31 mar"). The form has an optional "Ends on" date (`data-cy=subs-end`, `min` = First visit, client check `field.subs.endBeforeStart`); an edit sends `endDate: null` when blank. Pause on an active card sets a per-card `pauseId` showing `field.subs.confirmPause` with Pause (`subs-pause-confirm`) / Cancel; Resume stays one click. New lang keys `field.subs.end`, `endNone`, `endBeforeStart`, `confirmPause` in en + es.
**Evidence (2026-11-19), GREEN:** `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/domain/business/schedule/test.ts src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts --filter REQ-1004` → `ok | 2 passed | 0 failed`; neighbours `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/domain/business/schedule/ src/field/entrypoints/` → `ok | 72 passed | 0 failed`; `shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check --filter REQ-1004` against `PORT=5463 deno task serve` (BASE_URL; the self-started serve wedged on Vite "transport was disconnected" under host load ~110–160) → `2 pass · 0 fail`. `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on `islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx`, `clients/field.ts`, `schedule/mod.ts`, `field-controllers/mod.ts`; lang/en.json + es.json valid, 6280 keys each, same key set. Touched hunks are fmt-clean (`field-controllers/mod.ts` and `clients/field.ts` had pre-existing fmt drift elsewhere at the base, left alone).

## REQ-1005 — (LOOP-007 q1, cycle 1, q1-91) An empty day on /worker that is not today never says "No tasks today" (REQ-744 AMENDMENT)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q1-91** [polish/BUG_POLISH], LOOP-007 cycle 1: `/worker?date=2026-11-20` read "Viewing Fri, Nov 20 · 🔒 Preview … No tasks today · Nothing scheduled. · No tasks this day."
**Root cause:** REQ-744 (704703d6) added `workerTodayKey(n)` in `front-end/lib/worker-today.ts`, which picks the summary key from the task count alone; for `n === 0` it always returns `worker.today.none` ("No tasks today" / "Sin tareas hoy"). The worker view also shows Yesterday, Tomorrow and any picked day (REQ-194/362/528), and `WorkerScreen.tsx` holds both the shown day (`date`) and the real day (`today`) but calls `workerTodayKey(liveTasks.length)` without comparing them, so an empty other day still says "today" — under "Viewing <date>" and above the day-neutral `worker.none` line.
**Requirement:** when the shown day has no tasks and is not today, `[data-cy=w-count]` reads a day-neutral line — `worker.day.none`: "No tasks this day" / "Sin tareas este día" — chosen by `workerTodayKey(n, date === today)`; today's empty day keeps "No tasks today" / "Sin tareas hoy"; counts keep REQ-744's singular/plural forms.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/c5-worker-today-plural.test.ts` ("REQ-1005 …": `workerTodayKey(0, false)` → `worker.day.none`, en/es copy has no "today"/"hoy", `(0, true)` unchanged, both dictionaries carry the key, WorkerScreen calls `workerTodayKey(liveTasks.length, date === today)`) · int n/a — front-end copy only, no backend path · e2e `e2e/c5-worker-today-plural/c5-worker-today-plural.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1005 …": a worker with no tasks opens `/worker?date=<tomorrow>`; w-count reads "No tasks this day", and with `&lang=es` "Sin tareas este día", no "hoy").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-18):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/c5-worker-today-plural.test.ts` → `Tests: 4 failed, 7 passed, 11 total` (`Expected: "worker.day.none" Received: "worker.today.none"`; `Expected: "No tasks this day" Received: "No tasks today"`). `shots run e2e/c5-worker-today-plural -- --no-check` against `PORT=5617 deno task serve` → `✗ REQ-1005 … expectation failed: an empty Tomorrow does not say "today" (got "No tasks today")`.
**Fix:** `workerTodayKey(n, isToday = true)` in `front-end/lib/worker-today.ts` returns `worker.day.none` for an empty day that is not today; `WorkerScreen.tsx` passes `date === today` (the same comparison its day picker uses); `lang/en.json` + `lang/es.json` gain `worker.day.none` ("No tasks this day" / "Sin tareas este día") next to the other `worker.today*` keys.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern c5-worker-today-plural` → `Tests: 11 passed, 11 total` (at the base commit the same file was `4 failed`); whole jest unit lane → `Tests: 1 skipped, 6089 passed, 6090 total`. `cd front-end && deno lint islands/WorkerScreen.tsx lib/worker-today.ts` → `Checked 2 files`; `deno check` on both → clean; `deno fmt -` on the touched files → no diff; en/es JSON parse. `shots run e2e/c5-worker-today-plural -- --no-check` against `PORT=5619 deno task serve` → `✓ REQ-1005 …` (65.7s). The file's older REQ-744 story fails on its first, one-task assertion (`got "Thu, Nov 19"`): it reads `.greet small`, which renders `dayLine()` (fd52cfa2), not the count — untouched by this fix (the one-task key is unchanged) and red at HEAD for that reason.

## REQ-1006 — Deleting a task tells the owner whether the customer was texted (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-92)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q1-92** [minor/MISSING_IN_FLOW], LOOP-007 cycle 1: "Deleting a scheduled one-off doesn't text the customer, and the owner isn't told".
**Root cause:** the cancellation text of REQ-171 is sent only when the account's `fieldTexts` flag is on (REQ-177, on purpose); `featureOn` reads an unset flag as off, so a fresh account sends nothing and `DELETE /field/tasks/:id` answers `{ ok: true, texted: false }`. The front end throws that away: `fieldClient.deleteTask` is typed `{ ok: true }` and `FieldTasksPage.remove()` always flashes a bare "Task deleted", so the contractor cancels a customer's visit with no idea they still have to tell the customer. Whether `fieldTexts` should default on or be a contractor-facing setting is an owner call (REQ-177), not this fix.
**Requirement:** after a delete the flash says whether the customer was texted: texted → `field.tk.deletedTexted` ("… {customer} was texted …"); not texted and the visit is today or later → `field.tk.deletedNotTexted` ("… {customer} was not told …"); a past visit → plain "Task deleted". Chosen by `deletedNotice(texted, taskDate, today, customer)` in `front-end/lib/field.ts`; `deleteTask` is typed with `texted?: boolean`; en + es keys.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/field-task-delete-told.test.ts` ("REQ-1006 …": deletedNotice per case, both dictionaries, the client type, remove() reads texted) · int n/a — the route already answers `texted` (`field.int.test.ts` covers REQ-177 off → false and REQ-171 on → true) · e2e `e2e/field-delete-told/field-delete-told.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1006 …": fresh account, tomorrow's one-off for Ana Torres, Delete → Yes, delete → DELETE answers texted:false and the flash says she was not told).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-18):** `npx jest unit/field-task-delete-told.test.ts` → `Tests: 7 failed, 7 total` (`Expected: "function" Received: "undefined"`; `Received string: "{ ok: true }"`). `shots run e2e/field-delete-told -- --no-check` against `PORT=57461 deno task serve` → `✗ REQ-1006 … expectation failed: the flash tells the owner Ana Torres was not told (got "TASK DELETED")` (the texted:false assertion passed).
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `deletedNotice()` in `front-end/lib/field.ts` picks the flash; `fieldClient.deleteTask` is typed `{ ok: true; texted?: boolean }`; `FieldTasksPage.remove()` reads `res.texted` and flashes `t(notice.key, notice.vars)`; en + es gain `field.tk.deletedTexted` / `field.tk.deletedNotTexted`. No backend change: the route already answered `texted`.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `npx jest --selectProjects unit --runTestsByPath unit/field-task-delete-told.test.ts` → `Tests: 7 passed, 7 total`; full jest unit lane → `Test Suites: 608 passed, 608 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 6091 passed, 6092 total`. `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:57463 shots run e2e/field-delete-told/field-delete-told.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` against `PORT=57463 deno task serve` → `✓ REQ-1006 (LOOP-007 q1-92): delete tomorrow's one-off on a fresh account → the flash says the customer was not told · 84.1s`. `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on FieldTasksPage.tsx, lib/field.ts, clients/field.ts; en/es 6278 keys each, same key set, valid JSON.

## REQ-1007 — Add task and New work order fill the customer's known service address, not just their city (LOOP-007 q1, q1-93, cycle 1)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue q1-93 [minor/MISSING_IN_FLOW], LOOP-007 cycle 1: "One-off task and work order fill only the customer's city, not the known service address. The repeat visit already has the street address."
**Cause (from the RCA at 16e7e33e):** a customer whose record holds only city + state composes `customer.address` = "Myrtle Beach, SC" (`shared/customer-address/mod.ts` `composeAddress` drops the empty street). Their repeat visit was saved with its own full address, "1200 N Ocean Blvd, Myrtle Beach, SC", which lives only on the subscription; REQ-144 leaves the customer record untouched and REQ-340's write-back (`field-controllers/mod.ts` ~2096) only fills a customer with NO address, so the record stays city-only. /field/tasks Add task loads customers as `{id, name, address: c.address}` (`FieldTasksPage.tsx:98`) and prefills `picked?.address` (~1160); the New work order modal sets `serviceAddress = c.address` (`WorkOrdersPage.tsx:337`). Neither island looks at the customer's repeat visits, so both fill "Myrtle Beach, SC".
**Requirement:** picking a customer in /field/tasks Add task and in /work-orders New work order fills the address with the customer's known service address: the address of their most recently updated ACTIVE repeat visit when it is more complete than the customer record's address (the customer has no address, or no street — the visit's address contains it and is longer); otherwise the customer's own address (a customer with their own street address keeps it — REQ-340's separation). One pure helper, `knownServiceAddress(customer, subscriptions)` in `front-end/lib/field.ts`. A typed address is never overwritten (REQ-144 `prefillAddress`).
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/field-service-address.test.ts` ("REQ-1007 knownServiceAddress …": city-only + visit → the visit's street address; no visit → the customer's; another customer's / a paused visit ignored; the most recently updated of two; no address on file → the visit's; an own street address kept; a typed address stays) · int n/a — the fix is a front-end prefill over data the API already returns (`GET /field/subscriptions`); add a `field.int.test.ts` case only if the REQ-340 write-back is extended · e2e `e2e/known-service-address/known-service-address.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1007 (LOOP-007 q1-93) …": customer Ana with city=Myrtle Beach, state=SC + a repeat visit at 1200 N Ocean Blvd → Add task's `tk-add-address` and New work order's `wo-new-address` both hold the street).
**Evidence (2026-11-18) RED:** `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/field-service-address.test.ts` → 7 FAILED, `Error: front-end/lib/field.ts exports no knownServiceAddress(customer, subscriptions)`; `shots run e2e/known-service-address -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1007 … expectation failed: Add task and New work order fill the repeat visit's street address "1200 N Ocean Blvd, Myrtle Beach, SC" (got Add task "Myrtle Beach, SC", New work order "Myrtle Beach, SC")`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `knownServiceAddress(customer, subscriptions)` in `front-end/lib/field.ts` picks the most recently updated ACTIVE repeat visit's address when the customer has no address or the visit's address contains theirs and is longer; else the customer's own. `FieldTasksPage.tsx` `loadAllCustomers` fetches `GET /field/subscriptions` once and gives each customer that address; `WorkOrdersPage.tsx` loads the subscriptions with its lists and prefills `serviceAddress` from it. Typed addresses still win (REQ-144 `prefillAddress` / the `!serviceAddress.trim()` guard).
**Evidence (2026-11-19) GREEN:** `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/field-service-address.test.ts` → `ok | 7 passed | 0 failed`; `deno test -A lib/*field*.test.ts` → `ok | 33 passed | 0 failed`; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit <field/work-order files>` → `Test Suites: 607 passed`, `Tests: 1 skipped, 6084 passed`; `deno check` + `deno lint` clean, `deno fmt -` no diff on the 3 touched files; `PORT=5471 deno task serve` + `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5471 shots run e2e/known-service-address -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1007 (LOOP-007 q1-93) … both fill the visit's street address · 246.6s`.

## REQ-1008 — LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-94: "Foreman" means two different powers
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." QA issue q1-94 [minor/BUG_POLISH], cycle 1.
**Root cause:** the code has two foreman ideas and English gives them one word. The account-wide `FieldWorker.role: "foreman"` (REQ-138/141, fd52cfa2) sees and closes every crew's visits; the crew lead `Crew.foremanId` (REQ-840, 58ddd0cb) acts on its own crew only (`canActOn`, `backend/src/field/domain/business/crews/mod.ts`). REQ-840's keys reused "Foreman" (`field.crew.foreman`, `field.crew.leads`, `field.crew.foremanNone`) while the account-wide keys already said "Foreman" (`field.wk.foreman` "Foreman (sees and closes every crew's visits)", `field.wk.foremanBadge`, `field.asg.foremanTag`, `worker.foreman`). `publicWorker` in `backend/src/field/entrypoints/worker-controller/mod.ts` also answers `role: "foreman"` for a crew lead, so the /worker chip (`WorkerScreen.tsx`) reads the same for both powers. Spanish already splits them (Capataz / Encargado), but its checkbox says "toda la cuadrilla" (the whole crew) where it means every crew.
**Requirement:** the account-wide role and the crew lead carry different names in English and Spanish: no account-wide label (`field.wk.foreman`, `field.wk.foremanBadge`, `field.asg.foremanTag`) uses the crew lead's word (`field.crew.foreman`); the Spanish checkbox says "todas las cuadrillas"; `GET /field/worker/me` tells the two apart, and the /worker chip names the power the person really has.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/field-foreman-kinds-copy.test.ts` ("REQ-1008 …") · int `backend/src/field/entrypoints/foreman-kinds.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1008 (q1-94): GET /field/worker/me tells the account-wide foreman and a crew lead apart") · e2e `e2e/foreman-kinds/foreman-kinds.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1008 (q1-94): … /field/workers and /worker": the add checkbox vs the New crew modal's picker label; the crew lead's /worker chip vs the account-wide one).
**Evidence (red, 2026-11-18, at 16e7e33e):** jest → `Tests: 2 failed, 1 passed` (en: `field.wk.foreman: Foreman (sees and closes every crew’s visits)`, `field.wk.foremanBadge: Foreman`, `field.asg.foremanTag: foreman`; es: `"Capataz (ve y cierra las visitas de toda la cuadrilla)"`); int → `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` (`Expected actual: { role: "foreman" } not to be: { role: "foreman" }`); e2e against `PORT=5731 deno task serve` → `expectation failed: the account-wide checkbox ("Foreman (sees and closes every crew’s visits)") must not use the crew lead's word ("Foreman")`; with that line bypassed, the chip check also fails: `a crew lead's chip ("FOREMAN") must not read the same as the account-wide one ("FOREMAN")`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** the account-wide role is now **Supervisor** in English (`field.wk.foreman` "Supervisor (sees and closes every crew’s visits)", `field.wk.foremanBadge` "Supervisor", `field.asg.foremanTag` "supervisor", `worker.foreman` "Supervisor"); the crew lead keeps "Foreman" (`field.crew.*`). Spanish keeps Capataz (account-wide) vs Encargado (crew), and the checkbox now says "todas las cuadrillas". `publicWorker` (`backend/src/field/entrypoints/worker-controller/mod.ts`) still answers `role: "foreman"` for both (REQ-840's `field.int.test.ts` and the worker's ?all=1 list rely on it) and adds `crewLead: true` when the power is only their own crew's; `WorkerMe` (`front-end/clients/field.ts`) carries it and the /worker chip (`WorkerScreen.tsx`) reads the new `worker.crewLead` ("Crew foreman" / "Encargado de cuadrilla") for a crew lead, `worker.foreman` for the account-wide role.

## REQ-1009 — An invoiced task on /field/tasks is visibly read-only (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-95)
**Source:** Raphael: "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green." Add service, Edit dates and Delete are disabled `.btn`s but still drawn. Present since fd52cfa2 (REQ-137..143).
**Requirement:** on an invoiced task card: the price is plain text (`tk-price-locked`) beside the Invoiced chip, with no price input; Add service, Edit dates and Delete are not rendered; the done-check is disabled, named "Invoiced" (`field.tk.invoiced`) in aria-label and title, and dimmed (`.task__check:disabled { opacity; cursor: not-allowed }`).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/field-invoiced-task-locked.test.ts` ("REQ-1009 …": price text when locked and the input gated on `!locked`; the three buttons gated on `!locked`; the check's label/title use `field.tk.invoiced` when locked; field.css dims `.task__check:disabled`) · e2e `e2e/field-invoiced-task-locked/field-invoiced-task-locked.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1009 …": a completed task pulled into a batch and sent → /field/tasks card shows the Invoiced chip, no price input, a `tk-price-locked` $65.00, no Delete/Add service/Edit dates, the check disabled, titled and named "Invoiced", opacity < 1, cursor not-allowed) · integration n/a — the server's 409 on a price change to an invoiced task already exists and is pinned by REQ-141 in field.int.test.ts.
**Evidence (2026-11-18, RED):** `npx jest unit/field-invoiced-task-locked.test.ts` → `Tests: 4 failed, 4 total` (no `tk-price-locked`; the Add service guard is `{!adding && !asking && !editing && (`; the check's aria-label is `x.status === "complete" ? t("field.tk.markOpen") : t("field.tk.markDone")`; `.task__check:disabled` is only `cursor: default;`). `shots run e2e/field-invoiced-task-locked -- --no-check` against `FRONTEND_PORT=5611 BACKEND_PORT=5612 deno task serve` → `expectation failed: no price input on an invoiced task — expected 0, got 1` (after the Invoiced chip rendered).
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `FieldTasksPage.card()`: when `locked` the price renders as a `<span data-cy="tk-price-locked">` ($ + `priceCents/100`, titled "Invoiced") instead of the `tk-price` input; Add service, Edit dates and Delete are gated on `!locked` (no longer drawn-but-disabled); the done-check's aria-label/title read `field.tk.invoiced` when locked. `field.css`: `.task__check:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed }`. ## REQ-1010 — AMENDMENT of REQ-210 / REQ-609: a work order assigned to a worker shows on that worker's /worker day (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-96)
**Source:** Raphael (QA loop): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". Issue q1-96 [minor/MISSING_IN_FLOW], LOOP-007 cycle 1: "Work order assignee is free text and never reaches the worker's view" — QA assigned WO-001 to "Mike Carter" for 2026-11-24 and /worker?date=2026-11-24 as Mike said "No tasks this day."
**Root cause (at 16e7e33e):** work orders (REQ-210) and field tasks (REQ-141/164) are separate models. The WO Assignee is a free-text `<input>` (`WorkOrdersPage.tsx` `wo-new-assignee`, `WorkOrderPage.tsx` `wo-edit-assignee`), stored as `assignee: string` (`paperwork/dto/work-order.ts`, `work-order-store/mod.ts`) with no worker id, and nothing creates or links a field task. `GET /field/worker/tasks` (`field/entrypoints/worker-controller/mod.ts` `list()`) returns only field-day rows (`this.day.generate(...)` filtered by `onTask`), so a WO never reaches a worker. REQ-609 deferred "link a task to a work order".
**Requirement:** (a) The WO Assignee (new and edit forms) is a `<select>` over the account's workers, sending `assigneeWorkerId` with the name. (b) The API stores an optional `assigneeWorkerId`, refusing (4xx) a worker of another account. (c) A WO with `assigneeWorkerId` + `scheduledFor` lists on that worker's `GET /field/worker/tasks?date=<scheduledFor>` as a row carrying `workOrderId`, without prices, and on nobody else's day; moving the date, reassigning or cancelling the WO follows. (d) `workOrders.vsTasks` (en + es) says an assigned work order shows on the worker's day.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/work-order-assignee-worker.test.ts` ("REQ-1010 …": both Assignee controls are `<select>`, both forms load workers and send `assigneeWorkerId`, the client types carry it, the vsTasks copy) · int `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/worker-view.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1010 …": Mike's day lists the WO, not Pedro's, no price; date move / reassign / cancel follow; a foreign worker id is refused) · e2e `e2e/work-order-worker-view/work-order-worker-view.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1010 …": the owner picks Mike in New work order for day D; Mike's /worker?date=D shows the job).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-18, fix/q1-q1-96):** int → `FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed` ("Mike's /worker day … lists WO WO-001" `- 0 + 1`; "expected a 4xx for a foreign worker, got 200"); jest → 6 of 6 failed (`<input>` not `<select>`, no workers client, no `assigneeWorkerId`, vsTasks copy); e2e → `locator.selectOption: Error: Element is not a <select> element … resolved to <input type="text" data-cy="wo-new-assignee"/>`.
**Fix (2026-11-19, fix/q1-q1-96):** the WO carries an optional `assigneeWorkerId` (`paperwork/dto/work-order.ts`, kept by `WorkOrderStore`; an edit with `assigneeWorkerId: ""` unassigns — the id and the name go). Paperwork can't import Field (Field imports paperwork), so the controller checks the worker through a new `WorkOrderWorkerPort` (`paperwork/domain/coordinators/work-order-worker-port`) that Field's `FieldWorkOrderWorkers` registers on at boot (the REQ-699 port pattern): another account's or an unknown worker → 400 `invalid`; a picked worker with no Assignee text gets the worker's name. `GET /field/worker/tasks` appends the day's work orders read straight off the WO store (`field/domain/business/work-order-day`: assigned + `scheduledFor` = the day + not cancelled; a foreman's `all=1` gets the crew's/account's like tasks) as read-only rows with `workOrderId` / `workOrderNumber`, no price, no notes — so a date move, reassign or cancel follows with nothing to sync. Front end: both Assignee controls are a `<select>` over `fieldClient.workers()` ("Not assigned" + the workers; a pre-REQ-1010 free-text assignee stays as its own option and is left untouched on save); `/worker` renders a WO row as its own card (`visitKey` → `wo:<id>`, never merged into a one-off's visit) with customer, address, "Work order WO-001" and the job, no check/note/defer. New keys `workOrders.modal.assigneeNone`, `worker.workOrder` (en + es); `workOrders.vsTasks` now says an assigned, scheduled work order shows on that worker's day. Unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/test.ts` added for the projection.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q1-q1-96):** `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/worker-view.int.test.ts src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/test.ts` → `ok | 4 passed | 0 failed`; neighbours `deno test -A --unstable-kv --parallel src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/ src/paperwork/domain/data/ src/field/` → `ok | 236 passed | 0 failed`; `deno task test:unit` → deno `ok | 1795 passed | 0 failed`, jest `Test Suites: 608 passed` / `Tests: 1 skipped, 6090 passed, 6091 total` (incl. `unit/work-order-assignee-worker.test.ts` 6/6); `deno task test:int` → `ok | 1332 passed | 0 failed`; e2e `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5627 shots run e2e/work-order-worker-view/work-order-worker-view.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` against `PORT=5627 deno task serve` → `✓ REQ-1010 … · 7.4s`. `deno check` + `deno lint` clean on the touched front-end files and the touched backend modules; `deno check bootstrap/mod.ts` clean.

## REQ-1011 — LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-97: a deferred visit reads its date localized, and a deferred-only day does not draw a 0/0 card under "Sin tareas hoy"
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q1-97** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 1: on /worker (ES) the deferred visit's label shows a raw date ("APLAZADA DE 11-18"), and the deferred day shows "Sin tareas hoy · Nada programado." with a "0/0" card.
**Root cause:** two faults. (1) `front-end/islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` feeds `worker.fromYesterday` with `s.deferredFrom.slice(5)` ("11-18"), and `front-end/islands/FieldTasksPage.tsx` does the same for `field.tk.deferredFrom`, though `fmtDay(iso, lang)` (lib/field.ts, "mié 18 de nov") is already imported in both — since fd52cfa2 (REQ-137..143). (2) The summary counts `liveTasks` (`isLive` drops deferred/skipped), so a day whose only task was deferred reads `workerTodayKey(0)` = "Sin tareas hoy" + "Nada programado.", while the body chooses cards from `mine.length` (deferred rows included) and `renderVisit` draws the chip `${done}/${act_.length}` = "0/0" — the very "0 of 0" REQ-744 removed. `renderSection` (foreman) has the same split (`liveRows` for the count, `rows.length` for the body).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/worker-deferred-day.test.ts` ("REQ-1011 …": both labels go through `fmtDay`, not `.slice`; a `workerDayCounts(tasks)` helper in `front-end/lib/worker-today.ts` → `{live, deferred}`; the visit chip is never the bare `${done}/${act_.length}`; the body and renderSection do not pick cards from the unfiltered row count) · int n/a — the backend's defer data is right (`deferredFrom` is on the moved task, covered by the field int tests); the fault is front-end rendering only · e2e `e2e/worker-deferred-day/worker-deferred-day.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1011 …": ES worker defers today's one-off "Leaf cleanup" through the UI → no "0/0" chip, no "Nada programado" over a drawn card → next day the label reads "aplazada de <fmtDay>").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-18, cycle 1, at 16e7e33e):** `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern worker-deferred-day` → `Tests: 5 failed, 1 passed` (`Received string: "s.deferredFrom.slice(5)"`, `"x.deferredFrom.slice(5)"`, `workerDayCounts` `Received: "undefined"`, the 0/0 chip and `body = mine.length` still present); `shots run e2e/worker-deferred-day -- --no-check` → `expectation failed: no visit chip reads "0/0" on the deferred day (got ["0/0"]) | the summary does not say "Nada programado" while 1 card(s) are drawn (summary "0%Sin tareas hoyNada programado.") | no raw MM-DD date in the label (got "aplazada de 11-18") | the label reads "aplazada de mié 18 de nov" (got "aplazada de 11-18")`.
**Fix (2026-11-19, cycle 1):** both labels now pass `fmtDay(deferredFrom, lang)`. New `workerDayCounts(rows)` → `{live, deferred}` in `front-end/lib/worker-today.ts`. The worker body and `renderSection` draw cards when `live + deferred > 0`, so a deferred visit keeps its card and its "aplazada → mañana" hint, and a skipped-only list shows the empty state. A visit with no live services gets no state chip, where it used to show "0/0". When the day has no live tasks but does have deferred ones, the summary says `worker.allDeferred` ("Deferred to tomorrow." / "Aplazado a mañana.") instead of "Nada programado." EN and ES got the new key together.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'worker-deferred-day|worker-today|worker'` → `24 suites, Tests: 133 passed`; the whole `npx jest --selectProjects unit` run → `Tests: 1 skipped, 6090 passed, 6091 total`; `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5497 shots run e2e/worker-deferred-day/worker-deferred-day.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` (against `PORT=5497 deno task serve`, fresh KV) → `✓ REQ-1011 … · 30.3s`; `deno lint` and `deno check` pass on WorkerScreen.tsx, FieldTasksPage.tsx and worker-today.ts, and `deno fmt -` leaves all three unchanged.

No other en/es string claims "only today" for the worker view (`grep -i "only today\|solo.*del día" lang/en.json lang/es.json` → none after the fix). ## REQ-1014 — The /field/workers Away row formats its dates like every other field screen (LOOP-007 cycle 1, q1-99)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-18 (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q1-99** [polish/BUG_POLISH], cycle 1: "Away list shows the raw date '2026-11-26'" — every other screen formats the date.
**Root cause:** the Away panel row in `front-end/islands/FieldWorkersPage.tsx` (`data-cy="away-row-dates"`, ~line 905, added by REQ-842 in 58ddd0cb9) renders `{a.from === a.to ? a.from : `${a.from} → ${a.to}`}`, the YYYY-MM-DD strings straight from `GET /field/absences`, and never calls the field date formatter. The island imports only `fmtCell` and `PHONE_PLACEHOLDER` from `../lib/field.ts`, while /field/tasks and /worker run days through `fmtDay` (`front-end/lib/field.ts`), which gives "Thu, Nov 26" / "jue 26 de nov".
**Requirement:** the Away row reads one day as `fmtDay(from, lang)` ("Thu, Nov 26") and a range as "Thu, Nov 26 → Fri, Nov 27", localized in Spanish, never a raw YYYY-MM-DD. A pure helper `fmtDayRange(from, to, lang)` in `front-end/lib/field.ts` builds it.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/field.test.ts` ("REQ-1014 fmtDayRange — …": one day, a two-day range, Spanish) · int n/a — display only; the API correctly returns ISO dates · e2e `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1014: a crew marked out on /field/workers — one day, then a two-day range — …").
**Evidence (2026-11-18):** RED — `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/field.test.ts` → `FAILED | 10 passed | 3 failed` (`field.ts exports fmtDayRange(from, to, lang)`); `shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check --filter REQ-1014` → `expectation failed: one-day Away row reads "Wed, Nov 18" (got "2026-11-18")`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `front-end/lib/field.ts` exports `fmtDayRange(from, to, lang)` (one day → `fmtDay(from, lang)`, a range → `fmtDay(from) → fmtDay(to)`), and the Away row in `front-end/islands/FieldWorkersPage.tsx` renders `fmtDayRange(a.from, a.to, lang)` instead of the raw ISO strings.
**Evidence (2026-11-19):** GREEN — `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/field.test.ts` → `ok | 13 passed | 0 failed` (same file at the base field.ts: `FAILED | 10 passed | 3 failed`); `SHOTS_SERVE_TIMEOUT=400000 shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check --filter REQ-1014` → `✓ REQ-1014 … 123.3s`, and the Away-panel neighbour `✓ REQ-842 … 294.4s` (the filter ran the whole file under host load avg ~180; 8 other stories "did not finish", none on /field/workers' Away row — the known host-lane cut); `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → `Test Suites: 607 passed`, `Tests: 1 skipped, 6084 passed`; `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on both touched files, both already `deno fmt`-clean.
