## REQ-1020 — LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-11: the customer page's invoice tables stay reachable at 390px (balance, Remind, Mark paid)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-11** [major/BUG_POLISH], cycle 2: "Customer page Invoices table is clipped at 390px: SALDO column and Remind / Mark paid actions are off-screen".
**Root cause:** REQ-924 (1c0be6f7) renders every customer-workspace table as a bare `<table class="cws-table">` inside `.cws-card` (front-end/islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx: payments, visits, jobs, InvoiceTable for the Invoices tab and the compact Resumen "unpaid" table, quotes). The only rules at ≤640px in front-end/static/customer-workspace.css hide column 2 and stack `.cws-rowact` vertically. Because `.num`, `.cws-pill` and `.cws-btn` are `white-space: nowrap`, the invoice table's min-content width is about 570px, and `width: 100%` cannot shrink it into the 322px card. That card is `min-width: 0` and has no overflow rule. REQ-353 (dashboard.css) sets `overflow-x: clip` on the shell and `.main`, so the overflow is cut off and cannot be scrolled. SALDO, the balance and the per-row Remind / Mark paid buttons end up off-screen on a phone.
**Requirement:** at ≤640px every cws-table is either a stacked card (tr/td `display:block`, thead hidden, as the Outbox does) or sits inside an `overflow-x: auto` wrapper. At 390x844, every cell of an invoice row, its balance and its Remind / Mark paid buttons are on screen or inside a sideways scroller, the page itself never scrolls sideways, and Mark paid opens the payment sheet on that invoice.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/loop7-q2-11-cws-table-phone.test.ts` ("REQ-1020 q2-11 …": the ≤640px block makes .cws-table a card layout, or every `<table class="cws-table">` in CustomerWorkspace.tsx has a direct parent with overflow-x auto/scroll; the ≤640px block does more than the old two rules). Int: n/a, because this is CSS/markup only and no server behaviour is involved. E2E: `e2e/customer-invoices-phone/customer-invoices-phone.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1020 (q2-11): …": a part-paid invoice, $980 billed with $350 paid, at 390x844 on `?tab=invoices` and on Resumen; one read of every part's right edge, then Mark paid → payment sheet on that invoice).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/loop7-q2-11-cws-table-phone.test.ts` → `Tests: 2 failed, 1 passed` (`cardLayout: "tr block=false td block=false thead hidden=false"`, `"ok": false`, unwrappedTables cws-payments@799 …; `"onlyTheOldTwo": true`). `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> shots run e2e/customer-invoices-phone -- --no-check` → `✗ … Invoices tab: off-screen parts (table right edge 570)":["td6@436","td7@570","balance@428","remind@562","mark-paid@562"] … Resumen unpaid: off-screen parts (table right edge 513)":["td6@513","remind@505","mark-paid@505"]`. The Mark paid click step already passes today, because Playwright's synthetic click reaches the clipped button. It stays in the story as a regression guard for the fix. Both accepted fix shapes were checked against the unit test with a temporary edit, then reverted: a scroll wrapper on all five tables, or a ≤640px card layout. Each gave `3 passed`.
**Fix (2026-11-19, cycle 2):** the stacked-card layout, applied to all five cws tables. In `front-end/static/customer-workspace.css`, the ≤640px block drops the old "hide column 2" rule and lays `.cws-table`, tbody and tr out as blocks with the thead hidden. Each tr is a bordered card. Each td is a flex line pairing `label · value`, with the label drawn by `td[data-label]::before { content: attr(data-label) }`. The first `.cws-doc` cell (number + title) is the card's heading, and the action cell (`.cws-actcell`) puts Remind / Mark paid side by side across the card's full width. In `front-end/islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx`, every labelled cell in payments, visits, jobs, InvoiceTable and QuoteTable now carries `data-label={tFor(lang, "customerWs.col.<same key as its th>")}`, so the labels follow the page language. No new lang keys. The phone also shows every column again, the one hidden before included. Desktop layout is unchanged.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/loop7-q2-11-cws-table-phone.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 passed, 3 total`. `SHOTS_SERVE_TIMEOUT=300000 SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=~/Library/Caches/deno/npm/registry.npmjs.org/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/customer-invoices-phone -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1020 (q2-11): at 390x844 … · 103s`, `1 pass · 0 fail`. The serve timeout was raised only because the host load average was about 130 and the default 60 s boot window kept running out. Element screenshots of both tables at 390px show the cards with SALDO $630.00 and Recordar / Marcar pagada inside the card. Neighbours: `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` (full unit lane) → `Test Suites: 645 passed, 645 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6338 passed`. `cd front-end && deno check islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx` → exit 0. `deno lint islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx` (from a scratch copy, since lint finds no files under .wt-trees) → `Checked 1 file`, no problems.

## REQ-1022 — AMENDMENT of REQ-842 / REQ-1010: a work order follows its assignee's absence — covered, deferred or skipped (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-12)
**Source:** Raphael (QA loop): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". Issue **q2-12** [major/BUG_CONTRADICTION], LOOP-007 cycle 2: "Marking a worker out 'covered by' someone else leaves their work order with the absent worker" — WO-001 assigned to Jake for Nov 20; Jake marked out Nov 20 covered by Miguel; the Away row says "COVERED BY MIGUEL TORRES" while /work-orders keeps WO-001 on Jake and Miguel's /worker day is empty.
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** work orders and field tasks are separate models and only field tasks go through the REQ-842 absence resolver (`crews/mod.ts` `staffOn` / `coverStaff`; `redoAbsence` after `POST /field/absences` re-derives generated tasks only). REQ-1010 put work orders on /worker by reading them straight off the WO store (`field/domain/business/work-order-day/mod.ts` `onWorkOrderDay` / `workOrdersOn`: `assigneeWorkerId` + `scheduledFor` + not cancelled, no absence input), and `worker-controller` `list()` keeps each WO on `wo.assigneeWorkerId` without reading the AbsenceStore. `GET /work-orders` returns the stored `assignee` text with no absence awareness. So a cover changes nothing for a work order: Jake keeps it, Miguel never gets it.
**Requirement:** resolved at read time (the WO's stored assignee and date are untouched): when a WO's assignee is out on its scheduled day, cover → the WO is on the cover worker's (or the cover crew's available members') /worker day, with who they cover for, and off the absent worker's; the cover being out too → nobody; defer/skip → flagged, never silently moved. `GET /work-orders` and `GET /work-orders/:id` carry `coverAssignee` (the cover's name), and /work-orders shows "covered by <name>". Removing the absence puts it back.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/test.ts` ("REQ-1022 …": `woStaffOn(wo, { absences, workers, crews, date })` → cover by Miguel with `coverFor` jake; not out → Jake; cover by a crew → its lead + available members; cover out too → null; defer / skip flagged, date untouched) · int `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/worker-view.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1022 …": POST /field/absences cover by Miguel → WO on Miguel's `GET /field/worker/tasks?date=D` with `coverForName` "Jake Fowler", off Jake's; `GET /work-orders` and `/work-orders/:id` `coverAssignee` "Miguel Torres"; deleting the absence restores Jake) · e2e `e2e/work-order-absence-cover/work-order-absence-cover.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1022 …": Mark out Jake on /field/workers covered by Miguel → the /work-orders row says "covered by Miguel Torres" → Miguel's /worker?date=D shows the job).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-12 at 240a6443):** unit `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/test.ts` → `FAILED | 2 passed | 5 failed` (`REQ-1022: work-order-day/mod.ts exports woStaffOn(...)` `- undefined + function`); int `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/worker-view.int.test.ts --filter REQ-1022` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` ("Miguel covers Jake on 2026-11-22: WO WO-001 is on Miguel's /worker day" `- 0 + 1`); e2e `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5731 shots run e2e/work-order-absence-cover -- --no-check` → `expectation failed: the WO row says it is covered by Miguel Torres (got "Jake Fowler")`.
**Fix:** read-time resolution, the WO's stored assignee and date never change (REQ-1010's no-sync design kept). `crews/mod.ts` exports `coverStaff` (now over `DayPeople` = crews + workers + absences + date). `work-order-day/mod.ts` adds `woStaffOn(wo, { absences, workers, crews, date })` → staffOn's `Resolution`: the assignee out (their own absence, or their crew's) → cover (the named worker, or the named crew's lead + available members, `coverFor` = the assignee; null when the cover is out too), defer (flag + the next day they are back) or skip (flag); `woDayStaff` / `onWorkOrderDay(…, people)` / `workOrderRow(wo, names, staff)` put the row on the cover's day with `coverForName` (+ `crewId`/`crewIds`/`crewNames` for a crew). `worker-controller` `list()` reads the AbsenceStore and lists each WO on its resolved staff's day (defer / skip leave it flagged on the assignee; an uncovered one is on nobody's own day, the account foreman still sees it). Owner side: paperwork's `WorkOrderWorkerPort` gets `coversOf(userId, rows)` (registered by Field's `FieldWorkOrderWorkers`), so `GET /work-orders` and `/work-orders/:id` carry `coverAssignee` (cover's name / crew name) or `assigneeOut` ("defer" | "skip" | "uncovered"). `GET`/`POST /field/absences` rows carry `workOrders` — the WOs the absence takes off its worker (or crew members) with `coverName` when someone has it. UI: /work-orders row and WO page Assignee read "Jake Fowler → covered by Miguel Torres" or "Jake Fowler is out that day — reassign or reschedule" (`front-end/lib/work-order-assignee.ts`); /worker's WO card says "Covering for Jake Fowler"; the Away row on /field/workers lists "WO-001 on Fri, Nov 20 goes to Miguel Torres" or "… still needs rescheduling — nobody has it". New lang keys `field.away.woCover`, `field.away.woResched`, `workOrders.assignee.coveredBy`, `workOrders.assignee.out` (en + es).
**Test correction:** the unit case "covered by a crew" asserted `[...r.staff.crewIds].sort()` = `["ana","pedro"]`, but the test's own stated contract is staffOn's `Resolution`, whose crew `Staff.crewIds` is the crew's OTHER workers, never the lead (`crews/mod.ts` `crewStaff`: `members.filter((w) => w.id !== lead.id)`). The assertion now checks the whole crew as `[r.staff.lead.id, ...r.staff.crewIds].sort()` = `["ana","pedro"]` — same intent (the lead and the available members take the WO), no assertion weakened. Added jest unit `jest/unit/work-order-assignee.test.ts` ("REQ-1022 assigneeLabel": covered en/es, out for defer/skip/uncovered, plain assignee).
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-12):** unit `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/test.ts` → `ok | 7 passed | 0 failed`; int `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/worker-view.int.test.ts` → all 3 ok (REQ-1022 + both REQ-1010); e2e `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5847 shots run e2e/work-order-absence-cover -- --no-check` (PORT=5847 deno task serve) → `✓ REQ-1022 (LOOP-007 q2-12) … · 124.2s`, 1 pass · 0 fail. Neighbours: `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/field/domain/business/crews/test.ts src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/test.ts src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/ src/field/entrypoints/field-controllers/ src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` → `ok | 60 passed | 0 failed`; `src/field/entrypoints/business-day.int.test.ts src/field/entrypoints/multi-day-job.int.test.ts` → `ok | 7 passed`; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → `Test Suites: 645 passed, Tests: 6338 passed, 1 skipped`; `shots run e2e/field-tasks` → 32 pass · 0 fail (incl. REQ-842 / REQ-1014 Away stories); `shots run e2e/work-order-worker-view` → 1 pass; front-end `deno lint` + `deno check` on the touched islands/clients/lib → clean; backend `deno lint` + `deno check` on touched modules → clean.

## REQ-1021 — LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-13: a change order's Email goes to the customer on file, even when the quote was linked to her after it was drafted
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-13** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: on /quotes the CO-001 row's Email opens a bare `mailto:` with no recipient, though Maria's email (maria.g@example.com) is on file. REQ-565 promises "Email (a `mailto:` to her address)". The "nothing reaches the outbox" part of the report is by design: REQ-565 makes Email a mailto: link, not a server send.
**Root cause:** the CO row's recipient (`coRecipient` in `front-end/islands/QuotesPage.tsx` QuoteLedgerSection) reads the email only from `quote.customerSnapshot`. Only `QuoteStore.create` and `publishNumbered` (a published revision) write that snapshot. An assistant quote for a brand-new customer is created without `customerId` and linked later through `QuoteStore.update({customerId})` (BindConversationCustomer, send-quote). Neither `update()` nor `updateIf()` takes a snapshot, so a v1 quote linked this way never has one. `changeOrderShareLinks` then builds `mailto:` + "" + `?subject=…`. The open-panel loader already has the live `customer` row but uses it only for the name.
**Requirement:** linking a customer to a quote with update/updateIf (setting or changing `customerId`) snapshots that customer, and a later CRM edit still does not rewrite the snapshot (REQ-204). The CO row's recipient is the snapshot first and the live customer record second, through a pure `changeOrderRecipient(quote, customer)` in `shared/documents/change-order-actions.ts` used by QuotesPage.
**Tests:** int `backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/numbered-docs.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1021 (REQ-565/REQ-204, LOOP-007 q2-13): …" ×2: create without customer → `update({customerId})` has `customerSnapshot.email`, which a later unrelated update keeps; `updateIf` linking a customer snapshots her) · unit `jest/unit/change-order-surfaces.test.ts` ("REQ-1021 …" ×3: `changeOrderRecipient` falls back to the live customer, so Email is `mailto:maria.g@example.com?…`; the snapshot wins over the live record; QuotesPage uses `changeOrderRecipient(`) · e2e `e2e/co-email-linked-customer/co-email-linked-customer.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1021 …": quote drafted with no customer, PUT customerId, sent, signed, CO added → the `ledger-co-email` href starts `mailto:maria.g@example.com?`).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/paperwork/domain/data/numbered-docs.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 6 passed | 2 failed` (`update({customerId}) snapshots the customer just linked` Actual `undefined` / Expected `"maria.g@example.com"`); `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/change-order-surfaces.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 failed, 1 skipped, 6335 passed` (`changeOrderRecipient` Expected `"function"` Received `"undefined"`; `Expected pattern: /changeOrderRecipient\(/`); `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> BASE_URL=http://localhost:5613 shots run e2e/co-email-linked-customer -- --no-check` → `expectation failed: Email goes to Maria (mailto:?subject=Change%20order%20CO-001&body=Hi%20Maria%20Garcia%2C%20…)`.
**Fix:** `QuoteStore.update` and `updateIf` (backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/quote-store/mod.ts, `linkedCustomerSnapshot`) take the customer snapshot when the patch sets `customerId`, either to a different customer or to one the row has no snapshot of yet. A patch that only edits other fields, or re-sends the same `customerId` on a row that already has a snapshot, keeps the existing snapshot, so a later CRM edit still never rewrites it (REQ-204). A patch that carries its own `customerSnapshot` keeps that one. Switching to a different customer replaces the old customer's snapshot. Invoice, work-order and change-order stores need no change, because no caller links a customer to them through update. Front end: `changeOrderRecipient(quote, customer)` in `shared/documents/change-order-actions.ts` takes each field from the snapshot first and the live customer row second, and uses the live row only when it is the quote's own customer. `QuotesPage` passes the customer row its panel loader already fetched into `QuoteLedgerSection`, so quotes saved before this fix also get her address.
**Test amended:** `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/billing-actions.int.test.ts` (REQ-777 M9 ×5) asserted `bound.customerSnapshot === undefined` after the wizard bound Ana by id. That precondition was the q2-13 defect itself. The test now asserts the wizard's bind snapshots her (`customerSnapshot.email === "ana.diaz@example.com"`). It then strips the snapshot from the stored row, so REQ-777 still covers its case: a quote bound by id only, which is how rows saved before this fix look. The REQ-777 assertions after that are unchanged.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-13):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/paperwork/domain/data/numbered-docs.int.test.ts` → `ok | 8 passed | 0 failed`; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/change-order-surfaces.test.ts` (runs the whole unit project) → `Test Suites: 644 passed, 644 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 6338 passed, 6339 total`; `PORT=5627 KV_PATH=<scratch>/q213.kv deno task serve` + `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch>/shots SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5627 shots run e2e/co-email-linked-customer -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1021 (LOOP-007 q2-13): … the change order row's Email goes to her address, not a bare mailto: · 36.9s` (1 pass · 0 fail). Neighbours: `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/paperwork/domain/data/quote-store/ src/agents/domain/coordinators/bind-conversation-customer/ src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote/ src/core/data/numbered-store/` → `ok | 69 passed | 0 failed`; every backend test that names `customerSnapshot` (16 files) → `134 passed | 5 failed` before the REQ-777 amendment (the 5 above), then `billing-actions.int.test.ts` → `ok | 33 passed | 0 failed`. `deno check` + `deno lint` clean on QuotesPage.tsx, change-order-actions.ts, quote-store/mod.ts and billing-actions.int.test.ts, and `deno fmt -` on stdin leaves each touched file unchanged.

## REQ-1030 — An unsent change order is not "waiting on the customer" in the /quotes pipeline (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-14)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-14** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "/quotes pipeline says CO-001 is waiting on the customer though it was never sent" — the assistant made CO-001 for Maria Gonzalez's Q-001 without a send request, and /quotes read "CO-001 is waiting on Maria Gonzalez."
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** a `ChangeOrder` records nothing about being sent — `ChangeOrderStatus` is `pending | approved | declined` (`backend/src/paperwork/dto/change-order.ts`) with no `sentAt`. REQ-481 (7b74f055) added `changeOrderFold` in `backend/src/analytics/domain/coordinators/build-quote-cards/mod.ts`, which puts every `status === "pending"` order into `pendingChangeOrders` ("still waiting on the customer") — true when every change order was emailed at creation. REQ-652 (2037adbc) then made chat change orders unsent by default (`apply-chat-change-order/mod.ts` creates the order pending and returns `sent:false` without `deliver()` unless `asksToSendChangeOrder`), and the fold was never changed to match. So the unsent CO-001 flows through `QuotesPage.tsx` (pendingChangeOrders → {number, client}) → `heroCoWaiting` (`front-end/lib/headline-counts.ts`) → `quotes-hero-co-waiting` in `QuotesSections.tsx` → `quotesHero.coWaiting.one`.
**Requirement:** a pending change order that has not been emailed or texted to the customer is not listed in the quote card's `pendingChangeOrders` and the /quotes hero does not say it is waiting on the customer; the card lists it in `unsentChangeOrders` and the hero still names it as not sent. Once it is sent ("Send CO-001"), it moves to `pendingChangeOrders` ("waiting on").
**Tests:** unit n/a — the defect is the server-side fold, a private function of BuildQuoteCards over the stores; the int test pins it with in-memory KV, and `heroCoWaiting` is correct for the list it is given · int `backend/src/analytics/domain/coordinators/build-quote-cards/unsent-change-order.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1030 …": real ApplyChatChangeOrder + real SendChangeOrderAlert (transports captured): CO-001 made without a send → card `pendingChangeOrders` `[]`, `unsentChangeOrders` `["CO-001"]`; after `send({changeOrderNumber:"CO-001"})` → `["CO-001"]` / `[]`) · e2e `e2e/quotes-unsent-change-order/quotes-unsent-change-order.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1030 …": signed Q-001, chat "Make a change order for Maria Gonzalez on Q-001: add upgraded countertops, $2,800." → `sent:false` → /quotes has no `quotes-hero-co-waiting`, no "CO-001 is waiting on Maria Gonzalez", and still names CO-001).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-14 at 240a6443):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/analytics/domain/coordinators/build-quote-cards/unsent-change-order.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed` ("CO-001 was never sent to Maria, so the card must not say it is waiting on her" actual `["CO-001"]` expected `[]`; "and is no longer listed as unsent" actual `undefined` expected `[]`); `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/quotes-unsent-change-order -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1030 … expectation failed: no "waiting on the customer" line for an unsent change order (hero: "THE PIPELINE THIS WEEK CO-001 is waiting on Maria Gonzalez. …") — expected 0, got 1`.
**Fix (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-14):** a `ChangeOrder` now records when it reached the customer. `ChangeOrder.sentAt` is new, and so is `sendTracked: true`, which `ChangeOrderStore.create` stamps on every new order. `ChangeOrderStore.markSent` writes `sentAt` with compare-and-set. `SendChangeOrderAlert.run` (used by ApplyChatChangeOrder.deliver, UpdateChatChangeOrder and the invoice-controller create/resend paths) calls `markSent` only when an email or text actually reached the customer (`emailedTo || textedTo`). A delivery that reached nobody leaves the order unsent. `changeOrderWasSent(co)` (`backend/src/paperwork/dto/change-order.ts`) returns `!!sentAt || !sendTracked`, so legacy rows written before this change were sent at creation and keep counting as sent. `changeOrderFold` (build-quote-cards) now splits pending orders: sent ones go to `pendingChangeOrders` ("waiting on") and the rest to the new `unsentChangeOrders`. Front-end: `QuoteCard.unsentChangeOrders` (clients/quotes.ts, quotes-seed.ts) goes through `QuotesPage.tsx` to `QuotesHero`'s new `quotes-hero-co-unsent` line via `heroCoUnsent` (`front-end/lib/headline-counts.ts`), using the new keys `quotesHero.coUnsent.one/other` in en + es ("CO-001 isn't sent to Maria Gonzalez yet." / "CO-001 aún no se ha enviado a Maria Gonzalez.").
**Tests (amended):** unit is no longer n/a. `jest/unit/quotes-unsent-change-order.test.ts` ("REQ-1030 …") covers heroCoUnsent's key/vars and en text without "waiting", checks that the hero renders `quotes-hero-co-unsent` and that the page passes `unsentChangeOrders=`, and checks that both keys exist in en + es. Existing test adjusted: `build-quote-cards/int.test.ts` "REQ-481 card …" made its pending CO-001 with a bare `cos.create` and expected it to be "waiting on the customer". Under REQ-1030 an order nobody sent is not waiting, so the test now calls `cos.markSent(pending.id)` first. That is the precondition REQ-481 m10 meant ("the ones still waiting on the customer"). Its assertions are unchanged.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-14):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/analytics/domain/coordinators/build-quote-cards/` → `ok | 24 passed | 0 failed` (incl. both REQ-1030 int tests). `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/quotes-unsent-change-order -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1030 (LOOP-007 q2-14): a change order the assistant made but never sent is not 'waiting on' the customer in the /quotes pipeline · 52.7s`. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit …` (the whole unit project ran) → `Test Suites: 645 passed, 645 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6339 passed`. Backend neighbours of every touched module: `deno test -A --unstable-kv <the 27 test files outside handle-chat-message that import ChangeOrderStore/SendChangeOrderAlert/BuildQuoteCards/ApplyChatChangeOrder>` → `179 passed | 1 failed`. The one red is REQ-209's wall-clock `< 1 s` check in `invoice-controller/exports.int.test.ts` (GET /invoices · /search · export.csv · ledger; it never touches change-order sending), run while the host load average was 163 (29 concurrent `deno test` runs from other agents). The handle-chat-message files that ran before the per-file loop was stopped for host load (13 files, including apply-chat-change-order/*) → all green. `cd front-end && deno lint` + `deno check` on headline-counts.ts, QuotesSections.tsx, clients/quotes.ts, quotes-seed.ts, islands/QuotesPage.tsx → clean.

## REQ-1032 — A phone pay handle reads one way in the pay buttons too: the invoice email's Ways to pay and /i's Pay online say "(512) 555-0700", never "5125550700" (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-15)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-15** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2 (a re-check of REQ-965's fmtPhone fix): "Same Zelle phone printed as '(512) 555-0700' and as raw '5125550700' on one invoice". The Spanish invoice email read "Instrucciones de pago Zelle: (512) 555-0700 … Formas de pago Zelle: envía a 5125550700", and /i?lang=es read "PAGA EN LÍNEA Zelle Envía a 5125550700 Copiar".
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** the Zelle handle reaches the customer by two render paths, and only one formats it. The Payment-instructions line (`paymentInstructionsFromMethods`, shared/documents/invoice-form.ts, REQ-593/965) runs a phone through `formatPhoneDisplay`. The REQ-630 pay buttons (`payButtons`, shared/payments/pay-links.ts) return the Zelle copy row as `value: zelle.handle.trim()`, the handle exactly as typed, and both consumers print that raw value: the email's Ways-to-pay row (`backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/pay-ways/mod.ts`, `t('payLinks.email.copyTo', {handle: b.value})`, 1f330efc REQ-630) and the /i Pay-online row (`front-end/islands/PublicInvoiceClaim.tsx`, `tFor('payLinks.page.sendTo', {handle: b.value})`, 5a7c48a6 REQ-805). The REQ-326 formatter `fmtPayHandle` lives in front-end/lib/format.ts, so the backend can't use it, and on the front end only the claim flow's `methodInstructions` calls it. The two blocks appearing together is by design (REQ-980). The contradiction is the two formats.
**Requirement:** a phone-shaped pay handle (Zelle, and any app handle shown as a button's detail) reads as the REQ-965 phone, "(512) 555-0700", in the invoice email's Ways to pay block and on /i's Pay online card, the same as Payment instructions. Email, @name and $cashtag handles show exactly as typed. The Copy button still copies the raw handle ("5125550700"). `payButtons` carries a `display` for copy buttons and keeps `value` raw.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/pay-ways/phone-handle.test.ts` ("REQ-1032 (q2-15) payWaysEmailHtml: …": es '5125550700' → "Zelle: envía a (512) 555-0700" with no raw digits; en '+1 512 555 0700' → "(512) 555-0700"; an email handle unchanged) · jest unit `jest/unit/req-1032-pay-handle-display.test.ts` ("REQ-1032 …": `payButtons` Zelle display "(512) 555-0700" with value "5125550700"; email/@name/$cashtag unchanged) · int `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/pay-links.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1032 (q2-15) the Spanish invoice email shows the Zelle phone one way …": the real SendPaperworkEmail coordinator, with commsLanguage es and Payment instructions from `paymentInstructionsFromMethods`; data-payment-instructions and the data-pay-way="zelle" row both read "(512) 555-0700", and the email never contains "5125550700") · e2e `e2e/req-1032-zelle-phone/req-1032-zelle-phone.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1032 (q2-15): …": /i/:id?lang=es `[data-cy=pay-zelle-value]` reads "Envía a (512) 555-0700", and `[data-cy=pay-zelle-copy]` still writes "5125550700" to the clipboard).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-15 at 240a6443):** unit `deno test -A src/paperwork/domain/business/pay-ways/phone-handle.test.ts` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 2 failed` (`Expected actual: " Formas de pago Zelle: envía a 5125550700 " to contain: "Zelle: envía a (512) 555-0700"`); jest `npx jest --selectProjects unit req-1032-pay-handle` → `Tests: 3 failed` (`Expected: "(512) 555-0700" Received: undefined`); int `deno test -A --unstable-kv --filter REQ-1032 …/pay-links.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` (`- waysToPay: "Zelle: envía a 5125550700"` / `+ waysToPay: "Zelle: envía a (512) 555-0700"`); e2e `shots run e2e/req-1032-zelle-phone -- --no-check` → `expectation failed: the Pay-online Zelle row reads the phone like the payment instructions do — expected "Envía a (512) 555-0700", got "Envía a 5125550700"`.
**Fix:** `fmtPayHandle` (REQ-326) moved from front-end/lib/format.ts to `shared/identity/phone.ts`, next to `fmtPhone`. front-end/lib/format.ts re-exports it, so the claim flow is unchanged. `payButtons` (shared/payments/pay-links.ts) gives every copy button a `display: fmtPayHandle(handle)` and keeps `value` raw for Copy. A link button's `detail` now goes through `fmtPayHandle` as well. The email's Ways-to-pay row (backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/pay-ways/mod.ts) and /i's Pay-online row (front-end/islands/PublicInvoiceClaim.tsx) print `b.display`, and `copy(b)` still copies `b.value`. Test change: the exact-shape REQ-630 assertion in `jest/unit/pay-links.test.ts` ("payButtons: the app links with the amount …") gains `display: "pay@acme.test"` on its Zelle copy button. The button carries a new field, and the old assertions are all kept. The doubled Zelle line (Payment instructions + Ways to pay) stays as REQ-980 chose.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-15):** unit `cd backend && deno test -A src/paperwork/domain/business/pay-ways/` → `ok | 8 passed | 0 failed` (phone-handle.test.ts 3/3 + test.ts); jest `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/req-1032-pay-handle-display.test.ts unit/pay-links.test.ts unit/claim-handle-format.test.ts` → `Tests: 24 passed, 24 total`; int `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/pay-links.int.test.ts` → `ok | 5 passed | 0 failed`; neighbour `deno test -A src/paperwork/domain/business/doc-render/phone.test.ts` → `ok | 4 passed`; e2e `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… shots run e2e/req-1032-zelle-phone -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1032 (q2-15): … reads 'Envía a (512) 555-0700', and Copy still copies the digits · 27.4s`; `deno lint` (format.ts, PublicInvoiceClaim.tsx, phone.ts, pay-links.ts) → `Checked 4 files`; `deno check` front-end format.ts + PublicInvoiceClaim.tsx and backend pay-ways/mod.ts → clean.

## REQ-1033 — AMENDMENT of REQ-1016: every email's `<html lang>` is its language, not only the ones built by send-paperwork-email's `shell()` (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-16)
**Source:** Raphael (QA loop): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". Issue **q2-16** [polish/BUG_CONTRADICTION], LOOP-007 cycle 2: "Non-shell emails (owner approval, CO receipt, payment receipt) still have bare <html> with no lang" (QA2 emails 003 and 009, QA5 receipt 003).
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** the REQ-1016 fix (cycle 1, q1-102) changed only the `shell()` in `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/mod.ts`; that file's quote and itemized-invoice templates already wrote `<html lang>`. About eight other email templates build their own HTML from the same copied boilerplate `<!doctype html>\n<html><body style=…>` with no lang, though each takes a `lang` and translates every string with it: `payment-receipt/mod.ts:73` (REQ-963, the customer's payment receipt), `decision-alert/mod.ts:246` (a second, local `shell()` behind buildQuoteDeclinedAlert, buildChangeOrderDecisionAlert and the customer's buildChangeOrderReceipt, REQ-948), `send-accepted-alert/mod.ts:179` (the owner's "customer approved" alert), `send-change-order-alert/mod.ts:425/:469`, `send-payment-reminder/mod.ts:493`, `reply-to-inquiry/mod.ts:319` and `send-inquiry-alert/mod.ts:258`. No shared email root or guard test made every email declare its language, so the REQ-1016 fix stayed local to one file, and REQ-1016's body narrowed its heading ("every customer email") to "built by `shell()`".
**Requirement:** every HTML email the backend writes opens `<!doctype html>\n<html lang="<lang>">`, where `<lang>` is the language its words are in (the customer's doc/comms language for customer emails, the owner's UI language for owner alerts). No template under backend/src writes an `<html>` root without `lang=`.

**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-16 at 240a6443):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/business/email-html-lang.test.ts` → 11 of 11 failed (each builder: Actual `(no <html lang>: "<!doctype html>\n<html><body style=\"margi")` / Expected `es`|`en`; the guard lists 8 bare roots: send-inquiry-alert:258, send-accepted-alert:179, send-payment-reminder:493, send-change-order-alert:425 and :469, reply-to-inquiry:319, payment-receipt:73, decision-alert:246); `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/invoice-controller/paid-email-lang.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 1 failed` (`- <html>` / `+ <html lang="es">`); `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/outbox -- --no-check --filter REQ-1033` → `✗ REQ-1033 … expectation failed: the opened receipt's <html lang> — expected "es", got null`.
**Fix (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-16):** one shared opener, `emailRoot(lang)` in `backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/email-root/mod.ts`, returns `<!doctype html>\n<html lang="${lang}">`. ## REQ-1035 — An empty /worker day says it is empty once: no "Mis tareas 0/0" chip, no second or third empty card, no preview hint over nothing (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-17 + q2-50)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issues, cycle 2: **q2-17** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION] crew lead's empty day still shows a "Mis tareas 0/0" chip and a third empty message ("0% Sin tareas hoy / Nada programado." + "Mis tareas 0/0" + "Sin tareas este día."); **q2-50** [polish/BUG_POLISH] worker's empty future day repeats "No tasks this day" and shows a pointless "🔒 Preview — you can check these off on the day." hint, with a loading-like sparkle icon. Follows REQ-1011, which promised no 0/0 under "Sin tareas hoy".
**Root cause:** `front-end/islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` has three uncoordinated empty signals. (1) The REQ-196 summary (61c8f68a) always renders `workerTodayKey(0, isToday)` + `worker.freeDay`. (2) The body still draws its pre-summary empty states from fd52cfa2 (REQ-137..143): for a non-foreman a `w-empty` card with `ICN.sparkle` + `worker.none` ("No tasks this day."); for a foreman `renderSection(mine, t("worker.mine"))` is called even when `mine` is empty, its header `<span class="count">{done}/{liveRows.length}</span>` is unconditional ("0/0"), and it adds a fixed any-day `worker.noneCrew` card ("Sin tareas este día.") under the summary's "Sin tareas hoy". REQ-1011 removed only the per-visit 0/0 chip, and its e2e ran as a plain worker, so the foreman header chip was never covered. (3) The REQ-362 preview hint is gated only on `nav.preview` (date after today), never on the day having tasks.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/worker-empty-day.test.ts` ("REQ-1035 …": renderSection's count chip gated on `liveRows.length`; the foreman's empty "mine" section adds no fixed `worker.noneCrew` card; the preview hint is gated on the day's counts; no `ICN.sparkle` on the empty state; the body does not repeat the summary's "none") · int n/a — front-end rendering only; the backend correctly returns an empty list · e2e `e2e/worker-empty-day/worker-empty-day.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1035 …": at 390x844, a worker with no tasks opens tomorrow in EN and ES → no `w-preview`, no `w-empty`, "No tasks this day" once, one empty message; a foreman (ES) on an empty today → no ".count" "0/0", no "Sin tareas este día.", one empty message).

The `w-empty` card stays only for a day whose tasks are all someone else's, now with `ICN.cal` instead of the loading-like `ICN.sparkle` and `worker.noneCrew`. (d) The REQ-362 preview hint shows only when the future day has tasks to check off. The `worker.none` key stays in lang/*.json because REQ-527's `jest/unit/worker-one-noun.test.ts` pins it.

**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". HH." catalog cards ("DocuMonster worker account", "DocuMonster editor", "Welcome email (Postmark)", "Welcome text (your line)" and their descriptions) are English beside Spanish chrome ("Integrado en DocuMonster", "Agregar").

Attaching an entry copies the English name/desc into the stored HrSystem (hr-controllers attach), and the attached card prints `{s.name}`/`{s.desc}` raw, so an attached built-in stays English for good. lang/en.json and lang/es.json have no keys for the catalog names or descriptions.
**Requirement:** built-in systems (catalog cards and attached `dm-*` systems) render their name and description through `t("hr.systems.cat.<key>.name|desc")`, with those 8 keys in both dictionaries (Spanish in es); only custom systems print their stored `s.name`/`s.desc`. **Tests:** unit `jest/unit/settings-systems-catalog-lang.test.ts` ("REQ-1034 …": every SYSTEM_CATALOG key has `hr.systems.cat.<key>.name/.desc` in en+es; es carries none of the English catalog strings; SystemsTab never renders `{c.name}`/`{c.desc}`; the attached card does not print raw `{s.name}`/`{s.desc}` for built-ins) · int n/a — the backend payload is intentionally language-neutral by key; the fault is front-end rendering + dictionaries · e2e `e2e/hr-onboarding/hr-onboarding.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1034 (q2-18): …": an ES owner opens /settings?tab=systems&lang=es, the dm-worker catalog card's name/desc and every catalog name are not English, then attaches it and the attached card's name is not English).

The dm-email description is now the business's own welcome ("Your business's welcome note, with the handbook portal's login" / "La bienvenida de tu negocio, con el acceso al portal del manual"), not "from DocuMonster". The backend `SYSTEM_CATALOG` English stays as the language-neutral API default. No test changed.

## REQ-1036 — AMENDMENT of REQ-1003: the provisioner's welcome email (dm-email) is From the business too, and its Settings › Systems card stops saying "from DocuMonster" (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-19)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-19** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "HR catalog says the welcome email comes 'from DocuMonster', but the fix sends it from the business".
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** REQ-1003 (d6ff3ab3) gave the business From (`fromFor` → `businessFrom({alias, name})`, `hr-notices/mod.ts`) only to `HrNotices.sendLink` (the invite and its reminder). The REQ-913 (3fe1df39) "Welcome email (Postmark)" arm, `Provisioner.sendWelcomeEmail` (`provisioner/mod.ts` ~253), calls `this.email.send({ to, subject, htmlBody })` with no `from`, so `postmarkPayload` fills `From: input.from ?? HOUSE_FROM` = `"DocuMonster" <hello@documonster.com>`. The `SYSTEM_CATALOG` dm-email desc (`hr-stores/mod.ts` ~151) says "A welcome note with the handbook portal's login, from DocuMonster" — true to the code, but against REQ-1003's promise. One hire gets the invite from "Reyes Lawn & Landscape" and the welcome note from "DocuMonster". The desc is served as-is by GET /me/systems and copied into an attached system's stored desc.
**Requirement:** the dm-email welcome note is sent From the business (its alias + its name, as REQ-1003's invite); the dm-email catalog card (and a newly attached system's card) does not say the note comes from DocuMonster.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/hr/domain/business/onboarding/test.ts` ("REQ-1036 (q2-19) the dm-email catalog card does not say … 'from DocuMonster'") · int `backend/src/hr/entrypoints/hr-email-sender.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1036 (q2-19) the provisioner's welcome email (dm-email) is From the business …": dm-email attached, autoProvision on, the hire signs → the welcome arm's Postmark payload From + the GET /me/systems catalog desc) · e2e `e2e/hr-welcome-email-sender/hr-welcome-email-sender.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1036 (LOOP-007 q2-19): /settings?tab=systems …": the catalog card's and the attached card's description line do not say DocuMonster; the "Built into DocuMonster" badge is not checked).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-19 at 240a6443):** int `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/hr/entrypoints/hr-email-sender.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 1 failed` (`welcome From="DocuMonster" <hello@documonster.com> · catalog desc="A welcome note with the handbook portal's login, from DocuMonster"`; `fromName: "DocuMonster"` vs `"Reyes Lawn & Landscape"`); unit `--filter REQ-1036` → `desc="A welcome note with the handbook portal's login, from DocuMonster"`; e2e `shots run e2e/hr-welcome-email-sender -- --no-check` → `expectation failed: the catalog card says the welcome note is from DocuMonster: "A welcome note with the handbook portal's login, from DocuMonster"`.
**Fix:** one new-hire sender — `newHireSender({alias, company, hrEmail})` (pure, `hr/domain/business/onboarding/mod.ts`; `businessFrom` + the HR reply-to) — used by `HrNotices.fromFor` (the invite/reminder, REQ-1003) and by `Provisioner.sendWelcomeEmail` (the dm-email arm), which now passes `from` + `replyTo` to `EmailService.send` instead of falling back to `HOUSE_FROM`. The provisioner resolves the company and HR address as `HrNotices.settingsFor` does (HR settings → business name → legal name → owner name; HR email → owner email). The `SYSTEM_CATALOG` dm-email desc reads "A welcome note with the handbook portal's login, from your business". `HrSystemStore` (get/find/listByUser) reads a dm-email system attached before this change, whose stored desc is exactly the old catalog text, as today's catalog desc; a desc the owner wrote is kept.
**Test correction:** the int test's `fromIsHouse` probe was `wire.From.toLowerCase().includes("documonster")`. That can never be false: the business's alias address is on documonster.com by design (REQ-123 — every From is on SEND_DOMAIN; REQ-1003's own invite is `"Reyes Lawn & Landscape" <…@documonster.com>`). It now compares the address with the house inbox (`senderAddress(wire.From) === senderAddress(HOUSE_FROM)`), which is what "from DocuMonster" means. `fromName` and `cardSaysFromDocuMonster` are unchanged. Added: int "a dm-email system attached before the copy changed reads with today's catalog desc; an owner-written desc is kept", and unit "newHireSender: …".
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-19):** int `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/hr/entrypoints/hr-email-sender.int.test.ts` → `ok | 3 passed | 0 failed`; unit `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/hr/domain/business/onboarding/test.ts` → `ok | 14 passed | 0 failed`; neighbours `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/hr/` → `ok | 31 passed | 0 failed`; `deno check` + `deno lint` + stdin `deno fmt --check` on the 6 touched backend files → clean; e2e `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… shots run e2e/hr-welcome-email-sender -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1036 (LOOP-007 q2-19): /settings?tab=systems — … catalog or attached · 52.2s`.

## REQ-1037 — AMENDMENT of REQ-944: the Outbox prints the business's clock, the same one the chat uses (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-21)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-21** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "Outbox and assistant chat show different clocks for the same morning" — QA1 saw Outbox 8:01 a. m. vs chat 2:06 a. m. (Central); QA5 saw 7:55 AM vs 3:02 AM (the New York default).
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** `outboxWhen(iso, lang)` (front-end/lib/outbox.ts, REQ-784 f3ba1da1, doc comment "the viewer's clock") calls `formatClockTime(d, lang)` with no `timeZone` and builds the day with an `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with no `timeZone`, so `clockParts` (shared/quote-flow/locale-format.ts) falls back to `getHours()/getMinutes()` — the device's zone (UTC in QA's headless browser). The chat formats with `{ timeZone: chatZone }` from `ctx.state.user.businessTimezone` (REQ-944, islands/AsstChat.tsx), which /me always fills (picked, else the address's state, else America/New_York). The REQ-944 fix (e9db26d6) never touched outbox.ts, OutboxView.tsx, OutboxPage.tsx or routes/messages/index.tsx, and /messages renders `<OutboxPage />` with no zone.
**Requirement:** every time the Outbox prints for a message — the table row and the opened message — is that instant's wall time and day in the business's time zone (`businessTimezone`), whatever zone the device is in; /messages passes the zone to the Outbox island, which threads it to OutboxTable / OutboxDetail and `outboxWhen(iso, lang, timeZone)`.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/outbox.test.tsx` ("REQ-1037 q2-21: …" ×3: 08:01Z → "2:01 a. m." / "19 nov" Central, "3:01 AM" New York, "5:01 PM" Tokyo; 03:00Z → "Nov 18, 2026" Chicago; OutboxTable row and OutboxDetail with `timeZone` print Central) · integration (wiring) `jest/unit/business-tz-document-dates.test.ts` ("REQ-1037 …": /messages passes `businessTimezone` to `<OutboxPage timeZone>`; OutboxPage passes it to both views; every `outboxWhen(...)` call in OutboxView.tsx carries it; `outboxWhen` hands it to `formatClockTime`) · backend int n/a — /me already returns `businessTimezone`; the fault is front-end formatting only · e2e `e2e/outbox/outbox.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1037 (LOOP-007 q2, q2-21): …": business in America/Chicago, browser forced to UTC via CDP, an invoice emailed; the /messages row and the opened message read the instant in Central — the chat's clock).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-21 at 240a6443):** `cd front-end && TZ=UTC deno test -A --no-check lib/outbox.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 11 passed | 4 failed` (the three REQ-1037 tests: `Expected actual: "19 nov 2026 · 8:01 a. m." to contain: "2:01 a. m."`, `Expected actual: "Nov 19, 2026 · 3:00 AM" to contain: "Nov 18, 2026"`, `… "19 nov 2026 · 8:01 a. m." to contain: "2:01 a. m.": the row's time is Central`; the fourth, REQ-784's sidebar "Outbox is a root row", is red on the base too and unrelated); `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/business-tz-document-dates.test.ts` → the two REQ-1037 tests fail (`Expected pattern: /<OutboxPage[^>]*timeZone=\{[^}]*businessTimezone[^}]*\}/`, `Expected pattern: /<OutboxTable[^>]*timeZone=/`); `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5522 shots run e2e/outbox/outbox.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check --filter REQ-1037` (against `PORT=5522 deno task serve`) → `✗ … expectation failed: the row prints the business's (Central) clock — expected "Nov 19, 2026 · 2:38 AM", got "Nov 19, 2026 · 8:38 AM"`.
**Also for the fixer:** CustomerWorkspace's Messages tab (REQ-989) prints the outbox row's day as `day(r.createdAt, lang)` = `createdAt.slice(0,10)` read in UTC — the UTC day, not the business's; same fault class, thread the zone there too.
**Fix:** `outboxWhen(iso, lang, timeZone?)` (front-end/lib/outbox.ts) now formats both parts in the zone — the day via the new `outboxDay(iso, lang, timeZone?)` (`Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `timeZone`, so it flips at the business's midnight) and the time via `formatClockTime(d, lang, { timeZone })`; an unknown zone falls back to the device's clock instead of throwing. OutboxTable and OutboxDetail (components/OutboxView.tsx) take a `timeZone` prop; the OutboxPage island takes `timeZone` and passes it to both; routes/messages/index.tsx renders `<OutboxPage timeZone={user?.businessTimezone} />`. CustomerWorkspace's Messages tab: the island takes `timeZone` (routes/customers/[id].tsx passes `ctx.state.user?.businessTimezone`) and the sent-list day and the text-thread day use the new `instantDay(iso, lang, timeZone)` instead of `day()` (which reads the UTC date off the ISO string and stays for calendar dates).
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-21):** `cd front-end && TZ=UTC deno test -A --no-check lib/outbox.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 14 passed | 1 failed` — all three REQ-1037 tests ok; the one red is REQ-784's sidebar "Outbox is a root row", red on the base too (see RED) and unrelated. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/business-tz-document-dates.test.ts` → `Tests: 1 skipped, 6337 passed, 6338 total` (the whole unit project ran, customer-workspace.test.ts included). `PORT=5733 deno task serve` + `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5733 shots run e2e/outbox/outbox.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1037 (LOOP-007 q2, q2-21): … print Central time — the chat's clock · 37s`, `✓ REQ-991 q1-73`, `✓ REQ-1016`; `✗ REQ-784 d12` fails at its first API-level check (`GET /api/outbox` languages "en" where it expects "es" — the stored message language, before any page loads), reproducible alone with `--filter REQ-784`; this fix touches no backend/shared/lang file, so it is not this change. `cd front-end && deno lint` + `deno check` on lib/outbox.ts, components/OutboxView.tsx, islands/OutboxPage.tsx, islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx, routes/messages/index.tsx, routes/customers/[id].tsx → `Checked 6 files`, check clean. Neighbours `TZ=UTC deno test -A --no-check lib/zero-balance-label.test.ts lib/route-doc-title-format.int.test.tsx lib/customer-workspace-more-caret.test.tsx` → `ok | 10 passed | 0 failed`.

## REQ-1038 — AMENDMENT to REQ-944 / REQ-192 (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-22): the timeclock shows punch times and its week in the business's time zone, not the device's
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-22** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: a clock-in at 07:56 UTC (01:56 AM Central, business zone America/Chicago) shows "Clocked in at 7:56 AM" to the worker and "Thu, Nov 19 7:56 AM" on the owner's /field/timesheet when the browser runs in UTC.
**Root cause:** both timeclock surfaces format punch instants with `toLocaleTimeString`/`toLocaleDateString` and no `timeZone`, so they print the device's zone: `front-end/islands/TimesheetPage.tsx` (`fmtTime`, `fmtDayOf`, `fmtWhen`, `fmtRange`) and `front-end/components/timeclock/WorkerClock.tsx` (`fmtTime`, `fmtDayOf`, used by "Clocked in at {time}" and the week table), both from 61c8f68a (REQ-192 port). Neither island is handed the business zone: `routes/field/timesheet.tsx` renders `<TimesheetPage />` with no props, and `islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` renders `<WorkerClock hoursOpen …/>` without the zone it already holds for REQ-940. The week bounds have the same bias: `localWeek()` in `front-end/clients/timeclock.ts` builds Monday 00:00 from the browser's getDay/getDate, and the backend's `windowOf()` (timeclock-controllers/mod.ts) prefers those sent bounds over `weekBoundsIn(tz)`. REQ-944 named "the chat/list clocks use the device's zone" as a cause but fixed only AsstChat and PhonePage; REQ-940 says the timeclock week is the business's week.
**Requirement:** every punch time and day the worker clock and the timesheet print is the instant's wall time in the business's zone (`businessTimezone`); the timeclock week is Monday 00:00 → next Monday 00:00 in that zone (`localWeek(now, weeks, timeZone)`); Add-punch reads and writes its wall time in that zone too.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/timeclock-business-tz.test.ts` ("REQ-1038 …": `localWeek(2026-11-19T03:00Z, 0, "America/Chicago")` → from 2026-11-16T06:00Z / to 2026-11-23T06:00Z / today 2026-11-18T06:00Z; a Chicago Sunday evening stays in the previous week, also one week back; every toLocale*String call in TimesheetPage.tsx and WorkerClock.tsx names a `timeZone`; the timesheet route and WorkerScreen pass `timeZone=` to the islands) · int n/a — the server keeps instants in UTC and `weekBoundsIn(tz)` is already the business week; the fault is front-end formatting and the client-sent bounds · e2e `e2e/timeclock-business-tz/timeclock-business-tz.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1038 (q2-22) …": business zone Chicago, browser timezone UTC via CDP; a worker clocks in, `[data-cy=clock-since]` and the owner's timesheet punch log must show the punch's Chicago wall time computed from the returned `at`).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern timeclock-business-tz` → `Tests: 4 failed, 1 passed, 5 total` (`Expected: "2026-11-16T06:00:00.000Z" Received: "2026-11-16T05:00:00.000Z"`; `Expected: "2026-11-09T06:00:00.000Z" Received: "2026-11-09T05:00:00.000Z"`; 13 zone-less `.toLocaleTimeString(locale(lang), {` / `.toLocaleDateString(locale(lang), o)` calls; `Expected pattern: /<TimesheetPage[^>]*\btimeZone=/`); `BASE_URL=http://localhost:5731 shots run e2e/timeclock-business-tz -- --no-check` (against `PORT=5731 deno task serve`, fresh KV) → `expectation failed: the worker's clock reads "Clocked in at 2:39 AM" (Chicago, punch 2026-11-19T08:39:41.499Z); got "0h 00m · Clocked in at 8:39 AM" (UTC would be 8:39 AM) | the timesheet log shows the punch at Chicago's "Thu, Nov 19 2:39 AM"; got "Thu, Nov 19 8:39 AM" (UTC would be "Thu, Nov 19 8:39 AM")`.
**Fix:** one zoned-time module, `shared/field/zoned-time.ts` (`weekBoundsIn(tz, now, weeks)`, `dayStartIn`, `toZonedInput` / `fromZonedInput` for datetime-local values), now used by both the backend timeclock (`backend/src/timeclock/domain/business/shifts/mod.ts` re-exports `weekBoundsIn`/`dayStartIn` from it instead of its own copy) and the browser: `localWeek(now, weeks, timeZone)` in `front-end/clients/timeclock.ts` returns the business-zone week and day start when given a zone (the browser's week only when none is known). `routes/field/timesheet.tsx` passes `timeZone={user?.businessTimezone}` to `TimesheetPage`, whose `fmtTime`/`fmtDayOf`/`fmtWhen`/`fmtRange` take that zone, whose week window is `localWeek(…, timeZone)`, and whose Add-punch fields are written and parsed on the business wall clock (`toLocalInput`/`fromLocalInput`). `WorkerScreen` passes `timeZone={me?.timeZone}` (REQ-940's /field/worker/me zone) to `WorkerClock`, which formats "Clocked in at", the day and the in/out times in it and sends the zoned week; with no zone known yet it sends no bounds, so the server's `weekBoundsIn(businessZone)` decides rather than the device. Two wiring regexes that pinned the old prop-less JSX were widened to the new prop (`jest/unit/timeclock-feature.test.ts` `<TimesheetPage(?: timeZone=…)? />`, `jest/unit/worker-tabs.test.ts` `<WorkerClock hoursOpen onState={setClockState} timeZone={me?.timeZone} />`); the REQ-1038 unit gained a case for the Add-punch wall-clock round trip (Chicago 01:56 ↔ 07:56Z, CDT 08:00 → 13:00Z).
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, cycle 2):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'unit/timeclock-business-tz'` → `Tests: 6 passed, 6 total`; neighbours `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'unit/(worker-tabs|timeclock-feature|timeclock-business-tz|timeclock-worker-hours|business-tz-document-dates)'` → `Tests: 22 passed, 22 total` (and the wider `unit/(worker-|timeclock-|c4-|c5-|…)` sweep: 528 tests, only the two stale wiring regexes red before they were widened); `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/timeclock/` → `ok | 8 passed | 0 failed`; `deno lint` (6 files) clean, `deno check` on the touched front-end and backend files clean; `BASE_URL=http://localhost:5737 shots run e2e/timeclock-business-tz -- --no-check` (against `PORT=5737 KV_PATH=<fresh> deno task serve`) → `✓ REQ-1038 (q2-22): with the browser in UTC and the business in Chicago, the worker's 'Clocked in at' and the owner's timesheet log show the punch's Chicago wall time`; neighbours `shots run e2e/timeclock` → `✓ REQ-192 … adds a manual punch and voids one`, `✓ REQ-786`, `✓ REQ-1000`; `shots run e2e/worker-business-day` → `✓ REQ-940 (q1-11)`.

## REQ-1039 — The Spanish dashboard's money bar writes "4 dic", in the business's time zone (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-23)
**Source:** Raphael, 2026-11-18 (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-23** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "Spanish dashboard shows due dates month-first ('Vence dic 4') and uses the browser's local date" — the customer page shows "4 dic" for the same invoice.
**Root cause:** `front-end/components/MoneyBar.tsx` (REQ-798, 08b4524a) has its own private `shortDate` that always returns `${monthShort} ${day}` (English order) from `getMonth()/getDate()` — the browser's local zone — instead of the shared, language-aware `shortDate` in `shared/documents/linked-view.ts` ("4 dic" / "Dec 4"). So the open row reads "Vence dic 4 · INV-001", the paid ("Cobrada …") and sent ("Enviado …") rows print the browser's day for an instant rather than the business's (breaking REQ-944(a)), and the open bucket's days-until-due counts from the browser's local midnight. The row also renders `{item.title}<span>· {item.job}</span>` with no text space, so its text reads "Rosa Delgado· Instalación" (the on-screen gap is CSS margin only).
**Requirement:** MoneyBar dates follow the language ("Vence 4 dic · INV-001" in Spanish, "Due Dec 4 · INV-001" in English); an instant (paidAt, sentAt) prints its day in the business's time zone (`businessTimezone` from GET /me, passed as a MoneyBar `timeZone` prop); days-until-due counts from today in that zone; and the row text keeps a space: "Rosa Delgado · Instalación…".
**Tests:** unit `front-end/components/MoneyBar.dates.test.tsx` ("REQ-1039 q2-23: …" — Spanish day-first open row, English unchanged, paid day in the business zone for a New York and a Tokyo business, days-until-due in the business zone, the row's text space; the zone checks pair instants so they fail under any process TZ) · int n/a — front-end formatting only; GET /me already returns `businessTimezone` · e2e `e2e/money-bar-es-dates/money-bar-es-dates.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1039 q2-23: …" — a Spanish New York business browsing with CDP timezone Asia/Tokyo: open row "Vence <d> <mes> · <num>", paid row "Cobrada <New York day> <mes> · <num>").
**Evidence (2026-11-19):** RED — `cd front-end && TZ=Asia/Tokyo deno test -A components/MoneyBar.dates.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 4 failed` (`- Vence dic 4 · INV-001` / `+ Vence 4 dic · INV-001`; `New York business, paid 10:30 PM Nov 18: got "Cobrada nov 19 · INV-002"`; `New York business - Vence en 4 días + Vence en 5 días`; `client line text is "Rosa Delgado· Instalación de azulejo en baño"`), same 4 red under TZ=America/New_York and TZ=UTC; `shots run e2e/money-bar-es-dates -- --no-check` → `expectation failed: open row reads 'Vence <d> <mes> · <num>' — expected "Vence 9 dic · INV-001", got "Vence dic 9 · INV-001"`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** MoneyBar's private `shortDate` is gone; it uses the shared `shortDate(iso, lang, false, timeZone)` from `shared/documents/linked-view.ts`, which gains an optional `timeZone` — a full instant prints its calendar day in that zone (Intl `formatToParts`, as `formatLongDate` does for REQ-944), a bare YYYY-MM-DD keeps its day. Days-until-due is the whole-day difference between `todayInZone(timeZone, now)` and the due day. `routes/dashboard/index.tsx` passes `user.businessTimezone` to `DashboardPage`, which passes it to MoneyBar's new `timeZone` prop (default New York, the `businessTimezone` fallback). The row renders a real `" "` before `<span class="moneybar__row-job">· …</span>`, and `.moneybar__row-job` drops its `margin-left: 4px`.
**Green (2026-11-19):** `cd front-end && TZ=Asia/Tokyo deno test -A components/MoneyBar.dates.test.tsx` → `ok | 5 passed | 0 failed`; with neighbours (`MoneyBar.test.tsx MoneyBar.cents.test.tsx lib/deposit-due-schedule.test.tsx lib/loading-flash.test.tsx lib/invoice-headline-flip.test.ts lib/dashboard-receivables.test.ts`) → `ok | 33 passed | 0 failed` under TZ=Asia/Tokyo and TZ=America/Los_Angeles · `cd jest && npx jest --no-watchman <money-bar, money-bar-viewed-quote, linked-documents, dash-counts-truth, public-invoice-headline, document-titles-lang, dashboard-headlines-c4, public-doc-state, scheduled-invoice-ledger, q-pending-change-order, c4-search-status-scheduled, paid-how, pipeline-stats, quotes-hero-out-only, dash-anchor-hold> --selectProjects unit` → `Test Suites: 15 passed, 15 total · Tests: 202 passed` · `deno lint` (4 touched TS files) → `Checked 4 files`; `deno check` touched files + the test → clean · `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… shots run e2e/money-bar-es-dates -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1039 q2-23: the Spanish money bar reads 'Vence <d> <mes>' … · 57.3s`.

## REQ-1041 — LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-25: the sidebar's owed amount is the exact amount and never more than she owes (AMENDMENT of REQ-924(a))
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-25** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "Sidebar rounds $1,750 owed up to 'Debe $1.8k'". On the same /customers/:id screen the Balance KPI reads "TE DEBE $1,750.00".
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** `CustomersNav.statusLine` (front-end/components/CustomersNav.tsx) words the owes/overdue lines with `shortMoney(r.amountCents)` (front-end/lib/customer-nav.ts). That function rounds to whole dollars (`Math.round(cents/100)`), and from $1,000 up it rounds again with `(d/1000).toFixed(1)`, or to whole thousands from $10k. For 175000¢ that gives k = 1.75, which is exact in binary, and `toFixed(1)` makes it "1.8", so the line reads "$1.8k". In the same way $999.60 becomes "$1k", $15,500 becomes "$16k" and $50.74 becomes "$51". Every one of these overstates the debt, and the KPI on the same page uses the full currency format. The behaviour came in with 1c0be6f7 (REQ-924). REQ-924(a) only says "Owes $X", and the compact rounding was pinned only by a unit test, never chosen in a requirement.
**Requirement:** the sidebar row's amount (owes and overdue) is the customer's exact balance in the app's currency format, the same figure as the KPI ("$1,750"; cents may be dropped only when they are .00). It never shows more than she owes.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/customer-workspace.test.ts` ("REQ-1041 … $1,750 owed reads "$1,750", never "$1.8k"" and "REQ-1041 … never shows more than the customer owes, over a sweep of amounts"). The fix also replaces the old compact pins ($4.5k / $12k) in "short money for the narrow rail". · int n/a: pure front-end formatting, and the server's balance is correct · e2e `e2e/sidebar-owed-exact/sidebar-owed-exact.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1041 (LOOP-007 q2-25): a customer owing $1,750.00 — her sidebar row shows the same amount as the Balance KPI …", EN and ES).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'unit/customer-workspace.test'` → `Tests: 2 failed, 17 passed` (`Expected: "$1,750" Received: "$1.8k"`; sweep `"5074¢ → $51", "12685¢ → $127", …`); `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5763 shots run e2e/sidebar-owed-exact -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1041 … expectation failed: en: the sidebar row does not round the debt up to $1.8k (got "Owes $1.8k")`.
**Fix:** `shortMoney` (front-end/lib/customer-nav.ts) now returns `fmtMoneyTotal(max(0, cents))` (front-end/lib/format.ts, REQ-961). That gives whole dollars when the balance is whole ("$1,750", "$12,400") and the exact cents otherwise ("$1,750.25"), so it is the same figure as the Balance KPI and never rounds up. The old compact pins in "short money for the narrow rail" ($4.5k / $4k / $12k) were the overstating format this requirement removes, so that test now pins the exact amounts ($4,550 / $4,000 / $12,400 / $1,750.25). The REQ-1041 assertions are unchanged.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'unit/customer-workspace.test'` → `Tests: 19 passed, 19 total`; `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5847 shots run e2e/sidebar-owed-exact -- --no-check` (PORT=5847, fresh KV_PATH) → `tests finished rc 0` · `✓ REQ-1041 (LOOP-007 q2-25): a customer owing $1,750.00 — her sidebar row shows the same amount as the Balance KPI … in EN and ES · 105.8s`; `deno lint` + `deno check` on lib/customer-nav.ts and components/CustomersNav.tsx → clean.

## REQ-1042 — "Customer since" reads "Nov 19, 2026" like every other date (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-26)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-26** [polish/BUG_POLISH], cycle 2: on /customers/<id>?lang=en › Details, "Customer since Nov 19 2026" has no comma; the rest of the app writes "Nov 19, 2026".
**Root cause:** `front-end/islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx` (~line 731, from 1c0be6f7, REQ-924) renders `<dd>{day(c.createdAt, lang)} {c.createdAt.slice(0, 4)}</dd>`. The island's local `day()` calls `toLocaleDateString` with only `{month: "short", day: "numeric", timeZone: "UTC"}` → "Nov 19", and the year is the raw ISO prefix glued on with a space, so Intl never sees a year and en-US never adds its comma. es-US gives "19 nov 2026" either way, so only English shows it. Other screens (PaymentsPage, AdminsPage, SettingsPage) pass `year: "numeric"` and get "Nov 19, 2026".
**Requirement:** the "Customer since" value is the whole date formatted by Intl with `year: "numeric"` — "Nov 19, 2026" (en), "19 nov 2026" (es) — through a shared helper `fmtDayYear(iso, lang)` in `front-end/lib/format.ts`, never a hand-glued ISO year.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/customer-since.test.ts` ("REQ-1042 …": format.ts exports `fmtDayYear`; en → "Nov 19, 2026" / "Jan 2, 2026", a 23:59Z timestamp stays on its day; es → "19 nov 2026"; undefined → "—"; the island's since row renders `fmtDayYear(c.createdAt, lang)` and no `createdAt.slice(0, 4)`) · int n/a — pure client rendering, the backend's `createdAt` is right · e2e `e2e/customer-since-date/customer-since-date.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1042: …": a new customer's page in English reads 'Mon D, YYYY' equal to Intl's full date of her createdAt; in Spanish "Cliente desde" reads "19 nov 2026"-style).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/customer-since.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 4 failed` (`format.ts exports fmtDayYear(iso, lang)` Actual `undefined` / Expected `function`; `the year is not cut from the ISO string (got … <dd>{day(c.createdAt, lang)} {c.createdAt.slice(0, 4)}</dd>)`); `shots run e2e/customer-since-date -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1042 … expectation failed: 'Customer since' reads 'Mon D, YYYY' (got "Nov 19 2026")`.
**Fix:** `front-end/lib/format.ts` gains `fmtDayYear(iso, lang)` — the ISO calendar day (read at 12:00Z so a late-UTC stamp keeps its day) through `toLocaleDateString` with `{month: "short", day: "numeric", year: "numeric", timeZone: "UTC"}`, "—" when there is no date; `front-end/islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx` renders the since row as `<dd>{fmtDayYear(c.createdAt, lang)}</dd>`, no hand-glued `createdAt.slice(0, 4)`.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/customer-since.test.ts lib/format.test.ts` → `ok | 16 passed | 0 failed` (all 4 REQ-1042 tests) · `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/customer-since-date -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1042: a customer's Details card reads 'Customer since Nov 19, 2026' … · 54.2s` (1 pass · 0 fail) · neighbours: `cd jest && npx jest unit/claim-handle-format.test.ts unit/q1-35-owner-cents.test.ts unit/customer-workspace.test.ts unit/demo-stage-rename-push.test.ts --selectProjects unit` → `4 passed, 38 tests passed`; `deno test -A --no-check lib/zero-balance-label.test.ts lib/customer-workspace-more-caret.test.tsx` → `4 passed | 0 failed`; `deno lint lib/format.ts islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx lib/customer-since.test.ts` → `Checked 3 files`; `deno check lib/format.ts islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx` → clean.

## REQ-1043 — Settings refuses a junk website; it never reaches the customer as a dead link (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-27)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-27** [major/BUG_HARM], cycle 2: "Settings accepts a junk website, which becomes a dead link on the customer's invoice" — "reyes tile dot com" saved without an error (the email field next to it is validated) and showed as a dead link on /i.
**Root cause:** no layer validates the website. `front-end/islands/SettingsPage.tsx` (website input, `data-cy=settings-website`) runs `normalizeWebsiteUrl(site)` on blur and calls `saveIdentity({ websiteUrl })` with no error state, unlike the email/business-name fields (`emailErr`/`bizErr`, aria-invalid, inline message). `normalizeWebsiteUrl` (shared/quote-flow/format-helpers.ts) only trims and prefixes `https://`, so "reyes tile dot com" → "https://reyes tile dot com", which `new URL()` rejects. `UpdateBusinessIdentityDto.websiteUrl` (backend/src/users/dto/business-identity.ts) is `@IsOptional() @IsString()` only, so PUT /profile/identity stores any string; the public controller passes it to /i (`<a href={invoice.contractor.websiteUrl}>`), the email sender block and the PDFs. Since 65a31f66 (REQ-038, normalization only).
**Requirement:** a blank website is allowed (clears it); anything else must parse as an http(s) URL with no whitespace and a dotted host with a TLD of 2+ letters (`isValidWebsiteUrl` next to `normalizeWebsiteUrl`). Settings shows an inline error (`data-cy=settings-website-error`, aria-invalid=true) and sends no PUT; the server answers 400 and keeps the previous value; the customer's /i keeps the previous valid link.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/website-url-validate.test.ts` ("REQ-1043 …": refuses "reyes tile dot com", "asdf", "http://", "https://reyes tile dot com"; accepts "reyestile.com", "https://a2zlandscape.com/", "http://hans.work", "") · int `backend/src/users/entrypoints/business-identity-controller/website-validate.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1043 q2-27: PUT /profile/identity refuses a junk website with 400 and keeps the previous one") · e2e `e2e/settings-website-validate/settings-website-validate.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1043 (q2-27): Settings refuses 'reyes tile dot com' on blur — inline error, aria-invalid, no PUT — and the customer's /i/:id keeps the previous website").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --ci unit/website-url-validate.test.ts` → `Tests: 9 failed, 9 total` (`shared/quote-flow/format-helpers.ts has no isValidWebsiteUrl() — nothing refuses a junk website`); `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/users/entrypoints/business-identity-controller/website-validate.int.test.ts` → `PUT websiteUrl="https://reyes tile dot com" must be refused … - status: 200 / + status: 400`; `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:57311 shots run e2e/settings-website-validate -- --no-check` (against `PORT=57311 deno task serve`, fresh KV) → `expectation failed: no PUT /profile/identity carries the junk website — expected [], got ["{\"websiteUrl\":\"https://reyes tile dot com\"}"]`.
**Fix (2026-11-19, cycle 2):** `isValidWebsiteUrl` in shared/quote-flow/format-helpers.ts (blank ok; no whitespace; normalized value parses as http(s) with a dotted host and a 2+ letter TLD) + `websiteUrlError` in shared/quote-flow/settings-fields.ts (key `settings.websiteInvalid`, en + es). Settings (front-end/islands/SettingsPage.tsx) checks it on blur like email/business name: `siteErr`, aria-invalid, inline `data-cy=settings-website-error`, no PUT. PUT /profile/identity (business-identity-controller) throws a 400 naming the key and keeps the stored value. Safety net for rows saved before the check: the public quote/invoice projections (public-controller) and the email sender blocks (send-paperwork-email) leave out a stored website that fails the rule.
**Test correction (e2e):** `expect.eq(websitePuts, [], …)` could never pass — shots' `expect.eq` compares with `!==`, and an array is never identical to a fresh `[]` (the fixed run failed with "expected [], got []"). The story now compares `JSON.stringify(websitePuts)` to `"[]"`; the assertion (no PUT carries the junk website) is unchanged.
