## REQ-1061 — AMENDMENT of REQ-146 / REQ-601: the editor invite links to /login in the owner's language, not the bare site root (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-49)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-49** [minor/BUG_POLISH], cycle 2: "Editor invite text links to the bare site root (marketing page), not /login" — the text read "Dana Ruiz (Ruiz Lawn & Pool Care) added you as an editor on DocuMonster. Sign in with this number at http://localhost:5280", and a fresh browser opened the marketing page in Spanish for an English owner.
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** `backend/src/users/domain/coordinators/account-admins/mod.ts` `invite()` sets `const url = appUrl();` — the bare origin (`appUrl()` in `users/domain/business/app-url/mod.ts` never carries a path) — and uses it both as the SMS `{url}` (`sms.adminInvite`) and as `signInUrl` (the REQ-601 share block on /admins). The owner's `lang` picks only the dictionary. A signed-out visitor to `/` gets the marketing landing page (`front-end/routes/index.tsx`) in the ?lang / pm_lang / Accept-Language language, while `/login` honours `?lang` (`resolvePageLang`). The worker text already deep-links (`workerSignInUrl` → `/worker?lang=…`, REQ-285); the editor text never got the same. The bare root goes back to REQ-146 (d346384e2) and was hoisted into a variable by REQ-601 (42acdce53); no requirement chose the landing page.
**Requirement:** the editor invite SMS and `signInUrl` are `<appUrl>/login?lang=<owner's language>` (en/es); opened signed out in a browser asking for another language, it is the sign-in page in the owner's language.

## REQ-1062 — The "still covers Zone A" refusal does not stay on the worker card after unrelated actions (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-51)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-51** [polish/BUG_POLISH], cycle 2: "'Still covers Zone A' error stays on the worker card after unrelated actions". After the owner clicks Remove on a worker who covers Zone A and then saves a new crew, the error is still shown under that worker.
**Root cause:** `front-end/islands/FieldWorkersPage.tsx` keeps a single `rowErr` slot for the whole page, and the worker row whose id matches it renders `[data-cy=wk-row-error]`. REQ-1015's `askRemove` (b64124dc) puts the `field.wk.err.coversZones` refusal in that slot, with the zone names frozen into `vars`. Only the row's own actions clear it: `setLanguage`, `setCrew`, `askRemove` with no zones, and `remove`. `reload()`, which runs after a crew or absence is saved or removed, does not clear it, and neither do `openCrew`, `submitCrew`, `removeCrew`, `openAway`, `removeAway` or the Add-worker `submit`. There is no dismiss button either. So the alert keeps sitting under the worker after the owner has moved on to something else.
**Requirement:** the REQ-1015 refusal is feedback for one Remove click. Saving a crew, opening the crew or away form, or marking someone out clears it from the worker's card.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/field-worker-row-error-clears.test.ts` ("REQ-1062 …": `reload`, `openCrew` and `openAway` each call `setRowErr(null)`) · int n/a — this is client state only; the backend is not involved · e2e `e2e/field-worker-errors/field-worker-errors.e2e.test.ts` (two "REQ-1062 …" stories: a worker covering Zone A → Remove → the coversZones alert shows → (a) save a new crew, or (b) mark another worker out (skip) → `[data-cy=wk-row-error]` is gone).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --runTestsByPath unit/field-worker-row-error-clears.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 failed, 3 total` (`Expected pattern: /setRowErr\(\s*null\s*\)/` against `reload`, `openCrew`, `openAway`); `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:6947 shots run e2e/field-worker-errors -- --no-check` against `PORT=6947 deno task serve` → ✓ REQ-421, ✓ REQ-1015, ✗ REQ-1062 crew `expectation failed: no wk-row-error on the worker's card after the crew is saved (still shows: This worker still covers Zone A. Reassign those zones in Assignments first.)`, ✗ REQ-1062 away `expectation failed: no wk-row-error on the worker's card after marking a worker out (still shows: This worker still covers Zone A. Reassign those zones in Assignments first.)`.
**Fix (2026-11-19, cycle 2):** `FieldWorkersPage.tsx` — `reload()` (run after a worker is added, a crew is saved or removed, an absence is saved or removed) now starts with `setRowErr(null)`, and `openCrew` / `openAway` clear it too, so the coversZones refusal (and any other row error) is dropped once the owner moves on to another action. The row's own actions already cleared it.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, cycle 2):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --runTestsByPath unit/field-worker-row-error-clears.test.ts unit/field-worker-remove-zones.test.ts` → `Tests: 5 passed, 5 total`; every jest unit suite that names FieldWorkersPage (13 suites) → `Tests: 84 passed, 84 total`; `cd front-end && deno lint islands/FieldWorkersPage.tsx` → `Checked 1 file`; `deno check islands/FieldWorkersPage.tsx` → clean; `deno fmt` (stdin) → no diff; `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:7431 shots run e2e/field-worker-errors -- --no-check` against `PORT=7431 deno task serve` (fresh KV) → rc 0, deno `ok | 4 passed | 0 failed` for the file (REQ-421, REQ-1015, both REQ-1062 stories); shots summary ✓ REQ-421, ✓ REQ-1015, ✓ REQ-1062 (shots lists the two REQ-1062 stories under one title line).

## REQ-1063 — REQ-924 AMENDMENT (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-52): the customer page's RECURRING figure honours a repeat visit's end date
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-52** [polish/BUG_POLISH], cycle 2: on /customers/:id Overview a weekly $85 visit that ends Dec 31 (6 visits left) shows "RECURRING $368/mo · 1 active · next Nov 26", a full open-ended monthly estimate with no sign it stops.
**Root cause:** the customer workspace (1c0be6f7, REQ-924, written the day before REQ-1004 gave repeat visits an `endDate`) never reads `Subscription.endDate` for money. `monthlyVisits(s)` in `backend/src/analytics/domain/business/customer-workspace/mod.ts` is a cadence-only rate (52/12 weeks per month), `build-customer-workspace/mod.ts` sets `monthlyCents = round(perVisit × monthlyVisits(s))` = round(8500 × 4.333) = 36833 ("$368") and sums every `s.active` service into `summary.recurringMonthlyCents`; `workspaceSummary` counts `activeServices` the same way. The endDate is only copied onto the service DTO; only `nextVisits()` stops at it. So the KPI never says when the income ends, and once the end date passes the service (still `active: true`) keeps reading "$368/mo · 1 active" forever.
**Requirement:** the /mo rate stays (REQ-924 defines Recurring as a monthly rate), but: a service whose end date is past counts in neither `activeServices` nor `recurringMonthlyCents` (like a paused one); a running service with an end date carries `remainingCents` (per-visit × visits left until the end, counted like `nextVisits` without the 5-visit cap); the summary carries `recurringEndsOn` (the earliest end date among running services); the KPI hint appends "· until Dec 31" / "· hasta el 31 dic" and the service card's price line reads "≈$368/mo · until Dec 31 ($510 left)".
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/analytics/domain/business/customer-workspace/test.ts` ("REQ-1063 (LOOP-007 q2, q2-52) …": 6 visits / $510 left from Nov 19 — a regression guard, green; an ended `active:true` service → activeServices 0, recurringMonthlyCents 0; a running one → `recurringEndsOn` "2026-12-31", none without an end date) · int `backend/src/analytics/entrypoints/clients-controller/workspace.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1063 …": GET /customers/:id/workspace → `summary.recurringEndsOn` and `services[0].remainingCents` = 51000; an end date of yesterday → activeServices 0, $0/mo) · e2e `e2e/q2-52-recurring-end-date/q2-52-recurring-end-date.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1063 …": POST /api/field/subscriptions weekly $85 ending in 6 visits → `[data-cy=cws-recurring]` says "until <end>", the card "($510 left)", and in Spanish "hasta el <end>").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/analytics/domain/business/customer-workspace/test.ts` → `FAILED | 7 passed | 2 failed` (`an ended service is not an active one` actual 1 expected 0; `the earliest end date among the running services` actual undefined expected "2026-12-31"); `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/analytics/entrypoints/clients-controller/workspace.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 2 failed` (`the summary says when the recurring income ends` actual undefined; `an ended repeat visit is not an active one` actual 1 expected 0); `shots run e2e/q2-52-recurring-end-date -- --no-check` → `expectation failed: the RECURRING KPI says when it ends: 'until Dec 30' (got "Recurring$368/mo1 active · next Nov 20")`.
**Fix (2026-11-19, cycle 2):** `customer-workspace/mod.ts` gains `hasEnded(s, today)` (endDate < today), `isRunning` (active and not ended) and `remainingVisits` (the visits left up to the end date, counted as `nextVisits` counts them, with no cap and skipping days already done or skipped). `workspaceSummary` counts only running services in `activeServices`, `nextVisit` and the /mo figure, and returns `recurringEndsOn`, the earliest end date among the running services. `build-customer-workspace` adds `ended` and `remainingCents` to each service, sums only running services into `recurringMonthlyCents`, and sorts running services first. On the front end, `CustomerWorkspace.tsx` adds "· until Dec 31" / "· hasta el 31 dic" to the KPI hint (`customerWs.kpi.until`) and "≈$368/mo · until Dec 31 ($510 left)" to the card price (`customerWs.svc.until`). An ended card is greyed and gets an "Ended Dec 31" pill (`customerWs.svc.endedPill`). When every service has ended, the KPI says "Ended" (`customerWs.kpi.ended`), not "Paused". The /mo rate stays. No test was changed.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/analytics/domain/business/customer-workspace/test.ts src/analytics/entrypoints/clients-controller/` → `ok | 28 passed | 0 failed`. `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit …` (ran the whole unit project) → `Test Suites: 644 passed, 644 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6335 passed`. `cd front-end && deno lint islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx clients/customer-workspace.ts && deno check …` → clean. `shots run e2e/q2-52-recurring-end-date e2e/customer-workspace -- --no-check` → `3 pass · 0 fail · 0 skipped` (✓ REQ-1063 …, ✓ REQ-924 Recurring on her page …, ✓ REQ-924 Customers sidebar …).

## REQ-1064 — LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-53: a one-day service date reads as one date on /i and in search, as it does in the email and PDF
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-53** [polish/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "Public invoice shows a one-day service date as a range" — /i/<INV-001> reads "November 19, 2026 → November 19, 2026" under Service dates; the email for the same invoice shows a single date.
**Root cause:** `front-end/routes/i/[id].tsx` (~455-460) builds the Service dates string as `[serviceDateFrom, serviceDateTo].filter(Boolean).map(fmtDate).join(" → ")` with no from == to check, so a one-day job (from == to) prints the day twice. The email (`send-paperwork-email/mod.ts` ~681) and PDF (`render-invoice-pdf/mod.ts` ~460) both use `from && to && from !== to ? \`${from} – ${to}\` : from || to` and show one date. All three came in with 474f09dc (REQ-198..210); only the backend got the same-day check, and REQ-944 (e9db26d6) later touched the page's fmtDate without changing the join. `shared/documents/search.ts` `searchHitDates` (~750) has the same plain join, so the global search sub-line also reads "Nov 19 → Nov 19".
**Requirement:** when serviceDateFrom and serviceDateTo are the same day, /i, the global search line, the email and the PDF all show that one date; two different days still show both; only one end set shows that one. /i's Service dates text matches the email's for the same invoice.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/q2-53-same-day-service-date.test.ts` ("REQ-1064 search: …": same day en/es and full-ISO vs bare day → the day once, no "→"; a two-day range keeps both days; a single end shows that day) · int n/a — the backend email and PDF already collapse a same-day range (the correct side of the contradiction); the faulty /i SSR is exercised through the real server by the e2e story · e2e `e2e/invoice-same-day-service/invoice-same-day-service.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1064 q2-53: …": a draft invoice with serviceDateFrom == serviceDateTo == 2026-11-19 → the email from GET /api/invoices/:id/send-preview reads "November 19, 2026"; /i/:id `[data-cy=invoice-service-dates]` must show that date once, no "→", and equal the email's).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit -i --no-watchman unit/q2-53-same-day-service-date.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 failed, 2 passed, 5 total` (same day en / es / full-ISO: `Expected: 1  Received: 2`); `BASE_URL=http://localhost:5617 shots run e2e/invoice-same-day-service -- --no-check` (against `PORT=5617 deno task serve`, fresh KV) → `expectation failed: /i shows the one-day service date once (got "November 19, 2026 → November 19, 2026") — expected 1, got 2` (the email assertion before it passed: "November 19, 2026").
**Fix (cycle 2):** one shared helper `shared/documents/service-dates.ts` `fmtServiceDates(from, to, fmt, sep = " – ")` — both ends on the same stored day (`YYYY-MM-DD` prefix, so a full ISO stamp and a bare day of it match) or formatting the same → that one date; two days → `from<sep>to`; one end → that day. Used by `/i/[id].tsx` (now the en dash, same as the email/PDF), `send-paperwork-email/mod.ts`, `render-invoice-pdf/mod.ts` and `shared/documents/search.ts` `searchHitDates` (which passes `" → "` so REQ-713's pinned "20 nov → 22 nov" in `jest/unit/c5-search-localized-dates.test.ts` stays as specified). Added unit `jest/unit/q2-53-service-dates-helper.test.ts` ("REQ-1064 …": same day, bare vs full ISO, same formatted string, two days with default en dash, custom separator, only from / only to / neither).
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, cycle 2):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit -i --no-watchman unit/q2-53-same-day-service-date.test.ts unit/q2-53-service-dates-helper.test.ts unit/c5-search-localized-dates.test.ts` → `Test Suites: 3 passed · Tests: 18 passed`; neighbouring jest unit suites (every unit test importing search.ts or /i/[id].tsx, 34 suites) → `Tests: 389 passed, 389 total`; `PORT=6143 KV_PATH=<fresh> deno task serve` + `BASE_URL=http://localhost:6143 shots run e2e/invoice-same-day-service -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1064 q2-53: a one-day service date (from == to) reads as one date on /i, the same as the invoice email · 1 pass · 0 fail`; `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/ src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/render-invoice-pdf/` → `ok | 98 passed | 0 failed`; `deno lint` + `deno check` clean on the touched front-end, shared and backend files.

## REQ-1065 — LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-54: the worker screen writes the day with one capitalisation (header, day tab, "Viendo" label)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-54** [polish/BUG_POLISH], cycle 2: on /worker?lang=es the header reads "Jue 19 de nov", but the day tabs and the "Viendo" line read "jue 19 de nov".
**Root cause:** `fmtDay()` (`front-end/lib/field.ts`) returns es-MX `toLocaleDateString` output, which is lowercase in Spanish ("jue 19 de nov"). The WorkerScreen header goes through the local `dayLine()` helper, which upper-cases the first letter (`front-end/islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` ~642-646, fd52cfa2, REQ-137..143). The day-strip tab (`<small>{fmtDay(iso, lang)}</small>`, REQ-192..197) and the REQ-528 label (`{t("worker.viewing")} <b>{fmtDay(date, lang)}</b>`) call `fmtDay()` directly and stay lowercase. English is unaffected because en-US weekday names are already capitalised. The mid-sentence deferredFrom message ("aplazada de jue 19 de nov") is correct lowercase and stays.
**Requirement:** every standalone day label on the worker screen (header, day tabs, "Viendo" label) shows the same text for the same day, starting with a capital in Spanish ("Jue 19 de nov"); English stays "Thu, Nov 19"; the mid-sentence deferredFrom date stays lowercase.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/worker-day-label-case.test.ts` ("REQ-1065 …": the day tab's and the "Viendo" label's expressions are lib/field formatter calls that render the header's capitalised text in Spanish, English unchanged, deferredFrom still plain `fmtDay`) · int n/a — pure front-end formatting, no backend involvement · e2e `e2e/worker-day-label-case/worker-day-label-case.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1065 …": a Spanish worker signs in; `.greet small`, `[data-cy=w-day-today] small` and `[data-cy=w-day-label] b` all start with a capital and read the same).
**Note for the fixer:** `jest/unit/worker-day-picker.test.ts` (REQ-194) pins `fmtDay\(iso, lang\)` in WorkerScreen; reconcile it with the new formatter.
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern worker-day-label-case` → `Tests: 2 failed, 2 passed, 4 total` (`Expected: "Jue 19 de nov"` / `Received: "jue 19 de nov"` for the day tab and the "Viendo" label); `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/worker-day-label-case -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1065 … expectation failed: the selected day tab starts with a capital (got "jue 19 de nov")`.
**Fix:** new `fmtDayLabel(iso, lang)` in `front-end/lib/field.ts` (fmtDay with the first letter capitalised) is the one formatter for standalone day labels; WorkerScreen's `dayLine()` now delegates to it, and the day-strip tab (`<small>{fmtDayLabel(iso, lang)}</small>`) and the "Viendo" label (`<b>{fmtDayLabel(date, lang)}</b>`) use it. The mid-sentence deferredFrom message keeps plain `fmtDay`. `jest/unit/worker-day-picker.test.ts` (REQ-194) pinned the literal `fmtDay(iso, lang)` wiring for the tab's short date; it now pins `fmtDayLabel(iso, lang)`, which is the same date, capitalised as REQ-1065 requires.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern worker-day-label-case` → `Tests: 4 passed, 4 total`; neighbours `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'unit/(worker-|field-|c5-worker|timeclock-worker|work-order-assignee)'` → `Test Suites: 48 passed, 48 total · Tests: 301 passed, 301 total`; `cd front-end && deno lint lib/field.ts islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` → `Checked 2 files`; `deno check lib/field.ts islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` → clean; `deno fmt -` over both files → no diff. e2e `shots run e2e/worker-day-label-case -- --no-check` was still running at commit time (not yet observed green).

## REQ-1067 — LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-55: the repeat visit form's requirement hints show only while unmet
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-55** [polish/BUG_POLISH], cycle 2. On /field/subscriptions → New / Edit, the form still said "Pick at least one day." with Thursday ticked and "Add at least one task type with a price." with "Pool cleaning $85" listed. It saved fine anyway.
**Root cause:** `front-end/islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx` draws both requirement messages as fixed `<span class="hint">` text with no condition on the form state. The weekday picker always renders `t("field.subs.daysHint")` (~line 1113, fd52cfa2, REQ-137..143), even though a New form opens with today's weekday already ticked. The task-type block's `subs-items-hint` (~lines 1366-1370, 9cf25d5f, REQ-811) picks checklistHint or noItems from `form.checklistId` alone and never checks `form.items.length`. The real gates are the submit-time checks (`!f.items.length && !f.checklistId`, `!f.days.length`, ~lines 477-485), which is why the save succeeds. `front-end/islands/FieldChecklistsPage.tsx` (~line 620) draws its `field.subs.noItems` hint with no condition in the same way.
**Requirement:** "Pick at least one day." shows only while no weekday is ticked (`data-cy="subs-days-hint"`). "Add at least one task type with a price." shows only while no task is listed and no checklist is picked. The checklist hint shows while a checklist is picked. With items listed and no checklist, the form shows neither hint. The checklist editor's noItems hint shows only while it has no items. In Edit mode, a saved visit shows neither requirement hint.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/subs-requirement-hints.test.ts` ("REQ-1067 …": the daysHint span inside `subs-days` is guarded by an empty `form.days` and has `data-cy="subs-days-hint"`; the noItems hint is guarded by `form.items.length`; the at-commit `form.checklistId ? checklistHint : noItems` fallback is gone; FieldChecklistsPage's noItems hint is guarded by `form.items.length`) · int n/a — purely client-side rendering; the backend and the submit-time validation are correct · e2e `e2e/subs-requirement-hints/subs-requirement-hints.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1067 …": New, as opened, shows the day hint only if no day is ticked. Untick every day and the day hint shows. Tick Thursday and add "Pool cleaning $85" and both hints are gone. Save and the card appears. Edit shows neither hint).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest --no-watchman --selectProjects unit unit/subs-requirement-hints.test.ts` → `Tests: 4 failed, 1 skipped, 6335 passed` (only the 4 REQ-1067 tests fail: `Expected pattern: /!\s*form\.days\.length\s*&&|…/`, `Expected pattern: /form\.items\.length/` ×2, `Expected pattern: not /form\.checklistId\s*\?\s*t\("field\.subs\.checklistHint"\)\s*:\s*t\("field\.subs\.noItems"\)/`); `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/subs-requirement-hints -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1067 … expectation failed: New, as opened: the day hint shows only when no day is ticked — {"ticked":1,"items":0,"daysHint":true,"itemsHint":true} — expected false, got true`.
**Fix (2026-11-19, cycle 2):** `FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx`: the weekday picker's daysHint renders only under `!form.days.length` (as `data-cy="subs-days-hint"`). The task-type block renders checklistHint while `form.checklistId` is set, noItems only while `!form.items.length`, and nothing otherwise. `FieldChecklistsPage.tsx`: the noItems hint renders only while `!form.items.length` (as `data-cy="ckl-items-hint"`). ## REQ-1066 — AMENDMENT of REQ-277 / REQ-626: the customer card does not headline "Send a kind reminder" for an invoice that is not due yet (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-56)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-56** [minor/BUG_POLISH], cycle 2: "Customer board suggests a reminder for an invoice sent minutes ago" — right after the batch send the /customers card read "$85 outstanding · INV-001 · due in 30 days. … Send a kind reminder →".
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** the card's CTA chooser looks only at whether a balance is open. `front-end/lib/client-actions.ts` `ctaKindFor` returns `"reminder"` whenever `c.balanceCents > 0` (first branch), and `shared/card-actions/mod.ts` `clientCtaAction` / `clientCtaMessageKind` (REQ-626, e8b435f1) repeat the same balance-only rule. The backend card (`build-customer-cards/mod.ts`) already sends `balanceSubParts.kind` = `"overdue"` / `"dueToday"` / `"dueIn"` (with `days`), and `storyLineFor` prints "due in 30 days" from it, but the CTA never consults it; `ctaFor` maps the kind to `clientsDisplay.cta.reminder` ("Send a kind reminder"). REQ-277 (M31) and REQ-626 wired the balance-first precedence to real actions without a due-date check.
**Requirement:** the card's headline nudge (label, `ctaKindFor`, and the pre-filled message kind, `clientCtaMessageKind`, on one precedence) is a reminder only for money that is due: an invoice overdue or due today. An open invoice due in 30 days does not read "Send a kind reminder". The explicit Remind action on the customer page and the invoice stays available before the due date.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/client-cta-not-due.test.ts` ("REQ-1066 …": `ctaKindFor`, `clientCtaMessageKind` and `ctaFor` for $85 `dueIn` 30 days are not the reminder; `overdue` and `dueToday` still are) · int n/a — the backend already sends `balanceSubParts.kind` `"dueIn"` (covered by `receivables.int.test.ts`); the fault is the front-end/shared CTA rule only · e2e `e2e/client-cta-not-due/client-cta-not-due.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1066 …": an $85 invoice sent today, due in 30 days → the card says "due in 30 days" and its `ccard2-nudge` does not say "Send a kind reminder"; a 10-days-overdue invoice's card still does).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --runInBand --no-watchman unit/client-cta-not-due.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 failed, 1 passed, 4 total` (`ctaKindFor` / `clientCtaMessageKind` `Expected: not "reminder"`; `ctaFor` `Expected: not "Send a kind reminder"`; overdue/dueToday still pass); `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/client-cta-not-due -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1066 … · 46.8s · expectation failed: an invoice due in 30 days must not headline a reminder (nudge: "Send a kind reminder →")` (the card's "due in 30 days" and the overdue card's reminder assertions held).
**Fix:** one shared predicate, `balanceWantsReminder` in `shared/card-actions/mod.ts`, decides "is this balance due enough to chase". It is true for an open balance unless the card's `balanceSubParts.kind` is `"dueIn"` with more than `REMINDER_DUE_WITHIN_DAYS` (3) days to go. Overdue, due today, due within 3 days, and `"owes"` (open money with no due date, or a card without parts) still headline the reminder. `clientCtaAction`, `clientCtaMessageKind` and the front-end `ctaKindFor` (which also drives `ctaFor`'s label and `nudgeActionFor`) all go through it, so the label, the message and the action stay on one precedence (REQ-277). A balance that is not yet due falls through to the status verb; the backend gives an owing customer status `"owes"`, so the card reads "Open card" and opens the panel, where the explicit Remind action stays available. No new lang keys.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, cycle 2):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --runInBand --no-watchman unit/client-cta-not-due.test.ts unit/client-card-actions.test.ts unit/card-actions.test.ts` → `Test Suites: 3 passed, 3 total · Tests: 20 passed, 20 total`; neighbouring suites (every jest unit file importing clients-display / ClientsBoard / card-actions / client-actions, 22 files) → `Test Suites: 22 passed, 22 total · Tests: 355 passed, 355 total`; `cd front-end && deno lint` + `deno check` on `../shared/card-actions/mod.ts lib/client-actions.ts lib/clients-display.ts islands/ClientsBoard.tsx` → `Checked 4 files` with no lint errors, and type-check ok; `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> SHOTS_JOBS=1 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/client-cta-not-due -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1066 (LOOP-007 q2-56): an $85 invoice sent today, due in 30 days — the customer card does not say 'Send a kind reminder'; an overdue one does · 96.1s` (rc 0).

## REQ-1068 — New repeat visit can add a new customer inline (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-57)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-57** [minor/MISSING_IN_FLOW], cycle 2: on /field/subscriptions → New repeat visit, typing a new customer name gives "No matches." with no create row, though services can be created inline in the same form.
**Root cause:** the customer `SearchSelect` in `front-end/islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx` (~916-954, `data-cy="subs-customer"`) is rendered without `onCreate`/`createLabel`. `SearchSelect.tsx:79` builds the create row only when `onCreate` is passed (`offer = onCreate && !picked ? createOffer(...) : null`), so with no matching rows it draws `common.noMatches`. The only way out is the static hint `field.subs.manageCustomers` + a plain `<a href="/customers">` (from the REQ-137..143 port, fd52cfa20), which leaves the modal and loses what was typed. REQ-283 solved the same thing on /field/tasks (`createCustomer` → `clientsClient.create`) but scoped it to that page; the service picker in this modal already creates inline (REQ-979).
**Requirement:** the New repeat visit customer box offers `+ Add "<name>" as a customer` (`field.subs.addCustomer`, en + es) for a name that is not a customer; clicking it creates the customer through the existing POST /customers (`clientsClient.create`), picks them, keeps a typed address, flashes a confirmation (`field.subs.customerAdded`, en + es), and the visit saves on that customer. Creation stays off while editing (the box is disabled then).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/subs-create-customer.test.ts` ("REQ-1068: …": the customer SearchSelect has `onCreate` + `createLabel` using `field.subs.addCustomer`; the island calls `clientsClient.create(`; en/es carry `field.subs.addCustomer` with `{name}` and `field.subs.customerAdded`) · int n/a — no backend change; POST /customers and POST /field/subscriptions already exist and are covered · e2e `e2e/subs-create-customer/subs-create-customer.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1068 (LOOP-007 q2-57): …": type "Jim Baker" → create row reads `+ Add "Jim Baker" as a customer`, no `search-select-empty`; click → POST /api/customers ok; add a service + price, Save → the card shows Jim Baker; GET /api/customers?q=Jim Baker finds him).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/subs-create-customer.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 failed, 3 total` (`Expected pattern: /onCreate=\{/`; `Expected pattern: /clientsClient\.create\(/`; `Expected: "string" Received: "undefined"`); `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/subs-create-customer -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1068 … expectation failed: the box offers to add the new name as a customer (got {"create":null,"empty":"No matches."}) — expected "+ Add \"Jim Baker\" as a customer", got null`.
**Fix:** `front-end/islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx` gains `createCustomer(name)`, modelled on REQ-283's version. It calls `clientsClient.create({ name, address })` (the existing POST /customers, so REQ-137's customer store and routes are unchanged), merges the result into `customers` in sorted order, sets `lastPick` and `form.customerId`, keeps a typed address (or fills it from the customer's), and shows `field.subs.customerAdded` under the box (`data-cy="subs-customer-added"`). On failure it sets the form's error line. The customer SearchSelect now gets `onCreate={form.editId === null ? createCustomer : undefined}` and `createLabel` → `field.subs.addCustomer`, so creation stays off while editing. The `field.subs.manageCustomers` hint now reads "Type a new name to add a customer. To edit customers, go to [Customers]" (es likewise). New en + es keys: `field.subs.addCustomer` and `field.subs.customerAdded`. No test was changed.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/subs-create-customer.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 passed, 3 total`. `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/subs-create-customer -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1068 (LOOP-007 q2-57): New repeat visit — a new customer name offers '+ Add "Jim Baker" as a customer', creates him, and the visit saves on him · 111.3s`. Neighbours: `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit <FieldSubscriptionsPage + i18n suites>` → `Test Suites: 645 passed, 645 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6338 passed`. `shots run e2e/field-subs-modal-foot -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-734` en and es. `cd front-end && deno lint islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx` → `Checked 1 file`. `deno check islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx` → ok. `deno fmt -` (stdin) diff is clean on the island and on both lang files.

## REQ-1069 — A lawn or pool business's onboarding sample is a service visit, never the "Paver Patio Installation" (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-58)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-58** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: /welcome step 10 showed a "Paver Patio Installation" sample for "Ruiz Lawn & Pool Care" — the sample does not match the trade (REQ-256: "Its job follows the business").
**Root cause:** `shared/quote-flow/sample-quote.ts` (KEYWORDS, ~104-116) puts lawn-care stems ("lawn", "garden", "jardin", "yard", "tree", "pasto") and hardscape stems ("paver", "patio", "hardscap") in ONE "landscaping" trade, whose one sample is `ensureSampleQuote.landscaping.*` = "Paver Patio Installation" / "Instalación de patio de adoquines" ($2,200 + $1,500), and there is no pool trade at all. `inferSampleTrade` returns the first trade with a stem hit, so "ruiz lawn & pool care" → "lawn" → landscaping; the wizard's sampleQuote step (`WelcomeWizard.tsx` → POST /agents/conversations/sample-quote → `EnsureSampleQuote`, `inferSampleTrade(identity.businessName)`) builds the paver patio. "Blue Pool Service" falls to general, and `tradeKindFor` calls it a "project". REQ-343's `trade-fit.ts` lists landscaping as a SERVICE trade, which contradicts the hardscape sample. eadacf3c (REQ-256) and e01e8c9d (REQ-360) never split lawn care from hardscape.
**Requirement:** lawn / garden / yard / tree businesses get a "lawncare" trade, pool businesses (pool, piscina, alberca) a "pool" trade, each with its own service-visit sample (prices + `ensureSampleQuote.<trade>.{jobName,materials,labor}` in en AND es, no paver/patio/adoquín copy); the paver patio stays landscaping's alone (landscap, paver, patio, hardscap); every lawn/pool name reads as a SERVICE trade in `tradeKindFor`.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/sample-quote-lawn-pool.test.ts` ("REQ-1069 …": Ruiz Lawn & Pool Care is not landscaping and its copy names no paver; pool/lawncare picks; hardscape names keep landscaping; no lawn/pool name gets hardscape copy; the new trades' prices + keys; `tradeKindFor` = service) + `jest/unit/sample-quote.test.ts` (REQ-256's "Green Lawn Landscaping" case → "Stone Path Landscaping") · int `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/ensure-sample-quote/int.test.ts` ("REQ-1069 (q2-58): …": the coordinator for "Ruiz Lawn & Pool Care" stores no paver/patio/adoquín in jobName/jobNameByLang/line items, and its job names the lawn/pool work) · e2e `e2e/sample-quote-lawn-pool/sample-quote-lawn-pool.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1069 (LOOP-007 q2-58): …": signed-in "Ruiz Lawn & Pool Care" reaches /welcome step 10; the inline sample has no paver patio and names lawn/pool work; /q/<id>?lang=es has no adoquines).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/sample-quote-lawn-pool.test.ts unit/sample-quote.test.ts` → `Tests: 5 failed, 6 passed, 11 total` (`"Green Lawn Mowing" - "lawncare" + "landscaping"`; `Array [] + ["Ruiz Lawn & Pool Care", "Green Lawn Mowing", "Jardinería López", …]`; `Expected value: "pool"` not in SAMPLE_TRADES; `"Blue Pool Service" - "service" + "project"`); `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/agents/domain/coordinators/ensure-sample-quote/int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 8 passed | 1 failed` (`hardscape copy on a lawn & pool sample` → `["Paver Patio Installation", …, "Instalación de patio de adoquines", "Pavers, base and sand (materials)", …]`); `shots run e2e/sample-quote-lawn-pool -- --no-check` → `✗ … expectation failed: step 10 shows no paver patio for a lawn & pool business (sample: … Sample quote — not sent to anyone AWAITING SIGNATURE Paver Patio Installation TO Your customer FROM Story Person Ruiz Lawn & Pool Care …)`.
**Fix:** `shared/quote-flow/sample-quote.ts` splits the old bucket: new trade `lawncare` (lawn, mow, grass, garden, jardin/jardín, yard, tree service/care/trim, trees, pasto, cesped/césped; checked before landscaping, so "Lawn & Landscaping" names get the visit) with the "Lawn Mowing & Edging Visit" / "Corte y orillado de césped" sample ($15 + $65); new trade `pool` (pool, piscina, alberca; checked before cleaning, so "Alberca Limpia" is not a house cleaning) with "Pool Cleaning & Chemical Balance" / "Limpieza de piscina y balance químico" ($45 + $95); `landscaping` keeps only landscap, paver, patio, hardscap (the paver patio). Both trades are in `SAMPLE_TRADES`, `SAMPLE_PRICES`, `lang/{en,es}.json` (`ensureSampleQuote.{lawncare,pool}.*`), and `trade-fit.ts` `SERVICE_SAMPLE_TRADES`; `composerTradeFor` maps lawncare → landscaping (its composer lines were always weekly mowing) and pool → general (no pool composer line yet). The bare stem "tree" became "tree service/care/trim", "trees" so "Main Street …" no longer reads as a tree business.
**Test correction:** `jest/unit/sample-quote-leaks.test.ts` (REQ-360) also pinned `inferSampleTrade("Green Lawn Landscaping")` to "landscaping", which is the paver patio, the exact bug. The RCA asked for that case to be updated and the test writer only updated the copy in sample-quote.test.ts. It now expects "lawncare", and "Stone Path Landscaping" keeps "landscaping".

## REQ-1070 — AMENDMENT of REQ-366 / REQ-407: no Misc Technical glyph (U+2300–23FF, e.g. ⏭) as a UI icon; the worker's Defer controls draw an SVG (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-59)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-59** [polish/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "Literal '⏭' glyph in the worker Defer buttons escapes the REQ-366 guard".
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** the four ⏭ in `front-end/islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` (deferred-service hint :832, `w-defer-visit` :877, per-task deferred hint :976, per-task `w-defer` :994) came in with fd52cfa2 (REQ-137..143, 2026-11-03), before REQ-366. REQ-366 promises "every UI icon on an app surface … is an inline SVG from components/ui/Icon.tsx", but its guard `DINGBAT = /[✀-➿■-◿]/u` (`front-end/lib/ui-glyph-icons.test.tsx`) bans only U+2700–27BF and (REQ-407) U+25A0–25FF; ⏭ is U+23ED (Misc Technical), so it passes, sitting next to the Note/Services buttons' SVG icons. Same gap in `front-end/islands/PhoneChat.tsx:249`. The web fonts (Nunito/Inter) lack the glyph, so it renders through per-character font fallback — the risk REQ-366 removed.
**Requirement:** no app UI source or lang string uses a U+2300–23FF character as an icon; a keyboard-key label inside `<kbd>…</kbd>` (AsstComposer's ⏎ / ⇧⏎ send hint) is text, not an icon, and is exempt. Arrows (U+2190–21FF) stay exempt per REQ-407. Emoji (🔒 💬 …) are out of scope here — a separate owner call.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/ui-glyph-icons.test.tsx` ("REQ-1070 (LOOP-007 q2-59): no app UI source uses a Misc Technical glyph …" and "… no app lang string carries a Misc Technical glyph") · int n/a — rendering only, no backend or wire change · e2e `e2e/worker-defer-icon/worker-defer-icon.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1070 …": a signed-in worker's `w-defer-visit` and per-task `w-defer` each contain an `<svg>` and no U+2300–23FF character; `w-note-btn` is the control that already passes).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-59 at 240a6443):** `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/ui-glyph-icons.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 5 passed | 2 failed`; REQ-1070 lists `PhoneChat.tsx:249`, `WorkerScreen.tsx:832`, `:877`, `:976`, `:994`. (The other failure, REQ-366's own Dingbat guard on `CustomerWorkspace.tsx:1590` ✉️, is pre-existing at 240a6443 and not this issue.) e2e `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5733 shots run e2e/worker-defer-icon/worker-defer-icon.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` (against `PORT=5733 deno task serve`) → `expectation failed: w-defer-visit has no <svg> icon (text "⏭ Defer visit") | w-defer-visit text carries a Misc Technical glyph U+23ED ("⏭ Defer visit") | w-defer has no <svg> icon (text "⏭ Tomorrow") | w-defer text carries a Misc Technical glyph U+23ED ("⏭ Tomorrow")`.
**Fix:** `front-end/lib/dash-icons.tsx` gains `ICN.skip` and `ICN.lock`; `front-end/components/ui/Icon.tsx` gains `skip-forward` and `lock`. `WorkerScreen.tsx` draws `<I d={ICN.skip}>` on `w-defer-visit` (flex-column row, like Note/Services) and, wrapped in a new inline `.ico-in` span, on the deferred-service hint, the per-task deferred hint and the per-task `w-defer`; the 🔒 on the locked-service label and the `w-preview` hint becomes `<I d={ICN.lock}>` the same way (RCA step 2 — same file, same font-fallback gap). `PhoneChat.tsx`'s end-state control draws `<Icon name="skip-forward">`. To leave the guard file fully green, the pre-existing REQ-366 hit `CustomerWorkspace.tsx:1590` (outbox row 💬 / ✉️, U+2709 Dingbat, from a7fc1c90) now draws `<I d={ICN.msg}>` / `<I d={ICN.mail}>`. No test assertion changed. Emoji elsewhere (e.g. WorkerScreen's 💬 note hint) stay — the emoji ban is the separate owner call above.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-59):** `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/ui-glyph-icons.test.tsx` → `ok | 7 passed | 0 failed` · e2e `SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:6851 shots run e2e/worker-defer-icon/worker-defer-icon.e2e.test.ts -- --no-check` (against `PORT=6851 deno task serve`) → `✓ REQ-1070 (LOOP-007 q2-59): the worker's Defer visit / Defer buttons draw an SVG icon, never a literal ⏭ glyph · 45.8s` · neighbours: `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit …` (the 33 suites touching WorkerScreen / PhoneChat / CustomerWorkspace / icons; jest ran the whole unit project) → `Test Suites: 644 passed, 644 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6335 passed` · `cd front-end && deno test -A lib/ui-glyph-icons.test.tsx lib/zero-balance-label.test.ts lib/worker-ssr-lang.test.ts lib/customer-workspace-more-caret.test.tsx lib/lang-event.test.ts` → `ok | 19 passed | 0 failed` · `deno lint` (5 touched files) → `Checked 5 files` · `deno check` (touched files + the test) → clean.

## REQ-1071 — LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-60: a part-payment receipt shows the balance still due and a link to pay it, with money in cents
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-60** [minor/MISSING_IN_FLOW], cycle 2: after $500 of a $1,190.75 invoice is paid, the receipt email ("Recibo de INV-001") reads "Registramos tu pago de <strong>$500</strong>. Adjuntamos un recibo…". It does not say that $690.75 is still due, it has no link back to /i to pay it, and the amount prints without cents.
**Root cause:** REQ-963 (34f60c31) moved ConfirmPayment's receipt template into SendPaymentReceipt without changes and sent it from POST /payments whenever a balance is left. `renderReceiptHtml` (`backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/payment-receipt/mod.ts`) receives only the payment amount. It never gets the invoice total, the amount paid, the balance or a URL, and its output is a headline plus the one `confirmPayment.email.body` sentence. The email branch of `send-payment-receipt/mod.ts` passes `amount: payment.amount` and nothing else, while the SMS branch of the same coordinator does mint a `/s` shortlink to the invoice. The receipt's `fmtUSD` uses `minimumFractionDigits: 0`, so 50000 cents prints as "$500". The invoice emails' formatter uses 2 decimals, which gives "$1,190.75".
**Requirement:** a receipt for a payment that leaves a balance prints the amount with cents ("$500.00"), shows the balance still due and the invoice total ("$690.75" of "$1,190.75"), and has a button linking to the invoice (the `/s` shortlink, opened in the receipt's language) so the customer can pay. The wording is in en and es. When nothing is left to pay, the receipt has no balance line and no pay link.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/payment-receipt/mod.test.ts` ("REQ-1071 q2-60 …": `fmtUSD(50000)` → "$500.00"; `renderReceiptHtml({amount: 50000, totalCents: 119075, balanceCents: 69075, payUrl})` contains "$500.00", "$690.75", "$1,190.75" and `href="<payUrl>"` in en and es; with `balanceCents: 0` it has no balance and no link) · int `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/payment-controller/partial-receipt.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1071 q2-60 …": POST /payments $500 on a $1,190.75 invoice → the captured receipt email has "$500.00", "$690.75" and an `href` to `/s/…` or `/i/…`) · e2e `e2e/req-963-partial-receipt/req-963-partial-receipt.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1071 q2-60 …": record $500 in the Record payment dialog → GET /api/outbox/:id of the receipt email shows "$500.00", "$690.75" and a pay link).

## REQ-1072 — A customer's money reads to the cent on the customer page, the /customers board and the /invoices hero (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-61)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-61** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "Customer-page KPIs round one amount and not the next" — on /customers/<id> TE DEBE reads "$1,190.75" beside FACTURADO (TOTAL) "$1,191"; after a $500 payment the board card reads "$691 pendiente" while the customer page reads "$690.75", and the /invoices hero reads "$691 en camino" beside the Out tile's "$690.75".
**Root cause:** the same cents go through different formatters. `front-end/islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx` has a local `money(cents, lang, whole)` (REQ-924, 1c0be6f7) whose `whole=true` path sets `maximumFractionDigits: 0`; the owes KPI calls it without `whole` (cents) while billed, paid, recurring, unbilled and open-quotes pass `true` (rounded). The board's `dollars()` in `front-end/lib/clients-display.ts` (balanceDisplay, the to-bill/credit text, storyLineFor) always rounds to whole dollars, and the /invoices hero prints `fmtMoney(outstandingTotal)` while the Out tile uses `fmtMoneyTotal`. REQ-961 (e80608c7) set the rule — totals read against an exact document reconcile to the cent (`fmtMoneyTotal`: whole dollars only when the total is whole) — but covered only /invoices' tiles, the money bar and /payments.
**Requirement:** every customer-money total on /customers/<id>, the /customers board card and the /invoices hero reads whole dollars only when the amount is whole ("$2,400") and to the cent otherwise ("$1,190.75", "$690.75"), so side-by-side figures for the same money never disagree.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/q2-61-customer-money-cents.test.ts` ("REQ-1072 …": balanceDisplay 69075 → "$690.75 due" / "$690.75 pendiente", 240000 → "$2,400 due"; storyLineFor keeps "$690.75"; CustomerWorkspace has no `money(…, lang, true)` call and no `maximumFractionDigits: 0`; the /invoices hero uses `fmtMoneyTotal(outstandingTotal)`) · int n/a — the backend already returns exact cents; only front-end formatting is wrong · e2e `e2e/customer-money-cents/customer-money-cents.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1072 q2-61 …": a $1,190.75 invoice → owes and billed KPIs both "$1,190.75"; after a $500 check → owes "$690.75", billed "$1,190.75", paid "$500", board card "$690.75 due", /invoices hero "$690.75").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, cycle 2, at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/q2-61-customer-money-cents.test.ts` → `5 failed, 1 passed` (`Expected: "$690.75 due" Received: "$691 due"`; story line `"$691 outstanding · awaiting payment."`; six `money(…, lang, true)` calls — billed, paid, recurringMonthly, unbilled, openQuotes, sv.monthly; `maximumFractionDigits: 0` present; `fmtMoney(outstandingTotal)` present); `BASE_URL=http://localhost:47231 shots run e2e/customer-money-cents -- --no-check` → `expectation failed … expected {"beforeOwed":"$1,190.75","beforeBilled":"$1,190.75","afterOwed":"$690.75","afterBilled":"$1,190.75","afterPaid":"$500","board":"$690.75 due","hero":"$690.75"}, got {"beforeOwed":"$1,190.75","beforeBilled":"$1,191","afterOwed":"$690.75","afterBilled":"$1,191","afterPaid":"$500","board":"$691 due","hero":"$691"}`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `CustomerWorkspace.tsx` drops `money()`'s `whole` path; the KPI totals (billed, paid, recurring monthly, unbilled, open quotes, a service's monthly) go through a new lang-aware `moneyTotal(cents, lang)`, the es-US/en-US twin of `fmtMoneyTotal`: `minimumFractionDigits: 0` only when `cents % 100 === 0`, else the currency default of 2 places. The owes/overdue amounts keep the exact `money()` (always to the cent, "$500.00"), as REQ-924's story pins; they never disagreed. `clients-display.ts` `dollars()` (balanceDisplay due/credit, the balance sub, storyLineFor) now returns `fmtMoneyTotal(|cents|)` with the sign, and its only callers are in that file (SettingsPage's `dollars` comes from PlanCards and is unchanged). `InvoicesPage.tsx`'s hero prints `fmtMoneyTotal(outstandingTotal)`, like the Out tile.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-61):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit -w 1 unit/q2-61-customer-money-cents.test.ts` → `Tests: 6 passed, 6 total`; neighbours `npx jest --selectProjects unit` on q2-61, plain-dashboard-copy, field-sample-leftovers, customerless-invoices, q1-35-owner-cents, customer-step-feedback, invoice-kpi-claimed, customers-noun, new-customer-status, customer-card-docs, customer-workspace, es-copy-plurals-c1, live-lang-switch, format-helpers, dashboard-headlines-c4 → `Test Suites: 15 passed, 15 total · Tests: 208 passed, 208 total`; with `PORT=47231 KV_PATH=<scratch> deno task serve`, `BASE_URL=http://localhost:47231 shots run e2e/customer-money-cents -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1072 q2-61 … · 49.6s`, `shots run e2e/customer-workspace` → `2 pass · 0 fail`, `shots run e2e/owner-cents` → `✓ REQ-961 q1-35 …`; `cd front-end && deno lint` + `deno check` on CustomerWorkspace.tsx, InvoicesPage.tsx, lib/clients-display.ts → clean; stdin `deno fmt` → no diff.

## REQ-1073: a part-paid invoice reads "Partly paid" / "Pago parcial" on every screen, and search shows its balance (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-62)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-62** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "One part-paid invoice shows four different statuses across screens". QA issued INV-001 for $1,190.75 and recorded $500. The customer Invoices tab said "Pago parcial", the /invoices card said "Enviada", the header search said "INV-001 · Factura / $1,190.75 / Enviada", and /i said "PENDIENTE".
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** there is no single display status for invoices. A part payment makes `ComputeInvoiceBalance` store `status: "pending"`, and each screen turns that into a label its own way. `CustomerWorkspace.invoicePill` checks `paidCents>0 && balanceCents>0` and shows `customerWs.state.partly` (REQ-924). `InvoicesPage.enrich` has no partly-paid stage, so an issued "pending" invoice falls through to stage `out` and shows `invoicesPage.stage.out` ("Enviada"). `shared/documents/search.ts` sets `status: invoiceState(i)`, which returns `sent` for anything issued that is not paid/void/claimed/scheduled. It also sends `amountCents: i.amount`, the full total, and never calls `hitBalanceCents`, which has no callers. `invoiceStatusPill`, used by /i, has no partly-paid kind, so it shows `publicInvoice.status.due` ("Pendiente"). REQ-966's `invoiceDisplayStatus` already returns "partly paid" for this case, but only the CSV export calls it.
**Requirement:** an open invoice that is not overdue and has money paid on it (0 < paidCents < amount, or a stored "pending") reads "Partly paid" / "Pago parcial" on the customer Invoices tab, the /invoices card, the header search and the /i pill. Overdue still wins (REQ-966 order). The search hit carries `balanceCents` (the amount still owed), and the search row shows it ($690.75 for a $1,190.75 invoice with $500 paid).
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/loop7-q2-62-partly-paid-status.test.ts` ("REQ-1073 …"): the search hit has status `partly_paid` and `balanceCents` 69075; `search.status.partly_paid` reads "Partly paid" / "Pago parcial"; GlobalSearch renders `h.balanceCents`; the /i pill has kind `partly` with the customer-tab label in en and es, and overdue still gives `pastDue`; the InvoicesPage stage union has `"partly"` with `invoicesPage.stage.partly` "Partly paid" / "Pago parcial". int `backend/src/analytics/entrypoints/search-controller/partly-paid.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1073 …"): after POST /payments for $500 of $1,190.75, GET /search returns the invoice with status `partly_paid` and balanceCents 69075. e2e `e2e/partly-paid-status/partly-paid-status.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1073 …"): in Spanish, records $500 on a $1,190.75 invoice, then reads the customer tab pill, the /invoices card status, the header search row and the /i pill. All four must say "Pago parcial", and the search row must show $690.75.
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-62 at 240a6443):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --no-watchman --runTestsByPath unit/loop7-q2-62-partly-paid-status.test.ts` gives `Tests: 7 failed, 2 passed, 9 total`: `Expected: "partly_paid" Received: "sent"`; `Expected: 69075 Received: undefined`; `Expected: "partly" Received: "due"` (en and es); `search.status.partly_paid` undefined; no `h.balanceCents`; no `"partly"` stage. The two that pass are guards: REQ-966's baseline and the overdue order. `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/analytics/entrypoints/search-controller/partly-paid.int.test.ts` gives `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` (`- balanceCents: undefined, - status: "sent"` / `+ balanceCents: 69075, + status: "partly_paid"`). `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> SHOTS_JOBS=1 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/partly-paid-status -- --no-check` gives `✗ … expectation failed: /invoices card status (all: {"customerTab":"Pago parcial","invoicesCard":"Enviada","search":"Enviada","publicInvoice":"Pendiente"}) — expected "Pago parcial", got "Enviada"`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `shared/documents/invoice-status.ts` now holds the one partly-paid rule, `isPartlyPaid` (open, not void/paid, 0 < paidCents < amount). Every screen reads it. `invoicePillFlags` returns `partlyPaid` (after void/paid/claimed/past due), and `invoiceStatusPill` has a `partly` kind (key `publicInvoice.status.partlyPaid`, amber tone), so the /i pill and the PDF stamp say it too. `invoiceDisplayStatus` (CSV) uses the same rule. `search.ts` sets the invoice hit status with the new `invoiceSearchState` (`partly_paid` when `invoiceDisplayStatus` says "partly paid", else `invoiceState`), and the hit carries `balanceCents: hitBalanceCents(i)`. `GlobalSearch` shows "$690.75 due of $1,190.75" (`search.balanceOf`) when 0 < balance < total. `InvoicesPage.enrich` gives stage `partly` (label `invoicesPage.stage.partly`, Out-lane colours), and the stage stays in the Out lane: the out filter, the CTA/subline/read text, Payment received, the reminder, `hasNudgeButton`/`detailStageAction` (`CardStage` gains `partly`) and `invoiceKpiTotals` all treat `partly` as `out`. `CustomerWorkspace.invoicePill` calls `isPartlyPaid`. New lang keys in en/es: `search.status.partly_paid`, `search.balanceOf`, `publicInvoice.status.partlyPaid`, `invoicesPage.stage.partly`. One choice differs from the requirement text above: a stored "pending" with **nothing** paid does NOT count as partly paid. `ComputeInvoiceBalance` also leaves "pending" once every payment is deleted, so that bill reads as sent/due. The CSV now prints "sent" for it, not "partly paid" (the REQ-966 tests all carry paidCents and stay green).
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-62):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --no-watchman --runTestsByPath unit/loop7-q2-62-partly-paid-status.test.ts` gives `Tests: 9 passed, 9 total`. `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/analytics/entrypoints/search-controller/partly-paid.int.test.ts` gives `ok | 1 passed | 0 failed`. `SHOTS_JOBS=1 … shots run e2e/partly-paid-status -- --no-check` gives `✓ REQ-1073 (LOOP-007 q2-62) … · 37s`. Neighbours: the full jest unit lane gives `Test Suites: 645 passed, 645 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6344 passed`. Backend search-controller, global-search, render-invoice-pdf, invoice-controller exports and invoice-aging give `ok | 42 passed | 0 failed`. front-end `deno test` on lib/invoice-card*.test, invoice-detail-actions and global-search-focus-close gives `33 passed | 0 failed`. The e2e stories global-search, customer-workspace, invoice-pdf-matches-page, req-909-record-payment-search, req-963-partial-receipt, paid-month-agree, public-invoice-title, status-colors and es-invoices-grammar all pass. Six of them first failed with `backend_unreachable` while the jest lane was running at the same time, and passed when re-run on their own. `deno lint` and `deno check` are clean on every touched front-end/backend file.

## REQ-1074 — /invoices "Paid this month": the tile, its subline and track 06 tell one story, and the hero total keeps its cents (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-63)
**Source:** Raphael (QA loop): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". Issue **q2-63** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], LOOP-007 cycle 2: "/invoices says $500 was paid this month and also that nothing was paid". After a $500 check on a $1,190.75 invoice the tile read "PAGADAS ESTE MES $500 · 0 confirmadas", track 06 "0 facturas — Nada pagado todavía este mes", and the hero "$691 en camino" beside the Out tile's "$690.75".
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** two faults in `front-end/islands/InvoicesPage.tsx`. (1) REQ-959 (28346cf3) moved only the tile's VALUE to `paidThisMonthCents(s.payments, …)` (every payment received this month, so the $500 counts); the tile subline (`paidCount={paidThisMonth.length}`) and track 06 (`count={paidThisMonth.length}`, the `EmptyTrack invoicesPage.empty.paid` branch) still read `paidThisMonth = enriched.filter(stage === "paid" && paidAt >= monthCutoff)`, which drops a part-paid bill (no paidAt, stage "out") — so one screen says $500 and "nothing paid". (2) The "outstanding" hero renders `<em>{fmtMoney(outstandingTotal)}</em>`; `fmtMoney` rounds to whole dollars (69075 → "$691"), and REQ-961 (e80608c7) moved the KPI tiles to `fmtMoneyTotal` ("$690.75") but missed this exact total.
**Requirement:** (a) track 06 and the tile subline count from the same payment population as the tile's value: every invoice that received money on/after the month start is in track 06 (a pure helper `paidThisMonthInvoiceIds(payments, invoices, monthStart)` in `front-end/lib/headline-counts.ts`), and neither the subline nor the track reads "0" / "Nothing paid yet this month" beside a non-zero "Paid this month". (b) The hero's outstanding total is `fmtMoneyTotal`, so it matches the Out tile to the cent.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/paid-this-month.test.ts` ("REQ-1074 (q2-63): …" ×2: `paidThisMonthInvoiceIds` returns the part-paid bill; the count beside a non-zero amount is not 0) · unit `jest/unit/q2-63-paid-month-agree.test.ts` ("REQ-1074: …" ×3: 69075 → "$690.75" / "$691"; the hero's `outstandingTotal` goes through `fmtMoneyTotal`; track 06 and the subline do not count only stage-"paid" invoices while the value counts payments) · int n/a — the backend data is right (the payment lands, `paidCents` = 50000); the fault is front-end aggregation and formatting · e2e `e2e/paid-month-agree/paid-month-agree.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1074 (q2-63): after a $500 part payment, …": tile value, subline, track 06 header and body, hero).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-63 at 240a6443):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/paid-this-month.test.ts` → `FAILED | 2 passed | 2 failed` ("headline-counts.ts exports no paidThisMonthInvoiceIds …"; "track 06 counts 0 invoice(s) beside a "Paid this month" of 50000 cents"); `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern q2-63-paid-month-agree` → `Tests: 2 failed, 1 passed` (`Expected: "fmtMoneyTotal" Received: "fmtMoney"`; the stage-only population still feeds both counts); `BASE_URL=… shots run e2e/paid-month-agree -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-959 …`, `✗ REQ-1074 … expectation failed: the tile subline starts with 0 beside $500 (got "0 cleared") | track 06 counts 0 beside a $500 Paid this month (got "0 invoices") | track 06 says "Nothing paid yet this month" while $500 was paid | the hero total does not read $690.75 like the Out tile (got "$691 on the wayacross 1 invoice.")`.
**Fix (fix/q2-q2-63):** `front-end/lib/headline-counts.ts` gains `paidThisMonthInvoiceIds(payments, invoices, monthStart)` — the ids of every bill that received credited money this month, from the exact payment population `paidThisMonthCents` sums (non-reversed, receivedAt ≥ month start, credited > 0). `InvoicesPage.tsx`: track 06 ("Paid this month") lists those bills plus any bill marked paid this month without a payment record (`clearedThisMonth`, the old stage-"paid" filter, now only the "cleared" count); a part-paid bill shows there with its REQ-202 "partial" line, and `inView` is de-duplicated since it also sits in track 03. The tile subline counts the same bills and, when some are only part-paid, says so: "1 invoice · 0 paid in full" / "1 factura · 0 saldadas" (new `invoicesPage.kpi.paidSubBills.*`, `invoicesPage.kpi.paidSubFull.*`); when every bill cleared it keeps "{n} cleared". If money landed on a bill no longer listed, track 06's empty hint is `invoicesPage.empty.paidUnlisted` ("{amount} received this month, …"), never "Nothing paid". The outstanding hero and the scheduled hero amount render with `fmtMoneyTotal` (REQ-961), so "$690.75 on the way" matches the Out tile. No test was changed.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/paid-this-month.test.ts` → `ok | 4 passed | 0 failed` · `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern q2-63-paid-month-agree` → `Tests: 3 passed, 3 total` · `PORT=23417 deno task serve` + `SHOTS_DIR=… BASE_URL=http://localhost:23417 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/paid-month-agree -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-959 (q1-34) …`, `✓ REQ-1074 (q2-63) …` — `2 pass · 0 fail` · neighbours: `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check` over the 21 front-end tests that read InvoicesPage/headline-counts/lang → `ok | 132 passed | 0 failed`; `deno lint` + `deno check islands/InvoicesPage.tsx lib/headline-counts.ts` clean; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit <the 318 jest/unit files that read InvoicesPage, headline-counts or lang/*.json>` → `Test Suites: 645 passed, 645 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 6338 passed`.

## REQ-1076 — LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-64: "Send a text" on an email-only customer is not a dead end (amends REQ-924(c) / REQ-989)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-64** [minor/MISSING_IN_FLOW], cycle 2: on /customers/<id> → Más → "Enviar un mensaje" for an email-only customer (Tom Becker), the Messages tab shows only "Este cliente no tiene teléfono registrado." There is no email composer and no "add a phone" link, though the board card offers "+ Agregar teléfono".
**Root cause:** REQ-924 (1c0be6f7) built the workspace's Messages tab around the phone line only, and REQ-989 (a7fc1c90) added the outbox history but left the no-phone branch as static text. In `front-end/islands/CustomerWorkspace.tsx`, the More menu's "Send a text" item always renders and only calls `setTab("messages")`. `<Messages customerId={c.id} phone={c.phoneNumber} lang={lang} />` gets no email and no callback to the edit dialog. With `peer = null`, the thread card is only `<div data-cy="cws-msg-nophone">{customerWs.msg.noPhone}</div>`, with no action. The noLine branch, by contrast, links to /communications, and the same page's Edit details (`setModal({ kind: "edit" })`) can already add a phone. The Spanish label "Enviar un mensaje" (es.json) promises any message, while en says "Send a text".
**Requirement:** when the customer has no phone, the Messages tab's no-phone card offers an add-phone control (`data-cy="cws-msg-addphone"`, `customerWs.msg.addPhone`) that opens the customer edit dialog. When she has an email, it also offers an email action (`data-cy="cws-msg-email"`, `customerWs.msg.email`). The Spanish More item says it sends a text (or the item is gated on a phone). After a phone is saved, the tab shows the compose box or the get-a-line pitch, not the no-phone note.

## REQ-1078 — The Outbox heading never counts a refused text as sent (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-66)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-66** [polish/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "Outbox counts a refused text as 'Sent to customers'; receipt was tried by text on an email-only send".
**Root cause:** `front-end/islands/OutboxPage.tsx` (lines 93-94, since REQ-784's first commit f3ba1da18) puts `outbox.listTitle` ("Sent to customers" / "Enviado a clientes") over `<span data-cy="outbox-count">{rows?.length}</span>`, and `rows` is everything GET /api/outbox returns. REQ-784 records every message that went OR was meant to go, ok:false rows included, so the count includes unsent rows under a heading that says they were sent. In QA's run, Rosa Delgado (email + 843-555-0111) got an Email-only invoice and a part payment. `SendPaymentReceipt` (backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-payment-receipt/mod.ts ~232-248) emails the receipt, then runs `customerSmsTarget(customer.phoneNumber)` without looking at the invoice's send channel, and logs a not-sent text/receipt row ("fictional"). The page showed "Sent to customers 3", and one of the three rows said "Not texted".
**Requirement:** the outbox heading never claims more messages were sent than actually went. With [sent email, sent email, not-texted text], it shows the 2 that went, e.g. "2 sent · 1 not sent", or a neutral heading, never "sent" over 3 (en + es). The second half, whether the receipt follows the invoice's chosen channel, is an OWNER_CALL that is not decided here.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/outbox-count-sent.test.tsx` ("REQ-1078 (LOOP-007 q2, q2-66): [sent email, sent email, not-texted text] — the outbox heading never says … over 3; it shows the 2 that went (en|es)": mounts OutboxPage live with GET /outbox stubbed and reads `.panel__title`) · int n/a — the backend's rows are correct per REQ-784, and the receipt-channel change is an open owner call; if it is taken, add a test in send-payment-receipt (an invoice sent email-only → no text outbox row) · e2e `e2e/outbox-sent-count/outbox-sent-count.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1078 …": a customer with email + (843) 555-0111, an invoice emailed, a part payment, then /messages; heading + count are read in one page.evaluate).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, at 240a6443):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/outbox-count-sent.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed` (`the heading counts the refused text as sent: "Sent to customers3"`, `… "Enviado a clientes3"`); `SHOTS_SERVE_TIMEOUT=300000 shots run e2e/outbox-sent-count -- --no-check` → `expectation failed: the heading "Sent to customers3" counts all 3 rows as sent (invoice:email:sent receipt:email:sent receipt:text:not_sent)`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `front-end/islands/OutboxPage.tsx` no longer puts one total under a "sent" heading. The heading is neutral, `outbox.listTitle` "Messages to customers" / "Mensajes a clientes", and the count splits the rows by status: `[data-cy=outbox-count]` reads `outbox.countSent` "{n} sent" / "{n} enviados" (rows with status "sent"), and when any did not go, `[data-cy=outbox-count-not-sent]` reads `outbox.countNotSent` "{n} not sent" / "{n} sin enviar". The REQ-784 rows themselves are unchanged (unsent rows are still listed on purpose). The receipt-channel half (SendPaymentReceipt tries a guarded text even when the invoice went Email only) stays an OWNER_CALL: not changed here.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/outbox-count-sent.test.tsx` → `ok | 2 passed | 0 failed`; `SHOTS_SERVE_TIMEOUT=300000 shots run e2e/outbox-sent-count -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1078 (LOOP-007 q2, q2-66): … does not count the refused receipt text as sent · 76.8s` (the run also pulled in unrelated /field stories, 13 of which "did not finish" under host load avg ~140 — the known host-lane cut, none on /messages); `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → `Test Suites: 644 passed`, `Tests: 1 skipped, 6335 passed`; `deno lint` clean on the island + test, `deno check islands/OutboxPage.tsx` clean, island `deno fmt`-clean via stdin; en/es key sets identical, last key still `comms.a2p.sys.house`. Neighbour `deno test lib/outbox.test.tsx` → 11 passed, 1 failed: the REQ-784 d12 sidebar test ("Outbox is a root row", it reads `NAV`, which this change does not touch) — pre-existing, not from this fix.

## REQ-1077 — AMENDMENT of REQ-530: the one-customer /customers headline never calls the customer "first" (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-67)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-67** [polish/BUG_POLISH], cycle 2: "Board calls the remaining customer 'first' after another was deleted" — after adding two customers and deleting one, /customers reads "Your first customer is on your list."
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** the hero h1 in `front-end/components/ClientsSections.tsx` picks the `.one` keys (`clientsHero.titlePre.one` / `clientsHero.people.one` / `clientsHero.titlePost.one`) when `totalClients === 1`, and `totalClients` is `cards.length` of the customers that still exist (`backend/src/analytics/domain/business/clients-page/mod.ts`, fed via `ClientsPage.tsx`). The REQ-530 tests `jest/unit/clients-hero-singular.test.ts` and `e2e/clients-hero-singular` and the REQ-413 assertion in `jest/unit/es-copy-plurals-c1.test.ts` pinned the old wording, so they now expect the neutral copy. ## REQ-1079 — LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-68: the quote PDF (and the signed copy) attached to a Spanish email is named in Spanish
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-68** [polish/BUG_POLISH], cycle 2: "Quote PDF attached to a Spanish email is named in English" — the Spanish "Cotización Q-001" email carried "Quote-Q-001.pdf", while the receipt in the same thread is "Recibo-INV-001.pdf".
**Root cause (at 240a6443):** the attachment filename is a hardcoded English template that never receives the send language. REQ-945 (40250954) added the quote PDF with `quoteFileName(quote)` → `Quote-${docRef}.pdf` (`backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/mod.ts`), copying REQ-204's `agreementFileName(quote)` → `Agreement-${docRef}.pdf` (`send-signed-confirmation/mod.ts`, used for the attachment and the body's file card). `SendPaperworkEmail` calls `quotePdfAttachment(userId, quote, customer, sender, biz)` with no language (the PDF body takes `biz.commsLanguage`, not the send language), while the receipt already uses `t(lang, "confirmPayment.email.attachmentName")` ("Recibo-{id}.pdf" / "Receipt-{id}.pdf").
**Requirement:** a customer email's PDF attachment is named in the email's send language: the quote PDF "Cotizacion-<n>.pdf" in Spanish and "Quote-<n>.pdf" in English; the signed copy "Acuerdo-<n>.pdf" in Spanish and "Agreement-<n>.pdf" in English, the body's file card showing the same name. Spanish names drop the accent (filename-safe). The quote email's name follows the send language (an explicit `language` pick), not only the business's stored `commsLanguage`.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/attachment-name.test.ts` ("REQ-1079 q2-68 quoteFileName …": es → "Cotizacion-Q-001.pdf", en → "Quote-Q-001.pdf") and `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-signed-confirmation/attachment-name.test.ts` ("REQ-1079 q2-68 agreementFileName …": es → "Acuerdo-Q-001.pdf", en → "Agreement-Q-001.pdf") · int `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/int.test.ts` ("REQ-1079 q2-68 send-paperwork-email: a Spanish quote send attaches 'Cotizacion-<n>.pdf', an English one 'Quote-<n>.pdf'") and `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-signed-confirmation/attachment-name.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1079 q2-68 send-signed-confirmation: …" Spanish → "Acuerdo-…pdf" attachment and no "Agreement-….pdf" in the body; English keeps "Agreement-…pdf") · e2e n/a — the Outbox does not record attachments (REQ-945), so no browser surface shows the filename.
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-68 at 240a6443):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/attachment-name.test.ts src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-signed-confirmation/attachment-name.test.ts src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-signed-confirmation/attachment-name.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 3 passed | 3 failed` (`- Quote-Q-001.pdf + Cotizacion-Q-001.pdf`; `- Agreement-Q-001.pdf + Acuerdo-Q-001.pdf`; `the Spanish signed copy is named 'Acuerdo-…pdf' (got "Agreement-Q-001.pdf")`); `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/int.test.ts --filter REQ-1079` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` (`the Spanish email's quote PDF is named 'Cotizacion-…pdf' (got "Quote-Q-001.pdf")`).
**Fix:** new lang keys `paperworkEmail.quote.attachmentName` ("Quote-{id}.pdf" / "Cotizacion-{id}.pdf") and `signedConfirm.email.attachmentName` ("Agreement-{id}.pdf" / "Acuerdo-{id}.pdf"). `quoteFileName(quote, lang)` and `agreementFileName(quote, lang)` name the file with `t(lang, …)`. `SendPaperworkEmail.quotePdfAttachment` now takes the send language (`outboxFacts.language`, the language the subject and body were rendered in) and uses it for both the filename and the PDF body. The signed confirmation passes its resolved `lang` to the attachment and to the body's file card.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q2-q2-68):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/attachment-name.test.ts src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-signed-confirmation/attachment-name.test.ts` → `ok | 4 passed | 0 failed`; `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/ src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-signed-confirmation/` (both REQ-1079 int tests and every neighbour) → `ok | 144 passed | 0 failed`; `deno check` + `deno lint` on both touched mod.ts → clean; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` (lang parity included) → `Test Suites: 644 passed, 644 total`; en.json/es.json have the same key set, and the last key is still `comms.a2p.sys.house`.

## REQ-1080 — The customer API refuses a blank name and a phone the SMS path cannot dial (LOOP-007 cycle 2, q2-69; amends REQ-278 + REQ-352)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q2-69** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 2: "API saves a customer whose name is only spaces, and a phone with 'ext 9'" — POST /api/customers `{name:"   "}` → 200 and a nameless "?" card on the board; "+1 (843) 555-0124 ext 9" stored as typed.
**Root cause:** (1) `backend/src/crm/dto/customer.ts` — `CreateCustomerDto.name` is only `@IsString()` and `parseCreateCustomer` runs class-validator, `assertContact`, `assertAddressParts` and never trims or checks the name; `UpdateCustomerDto.name` has the same gap, so a PUT can blank a name. REQ-352's "a name is required" (`customer.nameRequired`) lives only in the front-end `customerFormErrors`, so a direct POST/PUT bypasses it. (2) `shared/quote-flow/customer-contact.ts` `customerPhoneE164` — its "+" branch (added in 68b76bf8, REQ-278) strips every non-digit, letters included, and accepts any 7–15 digits: "+1 (843) 555-0124 ext 9" → "+184355501249". The send path's `normalizeE164` (`backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/customer-sms/mod.ts`) has no such branch and answers undefined for the same input, so the number is saved but refused as "invalid" when texted — breaking REQ-278's promise that "a number that is accepted here is a number the send path can text".
**Requirement:** POST and PUT /customers refuse an empty or whitespace-only name with 400 `customer.nameRequired` (the name is kept trimmed; a PUT without `name` is unchanged); a phone carrying an extension ("ext 9", "x9") or a "+1" number that is not 11 digits is refused with 400 `customer.invalidPhone`; and the save rule and the SMS send rule give the same answer for every input (same E.164 or both refuse). Nothing is saved or changed on a refusal.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/crm/dto/customer.test.ts` ("REQ-1080 q2-69 …": parseCreate/UpdateCustomer refuse "", "   ", "\t \n" with 400 `customer.nameRequired`, trim the kept name, refuse the ext phones with `customer.invalidPhone`), `backend/src/paperwork/domain/business/customer-sms/mod.test.ts` ("REQ-1080 q2-69 save rule and SMS send rule agree on …": `customerPhoneE164` vs `normalizeE164` parity over ext / +1-12-digit / international / good / bad inputs), `jest/unit/customer-contact.test.ts` ("REQ-1080 rejects …": the shared rule the New customer modal uses refuses the ext phones) · integration: covered by the in-process HTTP `backend/src/crm/entrypoints/customer-controller/e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1080 q2-69 customer e2e: …": POST `{name:"   "}`, `{name:""}`, the ext-9 phone → 400 + key, list empty; PUT `{name:"  "}` → 400, name unchanged) · browser e2e n/a — the New customer modal already blocks the blank name (REQ-352 e2e) and its phone check calls the same `isValidCustomerPhone` covered by the jest unit; the defect is the API/shared rule.
