## REQ-1092 — AMENDMENT of REQ-1051: the English job name keeps "and" and every area, and the Spanish customer's name never turns "house + fence" into "of the fence" (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-1 + q3-2)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issues, cycle 3: **q3-1** [major/BUG_CONTRADICTION] "Spanish job name drops the house: 'Pintura exterior de la cerca' for a house-paint + fence-stain job", and **q3-2** [minor/BUG_POLISH] "English job name is ungrammatical: 'Exterior Painting Fence'". QA typed "paint exterior of house $3,850 and stain cedar fence $1,275.50". The chat summary read "Exterior painting and fence staining — Maria Lopez", the English subject read "… — Exterior Painting Fence", and the Spanish subjects read "… — Pintura exterior de la cerca" and "Firmado: Pintura exterior de la cerca".
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** the model's create_quote left out the optional `jobName`, so `QuoteStore.create` fell back to `summarizeJobName(summary, "en")` (3-word default). The English branch of `summarizeJobName` (shared/quote-flow/job-name.ts) is a bag-of-words picker. It drops every STOPWORD, including "and", and keeps the first 3 significant words: "Exterior painting and fence staining" becomes "Exterior Painting Fence". REQ-1051's `compactAreas` is called only from the Spanish branch and from `fitJobNameToBudget`. `areaObject` also only shortens an area that has "de/del/of", so `compactAreas("Exterior Painting and Fence Staining")` is null, and the Spanish "Pintura exterior y tinte para cerca" derives to "Pintura exterior". At send time `TranslateQuote` translates the stored English name on its own, and the model renders "Exterior Painting Fence" faithfully as "Pintura exterior de la cerca" ("exterior painting of the fence"). That is cached in `jobNameByLang.es`, and the email subject, /q, /i, the signed copy, /quotes and the dashboard all read it.
**Requirement:** a job that names two areas joined by and/y/&/+ keeps the joiner and both areas on every job-name path, in English as in Spanish, within the 5-word / 30-char budget. "Exterior painting and fence staining" becomes "Exterior Painting and Fence", never "Exterior Painting Fence". "Pintura exterior y tinte para cerca" keeps "cerca". An area with no "de/of" object still shortens to what it names ("Fence Staining" → "Fence", "tinte para cerca" → "cerca"). The Spanish customer's subject and SMS name the house and the fence ("… y cerca"), never "de la cerca".
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/job-name-two-areas.test.ts` ("REQ-1092 (LOOP-007 q3-1, q3-2) …": `summarizeJobName("Exterior painting and fence staining — Maria Lopez","en")` with the default and 5-word budgets is valid and starts "Exterior Painting and Fence"; the Spanish "Pintura exterior y tinte para cerca — Lupe Garza" keeps "y … cerca"; `fitJobNameToBudget("Exterior Painting and Fence Staining")` keeps "and Fence"; `compactAreas` of it is "Exterior Painting and Fence") · unit `backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/quote-store/job-name-areas.test.ts` ("REQ-1092 …": QuoteStore.create with that English summary and no jobName stores a valid name containing "Exterior Painting and Fence") · int `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/job-name-areas.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1092 …": an English create_quote with that summary and no jobName, followed by the real TranslateQuote (a scripted translator that replays the observed "Exterior Painting Fence" → "Pintura exterior de la cerca" and reads anything else word for word), then the real SendPaperworkEmail (en and es) and SendPaperworkSms (es). The stored name and the English subject contain "Exterior Painting and Fence"; the Spanish subject and SMS contain "y … cerca" and never "de la cerca") · e2e n/a — the browser lane runs the stub model, which never emits this summary; the int test drives the real chat coordinator, store, translator and email/SMS coordinators.
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-1 at 0a71387e):** `cd jest && ./node_modules/.bin/jest --watchman=false --ci --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'unit/job-name-two-areas'` → `Tests: 4 failed, 3 passed, 7 total`: `Expected: not "Exterior Painting Fence"`; 5-word budget `isValidJobName` false ("Exterior Painting Fence Staining", 32 chars); `Expected pattern: /^Pintura exterior y / Received string: "Pintura exterior"`; `compactAreas` `Expected: "Exterior Painting and Fence" Received: null`. The `fitJobNameToBudget` case already passes and guards against regressions. `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/data/quote-store/job-name-areas.test.ts` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 1 failed` (`Expected actual: "Exterior Painting Fence" to contain: "Exterior Painting and Fence"`). `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/job-name-areas.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 2 passed | 1 failed` (`the stored jobName "Exterior Painting Fence" dropped the joiner or the fence`). With the stored-name assertions disabled as a probe, the same test reaches the Spanish send and fails with `the Spanish subject names the wrong scope ("exterior painting of the fence"): Cotización Q-001 de Torres Pintura — Pintura exterior de la cerca`, which is QA's subject.
**Fix:** `shared/quote-flow/job-name.ts`: (1) the English branch of `summarizeJobName` first tries `summarizeAreasEn`. When the words list two or more areas joined by and/y/&/+ and carry no number or size, it drops the articles, Title-Cases the phrase with lowercase minor words (`translatedJobNameCase`), and returns it whole if it fits the budget, or else `compactAreas` of it. Otherwise the REQ-337/434 stopword path is unchanged. (2) `areaObject` also takes "para"/"con"/"for" as object markers ("tinte para cerca" → "cerca"), and an English area that ends on an action noun (staining, painting, repair, replacement, install(ation), removal, cleaning, washing, sealing, refinishing, restoration, remodel, cleanup, work) shortens to the thing it acts on ("Fence Staining" → "Fence"). (3) `cutAtRecipient` now counts the "two words before for/para" rule within the area the marker sits in, so "Pintura exterior y tinte PARA cerca" is no longer cut at "para" as if "cerca" were the recipient. A capitalized name after it still cuts. `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/polish-job-details/mod.ts`: the English `clampJobName` keeps a two-area name from `summarizeJobName` (one that contains " and ") instead of the raw 3-word slice. TranslateQuote is unchanged. The jobName and summary already ride the same translation call, and with an English name that names both areas, the Spanish copy names both too (the int test's translator proves the path).
**Test amended (REQ-1092):** `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/polish-job-details/int.test.ts` "REQ-434 M10 polish: a model jobName clamped to three words never ends on a connector" pinned `"Kitchen Renovation"` for the model's "Kitchen Renovation and Cleanup". That name is 4 words and 30 chars, so it is inside REQ-337's budget, and cutting it drops the cleanup area, which REQ-1051 and REQ-1092 forbid. The expectation is now `"Kitchen Renovation and Cleanup"`. REQ-434's intent, never ending on a dangling "and", still holds.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-1):** `cd jest && ./node_modules/.bin/jest --watchman=false --ci --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'unit/job-name'` → `Test Suites: 2 passed, 2 total · Tests: 27 passed, 27 total`. `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/polish-job-details/ src/paperwork/domain/data/quote-store/job-name-areas.test.ts src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/job-name-areas.int.test.ts` → `ok | 10 passed | 0 failed`. Neighbours: the jest unit project (every suite in jest/unit) → `Test Suites: 679 passed, 679 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 6536 passed`. The 232 backend test files that reference job-name, summarizeJobName, QuoteStore, jobName, polish-job-details or translate-quote → `1435 passed | 1 failed` before the amendment above (that one is the REQ-434 polish pin). After it, the re-run gave `1433 passed | 3 failed`. All three failures are environmental and unrelated to job names: `AddrInUse: Address already in use (os error 48)` in signed-links-lang.int.test.ts, plus a null OTP in publish-language.int.test.ts. Run alone, `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/public-controller/signed-links-lang.int.test.ts src/paperwork/entrypoints/revisions-controller/publish-language.int.test.ts` gives `ok | 3 passed | 0 failed`. `deno lint` and `deno check` on job-name.ts and polish-job-details → clean.

## REQ-1094 — AMENDMENT of REQ-1051: a within-budget job name still names every area the quote's lines cover (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-3)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-3** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "Job name, agreement title and email subject drop the fence entirely". "Exterior house paint $3,800 and paint the backyard fence $450.50" stored both lines but got jobName "Exterior Painting", so the /q heading and emails 005/006/008 ("— Pintura exterior", "approved your quote for Exterior Painting", "Firmado: Pintura exterior") named only the house.
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** nothing checks a job name against the quote's line items. `handle-chat-message/mod.ts` (create_quote, ~3854-3860) refits the model's `jobName` only when `!isValidJobName(...)`. "Exterior Painting" (2 words, 17 chars) is valid, so it is stored as typed. With no jobName, `QuoteStore.create` (`quote-store/mod.ts` ~122-132) falls back to `summarizeJobName(summary)`, which reads the same summary without the fence ("Exterior painting") and never looks at `lineItems`. REQ-1051's fix (a5981772) added `compactAreas` inside `fitJobNameToBudget` for over-budget names only. `isValidJobName` (`shared/quote-flow/job-name.ts`) checks only the length/word budget, and "name every area the work covers" (`lang/en.json` `prompts.tools.createQuote.jobName`) is a promise made only in the prompt.
**Requirement:** every job-name path (the model's within-budget name, the model's over-budget name, QuoteStore's derived fallback) gives a name inside the REQ-337 budget that names each area the quote's lines cover: house + fence → e.g. "Exterior Painting & Fence" / "Pintura exterior y cerca". The quote email subject and the SMS carry that name.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/quote-store/job-name-covers-lines.test.ts` ("REQ-1094 (LOOP-007 q3-3) QuoteStore derives …": no jobName, summary "Exterior painting — María José Peña" + house/fence lines → jobName contains "fence"; es "Pintura exterior — …" + casa/cerca lines → contains "cerca") · int `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/job-name-covers-lines.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1094 (LOOP-007 q3-3): the model's within-budget jobName …": stub LLM create_quote with jobName "Exterior Painting" / "Pintura exterior" + two area lines; real coordinator, stores, SendPaperworkEmail and SendPaperworkSms on KV :memory:; the stored jobName, the quote email subject and the SMS each name the fence / cerca) · e2e n/a — the browser lane's stub model never emits a short name that drops an area. The int test drives the real coordinator, stores and senders that every surface (the /q heading, the emails) reads from.
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-3 at 0a71387e):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/job-name-covers-lines.int.test.ts src/paperwork/domain/data/quote-store/job-name-covers-lines.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 4 failed` (`Expected actual: "exterior painting" to contain: "fence": the stored jobName "Exterior Painting" dropped the fence line` ×2; `Expected actual: "pintura exterior" to contain: "cerca": the stored jobName "Pintura exterior" dropped the cerca line` ×2).
**Fix:** `shared/quote-flow/job-name.ts` gains `jobNameCoveringLines(name, lineDescriptions, lang)`. Each non-cost line (labor, materials and permits are not areas) is covered when the name says its area noun (the object after "de"/"of", else the last area word of an English noun phrase) or a word only that line has; the action every line shares ("paint", "pintura") separates no area. Each uncovered area noun is joined on ("Exterior Painting & Fence", "Pintura exterior y cerca") and kept only inside the REQ-337 budget, with `compactAreas` as the fallback. A name that covers none of the lines (an umbrella like "Kitchen Remodel") is left alone. It is wired into `handle-chat-message/mod.ts` create_quote for EVERY model name, valid ones included (lines' language via messageLang, else replyLang), and into `QuoteStore.create`'s derived fallback. generate-job-options is unchanged: its options carry bullets, not priced lines, and the chosen option's quote is named through the two paths above.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-3):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/data/quote-store/job-name-covers-lines.test.ts src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/job-name-covers-lines.int.test.ts` → `ok | 4 passed | 0 failed`. Neighbours: `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents src/paperwork` → `ok | 2157 passed (3 steps) | 0 failed`; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → `Test Suites: 679 passed, 679 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6531 passed`; `deno lint` on the 3 touched files → `Checked 3 files`; `deno check` on the quote-store and handle-chat-message modules → clean.

## REQ-1087 — AMENDMENT of REQ-1046 / REQ-591: the quote email names the job the way its subject does, with no summary "— <customer>" tail (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-4)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-4** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "Same quote's job named three different ways; quote email still uses the summary's '— <customer>' tail". The subject and /q said "Exterior Painting & Fence Staining" (from jobName), the email heading said "Exterior Painting And Fence Staining — Maria Lopez", and the Spanish preheader said "Para Lupe — Pintura exterior y tinte para cerca — Lupe Garza".
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** the chat model writes `summary` as "<job> — <customer>" (REQ-576 depends on that tail) and writes a separate `jobName`. `renderQuoteSubject` (`backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/mod.ts` ~946) names the job with `jobNameByLang[lang] ?? jobName`. `renderQuoteHtml` (~1161-1180) builds the hero heading and the preheader from `quoteSummary(q, lang)` and strips only a leading "Quote:". `quoteSummary` (`shared/quote-flow/quote-translations.ts`) returns the typed summary verbatim in the quote's own language, so the tail stays. In English, `titleCaseJobName` (`shared/quote-flow/email-format.ts`) then upper-cases every word, which turns "and" into "And". The preheader adds "For/Para <first> — " in front, so the customer is named twice. REQ-591 chose the summary for the hero on purpose. REQ-1046 (b0f90a69) added `summaryWithoutCustomerTail` but used it only in the signed email, the alerts and /quotes, never in send-paperwork-email. The revision and resend emails go through the same `renderQuoteHtml`.
**Requirement:** the quote email (first send, revision, resend) uses the same job label in its hero heading, its preheader and its subject: `jobNameByLang[lang] ?? jobName`. Only when that label is empty does it fall back to the summary in the send language with its "— <customer>" tail removed. The customer's name never appears inside the job label, and the preheader names the customer once ("For Maria — <job> · $total"). The English hero never title-cases "and/or/of/for". /q's heading names the same job.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/job-label.test.ts` ("REQ-1087 (LOOP-007 q3, q3-4) …": en {jobName "Exterior Painting & Fence Staining", summary "Exterior painting and fence staining — Maria Lopez"} and es {jobName "Pintura exterior y tinte para cerca", summary "… — Lupe Garza"}. Checks: the hero has no customer tail; the hero equals the subject's job part; the preheader has no tail and contains the subject's job; no capital And/Or/Of/For in the en hero; with no jobName, the summary fallback has no tail) · int n/a: `renderQuoteHtml`/`renderQuoteSubject` are pure renderers, and the unit test calls them directly with the real `quoteSummary`/`titleCaseJobName`. The e2e covers the HTTP send → outbox path · e2e `e2e/quote-email-job-name/quote-email-job-name.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1087 (LOOP-007 q3, q3-4) en|es: …": the quote is seeded through the API with that summary/jobName pair, POST /quotes/:id/email, then GET /outbox/:id. Checks: the subject's job is the jobName; the email <h1> has no tail and equals the subject's job; the preheader has no tail; the /q h1.ctr__title contains the email heading).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-4 at 0a71387e):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/job-label.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 8 failed` (`- Exterior Painting And Fence Staining — Maria Lopez` / `+ Exterior Painting & Fence Staining`; `the preheader repeats the customer's full name: "For Maria — Exterior painting and fence staining — Maria Lopez · $6,000.00"`; `the hero names the customer: "Pintura exterior y tinte para cerca — Lupe Garza"`; `the preheader repeats the customer's full name: "Para Lupe — Pintura exterior y tinte para cerca — Lupe Garza · $6,000.00"`). `PORT=6743 deno task serve`, then `BASE_URL=http://localhost:6743 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/quote-email-job-name -- --no-check` → `✗ … en … expectation failed: the email heading carries the customer tail: "Exterior Painting And Fence Staining — Maria Lopez"`, `✗ … es … expectation failed: the email heading carries the customer tail: "Pintura exterior y tinte para cerca — Lupe Garza"`. The plain `shots run` without BASE_URL answered `backend_unreachable` on sign-in twice: parallel runs were sharing the session's shots serve at load ~36. Use your own serve + BASE_URL.
**Fix (fix/q3-q3-4):** `send-paperwork-email/mod.ts` gets two helpers, `quoteJobName` (`jobNameByLang[lang] ?? jobName`, verbatim) and `quoteSummaryLabel` (REQ-591's `quoteSummary(q, lang)` without a leading "Quote:" and with `summaryWithoutCustomerTail` from REQ-1046). `renderQuoteSubject` and `renderQuoteHtml` share them, so the first send, the revision ("Version 2") and the resend all name the job one way. The hero is the job name as typed and is not title-cased again. Only the summary fallback goes through `titleCaseJobName`. The preheader reuses the hero ("For Maria — <job> · $total"). The invoice email's summary fallback (`renderInvoiceHtml`) drops the tail too. In `shared/quote-flow/email-format.ts`, English `titleCaseJobName` keeps a/an/and/at/but/by/for/in/nor/of/on/or/the/to/with lowercase after the first word.
**Tests amended (superseded by this AMENDMENT, not weakened):** `send-paperwork-email/int.test.ts`: (1) the XSS test now puts its hostile text in `jobName` as well as in `summary`, because the hero renders jobName and the escape must still be proven there; (2) REQ-720 checks sentence case on the `<h1>` (the derived Spanish job name) and no longer looks for the typed summary; (3) REQ-756 checks that the hero has no "— Ana Pérez" tail and never shows "ana pérez", in place of the tail it used to require. `preview-quote-send/int.test.ts` (REQ-591): an English or Spanish preview's hero is the job name in that language (">Faucet Repair</h1>", ">Reparación de grifo</h1>"), never the cached summary in title case ("Faucet And Interior Door Repair"). e2e `quote-email-job-name`: the /q check now compares case-blind. Spanish /q puts the job mid-sentence ("Acuerdo de pintura exterior y tinte para cerca para Lupe Garza"), where Spanish lowercases the first letter. The words match the email heading "Pintura exterior y tinte para cerca", so the case-sensitive check was wrong.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-4):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/domain/coordinators/send-paperwork-email/job-label.test.ts` → `ok | 8 passed | 0 failed`. `deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-quote src/agents/domain/coordinators/send-invoice <every other backend test importing send-paperwork-email>` → 1187 passed, 0 failed (after the amendments above). `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/email-i18n.test.ts unit/ux-job-name-es.test.ts unit/invoice-email-status-label.test.ts` → `679 suites passed, 6531 passed, 1 skipped`. `deno lint` and `deno check` on the touched modules are clean. `PORT=6911 KV_PATH=<scratch> deno task serve`, then `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> BASE_URL=http://localhost:6911 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/quote-email-job-name e2e/quote-email-deposit e2e/quote-email-wrap e2e/single-line-quote-email e2e/signed-email-job-name -- --no-check` → `8 pass · 0 fail`, with both REQ-1087 en/es stories ✓.

## REQ-1088 — Every stored service / customer address is tidy, mixed-case typing included (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-5, q3-6; amends REQ-1047)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issues, cycle 3: **q3-5** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION] "Stored quote service address is not tidied (no commas, lowercase)" — QA1 "2210 Burnet Rd Austin TX 78757", QA2 "1408 Elm St Austin TX 78702" / "455 Calle Oak, San Antonio TX 78210" printed as typed on the card, preview and /q; QA5's quote carried the customer record's raw "12 oak st, myrtle beach, sc 29577". **q3-6** [polish/BUG_POLISH] "Invoice service address not tidied" — QA3's /i INV-002 "4410 avenue h, austin tx 78751"; QA5's customer header, /i and email "45 palmetto dr, conway, SC 29526".
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** two gaps in REQ-1047. (1) `tidyServiceAddress` (shared/customer-address/mod.ts:109) only re-punctuates when `reformat = !/\p{Lu}/u.test(s) && !s.includes(",")`, so an address with any capital letter, or with a comma after the street only, gets no ", " before the city / state ("2210 Burnet Rd Austin TX 78757" unchanged; "4410 avenue h, austin tx 78751" → "4410 Avenue H, Austin TX 78751"). (2) It runs at one call site only (handle-chat-message's create_quote chain). The wizard's customer step (`applyServiceAddress`, handle-wizard-answer/mod.ts:786-797) copies the typed value or the customer's `address` onto the quote with only `.trim()`; the invoice store (`create` spreads `...input`, `update` merges the patch) and the customer store (`addressWrite`: `composeAddress` of trimmed parts, or a free-text `address` "as given") store addresses raw, and /i, the invoice email and the customer header print them as stored.
**Requirement:** a stored address — a quote's or invoice's `serviceAddress`, a customer's `address` (composed from parts or free text) — is tidy whichever writer supplied it: lower-case words title-cased, the 2-letter state upper case, ", " before the city and before a recognised state + ZIP decided by the address's structure, not its letter case (mixed-case and partly-comma'd input included). An already-formatted address ("12 Oak St, Austin, TX 78701") is stored unchanged.
**Note for the fixer:** jest/unit/q2-33-service-address-tidy.test.ts (REQ-1047) lists "4410 Avenue F Austin TX 78751" as "left exactly as it is" — that case encodes the old case-based rule and must become "4410 Avenue F, Austin, TX 78751" with the fix.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/q3-5-service-address-tidy.test.ts` ("REQ-1088 …": the three mixed-case tester strings, QA3's "4410 avenue h, austin tx 78751", QA5's two strings, formatted ones unchanged) · unit `backend/src/crm/domain/business/customer-address/test.ts` ("REQ-1088 … addressWrite": lowercase parts and a lowercase free-text address are tidy; formatted unchanged) · int `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-wizard-answer/int.test.ts` ("REQ-1088 q3-5 …": pick_existing with a lowercase customer address; create_new with a typed "2210 Burnet Rd Austin TX 78757") · int `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-chat-message/int.test.ts` ("REQ-1088 q3-5 …": typed "2210 Burnet Rd Austin TX 78757" stored with commas) · int `backend/src/paperwork/domain/data/invoice-store/int.test.ts` ("REQ-1088 q3-6 …": create/update with a lowercase serviceAddress; formatted unchanged) · int `backend/src/crm/domain/data/customer-store/int.test.ts` ("REQ-1088 …": create with lowercase parts, update with a lowercase free-text address) · e2e `e2e/address-tidy/address-tidy.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1088 (q3-5, q3-6) …": a customer with lowercase parts + New invoice with "4410 avenue h, austin tx 78751" typed → the signed-out /i shows "4410 Avenue H, Austin, TX 78751" and the bill-to "45 Palmetto Dr, Conway, SC 29526").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-5, at 0a71387e):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/q3-5-service-address-tidy.test.ts` → `Tests: 4 failed, 3 passed, 7 total` (`Expected: "2210 Burnet Rd, Austin, TX 78757" Received: "2210 Burnet Rd Austin TX 78757"`; `Expected: "455 Calle Oak, San Antonio, TX 78210" Received: "455 Calle Oak, San Antonio TX 78210"`; `Expected: "4410 Avenue H, Austin, TX 78751" Received: "4410 Avenue H, Austin TX 78751"`). `cd backend && deno test -A --no-check src/crm/domain/business/customer-address/test.ts --filter REQ-1088` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 2 failed` (`- 45 palmetto dr, conway, sc 29526 / + 45 Palmetto Dr, Conway, SC 29526`). `deno test -A --unstable-kv --no-check src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-wizard-answer/int.test.ts --filter REQ-1088` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 2 failed` (`- 12 oak st, myrtle beach, sc 29577 / + 12 Oak St, Myrtle Beach, SC 29577`; `- 2210 Burnet Rd Austin TX 78757 / + 2210 Burnet Rd, Austin, TX 78757`). `… handle-chat-message/int.test.ts --filter REQ-1088` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` (`- 2210 Burnet Rd Austin TX 78757`). `… invoice-store/int.test.ts customer-store/int.test.ts --filter REQ-1088` → `FAILED | 1 passed | 4 failed` (`- 4410 avenue h, austin tx 78751 / + 4410 Avenue H, Austin, TX 78751`; `- 45 palmetto dr, conway, SC 29526`; `- 12 oak st, myrtle beach, sc 29577`). e2e `SHOTS_DIR=<scratch> SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 BASE_URL=http://localhost:5763 shots run e2e/address-tidy -- --no-check` (against `PORT=5763 deno task serve`) → `✗ REQ-1088 … expectation failed: the service address on /i is tidy (got "SERVICE ADDRESS\n4410 avenue h, austin tx 78751")`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** (1) `shared/customer-address/mod.ts` `tidyServiceAddress` — the case-based `reformat` gate is gone; commas follow the structure: a recognised 2-letter state before a ZIP gets ", " before it whenever none is there, and the street's end (a street-type word, or a type-first "Avenue H") gets ", " when no comma separates the street from the city yet. Title-casing still leaves mixed / upper-case words alone, and a formatted address is unchanged. New `withTidyAddresses(write)` tidies a write's `serviceAddress` (and an invoice's `billTo.address`). (2) Tidy at the write boundary, not one caller: `QuoteStore` create / update / updateIf / setPending / publishRevision and `InvoiceStore` create / update / updateIf / setPending / publishRevision run the write through `withTidyAddresses`; `addressWrite` (backend/src/crm/domain/business/customer-address/mod.ts) title-cases each street / city part, upper-cases a 2-letter state, and tidies a free-text `address`, so the customer header, the invoice bill-to and a quote copied from the record are tidy too. (3) `handle-wizard-answer` `applyServiceAddress` tidies the typed value and the customer's address before its no-op compare, so the transcript line ("Customer: <name> — <address>") shows the stored address and a quote is not rewritten for nothing.
**Existing tests changed (they pinned the old case-based rule REQ-1088 replaces; the requirement says these addresses are stored with commas):** `jest/unit/q2-33-service-address-tidy.test.ts` ("4410 Avenue F Austin TX 78751" moved out of "left exactly as it is" → its formatted form "4410 Avenue F, Austin, TX 78751" stays there, plus a REQ-1088 case for the comma-less input); `handle-chat-message/int.test.ts` REQ-435 M4 and `lock-quote/int.test.ts` REQ-435 M4 (stored / card address "4410 Avenue F, Austin, TX 78751"); `handle-wizard-answer/int.test.ts` REQ-386 m17 and REQ-531 p8-pair6-a (transcript "88 Oak Hollow Dr, Austin, TX 78745"); `public-controller/e2e.test.ts` REQ-263 (PUT "412 Oak St, Austin TX 78704" stored "412 Oak St, Austin, TX 78704"). ## REQ-1091 — The chat payment step names the deposit / balance to the cent, like the preview and agreement (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-7; extends REQ-961 to REQ-491 + REQ-678)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-7** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "Chat payment step rounds deposit/balance to whole dollars while the preview and agreement show cents" — e.g. $6,450.50 at 30% read "$1,935 / $4,515" against $1,935.15 / $4,515.35 in the preview, and on $4,250.50 the 50% chip read "$2,125 now · $2,125 when done" (halves that do not add up to the total).
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** the split is exact (computePaymentSplit, e.g. 193515 / 451535 cents) but it is printed through two local helpers, `usd = c => "$" + Math.round(c / 100)`, that drop the cents: (1) `depositBalanceSubVars` (`front-end/lib/payment-split.ts` ~157) builds `{deposit}` / `{balance}` for the "When do you want to get paid?" option sub-line (`termsWizard.paymentTerms.depositBalance.subAmounts`), read by the backend wizard emitter `localizeOptions` (`backend/src/agents/domain/business/terms-wizard-spec/mod.ts`), the island's fallback picker and the stated-deposit prefill (`AsstChat.tsx`); (2) `depositChoices` (`shared/quote-flow/deposit-term.ts` ~106) has its own copy for the "How big a deposit?" chips (`asstChat.depositPick.chipSub`). Both predate REQ-961 (REQ-491 1f6b8eab, REQ-678 b209bdd4); REQ-961 moved the owner money screens to the cents rule but never touched these chat sub-lines, while `dollars()` in deposit-term.ts already applies it.
**Requirement:** the payment step's Deposit + balance sub-line and the deposit chips name the same deposit / balance the preview, agreement and invoices bill — to the cent unless the amount is whole (REQ-961): $4,250.50 at 20% → "$850.10 / $3,400.40", at 50% → "$2,125.25" + "$2,125.25"; whole amounts stay compact ("$90 / $360").
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/deposit-split-cents.test.ts` ("REQ-1091 …": `depositChoices(425050)` 50% → $2,125.25 / $2,125.25, 20% → $850.10 / $3,400.40, `depositChoices(45000)` → $90 / $360; `depositBalanceSubVars(645050, "Deposit 30% + balance")` → $1,935.15 / $4,515.35, `depositBalanceSubVars(512550)` → $1,025.10 / $4,100.40, `(45000)` → $90 / $360) · integration `backend/src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-wizard-answer/int.test.ts` ("REQ-1091 (LOOP-007 q3, q3-7) handle-wizard-answer: …": TransitionToTerms + HandleWizardAnswer on KV :memory:, a $5,125.50 quote, the payment_terms step's `deposit_bal` sub = "… · $1,025.10 / $4,100.40") · e2e `e2e/deposit-split-cents/deposit-split-cents.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1091 (LOOP-007 q3, q3-7): …": a locked $4,250.50 quote at the payment step in /assistant; the Deposit + balance sub reads $850.10 / $3,400.40, then the 50% chip $2,125.25 + $2,125.25 and the 20% chip $850.10 + $3,400.40 — the chip's surrounding copy is not pinned, q3-8 / REQ-1082 may change "now").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-7 at 0a71387e):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern deposit-split-cents` → `Tests: 4 failed, 2 passed, 6 total` (`+ "deposit": "$2,125"` vs `- "$2,125.25"`; `+ "$850"` / `+ "$3,400"`; `+ "$1,935"` / `+ "$4,515"`; `+ "$1,025"` / `+ "$4,100"`; the two whole-dollar pins pass); `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-wizard-answer/int.test.ts --filter REQ-1091` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` (`- … · $1,025 / $4,100` / `+ … · $1,025.10 / $4,100.40`); `BASE_URL=http://localhost:57311 shots run e2e/deposit-split-cents -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1091 … expectation failed: … "Deposit + balance 20% deposit due a week after signing, rest when done · $850 / $3,400" | … "50% $2,125 now · $2,125 when done" | … "20% $850 now · $3,400 when done"`.
**Fix:** `dollars()` in `shared/quote-flow/deposit-term.ts` is exported as `depositDollars` (the REQ-961 rule: "$500" whole, "$1,500.50" otherwise) and is now the one formatter for `depositChoices` (the "How big a deposit?" chips) and `front-end/lib/payment-split.ts` `depositBalanceSubVars` (the "When do you want to get paid?" sub-line, read by the backend wizard emitter `localizeOptions`, the island fallback picker and the stated-deposit prefill). Both local `usd = c => "$" + Math.round(c / 100)` helpers are gone; whole totals still read compact ("$90 / $360"). No test changed.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-7):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern deposit-split-cents` → `Tests: 6 passed`; whole jest unit lane → `Test Suites: 680 passed, 680 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6537 passed`; `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/agents/domain/coordinators/handle-wizard-answer/int.test.ts` → `ok | 53 passed | 0 failed`; neighbours (transition-to-terms/, handle-wizard-answer/, terms-wizard-spec, terms-prefill, terms-edit, wizard-progress, billing-actions, completion-schedule) → `ok | 170 passed | 0 failed`; `deno lint` + `deno check` on both touched files green; `BASE_URL=http://localhost:57521 shots run e2e/deposit-pct-picker e2e/deposit-prefill-from-message e2e/deposit-split-cents -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-678 … ✓ REQ-936 … ✓ REQ-1091 … 3 pass · 0 fail`.

## REQ-1082 — AMENDMENT of REQ-1048: the "How big a deposit?" chips say the deposit is due a week after signing, never "now" (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-8)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-8** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "'How big a deposit?' step says the deposit is due 'now'; the agreement says a week after signing" — the payment step's "Deposit + balance" option reads "20% deposit due a week after signing, rest when done", the next step's chip reads "20% $850 now · $3,400 when done", and email 005 says "Vence una semana tras firmar".
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** REQ-1048 (q2-32) reworded the deposit timing only on the payment-step sub-lines (`termsWizard.paymentTerms.depositBalance.*`, `asstChat.terms.payment.depositBalanceSub*`/`fiftyFiftySub`, `assistantDemo.wiz.opt*Sub`) and, for REQ-678's DepositAmountPicker, only the question. Each chip of that picker (`front-end/islands/AsstChat.tsx` DepositAmountPicker, fed by `shared/quote-flow/deposit-term.ts` `depositChoices()`) prints `asstChat.depositPick.chipSub`, which has read "{deposit} now · {balance} when done" / "{deposit} ahora · {balance} al terminar" since b209bdd4 (REQ-678). REQ-1048's guard (`front-end/lib/deposit-timing-wording.test.tsx`) checks a fixed key list that omits `depositPick.chipSub` and bans only "upfront"/"por adelantado", never "now"/"ahora", so the stale wording slipped through. The deposit invoice is due at signing + SIGNING_NET_DAYS (7).
**Requirement:** every deposit-size chip names the deposit with REQ-1048's net-7 deadline (en "… due a week after signing · {balance} when done", es "… a una semana de firmar · {balance} al terminar") and no deposit lang key says the deposit is due "now" / "ahora".
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/deposit-pick-chip-timing.test.tsx` ("REQ-1082 (LOOP-007 q3-8) [en|es]: each 'How big a deposit?' chip names the deposit as due a week after signing, never 'now'" — renders `asstChat.depositPick.chipSub` with `depositChoices(845050)` values; "REQ-1082 … [en|es]: no deposit lang key words the deposit as due 'now'/'ahora'" — scans every lang key containing "deposit") · int n/a — the chips are front-end copy only; the backend wizard emitter is already covered by REQ-1048's deposit-timing int test · e2e `e2e/deposit-pct-picker/deposit-pct-picker.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1082 (LOOP-007 q3-8): the 'How big a deposit?' chips say the deposit is due a week after signing, like the step before — never 'now'": /assistant, the "Deposit + balance" option says "a week after signing", then each `deposit-pick-{10,20,30,50}` chip must not match /\bnow\b/ and must say "a week after signing"). The REQ-678 story's exact "$4,350 now · $10,150 when done" check was loosened to pin only the dollars, so it no longer pins the stale wording.
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-8 at 0a71387e):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/deposit-pick-chip-timing.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 4 failed` (`10% chip = "$845 now · $7,605 when done"` …; `10% chip = "$845 ahora · $7,605 al terminar"` …; `asstChat.depositPick.chipSub = "{deposit} now · {balance} when done"`; `asstChat.depositPick.chipSub = "{deposit} ahora · {balance} al terminar"`); `BASE_URL=<own serve> shots run e2e/deposit-pct-picker -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1082 (LOOP-007 q3-8): … expectation failed: the 10% chip does not say the deposit is due "now": "10% $1,450 now · $13,050 when done"`.
**Fix:** `lang/en.json` `asstChat.depositPick.chipSub` "{deposit} now · {balance} when done" → "{deposit} due a week after signing · {balance} when done"; `lang/es.json` "{deposit} ahora · {balance} al terminar" → "{deposit} a una semana de firmar · {balance} al terminar" (REQ-1048's net-7 wording, same as the payment-step subs). This was the only "deposit" key in either dictionary that said "now"/"ahora". The new unit test scans every deposit key, which closes the hole in REQ-1048's fixed-key-list guard.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-8):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/deposit-pick-chip-timing.test.tsx lib/deposit-timing-wording.test.tsx` → `ok | 8 passed | 0 failed`; `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/deposit-pct-picker.test.ts` → `Test Suites: 679 passed, 679 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 6531 passed`; `PORT=59450 WT_GATE=1 deno task serve` + `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:59450 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/deposit-pct-picker -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-678 … 30% lands on the quote …` · `✓ REQ-1082 (LOOP-007 q3-8): the 'How big a deposit?' chips say the deposit is due a week after signing, like the step before — never 'now'` (2 pass · 0 fail); en/es both valid JSON, 6461 keys, last key still `comms.a2p.sys.house`.

## REQ-1086 — The /customers hero reads money owed to the cent (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-9; extends REQ-961 + REQ-1072)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-9** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "/customers hero rounds money owed to whole dollars" — the hero said "$2,563 currently owed to you" while the board card on the same screen said $2,562.75 and the sidebar "Owes $1,935.15" sat next to a hero "$1,935".
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** `front-end/components/ClientsSections.tsx` `ClientsHero` formats the owed total with its own `owedTotal.toLocaleString("en-US", { maximumFractionDigits: 0 })` (lines 30-32, from 49a5d6ca, never changed) and renders `$${owedFmt}` before `clientsHero.owed` (line 96), so the amount is always rounded to whole dollars, in EN and ES alike. The input is exact (`ClientsPage.tsx` passes `summary.owedCents / 100`). The REQ-961 and REQ-1072 fixes moved the /invoices hero, the money bar, /payments, the CustomerWorkspace KPIs and clients-display `dollars()` to `fmtMoneyTotal`, but never this hero, and no test read it.
**Requirement:** the /customers hero's "currently owed to you" / "que te deben actualmente" amount follows REQ-961's `fmtMoneyTotal` rule: to the cent ("$2,562.75", "$690.75"), whole dollars only when the total is whole ("$2,400"), and it agrees with the board card and the sidebar on the same screen, in en and es.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/components/ClientsSections.cents.test.tsx` ("REQ-1086 (LOOP-007 q3, q3-9): …": renders `ClientsHero` with 2562.75 / 1935.15 / 600.25 / 2400 in en and es and reads the `$` amount in `.ph2__sub`; a source pin that ClientsSections.tsx has no `maximumFractionDigits: 0`; the props carry both `owedTotal` and `owedCents`, so the fix may pass either) · integration n/a — the backend already returns exact `owedCents` · e2e `e2e/customer-money-cents/customer-money-cents.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1086 (LOOP-007 q3, q3-9) en: …" and "… es: …": a $1,190.75 invoice part-paid by $500; /customers hero, board card `.ccard2__bal-val` and sidebar `nav-customer-line` are read in one evaluate and must all be "$690.75").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-9 at 0a71387e):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check components/ClientsSections.cents.test.tsx` → `FAILED | 2 passed | 5 failed` (`the hero rounds money owed to whole dollars (en): got "$2,563"`, same for es; `- $1,935 + $1,935.15`; `ClientsSections.tsx still rounds money with maximumFractionDigits: 0`; the whole-dollar $2,400 cases pass). `BASE_URL=<pre-warmed serve> SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/customer-money-cents -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1086 … en … hero line: "0 signed jobs in flight · $691 currently owed to you · …" — expected {"hero":"$690.75","card":"$690.75","sidebar":"$690.75"}, got {"hero":"$691","card":"$690.75","sidebar":"$690.75"}` and `✗ REQ-1086 … es … "$691 que te deben actualmente" … got {"hero":"$691",…}`. (Shots' own serve started the backend too slowly under host load, ~70 s, so the stories ran against a pre-warmed `PORT=52917 deno task serve`.)
**Fix:** `ClientsHero` takes `owedCents` (exact cents) instead of `owedTotal` dollars and renders `fmtMoneyTotal(owedCents)` from `front-end/lib/format.ts` (which carries its own `$`, so the literal `$` in the JSX is gone); `front-end/islands/ClientsPage.tsx` passes `owedCents={summary.owedCents}` straight from the backend summary, so no float division or re-rounding happens before the formatter. The `maximumFractionDigits: 0` call is removed. ES shares the en-US grouping with the card, as before.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-9):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check components/ClientsSections.cents.test.tsx` → `ok | 7 passed | 0 failed`. `PORT=61437 KV_PATH=<fresh> deno task serve` then `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:61437 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=…/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/customer-money-cents -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1072 q2-61 …`, `✓ REQ-1086 (LOOP-007 q3, q3-9) en …`, `✓ REQ-1086 (LOOP-007 q3, q3-9) es …` — `3 pass · 0 fail`. Neighbours: `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit …` → `Test Suites: 679 passed, 679 total; Tests: 6531 passed, 1 skipped`; `cd front-end && deno lint components/ClientsSections.tsx islands/ClientsPage.tsx components/ClientsSections.cents.test.tsx` → `Checked 3 files`; `deno check components/ClientsSections.tsx islands/ClientsPage.tsx` → clean; `deno fmt` (stdin) leaves both files unchanged. ## REQ-1085 — EXTENSION of REQ-961 to /quotes: one quote's total is shown to the cent (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-10)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-10** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "/quotes 'Decided this month' rounds totals" — QA saw "$6,451" for a $6,450.50 quote and "$7,601" for Q-001's CO-inclusive $7,600.50, which read to the cent on /q, the agreement, the PDF and the detail panel.
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** `front-end/islands/QuotesPage.tsx` builds each card's `value` from `quoteCardValue(c)` (`front-end/lib/headline-counts.ts`: estimatedTotal + approvedChangeOrdersCents, exact cents) and track 03 "Decided this month" renders `DecidedRow`, which prints `{fmtMoney(q.value)}` (`front-end/components/QuotesSections.tsx` ~414). `fmtMoney` (`front-end/lib/format.ts`) is the KPI formatter: `Math.round(|cents| / 100)`, no cents, so 645050 → "$6,451". format.ts's own rule says one document's amount is always `fmtMoneyExact`. The line dates from 49a5d6ca (2026-05-27), before the fmtMoney/fmtMoneyExact split; REQ-961 moved /invoices, the money bar and /payments but never touched /quotes. ## REQ-1093 — The dashboard shows one document's amount to the cent and Spanish dates day-first; a scheduled installment is "sent", not "se cobra" (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-11 + q3-12; amends REQ-473 + REQ-961)

**Requirement (Raphael's words):** "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green."
**Issues:** q3-11 [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION] Dashboard money bar "Próximo: $2,563 se cobra el dic 3": rounded, English date order, and "se cobra" for a scheduled send · q3-12 [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION] Dashboard "Trabajos activos" card: "$5,126" and "Vence nov 26" in Spanish.
**Root cause:** `front-end/islands/DashboardPage.tsx` formats these two places itself instead of using the shared formatters. The REQ-473 upcoming line passes `Math.round(upcomingBill.amountCents / 100).toLocaleString("en-US")` into `outstanding.upcoming` (whose copy adds its own `$`), so 256275 cents reads "$2,563", and its date comes from the island's local `fmtDay`, which hand-glues `${shortMonth} ${day}` for every language ("dic 3"). `jobToRow` builds the Active jobs amount as `$${Math.round(total).toLocaleString()}` (512550 → "$5,126"), and `fmtDueRel`'s >7-day branch uses the same month-first glue ("Vence nov 26"). REQ-961 / REQ-1072 moved the money bar's buckets, rows and headline to `fmtMoneyExact` / `fmtMoneyTotal` but never touched these lines; the rest of the page uses the language-aware `shortDate` ("26 nov"). Separately, `lang/es.json` `outstanding.upcoming` translates "bills" as "se cobra" (is charged), while /invoices and the assistant call the same installment "programada … te recordamos enviarla".
**Tests:**
- unit `front-end/lib/dashboard-cents-dates.test.tsx` (deno test; mounts DashboardPage live with `api.get` stubbed and reads the `upcoming` prop handed to `<MoneyBar>` and the `jobs` rows handed to `<ActiveJobs>`): "REQ-1093 … q3-11" es upcoming contains "$2,562.75" and "3 dic", not "$2,563" / "dic 3" / "se cobra"; en upcoming "$2,562.75" + "Dec 3"; es `outstanding.upcoming` copy uses the send wording and neither language's copy adds its own "$"; "REQ-1093 … q3-12" es job row `{amount:"$5,125.50", due:"Vence <d> <mon>"}`, en `{amount:"$5,125.50", due:"Due <Mon> <d>"}`; source check: no `Math.round(total)` / `Math.round(upcomingBill.amountCents` left in DashboardPage.tsx.
- integration: n/a — the backend already returns exact cents (`totalCents` 512550, invoice `amount` 256275); this is front-end formatting and copy only.
- e2e `e2e/dashboard-cents-dates/dashboard-cents-dates.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1093 (LOOP-007 q3, q3-11 + q3-12) …"): seeds a signed 50/50 $5,125.50 job (deposit paid, $2,562.75 balance scheduled 14 days out), opens /dashboard?lang=es and reads `[data-cy=money-upcoming]` and the first `.job` row in one evaluate.

**Fix (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-11):** `front-end/islands/DashboardPage.tsx` uses the shared formatters. `jobToRow` amount and the upcoming line's `amt` are `fmtMoneyTotal(cents)` (to the cent unless whole, REQ-961, so "$5,125.50" / "$2,562.75" and a whole "$925" stays compact). The island's hand-glued `${shortMonth} ${day}` (in `fmtDueRel`'s >7-day branch, `fmtDay` and `fmtRel`'s >7-day branch) is replaced by `dayOf()`, which feeds the local calendar day to the shared `shortDate(iso, lang, false)`, giving "Nov 26" in en and "26 nov" in es. `outstanding.upcoming` no longer adds its own "$": en "Upcoming: {amt} bills {date}", es "Próximo: {amt}, te recordamos enviarla el {date}" (the /invoices scheduled-send wording, not "se cobra").

## REQ-1083 — Spanish /invoices at-risk line agrees with its count in Spanish word order (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-15; extends REQ-986)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-15** [minor/BUG_POLISH], cycle 3: "Spanish /invoices hero grammar: 'en 1 vencidas factura'" — with one overdue invoice the hero reads "⚠ $225 en riesgo en 1 vencidas factura."
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** `front-end/islands/InvoicesPage.tsx` (the `[data-cy=forecast-at-risk]` paragraph, ~1805-1812) pieces the line together in English word order: `{money} {invoicesPage.atRisk.across} {n} {invoicesPage.atRisk.overdue} {invoicesPage.unitInvoice.one|other}`. Spanish needs noun then adjective ("1 factura vencida"), and `invoicesPage.atRisk.overdue` is one fixed feminine-plural string "vencidas" with no one/other forms, so n=1 gives "1 vencidas factura" and n=2 "2 vencidas facturas". Never "vencidas factura".
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/es-invoices-at-risk-q3-15.test.ts` ("REQ-1083 …": es/en one+other forms of `invoicesPage.atRisk.line`; the island's at-risk block uses `tnFor(lang, "invoicesPage.atRisk.line"` and no longer uses `atRisk.overdue` / `unitInvoice`) · int n/a — no backend or API change; the forecast's atRisk list is correct · e2e `e2e/es-invoices-at-risk/es-invoices-at-risk.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1083 (LOOP-007 q3-15): …": Spanish user, one overdue sent invoice → `[data-cy=forecast-at-risk]` reads "en riesgo en 1 factura vencida"; a second → "en riesgo en 2 facturas vencidas").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-15 at 0a71387e):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern es-invoices-at-risk-q3-15` → `Tests: 5 failed, 5 total` (`missing es key invoicesPage.atRisk.line.one`; `Expected pattern: /tnFor\(\s*lang,\s*"invoicesPage\.atRisk\.line"/`; `Expected pattern: not /invoicesPage\.atRisk\.overdue/`); `BASE_URL=<own serve on high ports> shots run e2e/es-invoices-at-risk -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1083 … expectation failed: one overdue invoice: noun then singular adjective — expected "en riesgo en 1 factura vencida", got "en riesgo en 1 vencidas factura"`. (shots' own serve answered on the frontend before the backend booted under host load → `backend_unreachable`; ran against a pre-started `PORT=61873 deno task serve` instead.)
**Fix:** `lang/en.json` + `lang/es.json` replace `invoicesPage.atRisk.across` / `invoicesPage.atRisk.overdue` (no other user outside the excluded ui-breakdown copies) with `invoicesPage.atRisk.line.one/.other` (en "at risk across {n} overdue invoice(s)", es "en riesgo en {n} factura vencida" / "en riesgo en {n} facturas vencidas"), same position, key sets still identical, `comms.a2p.sys.house` still last. `front-end/islands/InvoicesPage.tsx` renders the `[data-cy=forecast-at-risk]` line as `⚠ <strong>{money}</strong> {tnFor(lang, "invoicesPage.atRisk.line", forecast!.atRisk.length)}.` — the language owns the word order and agreement, as REQ-986 did for `sub.pastDue`.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-15):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern es-invoices-at-risk-q3-15` → `Tests: 5 passed, 5 total`; neighbours `npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'es-invoices-at-risk-q3-15|es-invoices-grammar|i18n|lang|invoice|req-920|a2p|forecast|headline'` → `Test Suites: 89 passed, 89 total · Tests: 920 passed, 920 total`; `cd front-end && deno lint islands/InvoicesPage.tsx` → `Checked 1 file`; `deno check islands/InvoicesPage.tsx` → clean; `deno fmt --ext tsx/json -` on the touched files → no diff. ## REQ-1081 — LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-16: the Record-a-payment picker shows the balance still owed, to the cent (cites REQ-961)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-16** [minor/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "Record-a-payment picker rounds the balance" — /payments → Record a payment listed "INV-002 · Greg Pruitt · $1,001" while the Amount field under it pre-filled "1000.5".
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** the "Which invoice?" option label is built by `recordOptionLabel` in `front-end/lib/payment-record-option.ts`, which fills `paymentsPage.record.optionLabel` ("{doc} · {customer} · {amount}") with `fmtMoney(inv.amount ?? 0)`. `fmtMoney` (`front-end/lib/format.ts`) is the whole-dollar rollup formatter (`Math.round(Math.abs(cents) / 100)`), so 100050 cents reads "$1,001", and it prints the invoice's full total, not the balance. `PaymentReceivedForm` in the same modal pre-fills `(amountCents - paidCents) / 100` ("1000.5"), so the label and the field disagree, and on a part-paid invoice the label shows the total while the field shows what is owed. The line came in with 5a4bf12e (REQ-587); REQ-961 moved the other /payments single-amount sites to `fmtMoneyExact`/`fmtMoneyTotal` but did not cover this helper.
**Requirement:** each Record-a-payment option shows the invoice's balance still owed (amount − paidCents; the full amount when nothing is paid), to the cent ("$1,000.50", never "$1,001"), in en and es — the same figure the Amount field pre-fills.
**Tests:** unit `front-end/lib/payment-record-option-cents.test.ts` ("REQ-1081 q3-16 (en|es): …": `recordOptionLabel` on 100050 cents contains "$1,000.50" and not "$1,001"; with `paidCents: 50000` contains "$500.50" and neither "$1,000" nor "$1,001") · int n/a — the backend already returns exact cents (100050) and paidCents; the defect is front-end formatting only · e2e `e2e/record-option-cents/record-option-cents.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1081 q3-16: …": a $1,000.50 invoice, /payments → Record a payment → type "Greg"; the option reads "$1,000.50", not "$1,001", and its amount equals the Amount field; POST a $500 payment, reopen: the option reads "$500.50" and matches the field). The fixer must also update REQ-587's `front-end/lib/payment-record-option.test.tsx`, which pins "$450" for 45000 cents if the fix uses `fmtMoneyExact` ("$450.00").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-16 at 0a71387e):** `cd front-end && deno test -A --no-check lib/payment-record-option-cents.test.ts` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 4 failed` (`AssertionError: label rounds the cents: INV-002 · Greg Pruitt · $1,001`; `Expected actual: "INV-002 · Greg Pruitt · $1,001" to contain: "$500.50".`, en and es); `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:47316 shots run e2e/record-option-cents -- --no-check` (own `PORT=47316 deno task serve`, because shots' self-serve started the story before the backend answered: `backend_unreachable`) → `✗ REQ-1081 q3-16: … expectation failed: the option does not round the cents: "INV-001 — Deck repair · Greg Pruitt 5960603 · $1,001" (field "1000.5")`.
**Fix:** `front-end/lib/payment-record-option.ts` — `recordOptionLabel` now formats `recordBalanceCents(inv)` (amount − paidCents; the full amount when nothing is left) with `fmtMoneyExact`, and `RecordOptionInvoice` carries `paidCents` (PaymentsPage already passes the whole invoice). `PaymentReceivedForm`'s Amount pre-fill uses the same `recordBalanceCents`, so the label and the field can no longer drift apart.
