## REQ-1160 — The worker greeting line names today, not the viewed day; Salir returns the screen to today (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-92 + q3-100)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issues, cycle 3: **q3-92** [minor/BUG_POLISH] "Worker header date follows the viewed day, not today" (tap Mañana on Thu 19 Nov: under "Hola, Luis Ortega" the date becomes "Vie 20 de nov", repeating "Viendo Vie 20 de nov"); **q3-100** [polish/BUG_POLISH] "Worker sign-in screen after logout shows the last viewed day, not today" (/worker?date=2026-11-20 → Salir → "Mis tareas Vie 20 de nov").
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** in `front-end/islands/WorkerScreen.tsx`, `const dayLine = () => (date ? fmtDayLabel(date, lang) : "")` formats `date`, the viewed day (?date=, pickDay), not `today`, the business's day (REQ-940 state). Both greeting blocks render `<small>{dayLine()}</small>`: under "Hola, {name}" when signed in and under "Mis tareas" when signed out. This dates from fd52cfa2 (REQ-137..143, when the screen showed one day); REQ-194/REQ-528 later added a separate viewed-day label, and REQ-1065 (e10f3e81) only changed casing. And `logout()` resets me/tasks/open/drafts/deferring/lang but never `date`/`dateRef` nor the `?date=` that pickDay wrote with history.replaceState, so the sign-in card (and the next worker, via takeToday's early return, and a reload) stays on the stale day.
**Requirement:** the date line under the worker greeting always names today (the business's day), signed in or out; the "Viendo" label is what names the viewed day. Salir puts the screen back on today: `date` reset to today and `?date=` removed from the URL, so the next sign-in lands on Hoy.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/worker-header-today.test.ts` ("REQ-1160 …": evaluates WorkerScreen's `dayLine` initialiser against the real lib/field exports — viewing tomorrow/yesterday it must return `fmtDayLabel(today)`; `logout()` must reset `date`/`dateRef` to today and delete `date` from the URL via history.replaceState) · int n/a — front-end island only, no backend involvement · e2e `e2e/worker-header-today/worker-header-today.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1160 …": Spanish worker signs in, taps `w-day-next`; `.greet small` must equal the Hoy tab's label and differ from the Viendo label; Salir → the sign-in card's `.greet small` is today and the URL has no `date=`; signing in again lands on `w-day-today` selected).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-92 at 0a71387e):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern worker-header-today` → `Tests: 3 failed, 2 passed, 5 total` (`Expected: "Jue 19 de nov" Received: "Vie 20 de nov"`; `Expected: "Thu, Nov 19" Received: "Wed, Nov 18"`; logout body `Expected pattern: /setDate\(\s*todayRef\.current\s*\)|setDate\(\s*today\s*\)/`). `BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port> shots run e2e/worker-header-today e2e/worker-day-label-case -- --no-check` (own `PORT=<port> deno task serve`, because shots' own serve answered `backend_unreachable` before the backend booted) → `✗ REQ-1160 … expectation failed: q3-92: under 'Hola, Luis' the date stays today while viewing Mañana — expected "Jue 19 de nov", got "Vie 20 de nov"`; with the q3-92 asserts disabled locally the q3-100 step fails too: `expected "Jue 19 de nov", got "Vie 20 de nov"` on the sign-in card after Salir. REQ-1065's `worker-day-label-case` passes (✓).
**Fix:** `front-end/islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` — `dayLine` now formats `today || date` (today, the business's day; `date` only before /me answers), so both greeting `<small>` lines name today; `logout()` sets `dateRef.current`/`setDate` back to `todayRef.current` (when known) and deletes `date` from the URL with history.replaceState before `load` runs, so the sign-in card, a reload, and the next worker (takeToday no longer bails on a stale day) start on Today. The day strip and the "Viendo" label keep showing the viewed `date`. No test changed.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-92):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern worker-` → `Test Suites: 30 passed, 30 total · Tests: 159 passed, 159 total` (includes the 5 REQ-1160 tests). Full lane `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit` → `Test Suites: 680 passed, 680 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 6536 passed, 6537 total`. `cd front-end && deno lint islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` → `Checked 1 file`; `deno check islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` → ok; `deno fmt - --ext=tsx < islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` → no diff. e2e (own `PORT=61880 deno task serve`, fresh KV_PATH): `BASE_URL=http://localhost:61880 shots run e2e/worker-header-today e2e/worker-day-label-case -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1160 … · 49s`, `✓ REQ-1065 … · 14.4s`; neighbours `shots run e2e/worker-tomorrow e2e/worker-language e2e/worker-business-day` → `✓ REQ-362/528`, `✓ REQ-285`, `✓ REQ-416`, `✓ REQ-494`, `✓ REQ-593 (/worker cell mask)`, `✓ REQ-714`, `✓ REQ-940`.

## REQ-1161 — AMENDMENT of REQ-1065: the worker clock table's Day column uses the same day label as the rest of the worker screen (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-93)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-93** [polish/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "Worker clock table day label lowercase/reordered". On /worker's Reloj tab the shift table's Day column reads "jue 19" (es) / "19 Thu" (en). The header, the day tab and the "Viendo" line read "Jue 19 de nov" / "Thu, Nov 19".
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** `front-end/components/timeclock/WorkerClock.tsx` has its own private `fmtDayOf` (lines 30-35): `toLocaleDateString(locale, { weekday: "short", day: "numeric", timeZone })`, with no month and no capital. Without a month, ICU prints es-MX "jue 19" and en-US "19 Thu". The Day cell (`<td>{fmtDayOf(s.start, lang, timeZone)}</td>`, line 227) renders that helper. It dates from 61c8f68a (REQ-192); 57f7e87d (REQ-1038) only added `timeZone`. REQ-1065 (e10f3e81) added `fmtDayLabel` in `front-end/lib/field.ts` and moved WorkerScreen's header, day tabs and Viendo line onto it, but it never touched WorkerClock.
**Requirement:** the clock table's Day cell shows the REQ-1065 label for the punch's business day: es "Jue 19 de nov", en "Thu, Nov 19". This is the same text as the day tab for that day. It renders through a shared `front-end/lib/field.ts` formatter, called as `<name>(s.start, lang, timeZone)` and imported into WorkerClock, not through a private helper. REQ-1038 still holds: a 23:30 business-time punch stays on its business day.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/worker-clock-day-label.test.ts` ("REQ-1161 …": reads the Day cell's expression from WorkerClock.tsx and runs it for 2026-11-19T14:00Z and 2026-11-20T04:30Z in America/New_York. It expects "Jue 19 de nov" / "Thu, Nov 19" (= `fmtDayLabel("2026-11-19", lang)`) and a lib/field export imported by WorkerClock) · int n/a — front-end formatting only, no backend change · e2e `e2e/worker-clock-day-label/worker-clock-day-label.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1161 …", es and en: a worker signs in, opens the clock tab and clocks in. The first `[data-cy=clock-shift] td` must equal the `[data-cy=w-day-today] small` text).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-93 at 0a71387e):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern worker-clock-day-label` → `4 failed` (`Expected: "fmtDayOf → Jue 19 de nov" Received: "fmtDayOf → jue 19"`; `Expected: "fmtDayOf → Thu, Nov 19" Received: "fmtDayOf → 19 Thu"`; late punch `Expected: "Jue 19 de nov" Received: "jue 19"`; `Expected: "fmtDayOf exported from front-end/lib/field.ts: true" Received: "… false"`). `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<PORT> shots run e2e/worker-clock-day-label -- --no-check` (against a `PORT=<p> deno task serve`) → `✗ … in en … the clock table's day reads "Thu, Nov 19" style (got "19 Thu")`, `✗ … in es … the clock table's day starts with a capital (got "jue 19")`. Note: run shots against a live server through BASE_URL. Shots' own serve starts the stories before the backend finishes booting (~50 s under load), and every story then fails with `backend_unreachable`.
**Fix:** `front-end/lib/field.ts` gains `fmtPunchDayLabel(iso, lang, timeZone)`: it takes the instant's YYYY-MM-DD on the business's wall clock (`Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-CA", { timeZone })`, REQ-1038) and returns `fmtDayLabel` of that day (REQ-1065). WorkerClock imports it for the Day cell; its private `fmtDayOf` is deleted. Tests unchanged.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-93):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit --testPathPattern 'worker-clock-day-label|worker-day-label|field'` → `Test Suites: 33 passed, 33 total · Tests: 267 passed, 267 total` (the 4 REQ-1161 tests pass). `cd front-end && deno lint lib/field.ts components/timeclock/WorkerClock.tsx` → `Checked 2 files`; `deno check` same files → ok. `PORT=61871 deno task serve` + `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:61871 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=… shots run e2e/worker-clock-day-label -- --no-check` → `✓ … in en, the clock table's Day cell reads like the day tab` and `✓ … in es, …`; `2 pass · 0 fail`.

## REQ-1162 — AMENDMENT of REQ-421/REQ-1015: removing a worker never strands their upcoming tasks (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-94)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-94** [major/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "Removing a worker strands their upcoming tasks; the task shows no worker but 'ASSIGNED'" — add a one-off task for Maya Chen on Fri Nov 20, Remove access, confirm (no mention of the task), then /field/tasks for 2026-11-20 shows header "—", Worker "—", "ASSIGNED", "TO DO 1".
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** `FieldWorkersController.remove()` (`backend/src/field/entrypoints/field-controllers/mod.ts`) checks one dependency only — zones whose `region.workerId` is the worker (409 `worker_covers_zones`, REQ-151/REQ-421) — and then hard-deletes the worker without looking at `FieldTaskStore`. Open tasks keep a `workerId` pointing at a record that no longer exists; `FieldViews.names().worker(id)` (`backend/src/field/domain/coordinators/field-views/mod.ts`) falls back to "—" while the stored status stays "assigned", so one row says both "no worker" and "ASSIGNED". On the page, `askRemove()` in `front-end/islands/FieldWorkersPage.tsx` refuses only on `mine` (zones) and otherwise opens the bare "Remove {name}'s access?" confirm; nothing counts the worker's tasks. No commit ever added a task guard.
**Requirement:** DELETE /field/workers/:id refuses with 409 `worker_has_tasks` (detail `{ count, … }`) while the worker has upcoming assigned tasks, the same way it refuses for zones; the /field/workers row tells the owner about those tasks (en + es, `field.wk.err.hasTasks` with `{count}`) before access is removed; and a task whose worker no longer exists is flagged `unassigned` by the task view, never shown as Worker "—" with status ASSIGNED.
**Tests:** unit `backend/src/field/domain/coordinators/field-views/test.ts` ("REQ-1162 (q3-94) FieldViews.task …": a task with a removed worker is `unassigned: true`; a live worker's is not) and `jest/unit/field-worker-remove-tasks.test.ts` ("REQ-1162 …": `workerError` maps 409 `worker_has_tasks` → `field.wk.err.hasTasks` with `vars.count`; the key is worded in en and es with `{count}`) · int `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1162 (q3-94) DELETE /field/workers/:id refuses 409 worker_has_tasks …": Maya + a one-off for tomorrow → DELETE is 409 `worker_has_tasks`, detail.count 1, the task still reads "Maya Chen", no "—" + assigned; after deleting the task the worker DELETE is 200) · e2e `e2e/field-worker-errors/field-worker-errors.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1162 (LOOP-007 q3-94) …": Remove access on Maya with an upcoming task → the row names the task before anything is removed; afterwards the day has no Worker "—" + assigned task).

## REQ-1163 — AMENDMENT of REQ-1022: "Deferred to the day they are back" moves the work order to that day, and the owner and the worker see the same thing (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-96)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-96** [major/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "Marking a worker out 'Deferred' doesn't move their work order; owner and worker screens disagree". The owner marked Luis out on Fri Nov 20 with "Deferred to the day they are back". The Away row then read "WO-001 on Fri, Nov 20 still needs rescheduling — nobody has it", in red with no link. Luis's /worker?date=2026-11-20 still listed "Orden de trabajo WO-001 Replace pool pump seal" ("1 por hacer").
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** REQ-1022 (a0381888) resolves a work order's staff at read time with `woStaffOn` (`backend/src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/mod.ts`). For a defer absence it returns `{kind:"defer", to, staff: usual}`, where `to` is the assignee's next day back, and the two readers each drop part of that. On the worker side, `woDayStaff` collapses defer and skip to `{workerId}`, which loses both the kind and `to`. `worker-controller list()` then selects WOs by `scheduledFor === d` (`workOrdersOn`), so WO-001 stays on Luis's day off as a plain row. `WorkOrderDayRow` has no deferred or out field and `status` is "assigned", and the WorkerScreen WO card only knows `coverForName`. On the owner side, `awayOrders` (`backend/src/field/entrypoints/field-controllers/mod.ts`) sets `coverName` only for `kind==="cover"` and ignores `r.to`. `FieldWorkersPage.tsx` therefore renders every uncovered WO as `field.away.woResched` ("… nobody has it"), as plain red text with no link to /work-orders/:id. The owner is told nobody has the job, the worker is told he has it, and neither screen moves it to the day he is back.
**Requirement:** a work order whose assignee is out with disposition **defer** sits, at read time, on the assignee's first day back within MAX_DEFER_DAYS, flagged `deferredFrom` = its scheduled day, and is off the day he is out. The stored WO is not changed. With **skip**, or a defer that finds no day back, it stays on the day out and is flagged `out: "skip" | "defer"` on the worker's row and on the Away row (the worker sees that he is off and the office will reschedule it). `GET /field/absences` gives each WO its `deferredTo` (defer) or `out` (skip / no day). The Away row reads "{number} moves to {date}" for a defer, keeps "still needs rescheduling — nobody has it" only for a skip or a case with no cover and no day, and links each WO line to /work-orders/:id. Luis's /worker day back shows the WO with "deferred from {date}".
**Tests:**
- unit `backend/src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/test.ts` ("REQ-1163 (LOOP-007 q3-96) …"):
  - defer with Luis back on D+1: `onWorkOrderDay(wo, luis, D, people)` is false and D+1 is true; `woDayPlacement(wo, people)` → `{date: D+1, deferredFrom: D, staff.workerId: luis}`, and the stored date is untouched.
  - skip: `{date: D, out: "skip"}`, and the WO is not on D+1.
  - defer with no day back within 31 days: `{date: D, out: "defer"}`.
- integration `backend/src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/worker-view.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1163 (LOOP-007 q3-96) …", over HTTP on KV :memory:):
  - POST /field/absences `{workerId, from: D, to: D, disposition: "defer"}`. Luis's `/field/worker/tasks?date=D` then has no WO-001, and `?date=D+1` has it with `deferredFrom: D`. The GET /field/absences row's `workOrders[0].deferredTo` is D+1, with no `coverName`. GET /work-orders/:id still shows `scheduledFor` D.
  - skip: the row on D has `out: "skip"`, and the Away row's WO has `out: "skip"`.
- e2e `e2e/work-order-absence-defer/work-order-absence-defer.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1163 (LOOP-007 q3-96): …"): Mark out through the /field/workers dialog with `away-disp-defer`. `away-row-wo` does not say "nobody has it", does say "moves to", and links to `/work-orders/<id>`. Luis's /worker?date=D does not list the job, and /worker?date=D+1 lists it with "deferred from".
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-96 at 0a71387e):**
- `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/test.ts` → `FAILED | 7 passed | 3 failed`. It reports "Luis is off on D and the owner picked 'Deferred to the day they are back': WO-001 is not on his day D … - true + false", and `woDayPlacement` is `- undefined + function` (not exported).
- `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/worker-view.int.test.ts` → `FAILED | 3 passed | 2 failed`. It reports "Luis is off on 2026-11-22 and his work is deferred: WO-001 is not on his /worker day D … - 1 + 0", and "the worker's row is flagged … - undefined + "skip"".
- e2e, run with a manual `PORT=<random> deno task serve` and `BASE_URL=… shots run e2e/work-order-absence-defer -- --no-check`, because shots' own serve only waits for the front end and the story hit `backend_unreachable` → `✗ REQ-1163 … expectation failed: the Away row does not say nobody has WO-001 (got "WO-001 on Sun, Nov 22 still needs rescheduling — nobody has it") — expected false, got true`.
**Fix (2026-11-19):** (1) `backend/src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/mod.ts` — new `woDayPlacement(wo, people)` → `{date, staff, deferredFrom?, out?}` built on `woStaffOn`: a defer with a day back places the WO on that day with the assignee and `deferredFrom` = its scheduled day; a skip or a defer with no day back keeps it on the scheduled day flagged `out`; an uncovered cover keeps `staff: null`. `onWorkOrderDay` (with people) and the new `workOrdersPlacedOn(rows, date, people)` follow the placement; `workOrderRow` takes the placement and carries `date`, `deferredFrom`, `out` (new optional fields on `WorkOrderDayRow`). (2) `worker-controller list()` selects WOs by placed day (`workOrdersPlacedOn`), not `scheduledFor === d`. (3) `field-controllers awayOrders` returns `deferredTo` (defer with a day) or `out` (skip / defer with no day). (4) `FieldWorkersPage.tsx` — each `away-row-wo` line is an `<a href="/work-orders/:id">`; a `deferredTo` line reads the new `field.away.woDefer` ("{number} on {date} moves to {to}, the day they are back", en + es), not red; `woResched` stays only for skip / uncovered / no day. (5) `WorkerScreen.tsx` WO card shows `field.tk.deferredFrom` ("deferred from {date}") on the day back, and `worker.woOffDay` ("You're off this day — the office will reschedule it") on an `out` row; `isLive` and `lib/worker-today.ts workerDayCounts` leave `out` rows off the to-do count (the card still draws). (6) /work-orders + the WO page: the Field coordinator adds `assigneeDeferredTo` for a defer with a day back; `lib/work-order-assignee.ts assigneeLabel(wo, t, fmt?)` reads the new `workOrders.assignee.deferred` ("{name} is out that day — moved to {date}, the day they are back"), not in danger red. The stored WO is never changed. No REQ-1163 test was changed; added jest cases `jest/unit/work-order-assignee.test.ts` ("REQ-1163 (q3-96) deferred with a day back …") and `jest/unit/worker-deferred-day.test.ts` ("REQ-1163 (q3-96): a work order flagged `out` …").
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19):**
- `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/domain/business/work-order-day/test.ts` → `ok | 10 passed | 0 failed`.
- `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/paperwork/entrypoints/work-order-controller/worker-view.int.test.ts` → `ok | 5 passed | 0 failed`.
- e2e: `PORT=6731 KV_PATH=<scratch>/kv.sqlite3 deno task serve` (backend 6732 `/me` → 401), then `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:6731 SHOTS_PLAYWRIGHT=~/Library/Caches/deno/npm/registry.npmjs.org/playwright-core/1.64.1 shots run e2e/work-order-absence-defer -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1163 (LOOP-007 q3-96): Luis marked out on D with 'Deferred to the day they are back' — … · 134.1s` (the same run also picked up unrelated field/HR stories, several "did not finish" under heavy host load from parallel agents; none reads the touched UI).

## REQ-1166 — AMENDMENT of REQ-157: untouched day picks follow the typed First visit date (LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-97)
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-97** [major/BUG_CONTRADICTION], cycle 3: "Monthly repeat visit uses today's day of month, not the typed first visit date" — New repeat visit opened on 2026-11-19, First visit typed 2026-12-01, Monthly: the card reads "Monthly · day 19" and the first visit is 2026-12-19, 18 days late, with no warning.
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** the New repeat visit form seeds its picks from TODAY when it opens (`blankForm()` in `front-end/islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx`: `days: [weekdayOf(today)]` from REQ-139 fd52cfa2, `daysOfMonth: [monthDayOf(today)]` from REQ-157 9be8ffd4, `month: monthOf(today)` from REQ-787). Typing a First visit runs `onStartDate(v)`, which only re-derives a pick list when it is EMPTY (`f.daysOfMonth.length ? f.daysOfMonth : [monthDayOf(v)]`); the auto-filled list is never empty, so today's day survives. Submit sends `daysOfMonth: [19]`, and the backend's `monthDaysOf()` (`backend/src/field/domain/business/schedule/mod.ts`) rightly prefers explicit picks over the start date, so `isDue` is false on 12-01 and true on 12-19. The weekly cadence has the same flaw (days stays today's weekday) and annual keeps today's month.
**Requirement:** picks the user has not touched follow the typed First visit date — weekday, day of month and (annual) month; picks the user chose by hand survive a First visit change.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/subs-start-date-days.test.ts` ("REQ-1166 …": blank form seeded 2026-11-19 → `withStartDate(…, "2026-12-01")` gives daysOfMonth [1], days [2]; annual follows the typed month; hand picks [15, 31] survive). The reducer was pulled verbatim (no behaviour change) out of the island into `front-end/lib/subs-start-date.ts` (`seedPicks`, `withStartDate`, `monthDayOf`, `monthOf`, `weekdayOf`) so the unit test runs the island's real code · integration n/a — the backend does what it is sent (explicit daysOfMonth wins by design); the defect is in the form · e2e `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1166 (LOOP-007 q3-97, REQ-157 amendment): …": New repeat visit, type First visit = the 1st of next month (2nd when today is the 1st), pick Monthly → only that day's `subs-dom-day` chip is on; the saved card reads "Monthly · day N"; GET /api/field/subscriptions carries that startDate and daysOfMonth [N]).
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-97 at 0a71387e):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/subs-start-date-days.test.ts` → `Tests: 2 failed` (`expect(f.daysOfMonth).toEqual([1])` received `[19]`; `expect(f.month).toBe(3)` received `11`); the hand-picks test passes. `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:47391 shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check --filter REQ-1166` → `✗ REQ-1166 … expectation failed: the typed First visit's day (2026-12-01) is the one on, not today's (19) — expected "1", got "19"`. The extraction left REQ-157's story green (`✓ REQ-157: … Monthly · days 15, 31 · 3.6s`).
**Fix (2026-11-19):** `front-end/lib/subs-start-date.ts` — the picks carry `daysTouched` / `domTouched`; `seedPicks()` starts them false and `withStartDate()` re-derives untouched picks from the typed date (`days = [weekdayOf(v)]`, `daysOfMonth = [monthDayOf(v)]`, `month = monthOf(v)`), keeps touched ones (an emptied list is still refilled from the date). `front-end/islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx` — `toggleDay` sets `daysTouched`, `toggleMonthDay` / `onMonth` set `domTouched`, and `formFor()` (Edit) marks a saved visit's explicit `days` / `daysOfMonth` / `month` as touched so editing the First visit never rewrites the owner's saved picks. Submit is unchanged (it sends only the schedule fields). No test was changed.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-97):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/subs-start-date-days.test.ts` (runs the whole unit lane) → `PASS unit unit/subs-start-date-days.test.ts` · `Test Suites: 680 passed, 680 total; Tests: 1 skipped, 6534 passed, 6535 total`. e2e on a worktree serve (`PORT=48713 deno task serve`): `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:48713 SHOTS_JOBS=1 shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check --filter REQ-1166` → `✓ REQ-1166 (LOOP-007 q3-97, REQ-157 amendment): … · 163.8s`; neighbours `--filter "/REQ-(787|788|1004|1013|1014|157):/"` → `ok | 5 passed | 0 failed` (✓ REQ-157, REQ-787, REQ-1013, REQ-1014; REQ-788 re-run alone `ok | 1 passed` after a shared-evidence-dir race with a parallel run). `cd front-end && deno lint lib/subs-start-date.ts islands/FieldSubscriptionsPage.tsx` → `Checked 2 files`; `deno check` same files → clean; `deno fmt -` on both → unchanged.

## REQ-1165 — LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-98: a removed worker's sign-in says the access was removed, and the bad-sign-in copy names the cell
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-98** [minor/BUG_POLISH], cycle 3: "Removed worker sign-in shows only 'Trabajador o PIN incorrecto.'" — the owner removed Maya Chen (Quitar acceso); she signed in on /worker with her right cell 8435551234 and PIN 1111 and read "Trabajador o PIN incorrecto.", though the field is "Tu celular".
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** Remove access (`DELETE /field/workers/:id`, `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field-controllers/mod.ts` `remove`) hard-deletes the worker; `OwnedStore.delete` (`backend/src/field/domain/data/field-stores/mod.ts`) also drops `["field_worker_by_phone", phone]` and leaves no tombstone. `POST /field/worker/login` (`backend/src/field/entrypoints/worker-controller/mod.ts`) gets null from `findByPhone` and sends the same 401 "wrong cell or PIN" (no code) that a typo gets. `front-end/islands/WorkerScreen.tsx` `login()` maps every 401 to `worker.bad`, whose copy (unchanged since fd52cfa2, REQ-137..143) is "Trabajador o PIN incorrecto." / "Wrong worker or PIN." while the form's field is `worker.cell` "Tu celular" / "Your cell".
**Requirement:** a wrong sign-in reads "Celular o PIN incorrecto." / "Wrong cell or PIN." A worker whose access was removed, signing in with that cell and the PIN they had, is answered 403 code `worker_removed` and reads `worker.removed` "Tu acceso fue quitado. Habla con tu oficina." / "Your access was removed. Ask your office."; the same cell with any other PIN stays a plain 401 (it never reveals the number belonged to a worker); once the cell is given to a new worker, that worker signs in (200) and the old PIN is plain 401.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/worker-signin-removed.test.ts` ("REQ-1165 …": en/es `worker.bad` name the cell; `worker.removed` en/es; `WorkerScreen.tsx` `login()` maps 403 `worker_removed` → `t("worker.removed")` before the 401 → `worker.bad`) · int `backend/src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts` ("REQ-1165 (LOOP-007 q3, q3-98) …": create, DELETE, login right PIN → 403 `worker_removed` and no cookie; wrong PIN → 401; re-create on the cell → login 200; old PIN → 401) · e2e `e2e/field-worker-errors/field-worker-errors.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1165 (LOOP-007 q3-98) …": the owner removes the worker through Remove access → Confirm on /field/workers; on /worker?lang=es a wrong PIN reads "Celular o PIN incorrecto.", the right cell + PIN reads "Tu acceso fue quitado. Habla con tu oficina.").
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-98 at 0a71387e):** `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts --filter REQ-1165` → `FAILED | 0 passed | 1 failed` (`the removed worker is told the access was removed, not "wrong cell or PIN" ({"status":401,"name":"FieldError","message":"wrong cell or PIN"})`, `- 401, - undefined / + 403, + "worker_removed"`); `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/worker-signin-removed.test.ts` → 3 failed (`Expected: "Wrong cell or PIN." Received: "Wrong worker or PIN."`; `Expected: "Your access was removed. Ask your office." Received: undefined`; `Expected pattern: /worker_removed/`); `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:61411 shots run e2e/field-worker-errors -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1165 … expectation failed: a wrong PIN names the cell, not a 'Trabajador' — expected "Celular o PIN incorrecto.", got "Trabajador o PIN incorrecto."` (REQ-421/1015/1062 neighbours ✓).
**Fix (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-98):** Remove access now goes through `FieldWorkerStore.remove` (`backend/src/field/domain/data/field-stores/mod.ts`). Before the hard delete it writes a tombstone `["field_worker_removed_by_phone", phone] → { userId, pinHash, removedAt }`. Only a SHA-256 of phone+PIN is stored, and the value carries `userId`, so the account wipe removes it. `POST /field/worker/login` (`worker-controller/mod.ts`) returns 403 `worker_removed` only when no live worker holds the cell AND the PIN matches the tombstone; any other PIN stays the plain 401. `POST /field/workers` calls `clearRemoved(phone)` when a cell is reused. `WorkerScreen.tsx` `login()` maps 403 `worker_removed` to `t("worker.removed")` before the 401 → `worker.bad` branch. In lang en/es, `worker.bad` is now "Wrong cell or PIN." / "Celular o PIN incorrecto.", and the new `worker.removed` key (placed right after it) reads "Your access was removed. Ask your office." / "Tu acceso fue quitado. Habla con tu oficina.". No test assertion was changed.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-98):** `cd jest && npx jest --selectProjects unit unit/worker-signin-removed.test.ts` (it ran the whole unit lane) → `Test Suites: 680 passed, 680 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 6534 passed, 6535 total`. `cd backend && deno test -A --unstable-kv src/field/entrypoints/field.int.test.ts --filter REQ-1165` → `ok | 1 passed | 0 failed | 40 filtered out`. In the full `field.int.test.ts` run, 40 passed and 1 (REQ-842) failed with `AddrInUse`, a port collision with parallel agents' servers; REQ-842 re-run alone → `ok | 1 passed`. Neighbours (business-day, worker-ssr-lang, field-notices customer-language, worker-welcome, foreman-kinds, multi-day-job, timeclock, hr, work-order worker-view int tests) → `ok | 29 passed | 0 failed`. `PORT=61431 deno task serve` + `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:61431 shots run e2e/field-worker-errors -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1165 (LOOP-007 q3-98): a removed worker signing in on /worker in Spanish is told the access was removed; a wrong PIN reads 'Celular o PIN incorrecto.' · 155.2s` (REQ-1015 ✓, REQ-1062 ✓). Lint, check and fmt are clean on every touched file (`deno lint`/`deno check` in front-end and backend; `deno fmt --check -` via stdin).

## REQ-1167 — LOOP-007 cycle 3, q3-99: the owner Tasks page in Spanish capitalises its day header and counts with plural labels
**Source:** Raphael (LOOP-007): "test every single aspect of this application … one Opus agent per issue to do root cause analysis, then one to write the test, then one to fix it and make it green". QA issue **q3-99** [polish/BUG_POLISH], cycle 3: "Owner Tasks page in Spanish: lowercase day header and mismatched singular/plural counters" — /field/tasks?lang=es showed "jue 19 de nov" and "COMPLETADA 1" next to "PENDIENTES 0".
**Root cause (at 0a71387e):** two causes on one row. (1) `front-end/islands/FieldTasksPage.tsx` renders the summary row's day header (`[data-cy=tk-summary]`) with plain `fmtDay(date, lang)`, whose es-MX `toLocaleDateString` output is lowercase ("jue 19 de nov"); REQ-1065 added `fmtDayLabel` (capitalised standalone day label, `front-end/lib/field.ts`) but switched only WorkerScreen to it. (2) The summary chips reuse the single task's status keys: `field.tk.done` is the singular "Completada" (written for the per-task status chip) while `field.tk.toDo` is the plural "Pendientes" (REQ-284), and `field.tk.skipped` is the singular "No realizada"; the row prints "{label} {n}" with no plural handling, so it reads "Completada 1 · Pendientes 0".
**Requirement:** on the owner Tasks page the summary row's day is a capitalised standalone label (`fmtDayLabel`, "Jue 19 de nov" in Spanish), and the summary counters are plural labels before a number, from their own count keys — es "Completadas {n}", "Pendientes {n}", "No realizadas {n}" (`field.tk.doneCount`, `field.tk.toDoCount`, `field.tk.skippedCount`, in en and es). The per-task status chip keeps the singular `field.tk.done` / `field.tk.skipped`.
**Tests:** unit `jest/unit/field-tasks-summary-es.test.ts` ("REQ-1167 …": `fmtDayLabel('2026-11-19','es')` → "Jue 19 de nov"; the tk-summary row uses `fmtDayLabel(date, lang)`, not `fmtDay`; its chips use `field.tk.doneCount` / `toDoCount` / `skippedCount`, not the status keys; es values are "Completadas" / "Pendientes" / "No realizadas", en has the keys) · int n/a — front-end formatting and copy only, no backend involved · e2e `e2e/field-tasks-summary-es/field-tasks-summary-es.e2e.test.ts` ("REQ-1167 (LOOP-007 q3-99) …": a Spanish owner with one completed task today opens /field/tasks?lang=es; the tk-summary day equals the browser's capitalised es-MX label, the done chip reads "Completadas 1", the to-do chip "Pendientes 0"). Note for the fixer: if en `field.tk.doneCount` is not "Complete", REQ-284's story in `e2e/field-tasks/field-tasks.e2e.test.ts` (`/Complete 1/i`) needs updating.
**Evidence RED (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-99 at 0a71387e):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/field-tasks-summary-es.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 failed, 1 passed, 4 total` (`Expected pattern: /fmtDayLabel\(date, lang\)/` against `{date ? fmtDay(date, lang) : ""}`; `Expected pattern: /t\("field\.tk\.doneCount"\)/`; es count keys `undefined, undefined, undefined`); `BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5947 shots run e2e/field-tasks-summary-es -- --no-check` → `✗ REQ-1167 … expectation failed: the day header is the capitalised label (["jue 19 de nov","Completada 1","Pendientes 0"]) — expected "Jue 19 de nov", got "jue 19 de nov"`.
**Fix (fix/q3-q3-99):** `front-end/islands/FieldTasksPage.tsx` renders the tk-summary day with `fmtDayLabel(date, lang)` (imported from `lib/field.ts`), and its three chips read `field.tk.doneCount` / `field.tk.toDoCount` / `field.tk.skippedCount`. New keys in `lang/en.json` ("Complete" / "To do" / "Not done", so REQ-284's `/Complete 1/i` story holds) and `lang/es.json` ("Completadas" / "Pendientes" / "No realizadas"), placed after `field.tk.skipped`, well before the trailing comms.a2p.* keys. The per-task status chips stay on the singular `field.tk.done` / `field.tk.skipped`. `field.tk.toDo` was only ever the summary's counter label, so it is now `field.tk.toDoCount` and the dead key is gone. **Test change (REQ-284):** `jest/unit/field-task-summary.test.ts` pinned the old key name `t("field.tk.toDo")` and its en/es values. It now pins `field.tk.toDoCount` with the same values ("To do" / "Pendientes") and still checks "never field.tk.assigned", so the intent is unchanged and only the key was renamed, as this requirement requires.
**Evidence GREEN (2026-11-19, fix/q3-q3-99):** `cd jest && npx jest unit/field-tasks-summary-es.test.ts unit/field-task-summary.test.ts` → `Test Suites: 2 passed, 2 total · Tests: 10 passed, 10 total`. Whole jest unit project (`npx jest --selectProjects unit …`) → `Test Suites: 680 passed, 680 total · Tests: 1 skipped, 6535 passed, 6536 total`. `cd front-end && deno lint islands/FieldTasksPage.tsx && deno check islands/FieldTasksPage.tsx` → `Checked 1 file`, `Check islands/FieldTasksPage.tsx`. Live server PORT=5947 on a scratch KV: `shots run e2e/field-tasks-summary-es -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-1167 (LOOP-007 q3-99) … 'Completadas 1' · 32.5s`. `shots run e2e/field-tasks -- --no-check` → `✓ REQ-284: … the summary reads Complete 1 · To do 0 … · 8.4s`, all other stories ✓ except `✗ REQ-143`. REQ-143 fails the same way when run on its own: it waits for "No tasks this day." on the worker screen's tomorrow view, but the screen renders `worker.day.none` "No tasks this day" with no trailing period (screenshot 036-click.png). That is a mismatch already present in WorkerScreen/its story. This fix does not touch WorkerScreen.tsx or any worker.* key, so it is out of scope here.
